title: A good game that tries to break the mold (but probably shouldn't have)
text:
This review is based on the final beta weekend, which after playing I decided to go ahead and pre-purchase, but the game is not without some flaws, yet it is far FAR better than other recent offers in this genre (The Secret World I am looking in your direction!).

The graphics are well done and you really get a good sense of an immense world... it ALMOST felt too big and the directions you could go were fairly limitless.

The questing system was one of the better ones, as it gave you enough guidance to get you where you needed to go, but not so much that it was holding your hand. Further, you felt free to pursue whatever quests you wanted without being forced in a particular direction.

The game makes use of dynamic events, which is a little similar to rift, in that SOMETHING happens nearby and asks all nearby players to work towards a common goal. These are often helpful in also completing your quests. However, on the downside, I felt they relied on the dynamic events a little TOO MUCH, as it seemed one was popping up every 5 minutes, making them quickly become less of a special thing and more common place. Spacing them out more (maybe 1 or 2 per hour) would make them feel more special. Withing a few hours of questing, I was starting to ignore the onscreen notification of "an event is taking place nearby".

I really liked the PvP systems they developed for this game. First you have an arena style pvp zone, where you automatically get pumped up to top level, given all your skills and given the high end gear for your character. There are several different "capture the flag" style zones that you can jump right into and start pvp'ing as soon as you get into the game. In this same zone they also have tournament PvP, where you can get together with a pre-made group and battle other pre-made groups in the same zones. ( I spent most of my time during this beta in this zone so I could get an idea of the full capabilities of all the classes and once I got my grove, it was a blast!)

Secondly in PvP you have a WvWvW (world v world v world) system in which your entire server battles against other servers for dominance by capturing forts and key points on a map from one another. This really adds a added bonus to the game in that you feel a greater sense of purpose in joining with people on your own server to work together towards a common goal. There is no need to party up or join a raid, but you can still join in the battle and work together.

For me, the biggest negative, and the only reason I give this game only 3 stars is that in a decision to "break the mold" of MMORPGs the developers decided to do away with the "holy trinity" of DPS/TANK/HEALER and rather make each class self-sufficient. While I completely appreciate the thought, I don't think it quite worked out the way they planned and it seemed to do more to frustrate gameplay a little bit. While I agree that the idea of "needing a healer" or "needing a tank" to complete a raid or form a team needs to change, trying to completely eliminate these roles really diminishes the fun for people (like me) who flat out LIKE playing the healer or tank. This is where I felt The Secret World had a great idea (keep the basic dynamic, but allowing a character change professions on the fly), but they screwed up the questing system so much they made the game unplayable. So.. if you are someone who likes playing a healer or a tank, this game will be a little frustrating, because the playstyle you have become used to isn't supported here.

Further, it seems that while they eliminated "traditional" roles, class makeup still seemed to play a HUGE role in who won matches. Two Guardians (the closest they have to a "tank class" could essentially act as a single tank for an entire party (by chaining their conditional removal and regeneration efforts, they become almost unbeatable) and Warriors, when paired with elementalists, could deliver HUGE burst DPS through combinations... so while the stated goal of not having a healing class or a tank class was to remove the necessity of particular group make ups, there is STILL the necessity of group make ups if you want to win matches.

In short, while each individual class is nicely balanced against each other (no one class is really OP), group makeup still plays the primary role in how you will succeed and if you don't have the right class composition, you are going to lose your match, thus undermining the entire reason they eliminated the "holy trinity" to begin with.

While these are problems with the game play, it is still a fun game with lots of potential. For a "beta" it seemed EXTREMELY polished and ready to go. I am looking forward to seeing the final release.

title: Not what it promises to be.
text:
This is a game that had a TON of potential, but completely missed the mark.

I was extremely excited for all that this game promise.. This game promises No Classes, No Levels, Total Freedom of Play...the reality of the game is quite different.

I think everyone understood there was some wiggle room in their marketing statements, as there would be some type of progression and "leveling", which there is. Instead of the traditional leveling, you earn Skill Points and Ability points and apply them to a "skill wheel", which unlocks different skills for different weapons. This ultimately allows for a single character to take on any role in the game.. wanna be a tank, switch weapons, wanna be a healer, switch weapons, so the only real reason to create an "alt" is to join a different faction or for cosmetic purposes.

Unfortunately, where the game goes horribly wrong is in the forced progression curve, which winds up being far more restrictive and linear than many of the other MMORPG's I played (including SWTOR, which had a very linear and specific storyline to follow).

The usual MMO experience is you move into a zone, pick up all the quests, do the quests, gain experience "clear" the zone and then move onto the next, harder zone. Some people choose to focus on one quest at a time, some people follow a specific storyline, and some people grab everything in place and grind through quests as fast as possible... Secret World is NO DIFFERENT in set up. If you do not clear most of the zone, you will not be powerful enough to move onto the next zone. However, unlike other MMO's, Secret World restricts HOW you go through the zone and forces you to constantly backtrack in a forced time sink.

In The Secret World, you accept mission A from character A. On the way to your objective you encounter character B who requests you also to complete a task at the same place. You go to accept this new missions thinking "cool, I can kill two birds with one stone" and you get a warning window that you must "pause" quest A to accept quest B. If you choose to pause quest A and take quest B, you have to go back to character A to "unpause" quest A, leaving you to run back and forth over the same ground several times... and it isn't just character A and B, you come across character C, D, E, F and G along the way and each time you talk to them you are told you can't accept their missions without abandoning the mission you are on... Freedom of play? Why can't I get BOTH bandages and medication from the pharmacy at the same time?? No, I have to get the bandages, return them to character A, then find character D again, go back to the same pharmacy and find the medication and return it to character D and then hunt out character B who wanted water from the store which was right next to the pharmacy.

The developers have offered several conflicting excuses for this baffling limitation, everything from "memory problems on the backend" to it being a high level decision made to force you to get immersed in each mission, instead of treating characters like mission hubs. Ultimately, one honest dev admitted that if they removed the limitation it would break the progression curve and they would have to reduce the amount of experience you gained from each mission and people would complain there isn't enough content. (ie, we need to force you to run back and forth because you would progress through the game too fast if we allowed you to follow a logical progression.)

This brings me back to the main selling point... "TOTAL FREEDOM OF PLAY" If I am someone who chooses to grind quests, why is there something wrong with that? If am someone who WANTS to focus on one quest at a time, great. If I want to do 3 at a time, why am I not allowed to make that choice? They made it 100% clear in the forums that this system was NOT up for debate and would NOT be changed under any circumstances. This non-intuitive questing system made the game feel like work, rather than fun. I was looking for a game that offered more freedom of gameplay and this felt exactly the opposite.

next zone. however, unlike other mmo's, secret world restricts how you go through the zone and forces you to constantly backtrack in a forced time sink. in the secret world, you accept mission a from character a. on the way to your objective you encounter character b who requests you also to complete a task at the same place. you go to accept this new missions thinking "cool, i can kill two birds with one stone" and you get a warning window that you must "pause" quest a to accept quest b. if you choose to pause quest a and take quest b, you have to go back to character a to "unpause" quest a, leaving you to run back and forth over the same ground several times... and it is not just character a and b, you come across character c, d, e, f and g along the way and each time you talk to them you are told you ca not accept their missions without abandoning the mission you are on... freedom of play? why ca not i get both bandages and medication from the pharmacy at the same time?? no, i have to get the bandages, return them to character a, then find character d again, go back to the same pharmacy and find the medication and return it to character d and then hunt out character b who wanted water from the store which was right next to the pharmacy. the developers have offered several conflicting excuses for this baffling limitation, everything from "memory problems on the backend" to it being a high level decision made to force you to get immersed in each mission, instead of treating characters like mission hubs. ultimately, one honest dev admitted that if they removed the limitation it would break the progression curve and they would have to reduce the amount of experience you gained from each mission and people would complain there is not enough content. (ie, we need to force you to run back and forth because you would progress through the game too fast if we allowed you to follow a logical progression.) this brings me back to the main selling point... "total freedom of play" if i am someone who chooses to grind quests, why is there something wrong with that? if am someone who wants to focus on one quest at a time, great. if i want to do 3 at a time, why am i not allowed to make that choice? they made it 100% clear in the forums that this system was not up for debate and would not be changed under any circumstances. this non-intuitive questing system made the game feel like work, rather than fun. i was looking for a game that offered more freedom of gameplay and this felt exactly the opposite.

title: A great start with lots of potential - Potential failed... Cancelled my sub.
text:
Leaving my previous review below, because it was written before patch 1.2 and what this game was to become, so you can read my original optimism!

What ruined potential. Once you hit level 50, the game becomes an absolute mindless grind, with no sense of purpose at all. It is one thing to do the same raids over and over if they are fun or have purpose, but it loses its luster quickly and becomes the usual (stand on the x, hit the 3 key seven times, then the 5 key times and then stand on spot Y). The PvP (basically now reduced to warzones ONLY) have absolutely no sense of purpose, except to grind for gear. They are supposedly introducing "team" play, but they missed the opportunity to have a overall purpose to the PvP, such as helping your chosen FACTION. Open world PvP is non-existent and had no sense of purpose either.

For a game that started off telling an amazing story... it completely loses its way towards the end and you just don't care about what happens anymore.

Space combat.. great potential gone wrong. You wind up repeating the exact same space missions during your initial progressions. (The level 40 missions are the exact same as the level 20 missions, just with slightly higher goals (kill 40 fighters instead of 20).

When they added content to the story in patch 1.2.. I didn't both to complete it as I had stopped caring about the storyline.

It's a shame, because this could have been a fantastic game, but they took the easy way out and decided to turn it into a mindless grind.

This is defiantly one of the better MMO's and has some aspects that make it much better than the rest.

The Best Aspects:

The story line is fantastic and the voice acting makes it much more enthralling than other games which simply present you with a wall of text. It maintains the feel of both an MMO and single player game.

Crafting. Finally a game got this right. You don't have to spend endless boring hours grinding away at resource gathering and standing over a forge. You get companions in the game and send them on missions and they gather the resources for you and craft the items, earning you experience. This is the first MMO where I am actually doing the crafting.

They have nice bonus systems to encourage you to group, but you don't HAVE TO if you don't want to in order to complete your story line. (If you group with others you earn experience from them completing quests as well as you own, so you level much faster!)

The Good Aspects:

Space combat is a lot of fun, but isn't fleshed out yet. You can do space missions, but are essentially stuck on a rail as your ship steers itself through space and you control where and what you shoot, with small room for movements.

Characters are pretty customizable, as you can switch your skill tree. So you can go up the healing tree and then decide you want to do DPS and go back to your trainer and spend some credits to reassign your skills. (You get the first swap for free). You can also create interesting hybrid characters, who can serve dual purposes.

What needs work:

The PVP just isn't there yet. There isn't anything to encourage people into open world PvP, so it is pretty much restricted to "warzones". These are mini, repeatable instances where they put equal number of republic and empire and give them a goal to achieve. Great idea.. execution isn't there yet. There is no in game voice communication, so you get thrown into a random group and then it becomes difficult to execute because you can't communicate quickly. Further they put people of all levels into the same warzone and although they scale your HP up to level 50, unless you are level 50, your gear and skills aren't on par. (Hopefully they will bracket the warzones in the future to make them more balanced).

Overall, however, this is a great game that has lots of potential. Hopefully they resist the urge to go with other MMO's have gone before them and just turn it into a constant grind for gear. Right now, it isn't grindy and that alone makes it worth playing!

title: Meh.. got really bored
text:
I really liked Dragon Age Origins and wound up playing it multiple times through on different classes. I believe my gameplay time was 60 hours, mostly because I wanted explore every nook of the game.

I just finished Dragon Age II this afternoon in 35 hours of playtime. I COULD have played longer, but was getting incredibly bored with doing the same types of quests in the same locations over and over again, so I ultimately chose to just head for the endgame and get it over with.

With Dragon Age: Origins you had a sense of purpose and a goal you felt you were reaching for...

In Dragon Age II you feel as if you are wandering about aimlessly doing quests for cash, because in reality that is what you are doing most of the time.

[tiny spoiler in next paragraph]

About 30% of the way into the game you feel as if you are finally breaking away from the city, when you join an expedition into the deep roads. I was excited when this part came up as I felt it was going to lead to the rest of the quest.. however, once you are done with the expedition, you go BACK to the city and start doing the repetitive questing again until the end of the game.

After 30 hours, the game started to feel really "grindy", just doing stuff so you can gain levels.. cash.. and equipment. If I want to grind I will go play an MMORPG.. PS3 games shouldn't have these aspects as part of the basic gameplay. Now that I am done, I have no desire to go back and play again with a different strategy. Of the 35 hours I played... I'd say 30 of them were spent in the exact same locations doing the same thing.

With the above said.. it is not ALL bad. The graphics were fantastic. The characters were interesting and fun.. especially the interplay between them. The fighting was ramped up a lot from the first version, making it a nice challenge at times and I was really enjoying it up until [same small spoiler about to happen] you wind up BACK in town after finally getting out of that place.

Overall.. if you are just looking for the Dragon Age experience... it will fill that void. However, if you are looking for an epic storyline and lots of adventure... find something else. This will likely frustrate you more than you will enjoy it.

title: Doesn't live up to its expectations...
text:
I am a huge fan of Roberta Williams, her King's Quest games have offered me hours of entertainment since I was about 9 years old. When I heard that she was taking on a more "adult" project featuring real actors and a gripping, horror-based storyline, I was more than excited. However, I received nothing but disappointment.
The graphics in this game are most impressive (considering the time that the game was created). They feature real actors who are placed in front of a blue screen with a cartoon-ish backround and props projected behind them. This gives the game a fairly realistic effect although at times the actors look so out of place in front of their backrounds that the occuring event is everything but real.
As far as the acting goes..it's about what you'd expect from a game which resembles a B horror movie. Most of the acting is barely believeable (although Adrienne, the main character, is not horrible) and the characters themselves are most annoying.
The story was just awful...cliched and robbed to the core, I found absolutely everything in this game to be entirely predictable. It focuses around a couple, Don and Adrienne, who move into a huge, spooky house on an island. The house was owned by a creepy count named Carno and it is said to be haunted. All of the islanders are afraid of the house and none of them are too keen on talking about it (with the exception of one eager old woman who serves as the "revelation of the evil within" source seen in all movies of this sort). The story proceeds just as you would predict. Without giving anything away I'll just tell you that Adrienne discovers ghosts, secret rooms, and a demon which has been wreaking havoc on the house for years. It borrows heavily from Stephen King's "The Shining" (as in..the house turns the husband into a raving psychopath). For anyone who is not too familiar with the horror genre, Phantasmagoria may provide a few hours of good story. To fans of classic horror movies and games, Phantasmagoria will become stale before the end of chapter three.
This brings me to the gameplay. The game itself is divided into 7 chapters (each chapter contained entirely on its respective disk). While this may seem as though it allows for a massive game, it must be said that each chapter can be completed in a quick half hour, even by the most inexperienced of adventure gamers. The puzzles that each chapter requires you to solve are completely lacking in challenge. They are solved by the use of obvious items in Adrienne's inventory and no logical thought is necessary. There was actually a chapter in the game which focused entirely on buying a bottle of Dran-O from the village general store and returning it to your husband. Yes - that's it. Later - a puzzle comes up where the very item you need can be found a single screen below and it is not hidden in the very least.
To fans of blood and gore - this game may serve as an enjoyable "shockfest". There is more than one moment of senseless violence which is not limited to beheading, faces being ripped open, and the funneling of human body parts down a woman's throat. For those too squeamish to even imagine such things, the gore can easily be censored with an in-game option requiring the entry of a password (to protect the little ones' virgin eyes).
Overall, Phantasmagoria lacks in every area required to make an adventure game reach "classic" status. The story is predictable, the gameplay simple and stale, and the characters annoying. For huge fans of senseless violence and B-movie horror plots, this may serve as some sort of "cult classic" piece. All others, don't waste your money.

title: Impressive
text:
"Wow," is the best I can think of to say about this game. It's really something and I like it a lot. Usually I only play serious strategy games such as Civilization and my past forays into console games have been far less than satisfactory. Thanks to the other reviewers here I decided to give this one a try and I'm very glad I did.

At first I was wondering if it is just an interactive story. I'm not much for the story aspects of games and it took several scenes before actual game play comes up. Surprisingly, I held in there and after the first couple short missions I was hooked. The story itself is not overly original but also not so common as to be boring. The main characters are likeable enough and as things progressed I found myself interested in what was going on and anxious to find out what would happen next.

So then, the Pros: The Graphics, great! I wasn't sure what to think of the watercolor/cartoon/anime mix at first but after seeing it in action I'm hooked. While most modern games seem to be going for the "real as life" look this game looks softer, less in your face. Also on the plus side of things is the ease of play. It was easy to learn how things work and to understand the goals and objectives set out. I got an Xbox controller to use with it, my first time ever using one, and I'm having a great time with it.

Another plus, to me, is the music. I often turn the music or all sound off when playing games because I usually find it distracting or somehow undesirable. This one is different and interesting is that parts of the music, while certainly different, is reminiscent of songs I've heard, some old and some not so old.

On the Cons side of things I'm coming up a little short. I would prefer to not have go through a configuration launcher every time and sometimes the story plays on emotions in ways I'd rather it didn't. Sometimes the story scenes are a bit long and I would get impatient for the next mission. And of course there's always those times such as when my best gunner totally misses the house sized tank 20 feet in from of him and gets me ranting and wanting an undo/redo/wtf button. But that's part of luck and chance and it wouldn't be a real game without. None of these things warrant losing even one star so my rating stands at 5 out of 5.

All in all I think this is one of the most refined and polished games I've ever played. It's done. Totally complete and playable on initial download. No waiting weeks or months for patches and updates. No hours spent grinding through forums hoping to find a fix for some inane problem. This game works and works well.

When the next episode or book in the story is released for the PC I will most certainly buy it too.

5 out of 5 stars for this one and kudos for the developers. Well Done!

Or for after my evening workout session, and I want to go lay on the couch comfortably.

title: You become a worse player!
text:
So we gave our Wii new life in this "Stay at Home" world. I bought the Wii when it first came out, back when I had no children. LOL! I have two kids now and the Wii is getting a new life. But I digress... about these guns. Three things I don't like....

1. You're kinda inserting your wiimote in at an angle. You basically place your wiimote on top of the gun mold "bed," but it cannot clear yet until you angle it and start to insert it into the connector. Then you can push it down flat. Connecting plugs and ports at an angle is uncomfortable to me. I feel eventually you will ruin the connector or port.

2. So in most Wii shooting games, the B button is your trigger, it is the button on the back of the Wiimote. So all these gun accessories are built so that when you pull the trigger, the mechanism inside then clicks the B button. So for a good gun accessory, the trigger on the gun mold should be as easy and as quick as clicking the B button on the Wiimote. Well, that's not the case with this gun, so you become a worse player. There is more resistance with the trigger, as well as more travel time. Travel time is how long it takes for you to completely pull the trigger. When you're just playing around with it and pulling the trigger. It's just like any other toy gun, you don't think anything about it. title: Wavebird owners, this is the adapter to buy!
text:
July 15, 2020 UPDATE:
--------------------------
This is not necessarily a review update, but more of a FYI, or food for thought. Though this is an excellent item, I've since discovered other products on the market that does the same job at a fraction of a price. There are adapters, for less than $10, that plug into your Switch, and it has 4 gamecube ports. I realized that for my use case scenario, I over spent. The main benefit of these Retro Fighter adapters is if you're using WIRED gamecube controllers. This way, you don't have wires running to and from your switch. You can just place the adapter at your feet, and the wires will be running from your feet to your hands. But it's overkill if you're using Wave Bird receivers. You are going wireless on top of wireless. There wasn't any lag issues, everything was fine. But you're paying a premium to do that. With those 4 port adapters. You plug it into your switch, and you can sill be wireless if you're using Wave Bird receivers. The downside is simply aesthetics because your switch will have these adapters plugged into it. But man, you can use 4 wave bird receivers for around $10 versus having to spend about $68 ($17 x 4) to use the retro fighter adapter, since each adapter is only good for one controller. Food for thought!

----------------------
Much better than the 8bitdo design. Not sure why 8bitdo insisted on their design, but because they did, they lose out on customers who own wavebird controllers. Their Gbros is only good for wired gamecube controlers. You could try and hack off some of the plastic to accommodate the wavebird receiver. But why pay more to do more modding? The Warrior adapter is less expensive and doesn't need modifications. Easy to pair too. Now, plug in your wavebird receiver and turn on your gamecube controller. Awesome!

title: Lack of info for PS3 controllers, and terrible design.
text:
I have two complaints.

Complaint #1
-----------------
They really leave you in the wind with this product. I figured it out, but I'm wondering about people who are not as resourceful. The description implies you just plug it into the Switch, and you start pairing. That is not the case, at least it's not the case for PS3 controllers. There are no instructions, so naturally, I went to 8bitdo's website. On their site, there is something called the PS3 PAIRING TOOL. Sounds like what I need, so I downloaded it. In the downloaded folder is a README file. How often do people read the README files? Luckily I did! It says that before I can launch the software, I need to install a program called the SixaxisPairToolSetup-0.3.0.exe, or I can "Temporarily disable driver signature enforcement." For this 2nd option, there is a bunch of screenshots showing you how to do it in windows. I tried the 1st option first, and after installing the sixaxispairtool, it told me to restart. After restarting, normally a software will launch itself to help you along where you left off, but not this one. Once you restart, it was gone. LOL! So I thought maybe the magic has been done, so I proceeded to launch the PS3 pairing tool, but it didn't work. It would not recognize my ps3 controller. So I decided to try the second option, temporarily disable driver signature enforcement. For this option, I recommend you guys put all the instructional screenshots in your dropbox, then you can follow along reading the instructions from your phone. Because doing these steps will put you in a RECOVERY mode, so you can't view those screenshots anymore. They didn't make this accessory for everybody. They made it for techies and tinkerers who will go out of their way to make it work.

Complaint #2
----------------
8bitdo isn't too good at adapter designs. Take their Gbros adapter for example. It doesn't fit wavebird receivers, not because it isn't compatible, but because of the design. So Retro Fighters basically just built a new shell for that receiver and fixed the issue. So it isn't too surprising to me that this wireless receiver is a bad design too. Why did they make the usb brick casing so fat? You have to imagine that many people have two ps3 or ps4 controllers, that they may want to buy 2 receivers like I did. Well, two receivers will not fit at the same time on the Dock side ports. If you want to use two, you'll have to use a USB A to A extender, or a hub. There is one more usb port in the back of the Dock between the HDMI and Power ports. Guess what, it won't fit there either. If I try to squeeze the brick in, it will lift the power and hdmi cables from their ports at an angle, and this can especially damage the power cable.

I like to imagine this is what happened during product development...

8bitdo: "This is a beautiful design, and when our fans buy ONE receiver to add ONE PlayStation controller, they will be very happy."
Employee: "Should we design it so TWO receivers will fit on the side ports? Maybe also make it fit on the 3rd port in the back? Also, we might want to add a step by step manual for ps3 controllers"
8bitdo: "What's your name? You are fired!"

title: Great in some ways, not so in others
text:
Ok first off, I had the Rift before this S model, so this is somewhat of a comparison.

The Rift S is definitely more comfortable than it's predecessor. The foam is soft and it seems a tad lighter. I wear glasses, and the S does not rest on them as much as the last generation, which is good. I can spend much more time using the Rift S because it's comfort is that much better. The S also slips on and off my face a lot easier than the last generation and I have a large head, being 6'5" @ 275lbs.

It is great that it does not use external sensors to track movement, because it is just far less cumbersome and more of a simple plug and play device now. I have an Acer Predator 17, which has a display port, but the Rift S does come with an adapter if yours does not.

The controllers are the same size and weight, which is really good. They are far less bulky than it's competitors, which makes using the VR much more enjoyable in my opinion.

Headset tracking of itself is flawless, it is right on when you move your head around. However, I do get headset out of bounds type messages just looking around sometimes and that is annoying.

Eye relief, I don't really know about. I've adjusted it to max (72) and least and noticed zero difference in anything.

The bad news.

External tracking of the controllers is glitchy and glitchy a lot. You no longer have a fine tracking experience that is so smooth, as it was in the previous Rift. Your hands in the VR like to twitch, jump and sometimes freeze. It's not 100% of the time that it does this, but it happens frequently enough to be bothersome. The rest of the time it is smooth and responsive.

Optics. This is where the Rift S falls even shorter, in my experience. For starters, your field of view has reduced and it is not quite as immersive as the previous Rift. For example, it is as though you are looking through toilet paper tubes now, as there are large black areas of nothing surrounding the visual field. Tunnel vision. Although the experience is still fun, I am very disappointed in this, as it has lost some of it's VR experience as a result.

The resolution is supposed to be higher, but I do not see that at all. Fonts are still grainy and it is too similar to the last Rift to say that there is much, if any improvement in resolution.

The screen brightness is less in the Rift S, so it loses points for that. Although still pretty vibrant, it's just lacking something I can't exactly put my finger on.

Overall, it is a step back from the Rift in the critical areas a VR should be and a step forward in comfort and convenience. It all depends on what is more important to you.

title: Excellent Value for a One-Handed Mechanical Gaming Keyboard
text:
RedThunder One-Handed Mechanical Gaming Keyboard is a functional half keyboard with mechanical keys. The only issue I ran into during my use of this item was that once the re-bindable macro keys were altered, I was unable to revert them into the original "F" keys they began. The instructions were difficult to fully understand. I am uncertain if it was due to translation difficulties or a lack of space on the small pamphlet.

RedThunder One-Handed Mechanical Gaming Keyboard allowed me to conserve space on my desk. The keyboard is a good starting point for any gamer interested in an mechanical keyboard that does not want to commit to the higher price for a full keyboard.

With small rubber-like feet to help keep it in place and the light weight design the product can help on-the-go laptop users. The keyboard had built in anti-ghosting, so you would not drop keys when pressing multiples at the same time. This will allow more hectic game-play without dropped inputs. The half of the keyboard you get with this covers most basic PC games (most First person shooters), but may leave you lacking for games which expect a full range (such as Smite or a multitude of strategy games).

A small card that came with the keyboard from the creator pressing for those with issues to reach out to the makers and those with positive opinions to share their opinion. The website advertised by the production company was mostly not useful as I was unable to find anything of great use and there was a number of translation errors on the physical box [example: "Fast eating chicken stability with many key no conflict reaction"].

Overall, I find RedThunder One-Handed Mechanical Gaming Keyboard is a good product. It's ideal for someone who is looking to reduce their wear and tear on a laptop, shared keyboard, an addition to their portable/space sensitive options, or anyone wanting to dip their toes into a mechanical keyboard.

Of note: the box does not mention support for windows 10. They keys are click-y and the extra volume can be jarring for those whom live in close quarters.

Thank you for reading my review. I hope you have found it helpful and informative.

title: Nicest headphones I have ever owned
text:
These headphones are really beautiful. I've used a lot of different headphones and these are the most comfortable headphones I have ever worn. They don't put pressure on your ears or head. The ear cushions are exquisite. So comfortable.

The sound quality is really good. While playing Valheim, I could easily detect the direction where the cackling Fulings are hiding in the brush, or when a Draugr is trying to sneak up behind me. I really appreciate that level of sensitivity in headphones.

I don't have a cellphone, so I can't speak about the Bluetooth functions. I will say though , that some of the technical mechanics of the headphones were a little hard for me to figure out. The instruction manual wasn't much help. I am a technical dummy. My level of technical expertise is basically, find the button, push it, and I expect it to work. If it doesn't work, I will get immensely frustrated. I found myself getting very frustrated trying to get my headphones to work. I thought I was following instructions, but it just wasn't working. I didn't realize that I needed to push so hard to get it to click into place. One of the things that confused me, is that the cord has a control on it, for sound. The control has no marks on it. There were 3 buttons and I couldn't figure out what all of them were for. The long was was a volume control. I got that one. I still don't understand what the other two buttons are for. It would have been nice if this was explained better in the manual, and if they were actually visibly marked with clear, understandable icons.

Basically, these are really great headphones. I just think that the company is trying to hard to look cool at the expense of functionality and customer accessability. Perhaps the company feels that it's customer base are savvy techies that would appreciate the level of coolness that they are trying to achieve, but that leaves us normals frustrated and struggling to understand how to use their product. If the company reads this review...fyi. Normals like great sounding gaming too. Make these easier to use.

Since you play as one type of character (mage, warrior, assassin, etc...) you can play the game more than once using a different skill set each time. You can also choose whether to be evil or good, which will change the story as well. If you like Oblivion, Dragon Age or The Witcher, I think you will really enjoy this game as well. There are multi-player online options of play as well, that will further extend your enjoyment of the game.

title: Smaller than I expected, but still useable.
text:
There are many third-party switch controllers on the market and each make claims about compatibility or useability. It takes a little bit of digging to actually know which one is worth getting.

The listing doesn't say it but this controller's brand is Sound Fox. It is a fairly compact controller that is noticeably smaller than the Switch Pro controller. It is actually well-built and has a great texture. The entire controller feels soft and satin with nice analog sticks that don't feel loose. The buttons feel good and the digital pad is fairly standard.

Outside of these basic features, the controller has two programmable buttons in the back and turbo mode for all of the face and shoulder buttons. The programmable buttons actually can remember fairly long sequences of button presses and digital pad inputs. I used it to go through some particularly annoying menus in Xenoblade 3 that I needed to do over and over again (collectopedia). I programmed a series of presses, holds and wait times that allowed me to go through the menu 5 times with each press of the programmable button.

What's more, the vibration strength is programmable, the face plate is easily removeable (although I haven't seen replacement faceplates available) and even Amiibo support is built in. It really is a good value for the price. Aside from the smaller size, this is a great replacement for the Pro controller.

On the PC, this is a great bluetooth controller that can operate in Xinput mode for maximum game compatibility. This feature is something you don't find in many other third party controllers out there.

The only problem I have with this controller is the fact that the ZL and ZR triggers are digital only. When using this controller on the PC, you really need to have analog triggers to get the most out of many games.

In the end, this product is geared toward the Switch and has the added option to be used on the PC and mobile phones but without analog triggers, it really is only good on the Switch.

title: No need for a fancy dock.
text:
The fancy docks that you see for the Quest 2 usually has a place for charging the goggles, and two spots for the controllers. The only problem is that the docks are made for the controllers without the silicone sleeves that people usually put on their controllers. In fact, there aren't many solutions out there that allow charging while using the silicone sleeves.

With this All-in-One Magnetic Charging Kit for Oculus Quest 2, I'm able to resolve all of my problems. This system is well thought out. It comes with two rechargeable batteries and special battery covers that expose a magnetic charging port on the side of the controller. It also comes with a magnetic type-c connector for your goggles.

By cutting a small hole in the silicone sleeve, I'm able to charge the controllers without removing the sleeve and the cables are easy to connect because of the magnetic connectors. The goggle is just as easy to charge with its corresponding magnetic connector.

There are two problems with this system that you need to be aware of, though. The first is that the type-c connector is not very strong. It means that when pulling off the charging cable, the type-c plug with come with it. The second problem is that the three devices will be sharing a single cable and thus, sharing the available amps. The charging speed will suffer as a result.

Overall, not having to go through the hassle of removing the silicone sleeve to change batteries makes this kit worth the purchase. I don't have long play sessions with the VR system so I'm not so worried about charging speed.

title: Great nose piece but headband needs work.
text:
This X-super Home product for the Oculus Quest 2 comes with a headstrap and silicone face cover. Both of these things are accessories that every Quest 2 must get and there are many options available to fit the bill.

Out of the box, the Quest 2 comes with elastic straps that just aren't enough to hold the VR Goggles in place very well. When turning your head, the goggle tends to swing around and feel like they will fall off. Also, if you're one of the early adopters that purchased the Quest 2 before Facebook issued their recall where they will send you a silicone cover for the goggles, you're stuck with a cloth face cover that lets too much light through and gets pretty disgusting after just a short time using the goggle due to sweat.

So the X-Super Home head strap features a battery holder at the back of the head, the theory being that the extra weight of the battery will help to counter balance the weight of the goggles, reducing neck strain while extending the play time of the goggles. In practice, the battery makes the entire setup too heavy and reintroduces the problem of the goggles swinging around when turning your head. In addition, there was a design error on the attachment bracket where the slot is shorter than the tab so the battery holder never fully slides into place.

Due to the placement of the battery, the tightening knob is offset to the right of the battery. This offset design creates a problem with the tightening system where one side would tighten more than the other, giving an unbalanced feel to the strap.

The silicone cover, on the other hand, is quite excellent. It has a texture on it that helps to keep a good grip around the eyes even when you sweat and the flaps over the bridge of the nose is larger than many others out there. While not perfect, it greatly reducing the amount of light that leaks in. Compare this to the silicone cover that Facebook sent as part of their recall, the Facebook cover is smooth and doesn't have a flap at all to cover the bridge of the nose. The X-super Home cover is much better.

So a less-than-ideal head strap and a great silicone cover. Unfortunately, this doesn't justify the price of this product.

text:
I went through a bit of flip-flopping with the Eyglo 5 in 1 Accessories Case for Oculus Quest 2. When I saw the listing for this product, I thought that it was a great set that included everything I needed for the Quest 2, although from the pictures, I did note that the hand strap seemed flimsy.

When I received it, I found that the head strap was made of stiffer plastic than the original straps so it was very difficult to install. I was still worried about the click-in button at the top of the hand strap and the fact that it was so narrow. I expected that any swinging of the controller could slip the strap off. The silicone eye piece fit well, but at first, it gave me a fright because when pressed against the head, the cover would flare out and obstruct the sensor that Oculus proximity sensor, making it think that the headset turn off because it didn't detect a face. I thought my Oculus was broken! Lastly, I found that the controllers were hard to fit into the case (They needed to be looped through each other just so) and even then, the case didn't close without the back piece of the headset pushing against the top, creating a slight bulge. I found that this was a case of "looks good on paper" but not great in actuality.

Because of all of these problems, I was going to give this product 3 stars, but after spending some time with it, I found that I didn't mind any of those shortcomings. The head strap is much more comfortable and secure than the original oculus. The eye piece is MUCH better than the original cloth as sweat is easily wiped off (Facebook is currently addressing this issue and the Oculus will now come with silicone eye pieces). The hand straps turned out to work well enough. I don't worry about losing the controllers because I find that I don't have a tendency to flick the controller with my hand completely open. Lastly, I find that I don't need to use the case when I'm at home so I will only face the awkwardness of putting in the goggles when I intend on taking it on travel.

In the end, I got a complete set of accessories all in one package and they do work. I'm much happier having this set than not. The out-of-the box experience with the Oculus leaves much to be desired and accessories are just a fact of life. Just as purchasing a case for a phone or tablet is just part of the cost of the device.

Firstly, it must be stated that in the early days of Nintendo Switch's launch, Nintendo Switch's adoption of the Type-C PD standard was unknown and news began to emerge that various Type-C chargers were causing electronics to overload. This wasn't limited to just the Switch, but cell phones and laptops were suffering the same issue. At this point, news of those issues have generally subsided. Power adaptor designers have taken safety more seriously and personally, I have been able to use multiple docks and hubs with the Switch with no issues. In short, this KIWIHOME Switch Dock did not blow up my switch.

This KIWIHOME USB C Charger is a very compact dock for the Switch. When travelling, it is usually necessary to pack the official Nintendo Switch charger for power. This third-party charger is no bigger than the OEM charger but has the additional advantage of a detachable charging cable, which means it is even easier to pack.

Of course, the best feature of this charger is the ability to act as a dock. In a normal case, one must add the large Switch dock in addition to an HDMI cable in order to play in docked mode while on travel. This charger allows one to leave the large dock at home. It is an elegant solution.

While on the topic of travel, this charger is rated for 110-220v. This means that with the addition of a plug adapter, this charger will work in Europe as well as the US and around the world.

An issue that one may face due to the design of this product is that the television may not be close enough to an open power socket. This would need to be solved either with a long HDMI cable or an extension cord.

title: joy-cons fit a little too tightly and charging status indication could be better
text:
I purchased this product because I wanted a grip for my second set of joycons and while I was at it, I wanted an easy way to charge those controllers.

Whie this grip looks like it will do everything I need (it will charge the joycons while connected to the power adapter or on battery power and it provides a satin grip that keep the controllers secure), execution could have been better.

Here are some of my complaints:
-- The grip has a satin surface which is somewhat outdated, I think. Most manufacturers mold textures into the plastic to give them grip. My past experience with satin surfaces is that after a few years, they become a sticky mess.
-- Perhaps it is the product that I got but I charged the grip overnight without the joycons inserted and the red charging light was still on when I checked on it in the morning so there is no indication that the charging has completed. This might mean that there is no cut-off for when the battery is fully charged.
-- The joy-cons fit too snugly. It is actually a little difficult to slide the controllers in and out of the grip. This could be because of the satin finish that is sprayed on to the underlying plastic.

Other features:
-- Charges the joycons with the built-in battery pack. A blue light indicates that the controllers are charging.
-- Not much heavier than the original switch grip.
-- Wider than the original grip. For me, this is actually more comfortable.

Again, this will meet my requirements but I wonder how long the internal battery pack will last if there is no charging cut-off.

title: Works with Nintendo Switch!
text:
I didn't know what to expect from this product as I have never owned a pair of gaming headsets, but I wasn't willing to spend hundreds of dollars on a pair of headsets that may or may not enhance my experience.

So let me break down the description given:
-- 7.1 surround - I've always see this more as a gimmick than an actual feature, even in headphones that cost hundreds of dollars but don't have discreet speakers. The computer sees these headsets as stereo and not 7.1 so whatever program you run, whether it's a trailer with Dolby Atmos or a game, the output will still be stereo. While their program supposedly tries to simulate virtual surround, you would still need the source to be 7.1 discreet channels so that their driver can process the signal to simulate surround sound. These headsets do not have DTS-HD or Dolby ATMOS certification so they aren't actually able to process raw 7.1 channel data. It means that in the end, the video player is still just playing stereo sound. The end effect of turning on virtual 7.1 surround sound is that the soundtrack is more "atmospheric" or "wider" sounding, but you wouldn't be able to tell that a sound is coming from your rear left flank. Since I never expected much out of this feature, I didn't mind that it wasn't true 7.1

-- USB - True plug and play on Windows 10. I plugged these headphones in and immediately, Windows output sound through them. No muss no fuss. It just worked. You can install their driver, which turns on the "virtual 7.1" feature but that's pretty much like installing drivers for any realtek sound card. You just have access to a few extra DSP effects. Honestly, I don't like extra processing to my audio signals. Being USB, it is a completely digital signal to your headphones all the way up until the speakers themselves. On 3.5mm headphones, the audio signal is analog at 3.5mm port, at which point, you will get some signal degradation just from the connection itself.

-- Gaming Headset with Microphone - I don't really play games online so I can't tell you whether the microphone is better or worse than any other headset but I can tell you that I used the Spirit Wolf with a few games and I was hearing sounds that I didn't hear in my Sennheisers.

-- PC Gamers - BONUS! This headset isn't just for PC gaming, it works with the Nintendo switch, too, using the USB port on the dock. Even the volume buttons on the headset works!

My overall experience with Spirit Wolf has been positive. The sound is crisp and clear and the high frequencies are very good but the bass could have been better. I'm not big on turning up the bass so it's not a big loss. I still feel that the overall sound quality is very good.

The headset is circumaural which means it surrounds your ears and the speakers are not pressed right against your head. It means that noise isolation isn't as good as earbuds or even supra-aural headphones (which press up against your ear), but there's a reason professional gaming headphones are this style. You can wear them for longer periods without discomfort and you are able to achieve a wider sound.

Overall, I recommend this headset for its price and overall sound quality. The ability to use it with my Switch is just bonus.

EDIT: I must amend my previous conclusions regarding the virtual surround sound. I recently started playing Shadow of the Tomb Raider and as a test, I went into the audio settings for the game. The options were stereo, 5.1, 7.1, and spatial sound. Reading the description for spatial sound, it states that it is meant to be used with Windows Spatial Sound (right click on the speaker icon in your system tray and you'll see an option to turn it on). Well, I tried the spatial sound in three different ways: with only the in-game spatial sound setting on, the in-game setting + Windows Spatial Sound on, and in-game setting + XEar driver 7.1 on. All three give slightly different positional sound effects but I found that the XEar effect was the best. The sounds simulate a wide environment and I was able to distinguish the direction of each distinct sound source. Very impressive.

title: Excellent gaming keyboard and a great value
text:
The switches (Cherry speed silver) are great for gaming with the higher actuation point (quicker key presses) and light actuation force. The keys are relatively quiet, but can be loud if pressed hard, like most keys. Construction seems VERY solid. I love the minimalistic design (it's not compact or scaled down - just less extra area around the outer edges) - it allows more desk space and the option to use your own wrist rests rather than a crappy plastic one many manufacturers add. It has a lot of nice tweaks specifically for gaming, such as wider left shift and control keys and alternate color WASD key caps. The RGB lighting is very customizable, with lots of good presets, but this leads me to the "room for improvement" part of the review, and the only reason I gave it 4 stars instead of 5...

The keyboard supposedly has onboard memory, but will not save custom RGB lighting schemes to the keyboard onboard memory. Arggh! This means that if you use the keyboard on multiple PCs/ other devices, the color profile you spent 30+ minutes designing won't work. Every device HAS to have the ASUS lighting software installed to use your custom RGB layouts, so that can be a problem. If ASUS fixes this, I will change this to 5 stars. One other nice tweak would be to add a silicone layer/barrier between the key caps edges and the keyboard to reduce noise from overly-enthusiastic key presses.

Overall, it's an excellent keyboard for gaming and also works well for typing. I would definitely recommend it - particularly the linear switch versions (cherry red or cherry speed silver) for gaming. This keyboard is also probably one of the best value boards for gaming if you want high quality construction, quality mechanical switches, RGB lighting with various effects and the ability to customize.

title: Decent HARD case for travel - charging a bit of a trick when in case.
text:
Many Nintendo Switch cases have hit the market since the release of the versatile gaming system and this this one meets all of the critical criteria of a good case but falls a bit short in order to be considered great.

The Switch fits perfectly in the top with adequate padding to protect the critical top glass LED screen. The 2 Joy-Con controllers fit snugly into individual slots beneath the main unit and there is another secure area to store the power adapter (and a few games) which is a huge plus for this case - which many other cases neglect.

As I stated, for travel purposes, this case is excellent.

While this case advertises itself as one where you can “charge and play” - that is awkward at best. First the Joy-Cons do not comfortably fit on the primary unit while in the case. If too much pressure is applied to the screen while propped on the stand it moves too much for accurate game play.

I have to give this case 3 STARS - it will definitely protect your Nintendo Switch and all of its necessary accessories when traveling better than many other cases but it won’t be staying in the case as you play...

UPDATE TO ORIGINAL REVIEW: Now that my son has had more time using this case he has told me that he liked it much more than he initially did.

Since I do not actually use the Switch I had to write my review based on his impressions and as he has used it he has liked it more and more. Often when the Nintendo Switch is played in handheld mode the joycons are held separately from the central screen unit so the fact that they don’t fit on it in the case does not matter.

In his opinion this is the best case he has used for his Nintendo Switch and we would definitely recommend it as a great way to protect your investment.

title: There's some good and some bad
text:
First, the good. I was so excited when I found out they were coming out with a second overcooked. I loved the first one and have had hours upon hours of fun playing this game with my family and friends. This second incarnation still has adorable characters and much of the original functionality that the first had. There are some new critters to use ( I personally like the octopus,) and you now have the ability to throw certain things into pots or to other characters, which is a nice improvement. Some of the worlds are challenging and there are new hurdles to overcome, like flames popping up here and there that have to be put out. So there are some good things about it, however, there are also a lot of things that I found lacking.

The levels are way too easy to earn points in. With the first game, you might be lucky if you served a handful of successful dishes and earned a couple of hundred points before the timer ran out. With the second game, you can easily earn more than a thousand points with hardly any effort. I was able to play through this game with my husband in a single afternoon and beat the final level without a problem, literally in less than six hours. That was not the way it was with the first game at all. Whereas in the original overcooked, the last level, when you face the giant meatball you have to really put your heads together and strategise and probably do it over and over again until you are successful, the final level in this game is easy. There isn't much holding you back from doing the level on the very first try.

Some of the levels in this game are simply annoying rather than challenging in any meaningful kind of way. The things that made the first game challenging and fun were the rocking boats, the slippery ice and stuff like that. In this game it feels like they tried too hard to go out of their way to come up with hurdles for you and most of them are just ridiculous. You can easily get around most of them after you figure it out the first time and they don't change much throughout the rest of the game.

The way the menu works annoyed me, because it isn't straight forward to change characters as you wish anymore like it was in the first game, and adding or subtracting players isn't easy anymore either. title: Excellent Quality for a Great Price!
text:
You can't beat the price here. And the quality difference is negligible compared to the actual Switch Pro controller. If you have the Nintendo-branded Switch Pro controller and are very detail-oriented like me, the only differences you will notice are:

1) No Nintendo Switch branding-logo on the front plastic.
2) Plastic is solid black colored vs the dark opaque Nintendo Pro branded controller. And the leopard-skin-like design on the grip handles is different (but I actually really like that--looks cool)
3) The home button cannot wake your Switch. Small price to pay. Either just hit the power button first on your Switch and then home button on this and it quickly connects--or just keep a right joy con near you to wake your Switch with that.
4) The rumble feature on this controller is different. It's a stronger rumble as opposed to Nintendo Pro's more soft and subtle haptic feel. But that's okay with me; and it does feel like it's all or nothing with the rumbling--no high/medium/low levels for it; but for most games, this doesn't bother me. Only on some games where you have a lot of action/shooting/etc, it may become obnoxious (but you can always turn off rumble option in your Switch options).

All in all, this is totally worth it. And just to add to this--the seller is GREAT to deal with. There was a bit of a mishap on my controller. The D-pad directions did not function correctly. I contacted their chat support, and was instructed to email YCCTEAM support; they were great--had me try a few things just to verify the issue. In the end, they quickly sent me a replacement which works perfectly. And best part was they let me keep the first controller! I am a very satisfied customer.

If you are considering a 3rd-party controller but want to keep the look and feel of the Nintendo-branded Pro controller, go with this one. For half the price, you still get practically equal quality. As long as you can withstand those differences listed above, then go for it I say! To me, it's worth saving the $30 from buying Nintendo's overpriced Pro controller.

title: The wireless version is just OK
text:
I noticed a lot of positive reviews for this so I had high hopes for sound quality. I see now that there are 3 different versions of this headset however, a wired standard 3.5mm TRRS one, a USB one, and a wireless one. I got the wireless one, which is also the most expensive version, and I have to admit I'm not impressed with the sound or features. With the glowing reviews, I have to believe the wired ones sound better and the culprit is in the transmitter. The quality of the sound over the wireless transmission is just OK. It's decent enough for VOIP and voice chats, maybe even gaming, but for music or watching videos it falls flat. I was watching a movie on Netflix and the dynamic range sort of collided with itself in such a way that it was hard for me to separate the voices from the background music compared to headphones that cost half as much as these.
That being said, I DO like the microphone and that it can be easily detached. For gamers that want wireless sound and mic for chats when needed, it can be a decent product when it works well. But that leads me to my next point:
The transmitter and headset seem to loose sync everytime one or the other shuts off. You you don't use the headset for a while, it seems to "go to sleep", and if the computer goes into sleep or hibernate, it doesn't seem to reconnect on its own upon waking up. I was trying this on my laptop and constantly felt like I had to power cycle the headset and unplug/plug the USB to get it connected again. Honestly, I feel like I could get a better connection experience and perhaps even sound quality from a pair of BT headphones, and just use my computer's bluetooth system to manage the connection upon waking up. If your computer doesn't have bluetooth, this system can be useful because it works like a USB sound card, but honestly I feel like for the price they are asking it should have been a better experience.
Giving it 3 stars because it's fine for chats, is comfortable to wear and DOES look pretty cool. I just feel like you could do better. The wired versions are likely better.

text: I'm a fan of retro gaming, but installing 8 and 16-bit classics on modern tablets and phones is frustrating to say the least. You need buttons. That's where this adorable and super useful controller comes in. I love that it has several modes for different devices (act like a generic controller, a keyboard, a switch gamepad, etc), and I was able to use it both with a tablet and my Fire TV over bluetooth. It's really great on the Fire TV since the remote that comes with that stinks for gaming. The size is a little less comfortable than a full sized controller, but the portability is great. The button combos to switch modes are a little bit difficult to figure out at first, you need to use the instructions to understand how to set the mode and then put it into pairing to set it up with different devices. For example, hold one button and start for Switch mode, another button and start for Android mode, etc. Then press and hold the other button until it starts blinking to put it into pairing mode after that. And if you don't commit the button combinations to memory, you'll need to look it up in the instructions again. If you only intend to use this with one device, that's less of an issue as you'll probably just set it up once and never change it. But otherwise, I wish there was a cheat sheet or something printed on the back so you wouldn't need to keep the instructions around. All in all, it's still a very functional and great little remote game controller for a great price.

title: Lots of connection types, but annoying USB
text:
These are decent low end headphones. I'm not expecting high quality sound for the price, but they get the job done and have quite decent bass, although other tones could be a little clearer. But I have some issues with the connection type, which is the exact same experience I've had with other headsets in this price range: I like that these come with an option for both stereo and mic jacks (as 2 TRS 3.5mm plugs), or a combined TRRS with both mic and stereo in one (for phones, certain laptops, etc) via an adapter. But it also comes with a big annoying USB A cable which I can't get rid of. I understand the USB cable is for power which works the lights, etc, on this thing, but unlike the 2 cables which can be combined into one for smaller portable devices, the connection ports are just messy with a dangling USB cable if you don't need it.
In my personal opinion, there should be an option to detach the USB cable and/or have it plug into a null adapter on the TRS/TRRS adapter wire so it has somewhere to go. It just looks messy like this, and requires too many ports to look clean on a laptop even if you're using all of them. On a desktop this is less of an issue, however the logo still seems kind of cheesy on the side, so I guess I'm just not a fan of the aesthetics of this set. It DOES work however, so if all you want is the utility of it, it works alright. Personally, I'd go with either a fully digital USB model if you wanted that (nice clean single plug, no analog jacks), or one without the LED lights and therefore doesn't require the USB plug.

title: An Amazing And Engrossing Story
text:
Trevor Noah is a comedian who now hosts the Daily Show. In this engrossing memoir, he writes poignantly about his childhood in South Africa. As the son of a black woman and white man, his birth was a crime since blacks and whites were separated with the strict apartheid laws and interracial marriages were strictly forbidden.

His mother, an unconventional, free spirit, chose to have him with a white man whom she did not love; she wanted a mixed race child.
Trevor’s Swedish father was not usually in the picture, although Trevor saw him in very rare circumstances. Trevor lived with his mother, but even going outside the house was dangerous. They would walk separately and pretend they were not together.

Trevor Noah did not fit easily into any race category. He was light-skinned and considered colored, although his culture was black. He went to a private English Catholic school and spoke perfect English. Colored people distrusted his accent and thought he was trying to be better than them. His mother stressed education, and he learned to speak various African languages, something that also set him apart.

I was unaware that there were so many categories of color under apartheid. The author struggled to fit into one of these groups: white, black, or colored. The categories were somewhat arbitrary. For example, the Japanese were considered white but the Chinese were considered colored.

Colored people were “the almost whites”. They did not have all of the privileges of whites but had more rights than the blacks. Every year some of the people would be recategorized, uplifted to what was considered a “higher” category. These people would have to submit an application and describe their hair, skin color, and other physical features. Some blacks became colored but, in some instances, the reverse occurred.

In addition to the distinct privileges of the racial groups, there were set places for the different color categories to live. This fostered hatred and distrust among the groups.

Trevor Noah writes with a keen sense of humor and dedicates this book to his mother. He credits his strong, fearless mother for giving him the strength and opportunities to be the man he is today.

title: I can't believe this controller gets such high rating. I've never owned a single Xbox. An unbiased review.
text:
I can't believe this controller has 4.5 stars. The only thing I can think of is Sony fanboys inflating the reviews. Here's my honest review from a casual gamer who's had a Sega Master System, Sega Genesis, N64, Dreamcast, Wii, PS3, and PS4. I'm not loyal to any brand or company, so my view should be unbiased.

GOOD:
1. The small speaker on the controller isn't much, but I like it and think it adds something to gaming.
2. The headphone jack is also helpful.
3. The light bar is cool, not only for looks, but to identify the player.
4. Sticks are better than the PS3 sticks.
5. L2/R2 curve in (not as much as it should) which is a big improvement from PS3.
6. The grips are a nice texture which give you a good feeling of control.
7. Sticks are symmetrical (I prefer this).

BAD:
1. Quality/design issues. I've had two controllers break with a faulty R2 button. I was able to repair them myself via YouTube videos, but as a casual gamer, this shouldn't happen since I don't play all that much (2 - 5 hours per week).
2. A big one....battery life sucks. The battery life is about half of my older PS3 controllers (even with the light bar dimmed all the way). I'm always having to charge or worry about if my buddy's controller will fire up since it might have been sitting awhile.
3. Quality/design issues 2: I just noticed the rubber splitting on one of my controller (the one I use the least!). This is unacceptable.
4. Not a big one, but annoying....the option and share buttons are too small and should be more triangular and follow the curve of the circle the face buttons are on (hope that made sense). And I have very small hands for a man.
5. The grips (though well textured) are just round cylinders and don't feel like they mold to your hand. It's not terrible, but could be much much better.
6. Touchpad. Love the idea, however it seems like it's barely used, which means that real estate could have been better used for a one color LCD screen or something else.

That's it! The controller gets the job done, but for how much crap people give the DS3, this DS4 improves upon the DS3 in some areas, and fails miserably at others.

text:
I had MVC3 and traded it in and waited for UMVC3 and I completely wasted my time and money. Hard core fighting gamers will probably love this game, but I consider myself a casual to moderate fighting gamer. Here's the pros and cons:

-Characters are varied
-Marvel superheroes are always cool!

Cons:

That's why everyone I sometimes face user names like "taj134dod"
-The endings are super lame and a huge disappointment.

One opponent used Magento and took almost all my life with one consistant air combo. Go back to a thinking man's fighting game and not fast fingers and NO EXPLOITS. Knocking an opponent into the air and then slamming them back to the ground is fine, but this is just ridiculous.

-Loading and saving. If this game isn't loading it's saving. If it isn't saving, it's loading.

I could go on and on about the game's cons, but unless you're a hard core fighting gamer, than stay clear away from this game. I am trading in my copy for Batman Arkham City or anything else really.

text:
Bought this to take with me and use with phone, tablet, Surface. It is relatively compact, though the thickness is prodigious. I'm not mad about that.

I have been using it for a few weeks and I am not coming any closer to familiarity with the DELETE and END keys (on FN1). It would have been much better to put end where the dedicated RGB button is, and then use FN1 + BACKSPACE for DELETE.

My second choice - still much better than the way it is - would be to use FN1 with the arrow keys to get PAGE UP, PAGE DOWN, HOME, END, since the analogy is easy to sublimate. I had a laptop with that arrangement years ago and I got used to it.

There is no app to program keys (like G-Hub for my Logitech products). Maybe I will look into third party remapping apps, but it's not the same. I already use AutoHotkey, so maybe I should just add something to my home script.

As it is this keyboard is no fun to write on. The keyboard is continually taking me out of my flow to look down and poke at essential keys.

The mode switch would be better IMHO with OFF and WIRED reversed. Again, it's a matter of attention. If you are using this wirelessly, you have to focus your attention and check that you have turned the power button to the center OFF position. When used in wired mode, you generally leave the keyboard plugged in and switched to WIRED, so it would make more sense to put WIRED in the fiddly, difficult switch position. Better yet, it could have another, dedicated switch for simple on/off.

This keyboard has good action, feel, and sound. It is nice to type on - until it isn't. I would say that if you don't use the DELETE or END keys, you can be happy with this.

It's probably the best use of my time to cut my losses now and switch to the K3, which has a slightly bigger footprint, in exchange for dedicated DELETE and END keys plus F1-F12. Or maybe I should look for something that it properly programmable.

I am frustrated and disappointed with this keyboard.

BTW I have ordered a K8 for my desktop computer (plus a Cherry numpad). I have been using this K6 on my desktop since my regular keyboard started having trouble. Keychron seems to make a decent keyboard for a good price, and a big draw for me is that the look is pretty much exactly what I would choose if I built it from scratch, anyway. I love the grey.

title: The ONE to rule them all? *NO SPOILERS*
text:
FIRST IMPRESSION

I didnt like the intro music. It sounds pompous and deviated from the atmosphere created by prior Souls series starting from Demon's souls (Didnt like the remake intro either. But Im OK with it now). However, actually getting into the character creation and into the game, that initial impression completely vanished. There isnt much music in Souls games in general, other than in Boss fights. But what little it had, was perfectly suited to the world. Elden rings, other than the intro, is no exception. There is music almost all the time. The compositions are perfectly suited for the world and really paints a wonderful picture. Beautiful with bleak and dark undertones. The musicians did a heck of a job

35 HOURS IN:

Character creation- Alot of interesting possibilities including cosmetics, which wasnt much of a focal point.

Graphics- Top notch. Beautiful artwork. The only issue is inconsistent 60FPS even in performance mode. Performance mode highly recommended still.

Gameplay- Dedicated Jumping on foot and horseback adds a vertical dimension to Souls games which makes it more interesting to play by giving more strategic options to tackle bosses and areas.

Overworld- interesting and actually fun and not just mindless wandering unlike other games. Game gives you subtle directional clues to major areas of the game but still get to decide where you want to go. I didnt realize this until 30 hours in as I wanted this to be a completely blind run and not reading any youtube videos- which ruin the experience.

Dungeon/Castle combat- side areas are easy and straightfoward understandably but the major areas have the same souls like intricacy and detail. Enemy/Boss AI is top notch and fun. Not overly difficult. Easy to get around. Convenient stations to respawn and transfer to.

Story- same as prior series. A bit sparse by todays "standard", but less so than prior Souls games. Still need to piece things together and use your imagination. Games/Movies today are just so verbose that it leaves little to the imagination.

Difficulty- Easier than prior souls games. It seems that they have many more respawn/transfer stations, which makes backtracking and progressing easier. Also, they give you a much bigger stamina pool to start off. You dont have to raise this stat unless you want a tankish build. This makes the game alot easier. In other Souls games you dont have to raise it either if you played the glass cannon builds, but the stamina pools were smaller and so you had to be more selective and strategic. There are also more clues as to where to go. The map is well done and interactive allowing you to pin areas of interest. Also they give you summoning options in certain areas, which makes it easy for you to do damage while the npcs tank for you. Works on most bosses. Not all. You still have the option of summoning other players.

Suggestion- Take it slow, soak it all in. Enjoy this wonderful creation. Avoid grinding/power leveling and collecting every little thing while playing. Avoid watching Youtube videos and reviews unless you are stuck at a boss for days on end. Its fun figuring out how to beat bosses. Its part of the fun. On difficult bosses, I usually spend one night dying over and over again, thinking through strats and then the next day I beat it rather quickly. Which makes me wonder why I couldnt do it before. I find this a rewarding experience. Usually im underpowered so my strats have to be perfect. But obviously there are ways around this.

But is it the best of the Souls Series? Its the most well rounded of all of them. Major Quality of life improvements makes the game more accessible and easier to get into and get back into and replay. But each Souls game absolutely stands on its own- Demons Souls, Bloodborne, Dark Souls.
