title: Spoiler-FREE Review
text:
Rating:

Graphics/Art 5/5
Gameplay a 4/5
Modernized Music 5/5
Translation 5/5
Added Scenes 4/5
Voice Acting (English) 3/5
Voice Acting (Japan) 5/5

4 stars doesnt seem that great, but its a nice remake. Not on the level of a Demon's soul remake, but still nice. Whats important is that they kept to the spirit of the original.

My favorite part of the game is how wonderfully they redid the music. For me, retrogaming is a good part about the music. I didnt think Id like it because I enjoyed the original so much. It was quite tastefully done. I think everyone will enjoy it. The only bad part is the option to play original compositions. It didnt come out so well. They must have paid very little attention to the transfer. The original compositions come off somewhat harsh. They shouldve borrowed my original SNES, which is modded for digital audio output with upgraded caps, audio quality internal wiring and power supply.

Main quibble with the game is the voice acting. Budget must have run thin considering they may have had trouble gauging what kind of reception the game would garner. Id opt for the japanese voiceover, although the English voiceover for Popoi is fantastic.

I really like that they added character development scenes, but the drawback is I ended up liking certain characters less- probably due to poor voice acting.

The other nitpicks are some of the animations which are needlessly long and drawn out- i.e., when talking to an NPC. Otherwise the art work is very nice.

The other notable thing is the difficulty. It has been modernized so that you can beat it without any effort or grinding. Kind of sad really. I dont like the grinding, which is fine. But the difficulty is skewed too much to the easy side for the bosses.

Overall, I think the gameplay experience is much better on the SNES even though this version is very much worth experiencing for the music, upgraded artwork and additional scenes.

title: Beautiful BUT some GLARING imperfections
text:
4.5 out of 5.

This remake, overall, is excellent. However, what plagues this game is what seems to plague a lot of the modern games which is that while it is technically superior to its predecessor, it doesn’t quite live up to the same level of emotional experience that you would get by playing the original. I am not saying this just to be an originalist or a video game snob. Here are the reasons:

1) The musical arrangements are elevator musicesque in some ways. Compare opening sequence. It doesnt have the sense of doom and dread that you have with the original. The opening cutscene art direction suffers from this as well, albeit still stunning.

2) visuals are fantastic and so detailed and is a wonder to see BUT it also detracts in a way bc it takes away from this dream state like nightmarish experience. Don’t get me wrong I love the new visuals but I became more of an observer than one who was actually experiencing. The PC emulation version was great for that reason, retaining the dream state like experience but with updated technicals with 60 FPS performance. That was really what PS3 version lacked. It would have been great if they could have included a technically updated ps3 version as well on the ps5 or even be able to play original ps3 discs with improved performance like xbox series x is doing with all their legacy titles. As an aside this is why I am a huge fan of the new xbox again.

3) for all its beautiful graphics and performance, what happened to the wonderful cut scene artwork that was in the PS3? They added depth and substance to the game. It wasn’t just an afterthought. While I grant you that the load times are so fast that it would have been hard to have the time to appreciate it. Why not at least include a section for it as a homage.

Anyways still an absolute must play.

title: PROS and CONS- Updated
text:
Im usually very critical when it comes to products. But when they work and they are good, I give them their due. I rather NOT spend 100 bucks on this thing. But it works and it works well. It upgrades your consoles whether your console directly outputs via HDMI or has to go through upscaler like an OSSC. It improves the visuals output from every single console from retro to ps4. The colors generally are richer and images are cleaner with more depth.

For example, I have a RGB modded Genesis Model 1 Non TMSS with every improvement you can think of to soup it up to get the best visuals possible. The problem is the tech is old and so you are prone to some blurriness when random motion occurs. If you are used to slow paced games, then you wont get the max benefit from it, but you still will because of how much it cleans up the signal making it look nearly HD. Most reviewers show static pictures or pre-recorded intros rather than actually playing on the thing to show how effective it is.

Fast paced, quick random motions- this is where its improvement is noticeable. It produces a smooth experience. It wont add more pixels or any of that. But it will clean up the image and get rid of that haze that your console is producing. This will make the image look richer, NOT brighter. It will also actually seem to reduce the lag in your gameplay because of the clarity and smoothness of the relayed video. You will respond much quicker because of this. If you like shooters like I do, it is helpful here. Also, the 4:3 mode is very nice. When using OSSC on some modes it stretches the image mode too much and this helps bring the image back into a more proper ratio. YMMV

On a PS3/PS4 you should get a similar improvement, but in a subtle way, believe it or not. If you have a discerning eye, it will be readily apparent. Games like Nier, which has an obscene amount of blurriness, will greatly improve. Colors look richer and visuals will have more depth. PS3 and PS4 are especially prone to blurriness because of the heavy demand on the processors. When you pop in the McCLassic, its like playing on your PC without the additional resolution. Just more clarity, richer colors, rock steady visuals. I play alot of Bloodborne, and your reaction time will be better because of the reduced motion blur and increased clarity. If you get one, turn the MCClassic on and play it for a while. If you dont see the difference turn it off after a while by putting it on bypass mode. You will never go back to it off. You can see this clarity clearly in scenes where there is fog rendered. I hadnt noticed the fog as much before, but with the McCLassic, it adds so much more to the experience. Did I mention reduced lag experience? Those times you got hit and you swore you didnt see what hit you? Thatll happen much less often, if at all. When you get hit, you'll know why.

As for whether its worth it? If the above doesnt convince you and dont find as much worth in it and assuming you get marginal improvement, think of it this way. If you own more than 1 console, and you own an HDMI switcher and you plug it in the output, you can effectively upgrade every single console you own. Divide the price by how many consoles you own and thats the real cost for the upgrade.

Cons
You need to reset the Mclassic from time to time. For whatever reason, when you switch consoles and it puts out different resolutions, the image doesnt register. This happens rarely so far. I believe this is when it usually doesnt work temporarily. The only solution is not to go to bypass mode, but to completely unplug the mini/ micro HDMI power cord from the Mclassic and power it down. Plug it back in and you're good to go. Assuming this issue doesnt keep cropping up as well as other potential issues, its a straight up buy recommendation. I will update as I spend more time on it.

Edit: I use OSSC line doubler. X in photos 2x,3x, etc. can only get 2x line doubling with ossc + m because of the unstable output from OSSC. (May be related to the retro console itself rather OSSC.)

UPDATE: Still works fine as it is supposed to. Any issues encountered in switching as noted in this review and comments below can be solved by simply unplugging the power and hard resetting it. Even if its on "off mode." Another item I would like to add since Ive had this since its inception is that some people may prefer the pixelated blocky look. Personally, I like this blocky look, but it only looks good when you have razer sharp output from your console, which usually takes modding, decent monitor and, what people dont mention, power quality. If you have poor power quality, it will affect your visuals. However, solving power/electricity quality issues costs more than this upscaler. Having a good power/electricity source, I prefer to NOT use the Mclassic just because I love the blocky, crisp, detailed look. Improving the quality of your power/electricity source will make everything look and sound exponentially better WITHOUT altering the original content. title: SKIP this game- NOT necessary to play Nier Automata.
text:
This game couldve been so good, but it turned out to be somewhat of a poor game. First the good. Combat mechanics are fun, not great like dark souls, but its fun. The magic spells are fun to use and execute throughtout the game. The ability to change out spells in mid combat makes it not a complete real-time combat, but thats fine. Its a nice compromise considering you are limited to using a joystick. The graphics are good for its time, if not a little gray. But it becomes really good and the colors and motion become much richer and fluid with an upscaler.

The bad: Dialogue, I appreciate that they are trying to wax poetical but its too verbose. I understand that they had alot to say, and alot of ideas, but they werent organized very well. Its also not elegantly written either. Its just all over the place. That being said, it does have to be translated so its probably better in Japanese. If you take a look at games like Demon's souls, Dark souls, Bloodborne, you dont have to write volumes to get the point across that life is harsh, brutal and cold, but with some beauty sprinkled into what we call life that sometimes makes it all seem worthwhile. Souls series does it through focusing intensely on creating a visual atmosphere and sparse dialogue that hints at what is. But what this series does is try to expound verbally, what can hardly be expressed through words. Even the epilogue is completely verbal. Could they not just throw in some animations to carry the message and make it worth watching?

That brings me to the next huge negative- Kaine. She could arguably be the most annoying supporting character Ive run across. Even her walking around half naked couldn't make up for it. She could even beat the handler in Monster Hunter World. The only saving grace is that you don't hear Kaine all the time unlike the handler. And at least in the PC version of monster hunter world you can mute her and even change her face. Thank goodness for that. In any case, I understand what they were trying to do, make a volatile, seemingly complex character, likeable by helping the player empathize with her background through small but meaningful moments throughout the game. But no, it just fails to work. Perhaps the Japanese version works, but this utterly fails imo.

The last negative- Music. Sound quality is fine. but the music is so repetitive. If they were going to recycle the same music over and over again, could they not use low impact, no vocal instrumentals? Or just use it once in a while to create a nice, lasting impact? Its fine to hear the full track a few times, but over and over again, it just becomes hard to bear. This is really a huge negative as music is a huge part of any game. They need to master things like this, which I will say, in the newest Nier Automata game, they seem to have done. So bravo for that.

All in all, this game is not necessary to play Nier Automata, a complete standaline, which so far plays like a masterpiece of a game in all areas. You can avoid this game and really not miss a thing.

title: State of the games today.
text:
This game is a prime example of what is wrong with today's game industry - it's absolutely confused. Its a perfect representation of what is going on today in more ways than one. It tries to appeal to everyone and in the end, the result is horrendous. Its a game with little imagination, it trivializes everything, the tone is completely off, the dialogue will set you back a few dozen IQ points. The game just doesn't take itself seriously, and frankly you shouldn't either. I received this game for free after upgrading my video card. Im usually a completionist but I could not bear to finish it after the first chapter.

Go play games like halo, dead space and bio shock (not the sequels) and you will understand. If you haven't played it in a while, Id suggest you try again. Great serious, story telling with fun game mechanics. Ive replayed them recently and it reminded me how terrible much of the games are today.

The pros- Wolfenstein's graphics are nice. I ran it in ultra-wide multi-monitor setup without a hitch. But on a 2080ti, I expect it to do so. Game mechanics ran fine. About the only positives I can think of. So it gets 2 stars for the visuals and that it ran smoothly.

I cant believe this is my first amazon review and its about this game. Its honestly not worth my time, but I didnt want anyone else to waste theirs. Maybe itll snowball, into a revolt against game makers of this ilk-just wishful thinking. But if it helps one person thats good enough for me. In any case, Id suggest moving on and looking for something else.

title: Bluetooth Connection is Not Reliable and Headphones Keep Shutting Down
text:
I got these headphones for my husband, who games occasionally and who was also looking for a set that would double as a high-fidelity, comfortable wireless set of headphones that also did Bluetooth for use when he is teleworking. He freely admits that he finds the headphones very comfortable, and the sound excellent. A lot of his calls are long distance; some even come from out of the country, and the sound is not always sterling. He was also pleased with the fact that the boom mike works flawlessly and his callers could hear him clearly and there was little request for him to repeat himself.

However, the Bluetooth has been a total disappointment. On the first day it took some time for the headphones to initially connect to his cell phone (a Google Pixel). He is usually taking calls one after the other, but after each call he must write a report where he is not actually using the Bluetooth, and also, at this time of year, people do not call as much because they are away for the holidays. So, as he waited for his calls to come in or as he wrote his reports up, the headphones would regularly shut themselves off after a pre-determined period of time. This seems like an energy-saving feature that I'm sure is helpful when you are gaming so you don't waste your battery charge, but if you have to be immediately available for a telephone call, it is definitely detrimental. He would slip the headphones off and turn them back on each time it happened, but this gets annoying having to do it over and over every 20 minutes or every half hour or whatever the time period was (he didn't time it). [I timed it after connecting the headphones to my Acer laptop. If you don't use the headphones after 20 minutes, they power down.] However, the moment he did turn the headphones back on, the Bluetooth immediately reconnected. So he did use them for the remainder of the day.

However, the next day he had the same difficulty connecting with the Bluetooth initially, and when the headphones shut themselves off automatically and he reconnected, the Bluetooth did not automatically reconnect. This happened several times, which was the final straw and he went back to using his old headphones.

I wondered if this problem stemmed from not having loaded the Turtle Beach app. Perhaps there was some way to turn off the energy-saving feature. That would solve all his problems. However, I did not find that option on the app after loading it on his phone.

In short, the sound is excellent as is the delivery from the boom mike. But the Bluetooth is not reliable, so we cannot give these headphones a good rating.

(If someone knows how to keep the headphones from shutting off while being used for Bluetooth only, please let us know! He was pleased otherwise with the headphones and would love to give them a higher rating.)

title: Good beginner wheel but expected more for the price point.
text:
[[VIDEOID:499ac84584cf56f9db85b46180571b61]] This is my first experience with Thrustmaster and a wheel in general. My expectations based on price and the Thrustmaster name were not completely met with the T128P for PS4/5 and PC. It’s a great $100 wheel but slightly above average $200 wheel. Primary user of the wheel is my 12 year old son but for testing purposes I have been driving race cars like I stole them, lol.

Arrival: The wheel arrived nicely package all component were in working order with no issues. However, I immediately notice some of the creature comforts I expected were missing based on price of the wheel such as cushion wheel or higher quality buttons with smooth action.

Instructions: Th instruction for setup were clear except for the computer driver download portion. A little more emphasis and larger font would be nice. Took me a second to locate them due to size of font.

Wheel: The wheel itself is made of hard plastics, buttons appear of low quality and make a loud audible click when pushed, especially the paddles shifters. They lack the quality you see with PS5 and the Xbox elite 2 controllers. The clamp worked fine but make sure you have room underneath your desk to attach, see pictures.

Pedals: I have similar thoughts when it comes to the pedals. The pedals assembly is very light and lack common sense in the design. It doesn’t take and engineer to understand center of gravity and how a lever works. To explain the pedals will slide forward when in use and have a tendency to want to pitch forward off the floor due the center of gravity begin shifted so far forward and the lack of weight to counter this affect. The design seemed to completely overlook that someone had to actually use this in game under various conditions. I guess that is why a pedal stand is sold by Thrustmaster as an accessory for ~$90. Just my thoughts but human in the loop and ergonomics should be considered in the design process hint…hint. You have to hold the pedals in place with your off foot, use a weight or hey buy their pedal stand.

Hooking up: Once everything was hooked up it was first tested on the PS5 with no issues. Worked well with GT7. For the computer…driver download was easy. Thrustmaster done have control panel for making adjustments to the settings. We first tried with Forza 4 and had issues. The game would not recognize the wheel. However, after some internet research we found this is a common issue across many brands of wheels and Forza 4. I found no immediate work around so we tried using the wheel with Forza 5. The wheel was recognized as a T248 and Forza auto-configured the wheel. The wheel worked as intended with all features being functional. My son did adjust the button layout to his liking. When also tried the wheel with the Crew 2 demo and it worked but not as well. Not all function worked on the wheel, mainly the center shift lights were not operable. This could be due to the game being only a demo though.

So to wrap this up the wheel is a good beginner wheel but without the creature comforts I expected for the price point. The design lacks in key areas of functionality and quality, especially regarding the pedals and use of quality components such as buttons. The dynamic functionality of the wheel lacks the feel I expected and in my opinion is cheap considering the price.

Note: the cord routing and layout could have been incorporated better considering it is a clamp on type mount. The cords are easily pinch during mounting and do not stay in the routing channels.

My review is solely based on my experience with this wheel and isn’t biased as I have never owned another.

title: It's more than you'd think for the price
text:
Considering the favored astrology software cost as much as my new laptop, WinStar was a relief to find. I thought I'd just be able to cast a natal chart, maybe do transits and synastry charts. Even though one can cast charts at astro.com for free there's times when there is no WiFi where I'm giving an astrology reading. I needed software installed on my new HP Laptop. Budgets being what they are for me I "settled" on WinStar.

I didn't expect what I found, a little treasure of an astrology program, and believe me I've been using astrology software since back in the day when I had to Boss my DOS, ok?

What I found that surprised me:

A second disc with tutorials for the beginner, and it's good to have as a reference even if you're not a beginner.

Atlas: An atlas that I've not been able to stump yet.

Reports: Natal, Transit, Synastry and Progressed reports that you can generate and save as pdf or text files, that you can email as an attachment to yourself or your client. BIG PLUS!

Wheels galore: An assortment of wheel types, single, double, different house systems. You can also email those.

To email wheel charts or reports hit "print" and it goes to a pdf format, from there you can save, print, or email. When I'm out and about doing astrology readings in a cafe with WiFi I can email the wheel and report to my client as something to refer to when they get home. I also email myself the same material for the client's folder on my home desk top. If I am not where there's WiFi I can burn the report to a DVD disc with my laptop and hand the disc to the client right there, on the beach, in the forest, under ground in a bunker.

When doing a double wheel the transit option comes up automatically. Nifty! If you want to select another chart for synasty you can do that but I like that the transit option comes up first.

Transit "Time Line": It's transits done for 3 days, 1 week, 1 month, 1 year, as a multi-colored ribbon, the dates run along this "time line". It shows when planets go into a new sign, or transit a new house for the client. It shows the transiting planets aspecting the natal planets in one color, progressed planets are shown in another color, solar arch are shown in another color. If you ever had a client ask just how long transiting Saturn is going to be opposed their natal Moon you can easily see it on this time line. One draw back is you can't do a time line for the current day, like if you just wanted to do general forecasts. The work around is to cast the birth data for yesterday, do the time line for a week or a month and you can have the information you need.

I know I have not exhausted the possibilities of this software. Don't let the price fool you. It's not light weight. It has helped me a great deal when doing readings away from home in my laptop and away from WiFi if that's the environment I find myself. I'm very pleased.

title: The Smaller Size Is Nice But It Does Present Some Issues
text:
As an old, retired guy I spend a lot of time online gaming every day. My favorite MMO is complex enough that I use three computers while gaming. The main one is for the game itself. A second one is for Discord so I can easily track who is talking and/or any text messages sent on that app. The third window is for the game's wiki and various other information sites that I often need to reference on the fly. As you can imagine, three computers on a desktop makes for some clutter. So the smaller size of this keyboard is very nice. That smaller size does come with some issues though that gamers particularly need to be aware of.

For one thing, there is no number pad and the function keys have been combined with the number keys. For me as a gamer, those kinds of changes have several ramifications. Most keyboards are standardized enough that switching to a new one is no big deal. In this case though, with significant changes to the keyboard arrangement, this one requires a learning curve to train the muscle memory to the new arrangement. My favorite game also uses a lot of keybinds. So, removing the number pad while combining the number and function keys, removes a noticeable amount of possible keybinds. The final issue I've had with this keyboard is that it's smaller size and novel arrangement means that I am hitting the wrong keys a significant number of times. That is not a good thing when the combat in your game is hot and heavy.

There is one other thing of note about this product. The white keyboard and it's light show looks like it was designed for a pre-teen who is into rainbows and pink unicorns. I don't have any strong reaction either way to that design aesthetic myself. Other folks may love it or hate it though so just be aware of that in case such things matter to you.

The de-cluttering usefulness of the smaller size is useful enough for me to give this keyboard a 4 star rating. I'll just put it on the machine I use the least and certainly won't use it on my gaming machine. That way I get the big advantage without worrying about it's disadvantages.

The MMO I play the most has separate volume controls for music, environmental sounds, dialogue, and special effects while movies, music, etc, generally have a single volume control. I don't begin to understand the technical issues involved but that may have something to do with why these headphones can take the different sound files in a game and weave them into a very real sounding, three-dimensional sound field while being unable to do so for other types of audio files. Where this becomes an issue for me, and where your mileage may vary, is in what I use headphones for.

There's two times I plug in headphones - when I'm gaming with fellow players via Discord or when I'm listening to something loud at night and I don't want to disturb my upstairs neighbor. Other than that, I don't use headphones to listen to the sounds of my video game. Instead, I'll be listening to music or audiobooks on some decent computer speakers while gaming solo. Their sound for such things is as good as these headphones. The advantage of speakers is they don't start getting uncomfortable after extended use, like headsets do for me.

Which brings us to another issue I had with this headset. The product page touts their comfortableness. When I first put them on, they did feel more comfortable than other headsets I've used. After two hours of running ingame raids with some guildies though, the headphones were becoming uncomfortable. I was glad when we finished our group raid so I could sign off of Discord and take off the headphones.

If you game with them on all the time and are comfortable wearing a headset for an extended period, you will love this product and it will likely be 5-star headset for you. If not though, this item will likely drop to 4-stars for you, excellent in one area but average in most others.

title: Pretty To Look At, Not Much Practical Use, But Ants Seem To Like It
text:
As a casual gamer I can't tell if this keyboard is serious overkill for me, is just filled with unnecessary frills, or is some combination of both. In any event, it has no noticeable impact on my gaming.

Let me give a bit of context. As an old, retired guy in the midst of a pandemic, I actually have a lot of time for gaming and easily spend 6+ hours a day in my favorite MMO. I call myself a casual gamer because I am too old and slow to be a hardcore, competitive player. So I don't play to beat others but to simply have a good time. My favorite MMO is Guild Wars 2, which has a variety of game modes, from relaxed casual to hardcore competitive. One of those game modes, World vs World is a series of open maps where players can roam as individuals, in small groups, or in massive zergs fighting other players to capture keeps, towers, supply camps, shrines, and the like. It's a nice mix of casual and competitive and even an old, slow guy like me can run wild there and the ingame rewards available make it worthwhile to do so. The action is fast-paced, fluid, and always changing and I usually spend a couple of hours a day or so in WvW.

That's the context in which I tried this keyboard and it worked no better than the basic $15 keyboard I had unplugged to try this one. Guild Wars 2 does not allow the use of macros so that feature did me no good at all. Roccat's macro set up seem clumsy anyway. You need to hit two keys, while looking at the keyboard to get the right ones. Other keyboards I've seen have a much better implementation of macros. My favorite option was one that had a dedicated set of extra buttons just for the macros. One button to hit and once you got the muscle memory down, you wouldn't have to look at the keyboard to hit the right key.

The "swift, precise key stroke" touted in the product copy had no practical effect for me. At times when my group was being swamped by a larger enemy horde, making swift action imperative, this keyboard seemed no faster than the basic keyboard it had replaced. Several times I had to hit a key twice before it responded.

Even something as simple as the audio controls seem clumsily implemented on this keyboard. There's three buttons and a knob. One button is for muting. One says FX and I still haven't figured out what it's for. The third button seems to turn the volume knob on, and the knob then adjusts the volume. The basic keyboard this one replaced had three audio control buttons - mute, volume up, volume down. Much simpler.

This is also not a plug and play product like basic keyboards are. After plugging it in, I had to go to the company website to download the necessary software. Once that was installed, I had to download/install an update. Once that first update was installed, I immediately had to download/install a second update. Not only was it a lengthy process, but the keyboard locked itself down during the download/install process, meaning I couldn't do other things on the computer while all that was being done.

Once all the software and updates were finally installed, I learned how unnecessarily irritating it was to use the software. The only instructions included with the keyboard were to go to the company website to download the needed software. On the website itself, there were no directions for actually using the software. So for me, it was a clumsy, hunt and peck process, trying different buttons to figure out how to do such basic things as set the color scheme, select the sound played when hitting a key, and set the profiles to change those settings depending on what I was doing. The company website was very pretty to look at but some simple step by step instructions for using their products would have been much more useful.

That description of the company website, "pretty to look at but of no practical use" is pretty much the way I would describe this keyboard. Yes, the lights are pretty. Yes, it's fun to choose the sound that plays when you hit a key but none of that does a thing to improve my gaming. The local ants really do seem to like this keyboard though. This morning when I sat down at my desk, they were swarming all over it, running around through its maze of colored lights. I have no idea what that was about but they seemed to be having fun.

title: Excellent Headphones
text:
The sound is very good. The headset is perhaps the most lightweight and comfortable I've used so far. It's also completely plug and play. You plug the headphones in and you are good to go, no drivers or other software needed. Some headphones show up as unique items under the audio settings. So when you want to use them, you need to go to your settings to manually select them after you plug them in. Not these. Just unplug your speakers, plug in the headset and go from there.

A lot of manufacturers seem to think all gamers are middle school kids who need and want flashing lights on everything. The last set of "gaming" headphones I tried put ridiculous colored lights on the headphones. I say ridiculous because you can't see those lights when you are actually wearing the headset. So I appreciate the fact that this headset eschewed such nonsense, focusing instead on audio quality and the comfortableness of the headset.

There are two cautions I need to add. Though neither was a big deal to me, you should be aware of them. The first is that the cord on this headset is shorter than other headsets I've used. My set up is a main computer that I actually game on with a second computer to the side that I run Discord on. That way I don't have to flip in and out of the game to deal with Discord issues. The cord on this headset is fine for use with my main computer but is too short to reach the secondary machine. Depending on your set up, the length of the cord may or may not be an issue to you.

For me that also means I haven't tried the microphone on this headset, just the headphones. Given the quality of this product I wouldn't expect there to be an issue with the mic, but you might check the other reviews here to see what they say about that. Thanks for reading this and I hope you enjoy this product.

title: Adequate Bur Not Particularly Awesome
text:
As a cranky old guy who spends a lot of his retirement time gaming in MMOs, I had some mixed reactions to to these headphones. On the plus side, they really are plug and play. No special software is needed, no tricky set up issues, just plug them in and they are good to go. MMO means massive multi-player online and it generally indicates the kind of game where you cooperate with some players while combating others. In a situation like that, headphones with a mic are essential to fast coordination. Gamers I know generally use Discord or Teamspeak to verbally communicate with each other. Once again, the set up was basically plug and play. With the headphones connected to my computer, I had no problem using them with either of those programs.

There were a few things that kept me from giving these headphones 5 stars. For one thing, the sound is okay but is nothing special to write home about. That's fine for gaming but if want to listen to music or watch movies, you'll probably want to switch back to your regular speakers. Which touches on another thing, this one positive. Some headphones and mics show up as unique items in my audio settings. So when I want to use them I have to plug them in and go into my settings to select them. This headphone and mic just show up as generic default input/output devices in my settings. So I can just plug them in without having to also adjust my settings.

Another negative is how flimsy the headphones feel. It took some effort to pull the earphones out enough to fit them properly on my head. It felt like I might break the thing if I pulled too hard so it took a bit to get the earphones extended as far as I need them. Moreover, the padding under the headpiece is similar to other headsets I've tried, only to have that padding rip and fall apart after only a few months of use. One other positive should be mentioned. There's an on/off switch for the mic on the headphone's cord. That's very handy as a mic that's always open can lead to echoes and squealing feedback that the other folks playing with you will not appreciate.

Oh, and there is one neutral thing to close with. Like most "gamer equipment" these headphones come equipped with pretty lights. That always seems like a silly marketing ploy to me, one aimed at 11 year old gamers. Those pretty lights are even more ridiculous than usual on a pair of headphones. The headphones are on your head, you can't even see those pretty lights like you can with a keyboard, mouse, or other "gamer gear".

So all in all, this headset/mic seems like it will do the basic audio job I need it for, talking with other gamers in the midst of fiercely fought battles. There's just nothing outstanding enough about it to boost its rating up from 4 stars to 5.

title: An Abrupt Crash From 5 Stars To 3 Stars And Possibly Lower
text:
EDIT: I'm leaving my original review below to show you why I initially loved this keyboard and gave it a glowing 5 star review. Sadly, just a few days after posting that review things took a sudden turn for the worse. For unknown reasons the G Hub software controlling this keyboard crashed and burned completely. Not only is it no longer working beyond the basics but the crash also pushed the keyboard into default mode. That means the extra macro keys that were so helpful in my game reverted to being standard F1-F5 function keys. My game already uses those function keys for essential combat moves so now, after deliberately training my muscle memory to use the macro keys, those keys do entirely different things.. Even a casual gamer like me knows how that destroys one's game play.

A google search showed that this G Hub crash is a common enough occurrence that there are YouTube videos and reddit articles on how to try and deal with it. I followed some of the basic suggestions - rebooting the computer, reinstalling the software, unplugging the keyboard and plugging it back in again, all to no avail. The G Hub loading screen just spins endlessly and I have no way of altering the default settings of this keyboard. The next step is to trying dealing with Logitech support, which does not have a good reputation online. At 70 years old, I'm too tired to deal with much hassle so I don't know when I'll have the energy to take that on. If they can't, or won't, help me, the rating on this review will go even lower. If they can show me how to fix the problem, the rating will stay at 3 stars or possibly go back up to 4 stars depending on how much difficulty is involved. In any event, the first bloom of 5 star love is definitely over.
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
First, let's give this review some context. As a retired guy I'm too old and slow to be a hard core gamer. I have five grandsons in high school and junior high who are hard core and their game play is in a whole different universe than mine. This review is not for them. I'm a relaxed, casual player and that's who this is written for. With that in mind, let's move on to this keyboard, starting with the fun stuff.

Fun - The Bright and Shiny Lights
A lot of gear branded for gamers seems to feature brightly colored lights and this keyboard revels in them. Before it arrived I wondered why it bothered to even have lights. When I first took the keyboard out of the box and plugged it in, the lights were so bright and were flashing so quickly that I was like "Whoa, how the heck can I even use this thing?? Those lights are just way too distracting and confusing!!!" Silly me. When I downloaded the control software I quickly discovered that I could tune the keyboard to my own liking, using other people's lighting designs or easily create my own. With a vast array of colors to choose from as well as a variety of shifting patterns and lighting sequences, I happily set about creating a lighted keyboard I really, really liked. Heck, you can set each key to have it's own color sequence if you want and you control how much the whole thing flashes and how often it all changes color. As far as I can tell, the colored lights have no impact on my game play but it's like having your own Christmas light show all year round and I love it! Why would anyone want one of those old, unlighted keyboards?

Fun - Clicky, Clicky, Clicky and Other Sound Stuff
When you order one of these keyboards you have have a choice of three different keyboard sounds. I got the Clicky version which sounds and feels a bit like an old school typewriter. The sound is unobtrusive but nice. I couldn't tell you why but that clicking in the background as you type feels comfortable to me. It's letting you know that you are actually doing something when you hit the keys. Again, why would anyone want one of those old, noiseless keyboards? They are so boring. 🙂

Another sound thing is the volume control on the keyboard. I don't particularly need it with my current set up as I have a small speaker, with volume control sitting right next to my keyboard. Still, my previous computer was an all-in-one who's volume control was awkward to use. So the keyboard mounted volume control would have been handy then.

The Serious Game Stuff - Macros and More Macros
Here's where we get down to the serious stuff. For those who don't know, macros are small scripts for doing a series of actions by pressing one key instead of having to press one for each action. For example, say you are playing a cowboy shooter and you ride into an ambush. You need to dismount, draw a rifle or pistol, aim, shoot, and reload when necessary. Normally each of those actions would require a separate key stroke. With a macro though, you could set it up to do all that with one key instead. As you can imagine, macros can be powerful, powerful tools in the game world. They are so powerful that the main game I play forbids using macros for more than one action at a time. Even with that limitation, the macro capability of this keyboard is still very useful.

There are five new keys on the left side of this keyboard that can be assigned to any use you'd like. Currently I have them set up to quickly mount and dismount from the various critters I can ride. That in and of itself is nice. However, you can also set up different macros on those keys which can be swapped in and out at the push of a button. There are a variety of professions and skills I can use ingame so if I wanted to, I could set up different macros to use with different characters in addition to the mounting/dismounting. I haven't done that yet but I fully intend to.

Just as nice is that the control software makes macro creation easy peasy. The control interface is minimalist in design and you have to poke around a bit to figure out how to use it but the learning curve is not onerous and once you have figured it out. using the software makes macro creation incredibly easy.

In case you can't tell, even as a casual gamer I love this keyboard. Hard core gamers will probably appreciate it even more than I do.

clicky, clicky, clicky and other sound stuff when you order one of these keyboards you have have a choice of three different keyboard sounds. i got the clicky version which sounds and feels a bit like an old school typewriter. the sound is unobtrusive but nice. i could not tell you why but that clicking in the background as you type feels comfortable to me. it's letting you know that you are actually doing something when you hit the keys. again, why would anyone want one of those old, noiseless keyboards? they are so boring. 🙂 another sound thing is the volume control on the keyboard. i do not particularly need it with my current set up as i have a small speaker, with volume control sitting right next to my keyboard. still, my previous computer was an all-in-one who's volume control was awkward to use. so the keyboard mounted volume control would have been handy then. the serious game stuff - macros and more macros here's where we get down to the serious stuff. for those who do not know, macros are small scripts for doing a series of actions by pressing one key instead of having to press one for each action. for example, say you are playing a cowboy shooter and you ride into an ambush. you need to dismount, draw a rifle or pistol, aim, shoot, and reload when necessary. normally each of those actions would require a separate key stroke. with a macro though, you could set it up to do all that with one key instead. as you can imagine, macros can be powerful, powerful tools in the game world. they are so powerful that the main game i play forbids using macros for more than one action at a time. even with that limitation, the macro capability of this keyboard is still very useful. there are five new keys on the left side of this keyboard that can be assigned to any use you'd like. currently i have them set up to quickly mount and dismount from the various critters i can ride. that in and of itself is nice. however, you can also set up different macros on those keys which can be swapped in and out at the push of a button. there are a variety of professions and skills i can use ingame so if i wanted to, i could set up different macros to use with different characters in addition to the mounting/dismounting. i have not done that yet but i fully intend to. just as nice is that the control software makes macro creation easy peasy. the control interface is minimalist in design and you have to poke around a bit to figure out how to use it but the learning curve is not onerous and once you have figured it out. using the software makes macro creation incredibly easy. in case you ca not tell, even as a casual gamer i love this keyboard. hard core gamers will probably appreciate it even more than i do.

title: A Good Headset With An Irritating Learning Curve
text:
THE BOTTOM LINE - Getting the headphones and mic to work properly took some irritating effort for a newbie but was worth it for how it immediately enhanced my online gaming.

The headphones themselves are nice. The sound is excellent and the headset is the most comfortable for extended wear I've found yet. Wireless Bluetooth speakers often stutter while streaming audio but these non-Bluetooth headphones worked flawlessly. The controls are positioned a bit awkwardly, on the lower back end of the right side ear cup. I've hit the wrong controls several times while trying to do something as simple as adjusting the volume.

The set up was extremely irritating for me. The minimal directions are on one very large sheet with 95% of the content being the same few sentences in a myriad of different languages. I don't mind multi-lingual instructions, it was just the layout on this particular broadsheet that was frustrating. I had to keep flipping from one side of the sheet to the other trying to figure out what to do. Then it took me 20 minutes to get the headset to actually work simply because I had pushed the USB cords in as far as they seemed to go but they needed to be pushed in even further.A google search showed that folks have had similar problems with other Astro gear. Someone used to these kinds of headsets will probably have a much easier time but for a first timer like me, this was a very irritating exercise indeed. It turns out that the Astro website has a set up video that is dramatically easier to understand than the included instructions so keep that in mind.

Then, after I finally got the headphones plugged in and working, it turns out I can't get the mic to work. A google search did not help here as people have had problems with a variety of Astro gear but I couldn't find anything pertaining to mic issues with this particular headset. About 45 minutes ago I put in a support request on the Astro website. So I also get to test how good their support it. Once I've dealt with them and hopefully gotten the mic working, I'll update this review and adjust the rating accordingly.

EDIT: Upgraded the rating from 3 stars to 5 stars. Customer service got back to me within a day as promised. They gave me a check list of things to try (included below). Testing the headphones on a different computer was the one that worked for me. They worked flawlessly on a different machine so the mic problem had something to do with my first computer, not with the headphones themselves. The reason for moving the ratings upwards to 5 stars is that setting up and using the mic was pretty straightforward and using the mic opened up new game realms for me. Just now I used headphones and mic for the first time ever in an online game, running some missions with my guildmates. Being able to talk to my guildies was a whole new level of companionable gaming, one I thoroughly enjoyed.

Even with the 5 star rating though, I do have to reiterate a caution I gave earlier in this review. Using this gear will likely be a cakewalk for a techie who knows what they are doing. For a newbie though, getting to the sweet spot with this gear took some frustrating effort. If you are a newbie, I suggest that you start with the appropriate astro a20 set up video on youtube and if you have any problems, try this checklist from Astrogaming support. Good luck.

The suggested trouble-shooting checklist:
- Watch the set up video to check your settings.

- Check to make sure your A20’s Base Station is in PC Mode. The PC/Console Mode switch is located on the back of the Base Station.

- Resync the A20 Headset by plugging the headset into the A20 Base Station as if it were charging.

- Test the alternate USB ports on on your computer. Test your equipment on an alternate computer or console. Use a different voice program (Discord, Skype, Teamspeak, etc.)

- Hard reset your A20 Headset by simultaneously holding down the GAME Button (Located below the volume wheel) and the EQ Mode button located below the power button. Please note: When doing the hard reset, have the headset plugged in directly to a confirmed power source, without the Base Station. Let charge for 15 minutes, then retry.

title: Just what I needed! Better than I hoped! Worth the money!
text:
I have one of the older Kindles and the only complaint that I have had over the years is that while traveling or at night, I can't read without some kind of light. Of course I have purchased various independent lights that either snap-on or attach to my old case, but this also means keeping up with two things (the Kindle and the light). So I finally asked myself "wouldn't it be easier to invest in one product that would offer both protection and light"? So I purchased this case and have not been disappointed! I'm glad I made the investment.

For the cost of the case, you get:

1. A sleek, attractive case that not only looks smart but is extremely functional. This case is made from a leather (a durable material) on the outside, and is well padded (in a charcoal grey material) on the inside. It definitely appears to be well made (sturdy) and seriously protects the device. The device attaches to the case with two prongs that secure it in place. It is pretty easy to attach. The bottom of the case is open, so you can access the area for the charger easily. Thus, charging your Kindle while it is in the case.

2. The case (with the Kindle enclosed) is not heavy. You can comfortably fit in your purse, book bag; backpack or briefcase, and it won't weigh your bag down.

3. There is a built in expanding (rubberband) type cord that is attached to the case that will allow you to either keep the case open or closed (as desired).

4. The light conveniently rises out of the top right corner of the case. I will warn you that there were times when it seemed difficult to pull out. (Just be mindful that you don't force it, but instead pull the tab up by the indention provided.) However, once it is up, the built-in light does illuminate the screen (more than I ever thought it would) well. The light cuts on and off with the device, so there are no batteries. The light works off the charge of the Kindle, and you control when you use the light. (I also haven't found that the light drains the battery any quicker normal). The light gives just the right amount of illumination, and isn't so bright as that it will bother others sleeping in the same room. My husband always complained that when I would read at night, in bed, that the lamp (on my nightstand) was too bright and kept him from falling asleep. And when I used the traditional clip on book light when traveling in a car, he use to complain that my book light was too distracting. He actually doesn't seem to be distracted or bothered by this gem. Perhaps because it seems to be more defused or softer.

In the end, I don't regret my purchase. I definitely got more than I had hoped and would definitely recommend this case. It is affordable and the benefits outweigh the cost. 5 stars!

title: Very nice headset but some problems with PC
text:
This headset is the best headset I've used to date. I used this exclusively for PC, and I moved to these from the Corsair Void Pro. These are much nicer quality, but it did have downsides.

Sound - best sounding gaming headset that I've ever tried. It sounds super crisp and has plenty of bass.

Mic - the recordings sounds pretty good for a headset, but nothing great.

Fit & Feel - Fit is great, very comfortable. Feel is meh for a $300 headset, feels plasticy and adjusting the arms (which you have to shorten most of the way for it to fit into the charging dock) feels a little janky in the way that it moves slowly, but if i apply more pressure, then I might break the headset.

Other notes: This is for XBox 1 and PC, but it feels like it was made more for the former, and merely is compatible with the latter. It has a volume toggle control on the side (as well as 4 other buttons, switches, and rollers) that is labelled "Game" on one side and "Voice" the other. I somehow triggered one of them that rendered me barely able to hear the audio even with my system maxxed, app volume at max, and even the headset volume roller (that for some reason does not control the system volume) at max. It made me wonder why I have 3 seperate volume controls, and then a 4th toggle that somehow also dramatically affects volume. It is because these were made with a console in mind (and it makes perfect sense for a console), but having that many additional buttons controlling just volume seems ridiculous when you have a mouse that can easily interact with volume sliders and a physical volume roller on my keyboard.

title: Above average gaming headset
text:
The corsair virtuoso is a pretty good headset. I previously used my Void Pro SE, and draw most of my comparisons off that. I broke down my thoughts into few categories.

Fit: The headset feels stiff and a little tight on the sides of my head. I prefer the fit of the void pro. I think I have a pretty medium sized head, and I felt a fair amount of clamping pressure on my ears. This also makes the headset feel lighter because there was less weight resting on the top of my head. I wish this were more adjustable because it's a little too tight.

Sound: (tested in wired & wireless mode, and experienced similar results): Just to clarify, I am no audiophile and have not owned a high quality set of headphone, but the sound seems ordinary. I tried to give this a big sample of uses: thx intro video, streamed music, I still have some .wav files, and gamed a bit. The headset handled all of it, but in much the same way as my void pro.

Mic: This was my favorite part of the headset. My experience with detachable my microphones has been less than stellar. Most of the time they look incredibly flimsy and generic. This mic matches the rest of the asthetics of the headset, and has sounded better and crisper than any mic I've tried. The mic is flexible, but I wish you could change the color of the mic LED. It is solid green when unmuted, and red when muted.

Design, look, feel: very nice corsair style. Perforated side RGB is cool, ear pads are a nice cushy leathery feel. It feels like all the surfaced are metal, padding, or coated plastic to make it nice to touch. With the mic removed they look like a nice set of headphones.

Other thoughts: I had some pains with the setup of these. They did not auto sync with corsair's icue software, and had a lot of crackling when used just with plug n play. I had to manually update the software and plug the headphones into the usb via cable. This fixed the sound issues, but the headset will sometimes not show up next to my other corsair devices in icue. This is frustrating, and I did not have these problems with my Void Pro.

I feel like these are very nice for a normal gaming headset, but it doesn't seem to be worth more than $200.

Hope this has been helpful:)

title: It was great fun until my town turned into a wasteland....
text:
I got this game as a new to videogames player. I loved it.

I thought it was cool that the snow seemed to be 'melting'. Then it snowed for two days straight, but I didn't get any more snow cover. I wondered why. So I found an online animal crossing community and learned the awful truth: playing the game destroys the look of your town! What???

Yep...all that wandering aimlessly lost I did in the beginning, racing around in hide-n-seek games, running to catch a present, and all the saves required by multiplayer gaming combined to turn my town into a virtual desert. I have probably made my last snowman. No snow also = no grass when summer comes as well.

I am very sad. The grass/snow will regrow eventually, but it will take months if not years, and you can't walk on it AT ALL during the process. My other choice is to tear down my town and start over, reminding myself to walk around as little as possible and NEVER run. Not as much fun anymore. Or I can just resign myself to life in the desert. Animal Crosssing: Desert Dwellers. Yippee.

Whatever, a lot of the lightheearted fun of it is gone for me now that I hesitate to walk in spots where there still IS some snow. I don't wander around looking for fossils or shaking trees, and hide-n-seek is out of the question. What is the purpose of planting and watering flowers and trees and pulling weeds if my town is still going to look like a dustbowl town when I'm done?

Boo to Nintendo for not testing this "feature" fully before release and not fixing it when when it became a problem. I would not recommend buying this game until a patch becomes available.

title: I bought 3 mice, including my two old ones, and this one won.
text:
I got the E-3lue Cobra , this and Razer to replace my MS wireless mice at home and work.

All amazing mice. 3lue's thumb buttons are too close to you/palm of your hand and hard to find. But for $11, that was great for work.

Anker and this were very comparable. Both have great feel, quite, both have braided cloth cables, though this has a slightly softer thinner cable.

As far as design & LEDs, and Anker was better. I like it's curve better and of course you can change the LED color to anything, and you can't change Razer's.

The buttons on Anker blew me away. They are ALL comfortably reached and distinguishable with ease (and I'm not good at that). AND they are programmable with a simple downloaded app. That's not to say Razer's buttons aren't great, they really are, but you get the standard 5 buttons. There you can 3 programmable thumb buttons that are fantastic for figuring out which is which by feel, and 4 buttons for your middle finger.

The software on the Anker also won. The Razer mouse software wants to log into their server every time you boot (or always stay connected as another option). As everyone else has said, WHY FORCE US TO CREATE AN ACCOUNT AND STAY CONNECTED??

Anker was going to be the winner in all fronts, including price for me, but alas I don't use a mouse-pad, I just put my mice on my desk with a wrist pad, and unlike the 3lue and Razer, the feet on the Anker would EVER so slightly stick to my desk. Never while in motion, but when trying to point at something precise, I'd end up a millimeter to the side, and trying to move back would mean the ever so slight jerk to get it from the ever so slight sticking to move, ending the cursor yet at the other side of where I wanted to point.

So I'm going to keep the Razer as my gaming mouse... because its feet don't stick to my desk, it slides around quietly and effortlessly on my desk.

So, if you have a mousepad, I'd recommend Anker instead. More buttons, better design, cheaper, no loggin in, great software, great LED colors, all around better mouse (though the Razer's cable is slightly nicer). Otherwise, get the Razer. If you don't have much money or don't care about the side buttons, then get the E-3lue Cobra Type-M EMS131BK High Precision Gaming Mouse

Ps. The "programming" software you see everyone talking about is fairly useless. You can't program the buttons. What it allows is assigning a program to execute when a button is pressed, to assign different button numbers than the defaults or have a mouse button map to a keyboard (so pressing a button will press that key). But you can't create programs or scripts.

title: Gorgeous Palette- Works Best With Eye Shadow Base
text:
I am a makeup artist. That means that I use all sorts of makeup from drugstore to high level professional. There are many things about eye shadow that I look for which determine if it is something I can recommend.

HOW THIS COMES
This came with no padding, no protection in a plastic mailer with no bubble cushioning. There is a plastic sheet over the surface of the eye shadow and no mirror in the case. There is no brush.

COLORS
The colors are beautiful. They have nuances that are very difficult to capture on camera. There are matte and shimmer colors- some of which are duochrome- something I look for in shadows.

HOW TO USE THESE
These eye shadows (like almost all other brands of shadow from professional down to drugstore) are best used with a very good eye primer. That will keep them in place and keep them intense too. The only eyeshadow I have ever come across which can be used without a primer and great success is Viseart.

QUALITY
These eye shadows are on a par with the high end cosmetics you find in the more expensive sections of makeup departments. They have a good amount of pigmentation and are velvety smooth too including the mattes.

MATTES
The mattes are not chalky, but are smooth and velvety. They show up well but again, these are best used with a primer.

SHIMMERS
These are some of the most gorgeous shimmer colors I have seen in a while. The collection compliments each other beautifully and look stunning on the eyes and even just in swatches.

ANY ISSUES
I have very sensitive eyes and these shadows did not cause any burning, watery eyes, or irritation of any kind the two days I wore them.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This set of eye shadows is gorgeous. For the price, it is excellent quality and is on a par with shadows much more expensive than these are.

When you get a top of the line Alienware laptop, of COURSE you are going to want an Alienware mouse to go with it.. Let’s take a look at how this performs with the Alienware M17 R2 laptop.

WHAT IS THE MOUSE LIKE?
This is a very ultra light USB mouse with RGB enabled lights all over it. It can be programmed to coordinate with the Alienware laptop and in individual games via the Alien Command Center.

CUSTOMIZABLE DPI

SCROLL WHEEL

This mouse is one of them. It could be from our original problems with the laptop and trying to re-download everything.

The mouse is nice and robust. The textured raised pattern makes it really easy to move it back and forth without slipping. This performs like expected for gaming. There is no lagging in tracking and it will work on almost any surface. The basic programming we have done has worked so far. We have not done anything intense or complex with it yet. We just use it as a mouse that lights up.

PAD FOR THUMB REST
The pad for the thumb to rest gives you dependable grip and helps you keep track of your thumb while gaming so you are not pressing buttons. There are three buttons above the thumb rest.

CORD
This has a mesh covering on the cord which allows the cord to move and keeps it from catching on surfaces or tangling when you are winding or using it.

THE BOTTOM LINE
If you happen to have an Alienware laptop (in our experience the M17 R2) this mouse is a great companion. We have had to spend so much time trying to get the laptop straightened out after an initial period of frustration that we have not had as much time to explore all of the dimensions of the mouse. title: Solid Headset For Computer Gaming, Adequate for Tablet and Phone, Make Sure To Download The Software
text:
When it comes to headphones, my family is a bit obsessed. There are always plenty of opinions and preferences flying around our house, so when I had the chance to test these out, there was a grabbing contest and then we had a winner! Let's see how these rated with our headphone fan.

WHAT ARE THESE HEADPHONES LIKE?
A full set of headphones, these are meant to be full coverage. There is plenty of padding on the top of the headphones and in the ears as well. There is a wheel volume control on the left side. There is a flip down mic that flips up when you don't need it. There is also a button on the left side that turns the mic on and off. There is not any light indicator to show if they are on or off.

The mic comes with a foam head that you can apply if you need to. There is a regular plug for a tablet but if you want to use it on the computer, the adaptor allows me to plug into the computer via USB. There is a dolby option for surround sound that seems to be only for the computer. If you want to use this with Xbox One, you need to purchase an adapter

HOW DOES THIS PERFORM?
I am going to break down what areas that this has performance in.

GENERAL SOUND
Just by itself on a tablet or phone, this is okay. It is not overly impressive, but still works well enough to be worth using. Later on in this review, we will explore the sound after the software engine was used on the computer.

CORD
The cord is a little over 6 ft long which is plenty long enough for comfortable moving around while listening.

COMFORT
These headphones are really comfortable. The cushioning is great and allows for many hours of use without any problems. The swivel of the ear pieces is fabulous. The set up is wonderful. These headphones excel in comfort and the way that the parts work as far as wear on the head goes and operation of the mic and such. The foam on the ears and top of head is cooler to wear than leather or synthetic leather as it breathes nicely.

CONTROLS
You can use volume on the headphones but also the base unit you are using it from. The controls are handy, so you don't have to be bound to use only the base controls from what unit you are using. The mic button is handy and much nicer than a wheel control.

MIC
Calls were heard fine and so far the mic seems to be good to use - people can hear well and it is clear. Used with voice activated systems it worked very well. When used with the foam cover it seems to block outside noise well.

DOLBY
It makes it sound like you are in a tin can. It just is not that great.

DRIVERS
The best performance from these headphones is using the Conair Utility Engine (CUE). That is only available through the computer use. It is really a nice separation of sounds, base is excellent, and the allowance for custom settings is great. This satisfied everyone and they really liked these better once this program was used.

Gaming was greatly improved using this engine. It is great surround sound using computer games which is what this was designed to be used for.

CONTRAST EXPERIMENT
We tested out the same song recording on a phone, tablet, and then on the computer. The sound difference was worth mentioning. When listening on the tablet and phone, the sound was muffled and there was not a great separation of sound. It was adequate but nothing to write home about. When listening to the same song on the laptop using the Corsair Utility Engine it was like a very different set of headphones.

COMMENTS
Is this a jaw dropping set of headphones? No. Is it a great set of headphones to game with and enjoy when you want a decent set that is comfortable, but if you are very picky about your headphones and are fanatical about sound separation and definition (aka realism) this is probably not the headset for you.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This set of headphones is a good starting set of gaming headphones. VERY comfortable to wear for long periods, the mic on these is good and works clear enough to be heard and operate voice activated software well. Separation is best using computers with the Corsair Utility Engine, but is adequate for tablets and phones if you just want to hear music or something without anyone hearing you. These are not top of the line, but they are a hit with our daughter who uses them constantly for everything from phone and tablet, to gaming and voice activated lessons.

MY RATING
Despite them not being top of the line, our daughter really likes these. We all feel that they are one of the most comfortable headsets we have ever used and they serve us well for her basic needs. As for five stars, I would say four is more accurate. The rating is more like FOUR AND A HALF STARS

The startup guide is, well, let me say really not as good as it should be with an expensive set of headphones like this. For visual learners, you might have some issues unless you are a real techie. There are no pictures of the back of the transmitter box or of the back of the playstation (or other items) you want to connect to so if you are not really good at understanding what goes where, you might have to look up online somewhere how to hook this up to your console or other devices.

WHAT ARE THE HEADPHONES LIKE?
The headphones themselves have a cushioned top and small ear covers on them. The retract and get slightly bigger, but not a huge amount. The top is cushioned and they hold onto the had pretty well, at times feel a bit tight. That will loosen up over time, I am sure.

The left ear pad has a retractable mic in it. When the mic is turned on, a red ring lights up. The disc on the outside of the left ear pad also twists off and that is there the lithium battery is put. When you want to replace, you quickly twist off the cover, replace the battery and you are good to go. There are two arrows that line up for you to replace the cover quickly so you don't have to fumble with it in a hurry to continue your game.

The right ear side has the on off switch on it located just slightly toward the back of bottom of the circle. If the ear pad was a clock with 12 at the top and 6 at the bottom and 9 toward your front with these on, it is about at 5 o'clock. To turn it on, you press for about a minute or so. The switch will light up. If you want to turn on the mic, you tap the same switch once and the mic goes on. Tap again and it goes off.

On the right ear side, there is also a control. It is a wheel which controls volume, but when pressing it, will change the menu on the transmitter box. Then if you move the wheel it will scroll the menu.

The ear pads do fold flat which makes them a bit easier to store when not in use.

I also find that the longer I use these, the more comfortable they seem to become- I imagine they will continue to loosen up over time.

HOW DOES THE TRANSMITTER BOX WORK?
I tested these headphones out on a PS3. I found very little on the internet about using these headphones with a PS3, so knowing that many still use the PS3, I wanted to test using that gaming console first.

SET UP WITH PS3
Optical cable- plug in to optical out on PS3 in back then plug into optical in on the back of the transmitter box.
USB- plug in mini USB side of the cable to the transmitter box and plug the regular USB side into the front of the PS3

POWER - this is optional. The power plug can be plugged in where it says DC but keep in mind that means the transmitter box will be on at all times. If you prefer that it turns off when your PS3 is off, then don't use it. The advantage of the power plug is if you want your battery to charge up when the unit is not on, you can have it plugged in for that. Once done, you can still remove the power plug until needed again.

SIDE SLOT
This package comes with an additional battery. One battery had a single bar of charge on it and the other had two bars of charge on it. So, while using on, the other is charging in the box. I found that with the power plugged in, it took about 45 minutes to reach a full charge or so. One battery took almost an hour. The battery pushes in and locks into place while charging, and then if you push on it again, it will dislodge and come out so you can use it and replace with the other one if you like.

FRONT PANEL
The front panel has a white light up design. It shows the battery charge, that the headphones are on and if you are using gaming and voice and the balance of the two. There is a dial on the right and a back button to the left of that. When turning on the headphones, I get a light that shows they are on then a quick large display of battery power left in them, and then it goes to the screen that shows me PS3 and how much volume is being used at that point. It will also show me the current battery charge of the battery that is charging on the side of the unit too so I can keep track of when it is ready to use should I need it.

The menu is pretty simple to adjust. You press the button to change menu and turn the dial to run through it. There are presets for equalizer and you can also set custom.

WHAT THE DON'T SAY IN THE INSTRUCTIONS
Call me dumb if you want, but although I have programmed computers and done a lot of technical work, I guess I was having a dull moment when I set up these headphones. I could not get them to work. I went through every setting over and over again and just could not make them work right.

Since I have never had headphones on my PS3, (I am the only one who hasn't) I did not realize that I had to change the settings in the sound menu. I should have, but I didn't remember. So, after much looking around, I finally found the setting that has to be changed. There is no mention of it at all in the instruction book. Since this review is geared more toward the casual gamer, I thought you might like to know that small important fact.

You have to go into the PS3 settings menu for sound and pick either the optical sound or you can have both going if you like- through the TV AND headphones. I like to do that when the family wants to be in the room and see what is being played but I want to hear details of sound you normally don't catch on just the TV speakers. You just have to remember to change the settings when you change how you prefer to transmit the sound.

HOW WELL DO THESE HEADPHONES PERFORM?
I am going to have to really work with these for a while to find the ins and outs of them. My first impression of them was awful. I really was disappointed. There was hissing, crackling and all sorts of noise with sound effects on various games. The music seemed fine, but every time there was an explosion or some sort of noise that was supposed to be electronic in nature, the headphones had so much other noise in them it was distracting and annoying. I messed with volume and settings and everything and it just didn't get as good as I thought it should have.

I kept on, however, changing to various games. As I moved through all sorts of different games, I realized that some games must be designed with engines that do not seem to transmit clearly over the wireless headphones. They just are awful. Then other games seemed to be clear and a lot easier to play.

DOLBY
So far, I have had the best results when removing Dolby on all of the games I have tried. I am not sure if that is because the headphones are designed for 7.1 and the PS3 is designed for 5.1, but it seems to be more muffled with the Dolby on and there are more annoying features that come up with sound effects. I will continue to play with this and see how to make it work if I can. I will update this review at that point. We have several different gaming consoles we can try these with, so over time I will elaborate if I find solutions or differences. The listing on these headphones does specify that it will work on both PS3 and PS4 so I plan to see what I can find out about this over time.

MUSIC
I have watched videos on these headphones and found them to be excellent. I can hear all sorts of nuances that I did not catch on just the TV speaker. I watched them via Netflix and also Bluray on the PS3. Sound was much better than some games. Like I said, however, it could just be the software used when developing some games that does not translate as well into the headphones as others.

I do want to point out, that these are GAMING headphones. They are not going to be the top of the line for music listening, so if that is primarily what you want them for, they probably will not be what you want. For the variety of needs I have on the PS3 of videos to music in games and movies, they are surprisingly good.

MICROPHONE
I have not had the opportunity to test out the mic yet with other players. I will update as that opportunity presents itself and will comment on performance during gameplay.

THE BOTTOM LINE
So far I really like these headphones but have a few issues with them. Some games do not sound right in these at all, and others sound beautiful. That is not always the fault of the headphones, but it does make for annoying experiences in some games. The design of the headphones is nice and I do love how they work when they work well with games. The transmitter is easy to use and battery life seems a bit shorter than 20 hours, but I like the fact that you can keep a battery charging while playing so when you need to replace you can.

I also like that you can opt to have the power on to them while the PS3 is off so you can recharge battery, but then unplug it so that it only turns on when the PS3 is on too.

For the price, I have rated these four stars at this time. As I continue to use them and learn more about them and the ins and outs over time, I will update and amend my rating if need be.

FUTURE UPDATES
I plan to test these out with other games as well on my PC games as well as tablet in the future and will comment on those experiences as well.

GAMES TESTED SO FAR (more coming soon)
Monkey Island (newest one)
Hydrophobia
Zen Pinball
Peggle
Planet Minigolf
Spellunker HD
Beyond Two Souls

title: Not Super High End But Great For Most Applications
text:
I have a family of headphone fanatics.

My daughter listens to music or does her school work using headphones most of the time. What is very helpful is having a microphone built into the headphones for some of her work which requires responses such as Spanish.

My son is a headphone enthusiast who goes into such depth about each set of headphones that my eyes tend to glaze over and I am not quite sure what he is talking about. It is THAT in depth. His favorite are Turtle Beach.

All three of us have tested these headphones.

I think they are great for music and gaming. I think they are pretty nice and I like using them. They cancel noise outside well too.

My daughter loves them when doing her school assignments because they cancel outside noise and it is hard to get her attention when she is using them for work online on our PC. They are comfortable and she does not remember she has them on a lot of time. She loves the extendable microphone but she wishes it was just a half inch longer or so.

She likes all of the different extensions that come with it. The cord seems to be a good length. The only other thing she was not keen on was the plastic quality.

My son's major comment about them is that often companies will sacrifice the midrange sounds in an effort to get the higher highs and lower bass sounds and he said that seems to be the case with these.

For what they are, however, the three of us agree it is a decent buy and pretty good for use in games, school programs, and listening to music as well.

We don't have an iphone to test it on so I can not comment on that application of it.
