title: Excellent Quality Cable for a Great Price
text:
Because we like to try out electronic cables and devices for a while before drawing a conclusion, I have made sure to test out this cable for several months now. The verdict is in- this cable is a very high quality cable which works beautifully with no problems at all.

Despite it being thick and a little tricky since you can not bend it at a sharp angle, it is easy to work with by looping a bit as the 6+ft of cable gives us plenty of room to do so, but I would advise you to check out any holes in furniture or other small areas that the cords might have to pass through to be sure you have enough room to pass this cable through if there is any question- BEFORE you install it.

We have checked this cable with various devices- PS3, HDTV, Blu-Ray player and most recently it is being used from a high quality amplifier to a very high level audio-visual computer system. In all cases, the picture/sound has been top notch, with no disintegration of information flow or integrity of signal.

The quality of this cable is definitely high and equals or surpasses the performance of cables that are much more expensive on the market but have brand names that people are more familiar with. We have a LOT of cables and cords in our house as we have an electronic addict in our home, so we have a lot of HDMI cables and devices to test and compare with. This cable is also a good choice for future equipment upgrading as it will be compatible.

The frustration free packaging is brilliant, by the way. Makes life a LOT easier!

I highly recommend this cable, as long as you are not required to make a sharp angle for installation with no extra cord to loop around, or as long as your cable does not have to pass through a very tiny space (as is often the case when you have multiple cables running through holes in furniture, or other small spaces.

title: The Most Fun Our Family Has Had in Years
text:
I waited a long time to write this review. Why? Because I wanted to test this game out thoroughly. Also, I wanted to play it just one more time before writing my review.

Buzz Jr allows you to play in multiplayer mode- up to four players. There are four buzz units which are connected at one point. Anyone can enter information that will be recognized by the game.

We played this across the room- about 8 ft from the PS3 and had plenty of room to move around without feeling restricted by the controller cords.

You can also play singler player.

There are practice options so you can learn the games.

You can also save and load games, align the screen, and there is a widescreen option. We played in widescreen mode.

When you are ready to play you have the following options:
marathon
single player
short game
medium game
long game

We played the short and medium so far as we did not want to be locked into anything long- everyone wanted a chance to win.

To play a game you have the choice of quick start, standard, and custom games. The nice part about custom games is that you can set up a list of games that you especially like and play them without having to suffer through games that you don't enjoy or that frustrate you.

The list of games to choose from is this:
Totem Poles
Whack a Squirrel
Wheel Running
Balloon Battle
Bridge Out
Bubble Bath
Card Counting
Elephant Baseball
Free Fall
High Voltage Voting
Island War
Jungle Hurdles
Keep It Up
Leaping Lily Pads
Lion Taming
Monkey Bomb
Monkey Bingo
Monkey Catapault
Monkey Slide
Odd One Out
Primate Penalties
Rocket Riders
Run Around
Simian Shootout (not sure of that one- can not read my own writing!)
Splat

WHAT I LOVE ABOUT THIS GAME

There is so much that I can write about this game in the positive mode- it would take pages.

For the first point, it is there is color- LOTS AND LOTS OF BRIGHT CHEERFUL COLOR! That in itself makes the game enjoyable to play.

We loved that you could personalize your monkey with crazy glasses, clothing, and feet, and the ability to name them is great too.

The music is delightful and fun - very happy music but it does not get to you to hear it over and over like some games.

The game controllers work beautifully. They are very responsive and everyone had chances to win games. The game is easy to use, and yet challenging enough for everyone that no one was bored.

What I especially like about it is that the games were challenging without being insulting or off color in attitude. There were a couple of crude things that some people might object to such as gorilla flatulence underwater and a few things like that, but on the whole it was really fun.

ONE THING I DID NOT LIKE

I did not like voltage voting, however, I thought that was in bad taste- that was the only game I recall being so irritated with that I refuse to play it- voting will electrocute a gorilla I think it is and it just seemed sadistic even cruel- and although it is just a cartoon, the attitude behind it upset me and I don't think it is family oriented.

FINAL COMMENTS

However, the rest of the games- and I think we have played all of them- are really fun and entertaining. All of the games take different skills so each member of the family had a chance of winning. That made it fun to keep going back to try playing over and over. No one felt that they were not able to have a chance at winning.

All in all this game is a huge winner- it gave the entire family a chance to play on Playstation without any concern for content and suitability for different family members. Playing this game has been one of the highlights of the last few months. Our son said it reminds him of Mario Party 3.

title: Great build quality!
text:
I ordered the ‘Logitech G915 TKL Tenkeyless Lightspeed Wireless RGB Mechanical Gaming Keyboard, Low Profile Switch Options, LIGHTSYNC RGB, Advanced Wireless and Bluetooth Support - Clicky, Black’ for review and would like to share some of my “unprofessional” thoughts.

I have been using the Logitech G815 wired keyboard for several years now and I absolutely love it. It has actually been my all time favorite keyboard and I have used many different brands throughout the years. The G815 is basically the same style/construction as the G915 TKL except that the G815 is wired and has the ten key pad. The G915 TKL (Clicky) is very well constructed and flex is minimal due to the solidly built metal frame. Because it is the TKL version it is considerably smaller and fits well on the pull-out drawer of my computer desk and it gives me the freedom of being able to easily pull it out from the pull-out drawer and place it either in my lap or on top of the desk. I also like the idea that I can use it with my smart TV.

I love the media controls on the G815 and was very happy to see that even though the TKL version is smaller, they still included the media controls on the G915 TKL. If they would have removed those, I may not have been as fond of the TKL version.

I also love the fact that the G915 TKL has two different angle settings which are nice and sturdy.

The battery life is actually pretty amazing especially if you turn off the lighting but I tend to keep the lighting on and even then battery life is impressive.

Personally I am not all that savvy with keyboard switches and the different benefits so I can not give any specific details as to how well the switches work other than I love the feel of the shorter throw compared to other keyboards I have used in the past. The “Clicky” keys are not as loud as other switches on other branded keyboards that I have used and I feel like I prefer the “clicky” keys vs the “Tactile” or “Linear”. This may be due to my love of the G815 that I have been using for a while which also uses the “Clicky” switches. To me the other two feel mushy.

Overall I love this version and feel like Logitech has continued to make great products throughout the years and it is a brand that I trust! Personally I feel that the G915 TKL is a bit on the pricey side but you really are getting a solid and well made keyboard that should last a good long time if taken care of.

*On a side note - I am having some issues with the Logitech G Hub software which I had to uninstall, as it was not working properly and now I can’t get it to install. I would dock stars for this but I think it has to do with my current PC which is not aging very well. When the software was originally installed it worked fine so I am hoping with some effort, I will be able to get it installed again at some point.

text:
I ordered the 'Corsair Gaming VOID RGB Elite Wireless Premium Gaming Headset with 7.1 Surround Sound, White' for review. First I would like to mention that I had originally ordered these in White. This was not a huge deal to me but you may want to make sure you get the color you order before you open the box.

I have had these for a while now and I must say that I am a Corsair fan but these are just a bit of a disappointment actually. The build quality is great, the sound is pretty good but the issue for me is the random static or lag that these have with my fresh install of Windows 10 Pro. I don't own a PS4 to test them on unfortunately so this review is entirely based on how they have performed on my PC. They do connect super fast and effortlessly to my system, they feel comfortable but they are a bit on the large side for my head. The feel just a tad bit loose. I think the static or lag issue may be due to that these run off of the 2.4ghz bandwidth and I am using them in the same room as my wireless router which may be the issue but even so they should (in my opinion) be flawless in this situation. I can't say that I don't like these, but I can say that they are not my favorite. The RGB lights on the side are pretty cool but my guess is that they can and will drain the battery faster. As for the sound quality, they really hit the Bass, Mids and Highs spot on. The battery life is actually great for Wireless gaming headphones and they seem to charge fairly fast although I have not completely drained the battery yet. As for the charging, I do have to point out that they charge via Micro USB which is another disappointment. It's 2020 Corsair and USB C should be the standard in my opinion. Overall I do like this headset, but it will be more of a backup to others that I have that I think are much better for the price. I hope that this was helpful.

Pros:
1 - This headset sounds great for gaming and for music both on Xbox One and PC. They are nice and clear and quite satisfying.
2 - I find that even after a few hours of wearing they are still comfortable and do not irritate my ears, nor my bald head which is impressive, as I have tried others that tend to either cause my ears to feel as if they are being squished and or irritate the top of my head. This set is nicely padded both with the ear cups and headband.
3 - The Mic performs better than most and I find that compared to others that I have tried and tested, the Mic performance is probably the top of my list out of all that I own.
4 - I have had zero issues with this headset connecting and pairing up (quickly) with the control module, both when connected to the Xbox One or PC.

Cons:
1 - Seeing as this was going to be my main Xbox One gaming headset, I was extremely disappointed that it would not connect to the Xbox One Astro Command Center App. I tried several things and eventually contacted Astro Customer Support. They were quick to respond stating that the A20’s were not compatible with the Xbox One Astro Command Center (ACC) and could not tell me why. They stated that even if they knew why, that they probably wouldn’t be able to tell me. This is my main gripe and why I docked one star. I mean, it makes Zero sense to me that if the A20’s are made and designed for the Xbox One and PC then why should I also need a PC to connect to the ACC to make adjustments to the EQ settings and update firmware. 2 - The placement of the volume control makes it so that if you are wearing a hoodie, and because the volume control is easily adjustable, it can easily be adjusted just by moving your head. Now with that said, it’s not a huge deal because fortunately it adjusts in very small increments but it is still a bit annoying. Also the A20’s don’t remember the last volume setting and every time you turn them on you need to adjust the volume, which for me means rotating the control up several times to get max volume.
3- I wish that the Mic was removable. Now this isn’t huge as it is nice to just be able to rotate the Mic down and it’s on, and rotate is back up and it’s muted but it would be nice to be able to remove it if you wanted.
4 - lastly I don’t like the overall look of this headset. I was concerned that because of the “square” boxiness look, that it wouldn’t fit right but as I stated in the Pro’s, this set is perfectly comfortable and because of that, I will give them kudos - but they do look a bit funky compared to other brands and styles out there.
Overall and even with the listed Cons, I love this headset and think that Astro has produced a fantastic headset at a great value for the money but again, it makes no sense that it doesn’t work with the Xbox One ACC App.

title: Volume control design is probably my favorite feature!
text:
I ordered the ‘HyperX Cloud Stinger Wireless Gaming Headset with Long Lasting Battery Up to 17 Hours of Use, Immersive in-Game Audio, Noise Cancelling Microphone, Comfortable Memory Foam, and Designed for PC’ to use mostly for video editing and listening to music on PC. I would like to share my thoughts after quite some time using these headphones thus far, but first I would like to say that I am a big fan of HyperX and the quality products they produce.

Cons:
Comfort - My initial impression was how light these headphones are and expected them to be extremely comfortable, however after about an hour into wearing them I noticed that the head padding just doesn't work for me. I have a bald head and find that many headphones just don’t have either the right amount of padding, or use a “not so comfortable” material. I much prefer my wired HyperX headphones for comfort.

Sound - Although the sound quality is good, I expected it to be much better. For me there just isn’t enough Bass nor Volume to these Cloud Stingers. Don’t get me wrong here. The sound is nice, clear and not muddy but I really think that my wired HyperX cloud headphones sound much better.

Frame - The Steel Slider frame is nice and light however the slider is a bit loose and tends to adjust too easily which gets annoying when you find just the right fit (btw they fit big in my opinion).

Pros:

Swivel Earcups - I absolutely love the Swivel Earcups which make it easy to turn the earcup away from your ear so that you can listen to someone talking to you in the same room without having the headphones slide off you head. I wish my other headphones had this feature.

Sound - I may have expected better sound quality however as I stated in the cons, but they do actually sound good and are very clear.

Earcup Padding - I have no issues at all with the comfort of the Earcups nor padding. In fact they are very comfortable, just as my other HyperX headphones.

Wireless Connection - The 2.4Ghz Wireless Connection has exceeded my expectations and works much better than Bluetooth in my opinion. I can walk into the next room without any loss in sound quality or losing connection.

Battery Life - I have not fully tested how long the battery “actually” lasts but it does last a long time. I don’t charge them after every use but I will say that I have used them for hours at a time, then turned them off and came back days later to find them still capable of several more hours of use with zero issues.

Volume Control - Though the Cloud Stingers don’t have the volume level that I expected, I do like that the volume control is nice in the sense that you can “fine tune” the volume level. By that I mean, as you slide the volume control it doesn’t jump up or down super fast as most do. As you rotate the volume control, it’s very gradual. The control doesn’t stop either way you rotate it. To adjust the volume you need to rotate it several times to go all the way up or down and the tension is absolutely perfect. This makes it nice so that if it slightly gets bumped by just putting the headphones on or taking them off (or rubbing against your hoodie) you’re not going to suddenly change the volume by much at all. I appreciate this feature probably most of all!

Other Thoughts - The Swivel Mic does seem to work well the few times I have actually used it however I kind of wish that it was removable. The USB Dongle is nice and small however I have to admit that I have lost it a few times. I have recently however found a solution to this problem by placing the Dongle flat inside the earcup and twisting it slightly to fit snug and secure (see attached images)
Overall I am a fan of HyperX products and do feel there is definitely value to the Cloud Stingers and I do plan to continue to use them for video editing. However, I think there are better “wireless” headphone options for gaming and listening to music, but you will spend considerably more for those options.

The other thing that drove us a bit crazy was the fact that it was a USB attachment into the Wii station instead of using its own power cord. So, it was always glowing right in front of the TV. We have always just used batteries, so we were hopeful this charging station would work well. However, I think we will go back to using our regular batteries. Maybe if we were true gamers and played all the time, I would think twice, but right now we only replace the batteries in the four chargers ever couple of months and maybe only play the Wii a couple times during the week.

title: Lovely keyboard, worth considering.
text:
[Note: I updated this review and changed rating to 4*, since I was mistaken about the lighting.]

This was the first mech keyboard I tried, and I really liked the feel and responsiveness. I was switching from a Logitech Wave keyboard, and found that the slightly smaller keyboard and different layout gave me a little trouble at first, but I began to adjust fairly quickly. The Logitech G-Hub software is ok: in my opinion not quite as good as the Razer Synapse software in ease of use and configurability, but good enough.

Unfortunately, the new GX keys do not allow the secondary characters on the keys (the symbols accessed by using Shift) to be illuminated. So there I am, looking at brightly lit characters, and finding myself peering occasionally to be sure I'm hitting the right key for the shift character. Maybe a perfect touch typist wouldn't care, but I need to occasionally look, especially when I'm typing the less frequent characters. (My understanding is that this is a limitation of most mechanical keys: only the upper part of the key can be properly lit, so the only solution is to have the two characters side by side at the top.)

A minor flaw is the need to use two USB slots to plug in the keyboard, because one powers the pass-through USB slot. What? How is that useful? I'd rather just use a separate USB cable or hub and have the option of using USB 3, multiple ports, etc. I think this is just dumb, although I know that many buyers want a pass-through no matter what.

I ended up returning this one and switching to a Razer TKL with linear switches, which has even better responsiveness and feel, and is just a bit more convenient to position. And as I said above, I like the Synapse software better.

title: cloud feature is disappointing
text:
I upgraded (from 2012) in order to have mobile access to the data. And that is a useful & long-desired improvement.

Unfortunately, Intuit did its usual half-hearted, half-designed job with this feature, and it's quite disappointing:
1. You can't sync investment accounts. The old investing.quicken.com site is very limited, not worth using. (For example, you can't see simple consolidated views of your investments, can't run basic reports. etc.)
2. The sync from the desktop isn't automatic, and takes a long time. If you're used to other online products that sync to the desktop (think Dropbox & Google Drive as two very popular examples, there are many others), you will find this clunky & old-tech. Everytime you open Quicken, it will tell you you made changes, whether you did or not, and suggest that you sync. This should be an automated, behind the scenes process, it's not hard.
3. The alerts are rather dumb, and they're essentially hard-coded. You can't create your own rules, and you can't even do a lot with the built-in rules (you can just pick some parameters from a limited list). You can't delete them all either, if you consider them dumb and pointless. Again, not hard to do a lot better.

There are no significant improvements in reporting, or in investment analysis. If you look at the "What's new in 2013" page, you see mobile, alerts, and "more flexible budgeting", whatever that means.

There is a tweak to how accounts show up in the nav bar, where you can put some accounts in the "Separate" list, which means "show but don't include with main set of accounts". This is mildly useful. There's also a feature to mark an account "closed", also slightly useful -- in theory. These account still show up in the list of accounts when you're doing a transfer between investment accounts! Clearly someone forgot what the word "closed" might mean.

So all in all, same old Intuit, same old Quicken. Buy it if the mobile feature is useful to you. (BTW, I tried Mint as an alternative, and I couldn't stand the heavy-duty selling on every darned screen. Maybe some people can tune this stuff out, I couldn't.)

text:
There's not a lot that's obviously changed in this version from Office 2007. (See [...] for detailed descriptions of changes.)

There are also some security improvements that are useful: e.g., Word opens downloaded files in a protected mode; PowerPoint allows presentations to be restricted from editing/copying.

If you're trying to decide between this version and a previous one, definitely I'd recommend this one. If you're trying to decide whether to pay for an upgrade, it depends on how irritated you get with the limitations of the ribbon in the 2007 version.

title: pretty good VR gaming headset
text:
I have tried a few VR setups in the past, but the Oculus Rift S is the first VR headset that I have owned personally. I like the fact that it doesn't need any external sensors, as it gives you a lot more flexibility with how you can set it up in a room.

The setup is really easy, and it's quick to get up and running. It doesn't really come with much in terms of apps or games, other than some tutorials, so you have to purchase games or apps through the Oculus store or Steam. I picked up Robo Recall so far, and it's a fun game.

A couple things I noticed that detract from the experience slightly are the field of view and the audio setup. The field of view seems less than on some other setups. You can see quite a bit of black-space to the sides in your peripheral view, which takes away from the immersive feel. Also, the speakers are in the headband near the ear, and are not an over-ear setup, which from an audio perspective also takes away from the feeling of being really immersed in the environment.

Overall for the price, I feel it is a good value, especially if you want to set it up in a room where it might be difficult or cluttered to try and position sensors and sensor-towers. If you are looking for a more immersive experience, than the pricier alternatives might be a better option for you.

title: Not perfect, but it works, nothing was broken :-)
text:
From purchase to setup, I am pretty pleased. However the hiccups were there.

While others chose All Access, which is actually separate from this bundle offer, considered a "new model." I chose the Black Friday limited time offer, then paying in equal installments over 12 months, using Amazon Prime Visa. I did this, because I converted from Live Gold to Ultimate Access, recently, and have two years prepaid. Over two years, though, the Xbox One X bundle is actually cheaper, when considering Ultimate is two thirds of the cost. On top of that, All Access requires a Capitol One credit check, and I didn't want that in my wallet.

The order was shipped across the country, why? I don't know, I would have thought the local Amazon warehouse would have had it ready for same day delivery. When it arrived, it was raining, though no attempt was made to deliver it to the door. It was dropped 6ft over the fence. Strange, you tell them once, deliver over the fence for a soft package you weren't going to be home for, then for the rest of your life everything gets tossed over the fence, no matter what it is. Fortunately only the outer box got soaked. The rest remained dry.

Somethings I noticed. The Xbox One X was made mid 2019, yet Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order is a new game bundle. There was a secondary set of circular stickers sealing the sleeve to the packaging. Also the primary box was dusty. I have a theory. Somewhere along the chain, the box was opened, and the contents replaced/changed/updated, then the bundle sleeve was added. I don't know who does this, Microsoft or Amazon.

I was disappointed that the game was a digital download, and not a disc. The item presentation suggests a disc. Still, I cannot play the game. After downloading over night, it has 11 hours left. Not everyone has gigabit.

Setting up the unit wasn't as easy as documentation suggested. The iPhone Xbox App does not use the camera, therefore you cannot use the QR code to set things up. Also because the unit was so old, there was a 700MB+ update required and this disrupted and complicated the setup. Where I could type in a code to setup the unit from my phone, it forgot after the update, and I had to do it again on reboot - the iPhone app was no longer able to participate. Also, I had to manually enter codes to add the game license and extend Xbox Live Gold, by 20 days. What ever happened to using the camera and OCR to read the codes? Oh that feature is with the QR code reader - non-existent.

I replaced my Blu-Ray player with the bundle, on a new 4K TV. I decided to reuse the HDMI High Speed 1.4 cable, already run to the previous component. This may have been the source of screen blackouts during setup. I have reseated the cable and it hasn't blackout since. But the situation has been noted.

I liked that the Xbox detected the TV was 4K and a switched over to the higher setting.

title: Click click click, this is responsive and clean
text:
During my very first typing class in 7th grade, I had an instantaneous awe of the way I could press a button and the letter or number on that key would appear on paper. Older computer keyboards felt a little similar but not the same, really, you know like when you're thinking and rub your fingers on the keys. If you type a lot or enjoy gaming on a computer, responsiveness is critical for speed and comfort. With the tactile but pretty quiet keys on the [[ASIN:B00N2ROO2S Corsair Gaming K70 RGB LED Mechanical Gaming Keyboard - Cherry MX Red (CH-9000068-NA)]], I'm brought back to the days when I typed on that old typewriter and even though the area of the keyboard is smaller, I'm in heaven.

For gamers, this keyboard will likely take you to heaven. Since the K70 is now in RGB, you can set it up with colors beyond the imagination and save your profile/s for play on any machine. For non-gamers, the RGB is not really necessary, but it sure adds another dimension if you type, as I do, in the dark. If you don't want the keys lit, you can dim them or turn them off.

The black aluminum case of the Cherry MX Red version which I have is classy to look at and impressive to hold. I especialy love the right angled corners and I use the removable wrist rest which has a texture that is smooth, almost leathery. On a table or desk, I can keep it flat and rely on the rubber strips to hold it in place or I can raise it with four simple feet. Right now, I'm typing with it on my lap and I have the computer on a chair a few feet away. Although the quick start guide says I must use both of the two USB plugs, I have simply plugged in the one with the keyboard on it and it's working fine. For gaming or utilizing more than just typing or with a computer of USB 1 or USB2, both plugs are needed, but with a USB3 port on the computer, the single works fine.

A complete manual really should be downloaded and if you've ordered this keyboard, you can do that while waiting for it to be delivered, so you'll be ready when you take it out of the nice looking box. I know that some people have criticized the software, but I have not had problems when I used this on a Windows computer. On the Mac, I was unable to access the Cue software at all. I've switched between a Mac and a Windows based computer and since I saved the profile, it's working fine on both. I am really hoping that Corsair is able to develop for us Mac users.

So, in summary, if you want a mechanical keyboard and use a Windows computer, this is wonderful. If you use a Mac, I'd suggest skipping this RGB version if you love the keyboard and save some money by getting the previous version. title: Protection and handy light outweigh its cost

With the reduction in price and the advent of the Special Offer Kindle, countless more will find their ways into the homes of readers all over the world. The Kindle Lighted Leather Cover is lighter in weight than I'd expected, more rigid, better constructed of a high quality beautiful leather, and ergonomically designed for every day use. When the front cover is folded back for reading, the round elastic band can be reversed around both front and back covers to keep them joined and make the covered Kindle easier to hold. If I find myself thinking about the irregularity of the lighting on the screen, I go to my Home Page and select another book.

title: A great mouse but not for me, not full-time anyway
text:
I had high hopes for this mouse and wanted to love it. I will probably keep it, but it won't be my main mouse.

Pros:
* It is heckin' adjustable! I wasn't expecting thumb depth to even be a thing.
— The clickable side is adjustable to a higher angle than any of my other vertical mouses.
— Thumb tilts in several directions, moves forwards and backwards (closer and further away from your palm), and it's possible to pull the thumb rest out further from the clicky side.

Cons:
* It still feels really large for my hand.
— I can adjust to a good shape, but I feel like I barely have hold of it and it's going to slip out of my hand at any moment.
— Something about trying to grab it with my widdle hands means I often click accidentally when I don't want to and end up accidentally closing out windows. Oops!
— Also sometimes when I lose my grip on it, the thumb rest moves out of place. Maybe my hands are just too messed up to use mice any more. It's a real possibility.

* It's not silent. I know it wasn't advertised as silent, but I have gotten used to silent mice, and kind of expect that now. So no false advertising or anything, but I prefer silent clicks.

* I feel like it needs a skirt or some part protruding out the back for my hand to rest on. I don't like vertical mice with giant skirts, but a not toward a skirt might help me feel like I'm gripping it better.

* What the heck even with the middle button. This is maybe a "just me" thing. But I'm not used to middle buttons, and I keep hitting the middle button when I want to right-click, and DISASTER. I tried to reprogram the buttons with X-Mouse button control, and it fixed it sure enough, but then it messed up all of my other mice. [Edit: I set both middle and right buttons to right-click, so no more problem there, I guess.]

Oh yeah, time out: I have to alternate through a bunch of mice due to various RSIs, so having to reprogram buttons is no bueno for me. Also maybe a sign the mouse is too big for my hands.

So I doubt I'll send it back and will keep it for arm pain flare-ups, but it's not worth $80 *to me*. The concept is gold, and with some tweaking and maybe actual different size options, the product itself could be outstanding.

Maybe with more use I'll get used to it. Le sigh.

The bottom screen shows the map, but now there is no dot on the map making it easy to know where you are, and where you want to go. I found that convenient, and used it all the time on the other games. It takes getting used to this change, and wish it was still available.
One last thing I want to point out is there is no way we think this game should be compared to Pokemon. It is my opinion it's being compared as a selling tactic because of Pokemon's popularity. The Pokemon games are a favorite with our friends and family.

title: Good, but flawed product
text:
Pros:
1. It's kind of like playing real guitar with rock band 3
2. It seems sturdy, I've been wailing on it for a month now and It's still working.
3. It's wireless with batteries included
4. No restringing or tuning frustrations like with real guitar.

Cons:
1. Strings don't extend up the fretboard, so there's no physical correlation between what you're picking and what fret you are pressing.
2. All buttons are the same height, no physical difference between the top "string" and the bottom "string".
3. Only 17 frets, the neck is 2 inches shorter than my gibson.
4. Strings are plastic, and make an awful scratching noise when you pick them.
5. I don't want to think about what will happen if one of the 100s of buttons stops working or if one of the strings breaks.
6. No string bending, pinch harmonics, or pick scratching are detected by the game.

I've had a lot of fun with this game over the past few weeks. I've been playing it several hours a day using only this controller. Using the controller and the game I've learned a lot of songs that I otherwise would not have bothered with, such as Rock Lobster, Whip It, and Stayin' Alive. Skills learned playing Rock band 3 translate over to playing real guitar, but I think you do need a real guitar to get the most out of this. Many times I can't figure out what I'm trying to play in Rock Band without banging it out with the real guitar first. It's just too frustrating trying to figure out what you're pressing and what you're picking, especially when playing arpeggios or guitar solos. In a way, the mustang is kind of like playing two different instruments with each hand. I plan to buy the Fender Squier that is coming out in March, but I had to get my hands on this game. I do not regret buying it and I will continue to play it, but when the Squier comes out I'm not going to use it anymore.

title: A great protector, or how I learned to banish dust particles from my Switch
text:
Intro

As we all know, the Switch comes with a plastic screen. Whether it was to save money, or to make a more durable product, a plastic screen is obviously very easy to scratch up. This was especially true as putting the Switch inside the dock could easily cause the screen to rub against the side of the dock. Thus, I went ahead and bought this screen protector. It was one of the best reviewed ones at the time, and also one of the best deals, and I am very happy with the purchase.

Durability

I haven't had any issues with durability. I haven't dropped my Switch, but I've taken it on many trips and have yet to see any scratches.

Fit

The fit is very good on the protector. It fits over the entire glossy black area on the switch, including the bezels around the screen itself.

Clarity

I haven't had an issue with this. Most of the time I don't even notice the screen being there.

Application Process

I read through some reviews and many people were having trouble with installation. Since it's such a large screen it's a lot easier to get dust under the protector - one of my pet peeves. My process was to remove any towels and carpets from my bathroom and to steam it up and to do some minor cleaning. Then I sat down with the switch on a table in the bathroom and cleaned the switch and protector carefully with rubbing alcohol to remove dirt and discharge static.
I practiced some dry runs, and then used some canned air to blow dust off the switch and then quickly checked for dust, removed the backing on the protector, and applied it immediately. This resulted in no dust on the first try, which was great.

I have seen that the Switch itself could also be bent a little (it seems like a common problem), so if yours is bent you might have some trouble applying it. In that case it might be better to get a plastic protector.

Conclusion

Overall, a great product and highly recommended. The fact that they include two is an even better bonus in case you break one or fail on an application attempt.

title: Unique Christmas-Themed Stories of Unexpected Connections and Love!
text:
In this collection of unique Christmas-themed stories there are many unexpected connections and the women find the love of their dreams despite circumstances they can't control.

"A Joyous Christmas" is about an author and motivational speaker who writes books like "Me First" and "You Deserve It All." Except after her life is saved by a stranger she feels fate pulling her in a different direction. This movie deals with a lot of issues that are common during the holiday season. I felt this movie was one of the most loving and encouraging expressions of Christmas I've ever seen. All the main characters find happiness in the end.

In "Romance at Reindeer Lodge" the most unlikely of things happen when the characters least expect them to. A woman wins a radio contest but ends up in freezing Vermont instead of warm Jamaica. Imagine packing all the wrong clothes. She thought she was going on a beach vacation but ends up with a lot of snow. This is a slower story with romance and holiday themes but a satisfying ending.

"Rocky Mountain Christmas" was my favorite of the three movies. When a woman leaves New York to get away from her problems with her ex she doesn't realize that she is still attracting fame into her life. Even a famous actor preparing for a film role recognizes her so in some way they have one thing in common, staying out of the news while at a real ranch. Lots of things happen including a great deal of Christmas decorating, parades and ranch work with horses. But what is going to happen when Christmas is over and everyone heads home to their real jobs? As is common in many Hallmark movies the woman has a choice between the man or her job? Which will she pick this time?

So if you are looking for some cozy Christmas movies these are fun. My husband even enjoyed them. Usually he can figure things out way better than I can and gives me insight into the characters and plot. He always seems to know something before I comprehend it. So it makes watching these fun.

~The Rebecca Review

title: Cute story about a writer struggling for independance
text:
My main interest in this movie was the story of Marjorie Kinnan Rawlings. She is a writer who is leaving her life to pursue her writing dreams and find fulfillment in publishing a novel.

Her husband is not interested in her dreams. She decides to seek solitude in an isolated orange grove in Florida. Little does she know, this will not be an ideal life. After 30 years of urban life, she is not prepared for a small Florida town.

After many rejections, Marjorie finally realizes "Gothic Novels" are not her specialty. Her agent helps her see how interesting her life actually is and she begins to write about what she knows best. In the process she falls in love, makes a best-friend, helps the community by hiring everyone who lives around her to help remodel her house and fix up her orchard.

Cross Creek is based on the best-selling memoirs of Marjorie Kinnan Rawlings and has some very human moments when you realize the beauty or ugliness of life. The local business man (Peter Coyote) who falls in love with her, does something so amazing. It reminded me of when my father bought my mother her first car. I only know the story, but the situation is similar. Marjorie of course is very head strong and not about to take help from another man. Until she realizes what Norton Bascomb has secretly done.

Slow-paced movie that is more "cute" than "dramatic." Although, there are a few heart-wrenching moments. I thought they dwelled too long on the party, however the chocolate cake sure did look good!

Only view this movie if you have chocolate cake in the house! Preferably decorated with candied orange slices.

~The Rebecca Review

title: Finally wireless freedom while maintaining traditional gaming expectations
text: So to answer the question at the start, Yes this is a good mouse and no wireless doesn't hold it back from maintaining gaming performance. I'm coming from an older logitech gaming mouse the G500 which I've used and enjoyed for years due to it's ergonomics and gaming performance. I've always enjoyed the G500 so this Logitech G403 does carry many of the similar ergonomics as well as overall feel. The surface of the mouse has a nice soft touch plastic which gives it a good grip as well as comfort for longer use sessions. Not having a wire is really fantastic, as that was one of the drawbacks to the G500 in that the wire would often make you feel restricted when moving the mouse in specific directions. By default the G403 does feel really light, but comes with a weight to install which I would recommend using. I've not played around with the RGB lighting as of yet, but it does cycle through a gamut of colors so you could easily tailor the colors to match your pc lighting or match an rgb keyboard. The build quality is top notch, and the cable has a nice sleeve for a clean appearance. To charge the mouse you need to connect the mouse to the cable itself and it will allow you to use the mouse as a corded option while charging if you would prefer which is a great option for Logitech to have included. The mouse is super responsive and the buttons have a satisfying click to them and I've not noticed any increased latency in games while using the mouse wirelessly. Overall I'm very satisfied with this mouse and glad that I can finally have the freedom of wireless gaming without having to sacrifice either performance or comfort!

title: My Switch Lite is freaking adorable
text:
Last Friday night I noticed my OEM switch shell was no longer closing correctly; likely due to case clips breaking during one of the two times I have replaced my left joystick (this Switch Lite has at leas 1000 hours of play time, and is the only Switch controller that I have had drift issues with). By midnight, I had fully fallen down the shell swap rabbit-hole.

I decided on this pink case, but having a turquoise Switch Lite, I was apprehensive about the screen bezel as I don’t feel like a screen protector is the best solution. Pretty soon, I had this shell, a “white” digitizer (which ended up actually being gray), a new LDC (because separating the original screen from the digitizer seemed like a good way to break it), thermal paste, screen adhesive, and a fan (because mine has been sounding a bit loud lately, but the one I ordered ended up not fitting, so I just cleaned the original one well and reinstalled it). Overall, the price was a bit much considering this was an impulse purchase in the middle of the night, but I did what I did and I don’t really have any regrets about it.

The swap took a little over an hour to complete (remember, I didn’t remove the old screen, so I got done a little quicker - besides, this isn’t a race). It wasn’t too hard, but I had already disassembled my Switch Lite a couple times for joystick replacements, so I felt well prepared (plus I watched some videos and reviewed iFixIt’s screen replacement instructions). I didn’t find anything to be terribly difficult, only tedious. Anyone who has the right tools, takes their time, keeps track of their screws, and follows instructions shouldn’t have too much of an issue with this swap. If you have ever replaced a joystick, you shouldn’t have much of an issue with this.

Things to note: The finish on this case feels velvety soft- very pleasant in the hand. It makes me wonder how it will hold up to wear and use in the long term though. I have seem some reviews that show what looks like the finish wearing off, but those switches were put into cases. I haven’t seen anyone who uses their switch lite naked complaining of issues- only time will tell. This case also has a less than 1mm gap along the top and bottom - isn’t really anything that will ruin my day, but I felt it needed to be mentioned since I can’t account for it (putting the tiniest amount of pressure on the case closes the gap - I made sure my screws in the back of the case were tight, but still, there is a gap). Other than that, I am very happy with the way this turned out :)

Tips for success:
-Have the right tools. You will need 00 Philips, 00 Tri-wing, Spudgers, adhesive (in case the screen adhesive isn’t usable when you remove the old one or want to use a new one), thermal paste (it isn’t really expensive and will save your device from overheating), heat gun (if you aren’t replacing the screen with a new one)
-Take your time - this isn’t a race. A mod that takes 60 minutes instead of 4 hours is not worth it if you break your device.
-Clean as you go - If you are using a switch lite that has been around, you will likely find dust and grime inside, have some rubbing alcohol and canned air to clean anything you run into. Just make sure any alcohol you use has evaporated before turning the device back on.
-Replace any parts you have concerns about. The fan and joysticks are common parts that fail. If you have issues that you notice (loud fan or slight drift), use this opportunity to swap the part(s) while you are in there. That being said, the fan I bought ended up not fitting my Switch Lite - I cleaned it out well with cabbed air while the device was open (see Clean as you go) and it runs much better now.
-Follow instructions. iFixIt has a screen replacement guide that I followed. It identified the screw type for each hole. I separated my screws by size and had no problem grabbing the right one for each step when I reassembled.

A little more on why I decided to replace my screen and digitizer. At the end of the day, I wanted to end up with a mod that made me most happy and a screen protector wouldn’t do that (nor would a turquoise bezel around the screen). In addition to being a better fit for my desired outcome, it gave me the flexibility to more easily move back into the old case if I ever felt the need (or ended up breaking the screen). I considered trying to separate the digitizer, but decided it was too risky (in hindsight, it probably would have been fine). Even if, at the end of the day, the screen bezel ended up being gray, I feel like it is the best end product I could have ended up with and the one that makes me most happy.

Update 9/22: this shell had me a little worried since the soft-touch finish feels like it will wear off with use. I am happy to report that I see no signs of an issue after 10 months of use. I will note that the shell makes the switch 7g heavier than the original for anyone interested.

I like the layout of this console better. The cartridge in front design seems more ergonomic than the last 3DS, which had it in back where your fingers naturally lie.

Overall, I think the New 3DS is a wonderful, polished console. It is the perfect size for travel. The new features increase the options for game developers (ZL/ZR buttons, c-stick). As for the Happy Home Designer, I don't really have any interest, but all of those components are interchangeable, and the game arrives as a code that can be given to someone who will actually use it (it is not locked to the device).

I have no regrets with my purchase of this console. If I had list any complaint is that the new 3DS consoles do not come with the power supply.

title: Wonderful, but not without some faults!
text:
I enjoy the occasional game and decided I wanted to get back into handheld gaming. While cell phone games do have plenty of engaging time-killing games to offer, I was missing games with some depth and story; like Zelda! So I decided to go back to my roots and get a Nintendo console (my roots are the old DMG-1).

After a shockingly small amount of research, I went and impulse purchased the New 3DS XL. If this is your first 3DS, be sure to pick up a charger as well, since, unlike just about any other device that NEEDS a charger, this system does not come with one! Taking the device out of the box, the first thing you will notice is the pristine shiny surfaces that greet you! The exterior is shiny, but don't expect it to stay pretty. It will pick up finger prints if you just look at it. Not only that, but I had scratches on it after a couple weeks of keeping it in my bag (in a pocket that was microfiber lined and all by itself).

Next thing you will notice is the weight. This device actually has some heft to it! It is only 1 or 2 tenths of an ounce lighter than the original Nintendo! I found that I did get a but of hand and wrist strain during the first could days of play. Just something to keep in mind!

Another thing you will notice is that the hinge is a bit flappy. When you open the hinge, you will hear it snap into place in two positions (and by snap, it sounds and feels like you are doing something wrong). This wouldn't be a problem since the second position is where you will want the screen opened to, but the screen moves within that position. I play a lot from a reclined or laying position, so I do notice the top screen wobbling quite a bit. I would estimate that the movement is about 5 degrees. It is enough that, if I am playing while laying down, I often find myself awkwardly positing my index fingers so they wrap around to the front of the device to keep it from moving while I am playing. I have seen video of New 3DS XLs that do not have this issue with the hinge, but most people seem to have it, and people who have contacted Nintendo say that Nintendo does not consider this to be a defect.

Even with all of the negatives I have listed, there is still so much to love about this device. The top screen is beautiful and sharp. The Super Stable 3D does great (even when you play in the dark). The console comes with a few interesting games, so even if you don't by games right away, there is definitely lots of interesting stuff to do on the device. The e-shop is great and even has some great games that you can get for relatively cheap including some old NES and Gameboy games. The controls are generally ergonomic, although I find that the D-pad can be a little uncomfortable if you are playing a game that uses that instead of letting you use the thumb pad. Streetpass and spotpass add a whole other dimension of entertainment. There are a lot of great games available for the system for almost any genre. All the old Nintendo franchises have games for the 3DS that have a terrific balance between familiar characters and new spins on gameplay that develop the story.

title: An amazing collection of video game history
text:
From my teenage son:

This is by far my favorite smash game. In every inch of this game you can really feel how much heart the developers put into this. This game is massive and I have been playing it on and off for nearly two years.

To start with there are over eighty different fighters all of which are unique and express their own individual personalities. I can't even imagine how much work it must have been to accomplish this, I have the utmost respect for these developer. Since I got the game I have spent nearly the entire game mastering the character link, it would take a lot of gameplay to master all of them.

There are two major complaints when it comes to this game: online mode, and balancing. First of all, yes... I agree that online mode lag can be excessive, but I don't find that it causes me to lose many matches. Balancing is kind of tricky... As it is quiet apparent that not every fighter is made equally, I feel like most of these accusations of overpowered or weak characters are over exagerated, as every fighter has their own strengths and weaknesses. for example, little mac is well known to be one of if not the worst characters, due to his trouble returning to the stage, but when on stage, a good little mac player can be hard to challenge.

The point is I think this is an amazing game, and I would absolutely recommend it to anyone of any skill level.

title: An Experience Unlike Any Other
text:
It’s about as easy to describe the game Journey to someone as it is to describe Doctor Who. You love it, you know why you love it, but to put it into words is nearly impossible. While describing your love for Doctor Who may make you sound certifiably insane, trying to describe Journey makes it sound boring, which it is certainly far from. Yet, despite that potentiality, I will do my best to paint a more detailed picture as to why we still love it and will continue to love it for years to come.

You’ve probably heard from so many mouths that Journey (crafted by thatgamecompany) is “touching” and “beautiful” to the point where it almost sounds cliche, but it’s true. This game genuinely provides you with an experience unlike that which you could have with any other game. I haven’t played it in nearly two years, and yet I can still remember precisely how I felt when I reached the end.

This is going to sound cheesy, so prepare yourself, but you don’t play Journey to have fun, you play Journey to be moved and to be taken on a ride you’ve never been on before. If you end up having fun anyway, then that’s great, but sitting down to play Journey is more like going to a museum of art, as opposed to strapping in for a day at the theme park.

I don’t want to spoil the ending for you, but to sum up, it pretty much falls into the categories of: unforgettable, shocking, moving, touching, resonating, and sobering. It will put a smile on your face moments after it makes you cry, and you will come to understand how you can bond on a deeper level with a real person whom you’ve never met. And single player is not an option - well, at least at certain points. You’ll understand why when you play.

While you may delightfully frolic with your anonymous companion on your mission to get to the mountain (located at the end of what seems like the largest desert imaginable), you can do nothing more than jump or speak to each other in song, something that would, in reality, be more than sufficient, should we ever end up alone on such a quest - a quest that becomes more evident by the end of the game and will have you nodding in approval.

Under any other circumstances, Journey would probably suck. But it’s with those kid gloves with which thatgamecompany makes all of their games, including flOw (a subtle game of evolution) and Flower (where you control flower petals on the wind), that make their gaming experiences more of an interactive meditation than a traditional gaming session. You play games like Call of Duty and God of War to release your aggression, but you pick up a thatgamecompany game to soothe your soul.

The fact that Journey is an indie title makes it even more impressive that it was so memorable, though less surprising that it is as profound. The visuals are breathtaking, particularly the glimmering pink sands, and the soft sounds are unlike any you’ve heard before in a video game. Journey is the perfect example of why you don’t need a lot of glitz and glamour - sometimes less truly is more...so much more.

title: Solid Game from the Franchise
text: Dynasty Warriors 8 essentially plays like every other Dynasty Warriors game.  Read as: you don't play for the plot, you play to level up your weapons and your attack power so that you can take down foes in one hit.  Thankfully, the beautifully rendered cut scenes (which, while appreciated, are slowing our progress), can be skipped, though there is an option on one of the boards in the Wei dynasty where, if you play it a certain way, you can unlock new dialogue for Lu Bu.  I can't imagine anyone racing to do that.  Anyway, the generals, of course, have musou, too, and here they'll take you out in one clip, even if you have full health.  So unless you are seriously packing heat, you might want to stay out of the way until they're done raging.  In "Story" mode, you can play through each dynasty to unlock boards and characters that you can then play on "Free" mode, which is normally a less than satisfying mode in other games, but since we're not here for the plot, "Free" mode is a great way to level up your favorite character., as well as their respective weapons.  Though, you don't have to stick to the weapons you're given - you can choose from any on the list.  One annoying thing about this, though, is that you do not land, by default, on your character's weapon when you choose the list.  You have to scroll down until you see the "EX" next to the weapon - that's how you know you're on your character's default weapon.  But don't feel limited by that - you can mix and match the "elements" of different weapons to provide better attacks (though, of course, your default weapon will give you a specific attack that only your character can do).  You can also use animal accompaniments which come with their own perks, depending on the sidekick you choose.  There's also "Ambition" mode, which is new to the series, and here you can build up a town, but not in the "Farmville" engine that every app seems to come with these days.  You make the area stronger by participating in various battles, and these battles will either give you materials to construct the Tongquetai Tower, fame, or new partners.  Later on, you can also unlock a co-op version of "Ambition" mode.  My favorite character is "Flute Chick," a.k.a. Zhang He, and while her attacks are purple and pretty, her musou was a bit of a let-down.  Plus, you don't get to unlock her until much later, which leads me to believe that she's one of everyone else's favorites as well.  All in, it's a solid game, and it doesn't fall short of what you would expect from the Dynasty Warriors series.

First of all, the band that is supposed to go around your thigh did not fit mine, so I had to put it just above my knee. I think it still worked ok, but it just wasn't comfortable and wanted to slide down. Secondly, I have bad ankles and knees and the exercises were not meant for beginners at all, with the squats causing me pain. I think this would be a great game for anyone who is already in shape and wants to add variety to their pre-existing exercise program, but it was just not for me. Eventually it might be once I get in better shape, but if you're a beginner, I recommend the Wii Fit over Wii Active, as there are more progressive exercises on the Wii Fit than on the Wii Active....just be careful of the Wii Fit's weight limit. Much of the adventure spans just four regions, each with a city that needs saving, a handful of dungeons and various side missions as well. This game has amazing visuals with a combat system that both veterans and newcomers will love.
It has excellent characters with a rich in-game world, and delivers it with a majestic OST. It's not perfect but it's an excellent RPG that every Switch owner should try.
Overall, I recommend it and is fun to play.

title: Fun game
text:
007 Nightfire is out for all major platforms, in time for the latest Bond film. The graphics are stunning, gameplay is amazing. Well worthy of the series!
I'm a huge fan of the Bond games, and we have all of the previous ones. We got this one as soon as it came out, and were definitely not disappointed!
The graphics are a huge step up from previous versions. In the first 'training' mission, you're driving a car through city streets. The lights reflect off of the curves of the car, you can see inside to all of his controls and movements, the dents show up realistically, the back up lights glow softly, and if you bash it a bit, the trunk comes loose. The city around you has cobblestone streets, water rippling, streetlights that come down when you hit them. The attention to detail is just amazing!
As you then move on through the various levels, you see this same level of detail everywhere. From the Austrian castle and other alpine scenes, to the city scenes, watery scenes and more, each really shines.
The plot is very engaging and typically Bond. But in an attempt to show that this isn't about violence - he's a SPY after all, not a Rambo - you get bonus points for being stealthy instead of blasting in with guns, and for stunning or capturing enemies instead of killing them.
In fact, just about every area can be 'accomplished' in many ways. Bluster your way into an objective by a full frontal assault ... or sneak in the side way for extra points. Since you're also rewarded for your time and health, often the sneaky, non-violent way is the best.
You've got a huge array of equipment, weapons, armor and vehicles, and all work just the way you'd expect them to. I found the default controller configuration REALLY annoying, but a quicks stop in the config area got it back to the way I'm used to playing.
Plus, there's multiplayer! Play with up to four people at once on REALLY great maps with quite a bit of customization options on each one. Grab some bots for practice, and play arena, team arena, king of the hill, capture the flag, or other game types.
Definitely worthy of the Bond series, and highly, highly recommended to any first person shooter fan!

title: Frustratingly difficult. Despite anything you do, you're punished!
text:
I've been playing the game for the last 3 days, and I'm about to just give up in frustration. A game is supposed to be fun, isn't it?

My Player mode is extremely unforgiving difficult game.
Part of the goal of the mode is to be a good team mate and work your way up as a starter. To do that, you do the nitty gritty things like set screens for your players. This works, only sometimes, and other times the AI players simply just stand there. Wasting time, waiting for your ballhandler to make a move. I'm begging the AI to come on, please start the play! We'll talk about being hypocritical in a moment here.
Playing as point guard, you get punished for holding the ball too long, by a large margin. Hey now, I'm trying to survey the floor looking for a good pass! Oh hey, a player is cutting towards the basket so I'll pass the ball to him. But oops! He continues running around the opponent and they intercept or tip the ball. Bass pass penalty, major points lost. What? So what is it? Do I take my time looking for the players to stop running and get the good pass or do I try to rush a pass to a running player?
Playing defense is brutal as well. You can't stand in close because the opponent will run right past you leaving you chasing them. Or you can't stand back a bit and they'll just shoot a jumper over you. Is there even anything we can do to prevent the major lost of points for allowing your man to score?
Okay well another problem is deciding who to defend running back after your team misses a shot. Well, hmm, the player defending arrows is pointing one way.. okay I'll go head there to defend. If you rely on the blue circles around opponents to defend, well, good luck because sometimes there are two players which you need to defend at once. Huh? WHAT? Okay, let's pick our position to defend instead. Makes sense right? Wait why is my team mate defending this guy too? The open opponent who just scored was the guy you were supposed to defend. You just lost a major amount of team mate points. Okay now we're chasing a fast breaking opponent down. There are 2 other team mates in front of him and the guy still makes the basket....just trying to help out, but yes more penalties to the team mate score. Oh also, sometimes the passes don't go to the right guy as well.

Whatever you do, you're going to get penalized. It's extremely frustrating.

There's probably more things I've forgot to mention that's wrong with this game, but let's close up this review. I realize I've ranted long enough already.

Another major issue is that it loads slowly. Can't the game play the cut scenes while loading? You simply have to wait out the load times, and watch the cut scenes that are forced on you, for the hundredth time. Get me into the game please!

I mean, parts of the game can be fun when you get to play but there are some really difficult things to master, like the shooting timing, the freethrow timing, the idiotic penalties. Don't add on to the frustration with it being just so darn slow to load. And come on, don't throw the player in there on Pro difficulty with no chance to learn the system. Why don't they have rookie enabled for My Player, I don't know.

PvP is a joke, if someone runs around in circles you are screwed (Had lvl 50 Engineer). Maybe I am getting to old to keep up with the younger players, but the combat system felt silly to me. I have played every MMO out there, and this one was just a boring game to me. I am sure some will love it, but this is just not for me. I am gonna go check out Arch Age.

title: Fun... Fundamentally flawed.
text:
I've been a Pokè-maniac since I was wee little, since the beginning. As soon as it hit the states I was hooked. I didn't want make up and barbies, everything had to be Pokémon. EVERYTHING. Even as an adult, I spend much of my life on Pokémon.

That being said, I'm not quick to hate anything Pokémon... But I'm open and honest to criticism.

25 hours in

Positives- It is fun! If you can ignore the sluggish lag, and frustrations, it's pretty okay. It doesn't feel like a chore as some of the recent main title games have. Exploring with my mons was great, but for me the best part was avoiding all possible leaks and spoilers and actually jumping in blindish, aside from announcements from Pokémon. It was so much fun seeing new creatures like "...what is that???" But also... They're ugly! So many disappointments!

The negative-

Okay... I'm disappointed I haven't had any major hilarious bugs as others have. I want to fall into the void! At best pokemon were in the floor and walls. At worst, the LAG and broken controls.
Travel is so sluggish in areas- like holy cow, get the bricks out of your socks! I'm not an FPS queen, I still love my older games, but man... This is painful sometimes. There have been times where I'm like "oh, here it is!" Only to snap out of it after freezing momentarily. I can admit I'm anxious and won't be transferring my special past pokemon, out of fear of save corruption. I feel this game is trying so hard to keep itself together and is losing will to keep fighting.
Controls... Mainly when auto-battling. Okay. I'll send out my pokemon, or try to, and they just stand there or run off somewhere else. The star bases were unreasonably frustrating. Sure, we got PLENTY of time to beat the swarms, but I'm still panicking when it seems my LR button isn't even working. I had to look up guides and exposed myself to spoilers, trying to figure out what I'm doing wrong- it's not me. I just have to run around the enemy's pokemon spamming the button, hoping my Pokémon will eventually cue in and attack. I've even used multiple joy cons. It's not me.
The UGLY pokemon... I'll avoid spoiling, but there were two pokemon I got very excited for! The one has a RIDICULOUS evolution... Like, fans wanted this creature of the sea in Pokémon form for years, and you did WHAT to it!? I boxed it forever. And this one cutie, I love! But there's no evolution, and as of now, I can't find a way to make it carry it's place on the team... Literally, turn it into a beast or roll or literally something. It's too cute to end there. Otherwise, most evolutions are sad... Most Pokémon are too. Don't get me going on starter evolutions I feel GF designed some of these to be as unappealing as possible and to pull a joke on long time fans.

Despite it all, this is better than SW/SH. I was so bored with that game... But this had so much potential and promise, and it feels like a slap in the face. I didn't even criticize SWSH much because it was new to the Switch console- I don't have that excuse here. I'd have rather waited for a better game. I'm very happy we got a few more Pokémon this gen than the last 2, but please- build the numbers! I need a game with more to do and more creatures to hoard.

Also! PLEASE MAKE SHINY POKEMON GLIMMER IN THE OPEN WORLD! I'd been shiny hunting since day one, and found my 1st at hour 24. I only knew it was shiny because it was so drastically different, and I barley saw it having to make a double take. I hate knowing I probably passed other shiny mons not knowing any better. Some just don't stand out so much, some you can't tell at all... Without that glitter, we have no clue unless we battle it. It hurts the progress of wild and open spawns. Let's stop stepping back from Arceus.

Also... I know Nintendo games are built around children in mind... But please, let's consider the adults who have been in this franchise for literally all their lives. Story is childish, I'm so sick of being a little kid in school. My school years were my worst, I hate anime revolving around school even. Just... Last game, Arceus, had a much better story. I find myself quickly spamming through text, not caring about the bullying arc especially. I was horribly bullied in school, but have been out of class for over 12 years... It's not a problem I can care about. And the tutorials... Let us skip them. I believe SunMoon had the longest tutorials, maybe not- but please make it stop.

title: Seriously, get this one...
text:
My fiance and I just got a Switch and we wanted the screen protected, so we went with some “officially licensed” garbage from Best Buy for $8. As soon as I put it on, there were bubbles all over and two ridiculous smudges that seemed to have appeared out of nowhere (and I know I didn’t cause them). I put up pics of both the Best Buy one which brought only one protector, a wipe, a crappy cheap cloth, and a thing for bubbles (barely worked) and the Cellularize one which brought two protectors, two wipes, two nicer cloths, two things for bubbles (which I only had a couple very tiny ones so not a big deal), and two sticky sheets in case anything got stuck to the adhesive side of the protector.

The quality between the two products is immediately noticable, especially when you feel the protectors. I feel like the Best Buy one was plastic. No joke it could bend like crazy. If you do that with tempered glass (what an actual screen protector SHOULD be) then it will shatter after force is applied. Anyways, this one feels SO nice and heavy duty. It was easy to apply and is VERY clear with perfect cutouts for the little areas that need them.

I highly recommend this to anyone thinking about switching screen protectors or buying a new one. I mean $6 for two quality pieces. You just can’t beat this. My ONLY minor complaint is that they advertise it as “bubble-free” but that’s not accurate. However, if you know what you’re doing, it takes seconds to get rid of them. If you have trouble using the bubble-removing thing, just gently and slowly lift the corner nearest the bubble and reapply which will make it disappear.

title: Almost perfect...
text:
I bought this at a Frys and decided to leave a full, honest review on here. I got this because of the review for this product I read that gave it 5 stars, but ended up returning it after trying it on in the parking lot. So here are some pros and cons if you are reading this and trying to make a decision.

PROS:
- Feels great in your hands
- Solid grip, not slippery
- All cutouts are almost completely accurate
- Has big controller-like bumps in the back for better grip
- Kickstand is still usable unlike with most cases
- Easily removable- hassle free

I’d say this case is worth $10, maybe $15 if these problems were addressed. I would definitely buy again if they were. But those small things were enough to bother me (I’m a perfectionist with stuff though so I’m very articulate/picky). However, this would definitely be a 5-star product for the people who would shrug these issues off. Overall, I do recommend but I definitely wouldn’t buy again for $30.

title: This game was wicked fun, especially with 2 players.
text:
It's less a game and more of an interactive movie, you can't really lose but you can change how the story goes. The graphics are great, the gameplay is fun and the sound is very good.

When I got the game, I popped it in to the PS3 and after an update was at the main menu. I went through the options and stuff, and found out there could be two players. My daughter quickly grabbed a controller and decided to play as the "spirit".

I played as the main character, doing things like walking around and beating people up. She played as the ghost or "spirit" Aiden(?) and could move stuff and do other supernatural things. Basically you switch between the two characters to get things done, CIA spy stuff or teen "Carrie" stuff, or even saving homeless people stuff. She got really mad when I wouldn't do what she wanted me to do, but I told her I play like I want and she plays like she wants.

As Aiden she can be mean and vengeful or helpful and peaceful. Once we finish the game we will have to switch parts, I want to try being a ghost and totally poltergeist that party of rowdy teens!

If there was more gameplay and less interactive movie, I would have given 5 stars. It's major funage, and even better with a friend (or relative). It's mostly like Heavy Rain; press a direction or hit a button fast. Sometimes I didn't know which direction to press in a fight, it was confusing a little, but I couldn't "die" so it was all good (after some practice I got better, but the fight sequences could have been a little more clear).

So if you are looking for a good story (told out of sequence, yeah for nonlinear) and like interactive movies, this is the game for you. And it's cheap.

And buy "Heavy Rain" too! It's also wicked fun, more so with the PS3 Move.

title: The 90s are missed.
text: I’ve been looking forward to this release since I first heard about it, I flew to Amazon to preorder the T. rex edition (I’m a fan, and a collector of physical media with games) I have the original Joe and max and it’s sequel on snes with cartridges and box, I even got the limited edition re-release when it came out! So trust me when I say, I love the series. HOW DID THEY MESS THIS FORMULA UP SO BAD?!?! We live in times where the properties from back in the day are getting sequels or remakes and they’re coming out in top shape! Streets of rage 4, Battletoads, TMNT…and so forth. The devs of this game completely missed the mark on what made the originals so good, First off for you to start and have 30 enemies on screen not letting you get past the first screen without dying a few times is a TERRIBLE first impression and unfortunately it doesn’t get better from there. The graphics are the selling point of the game, They’re definetly nice to look at, Other than that though it’s just poorly done. The game has no soul, The hit detection is off, The weapons have barely any impact, Too much going on at 1 time to even appreciate the art in the game, I honestly jumped back on the originals to see if I just remembered incorrectly, I beat the original game with only 2 lives lost. It took me 3 continues to beat this first stage, They really need to balance out the difficulty and the overall layout, It went from platforming fun to just frantic “where the heck am I on the screen” type of gameplay. It hurts to say that this is a hard pass until it (Hopefully) gets patched and updated, hard pass. 2.0/10

title: Z for Zorro
text:
Honestly, know what you’re getting. I actually recieved this game accidentally. I had no idea it was based on an existing TV show, I had put it as a preorder thinking it was one thing and forgot to cancel! But I’m so glad I didn’t. It’s a super charming game. I’m 37 years old so I’m definetly not the target audience for this, it was more for the kids but I decided I’ll try it out and more than likely return it since I’m the only one that cares for the big Z here, But let me tell you…it’s AWESOME.
It’s not a simple game, I actually think kids will have a hard time with this one. The graphics are nothing crazy but they look really nice for the asthetic its attemption to give which is the Saturday morning cartoon vibe. You have a stage and certain missions to complete in whichever order you choose, You can do the missions stealth wise by attacking enemies through rooftops, Light poles, In the shadows, You also get enough of
These and you build up your power meter which gives you an attack that gets rid of the enemy in one hit! There’s 18 stages in all and each stage aside from the first one take about 30-40 minutes to complete! So do the math, it’s outstanding amount of gameplay! The reason I don’t give it a perfect score is because the audio department, While serviceable is lacking, But honestly if you’re a fan of sorrows, Want a game that resembles something from the ps2 era, Done completely right, Then look no further! It’s a budget game and a complete surprise for me, Still haven’t passed it
For the kids to play…It’s quite the addictive gameplay loop here! You can wait until it’s on sale but honestly it’s worth the $40 asking price. $30 would be the sweet spot though! 8.5/10 Don’t sleep on this one.

text:
I’m not a xenoblade fanboy, Got the original, Didn’t care for it…Got chronicles X on Wii U and didn’t care for it either, Skipped part 2 because I thought it was an overhyped game that was just barren/empty wastelands, But my friend convinced me with all the footage he saw and leaks and so forth, And I was like I’ll give them one more shot, 2 days later as I write this review I’m 16 hours in, And I’m confident enough to write a review, Give it a perfect score of 5 stars, And tell you that this game is a MUST OWN title for EVERY RPG fan. The graphics are nice, But that isn’t the main draw of the title, We all know the switch is dated hardware, But the gameplay is PHENOMENAL.
The story, To the point where I am at least has been absolutely engaging. It knows how to hook you in and develop in a way that you want to know what’s next.
