title: *Snap Snap*
text:
It’s hard to write a review for a simple game like this, I’m an 80’s baby and have a huge collection of games, So I’ve played all kinds of games, Seen innovation, Watched them for from sides scrollers to platformers to Vr and right back to 8-bit.
The point I’m getting to is that out of those games there are very few where I can sit and play with my wife and kids and just everyone have a great time and point out where they see secret items or which character is best to take out the most difficult enemy, If you’re going to go at it alone, I wouldn’t reccomend it only because it’s meant to be played with someone else. It’s simple, You have infinite continues, There’s checkpoints everywhere, The graphics are sub-par, No adams family theme song anywhere in the game, HOWEVER this one got me.
It’s been ridiculously fun to discover secret areas, Fall off the most absurd cliffs, Play the minigames in between the levels (There are plenty which is cool) And to be honest that’s not a feeling that most games give me. I can’t rate it higher than a certain threshold because if not ID be comparing it with the greats since Amazon doesn’t have at the very least a 10 point grading scale even if it only goes to 5 so it doesn’t have to be whole numbers.
The game is fast, It’s funny, It’s innocent, It’s forgiving, It’s friendly, And purely innocent…But it’s A LOT of fun, it’s about 8 hours long, Nothing your child can’t see here, No force fed story or agenda, The story is just kind of there, But trust me if you’re looking for one to play with your kids or partner and don’t want to break the bank I highly suggest you check this one out! All in all for what it is I give it a 7/10 based on price, gameplay, and fun factor. Check it out!

title: GatorDone
text:
This game is quite funny, You’re an alligator walking around and eating everything in sight until you level up and can eat bigger stuff and so forth, It’s a novelty game that’s fun for half an hour to laugh with and a few beers, And then you put it on the shelf until your buddy reminds you it exists years later. I paid $8 for it on sale, And I still feel I overplayed. It’s funny, But it’s not good. The controls are a nightmare, Just to get this animal to walk where you want it to walk at any sort of speed is disastrous. It’s “open world” in a very small way. You can only access areas based on your level, because if you’re underpowered you will die. If you go into the wrong river you will die, If you stay out hunting too late you will die. Get used to dying again, and again.
The graphics are ok I guess, I mean who plays this for the beauty of it? It’s an idea thrown by a couple of new devs to sell copies to kids and adults who are into crocodiles or to players who thought they’d get some sort of animal like experience through the title. It’s simplistic in nature but the controls make it a lot more challenging than it has to be. Not much else to say about this title, it’s a 3.5/10 due to the humor factor stated above, But once that novelty wears off you’re left with a shallow, boring, repetitive, ugly game that you’ll probably never play again, you can safely skip this one. Save your time

title: Rico-less.
text:
The original Rico game is one I purchased on sale on the switch and knew nothing about. It was about $10 a few years back and to my surprise I had a complete blast with the game! It wasn’t perfect by any stretch of the imagination but it was an Indy Roguelite Fps game done with love and a limited budget, So when I saw a sequel was coming out I had to get it! Oh boy..

I’ll start with the positives: This is leagues above the original with the targeting and shooting elements, And the cel shaded graphics don’t look bad at all! Unfortunately that’s where the compliments end. All 2 of em.

The first RICO as I wrote above had innovation, Even in its crudeness and low budget, It had a campaign and as you were doing your campaign it would randomize missions such as rescue the hostage, Get files, Clear the floor, Breach the doors, Etc…This game tosses every one of those
Elements out the window in favor of a completely streamlined experience. You have hostages maybe twice during the “campaign”. I say campaign in quotation marks because the story is as generic and throwaway as they come, You start off by breaching the doorway in front of you (There is barely any room that has more than one door available to breach, So 2 players playing co op and breaching from 2 different sides has as well been tossed out minus VERY few occasions) you get the slow-mo time to shoot, You get them all and you can now pick up their weapons. You have throwing knives as well which 1 shots the enemy, You go to the next room and clear it after breaching the doorway. I hope you REALLY ENJOY breaching endless rooms because this is literally ALL you do for the incredible 1 hour and 48 minutes it took me to beat the story mode. Yes, a whole almost 2 hours. The levels feel stretched, So stretched in fact I was wondering if the game glitched and I’m just going into the exact same rooms I was in previously over, and over and over again (This is all true, I was about to restart the game until I realized a different color door in front of me and the level finally ended)
After those extremely repetitive, boring and just plain bad 2 hours I was like well let’s see what I unlocked…You get nothing, the ONLY OTHER MODE is a daily mission, Which mind you is set in the same exact locations as the story mode. No variety or thought was put into this title at all. It’s so basic, so boring and repetitive I’m still in disbelief. It’s incredibly buggy as well, There’s barely a game here and somehow before you reach the next room the frame rate drops so incredibly low that the music skips and you stutter while walking, and there is no one but you in that room. The music is repetitive, 3 house tracks that loop every 50 seconds or so, I hope you love the beats or the mute button shall be used, It drove my wife crazy.
Terrible story mode, Repetitive mission structure, No variety, Re skinned versions of the same weapons you use throughout the entire game, No rogueLike elemtents at all, No other places to go aside from the same building, No branching pathways like the original, It’s baffling that this is what they chose to put out. This could’ve been great as a DLC to the first game to just add more content, But this is NOT worth $40, $30 or even sadly $20. This is a $10-15 super budget title that will be in bargain bins for the forseable future. Save your time and money, And skip this one, This one game is going to put this franchise on a complete halt unless someone comes in and gives the fans of the original game what they want. This isn’t even worth a rental, It’s a 1.5/10. SKIP AND AVOID.

title: Oh man…
text:
So I didn’t expect a massive rpg, Nor any action, TBH my expectations were pretty low for this game…And this is coming from someone who liked both visual novels and loves the original bloodlines game, HOWEVER…
This game is a huge buggy mess, peoples faces have just straight up dissapeared when I’ve spoken to them, Pop in texture is horrifying, I haven’t seen. It this bad in a game in years, And this is the series X version we’re speaking of here. The graphics look like the characters were dipped in grease and have the most dead looking faces I’ve ever seen, Nothing in this world feel alive.
The gameplay is just as bad, Aside from there being ABSOLUTELY NO ACTION, 0%, None, Nada, Could’ve been forgiven if the game has a strong plot since you know…That’s what would have to hold it down as it has pretty much nothing else to rely on, It is excruciatingly boring. It’s hard to get through the story, Hard to care for the characters, And in a game that gives the illusion of dialogue choices, You pick the answer you like and you guessed it, You get it wrong. So you have to power up some of your abilities to be able to answer these questions, But the game mentions a brief introduction on how to do this in text on a menu and you never see it again. Right when you begin you can’t talk much, So why are the options even available? Is it for a second play through? This is the kind of confusing mess you’d be walking into. This game is worth at MAX $15-$20 price range. I support devs, I support indie games, I give things a chance, But save your hard earned money, And your time. It’s bad, Maybe if you catch it on a super sale and if you’re still interested with the knowledge of what I wrote above then hey, Power to you and I hope you enjoy it, But in all honesty…This is the worst next gen game I’ve played, And one of the worst full priced releases I’ve ever touched. Well its $10 less or $20 less depending o the generation you own. text:

I rate games based on what they are. For a cartoon Shmup with mascot characters that’s going for the SNES feel and look, The boss fights, The stages, The rebuilding the town it’s an easy 7.5/10

text:
This game in all honesty is a game made from simpler times in an arcade machine. On rails shooter (You can’t freely move for those that don’t understand the lingo) That you button mash and find weak points on the zombies, Fight a boss, Fight a super zombie, Fught a super boss. title: Where’d the rest of my game go?
text:
I’m a HUGEEEE Mario fan. Super Mario bros on NES was the first game I ever played in my life, I was 3 yrs old in 1988 and it came bundled with my Nintendo, I get EVERYTHING MARIO, I mention this so you don’t think I’m just hating on this just to hate, Quite the opposite, It hurts that I’m writing this review m, But if I can help someone save $60 I will, In this economy I know ID appreciate it.
I’m not going to go too much into detail here so let me simplify it, It’s a fun game, Really fun in fact..IF there was ANYTHING to do! No story mode for some illogical reason so we get cups, ok fine I was willing to live with that, The cups are ALL THE SAME EXACT THING. Since there’s BARELY any characters to play the game with, All characters you choose you’ll be going up against, I’ve played against the exact same team that I’ve chosen multiple times! This looks like it was made in a few months, Aside from an amazing looking opening introduction FMV, This game falls completely short and is an utter disappointment not only to sport fans but Mario fans.
Nintendo has had the trend recently with their sport games to release unfinished titles, Mario golf star rush didn’t have a lot to do but honestly I feel bad that I EVER COMPLAINED with that game. It had a story mode, it had competitions and a competent multiplayer. The multiplayer aspect of the game is an utter letdown, You believe well they didn’t concentrate on single player so Multiplayer must be making up for it somehow, Absolutely not. You would think if everyone had their own switch they can play each character on your team (There’s 4 of them) But no, You can’t. Up to 2 only. And get this, YOU CANT CONTROL THE GOALIE. Ever! One of the biggest points of strategy in sports games is controlling every aspect, And the goalkeeper has to be a dumbed down CPU controlled player. In all honesty I can keep going over how utterly bare bones and disappointing this game is, But..Don’t waste your hard earned money. Times are tough right now, And this game can care less. Shame on the industry for releasing this at $60, But I think we’re the biggest suckers here. 3.5/10. AVOID.

text: Wow, This is a review in progress, I’m 15 hours in and I’m having a complete and total blast with this game. Thank me later! But remember, Don’t expect AAA. Small team, small budget, BIG ideas. Hope this helps!

title: Classical gaming Bliss
text: So I’m sure if you’re on this page you know what to expect from Wonder boy, Or if you’re in the younger generation and have seen collectors play these games on YouTube or have played the remakes that have come out the past few years, Regardless wonder boy is known in the gaming community for its Platforming/RPG elements and revolutionizing a genre that wasn’t thought of until this title. Let’s start with part 1, It’s an arcade port. Think of it as an endless runner with being able to kill the enemies and platforming that gets gradually more difficult, It’s the weakest in the series but has held up pretty well! Part 2, An arcade port once again but the dynamics that are featured heavily in later monster world titles come from here, This game is the foundation of the game as we know it today so probably the most important one in the series, Be forewarned it is a quarter muncher as it is an arcade title but with an endless rewind feature and save states, You won’t have much trouble getting through it. There are some parts that I’m left wondering how you’re not supposed to spend $10 in quarters to beat it back in the day. As for 3 and 4 there’s a huge shift in quality and gameplay, These are not arcade titles but ports of the Sega console titles, They’ve honestly aged really well! After playing part 2 know what to expect from part 3, But part 4 is my personal favorite! It’s the metroidvania of the series very reminiscent of the Shantae series. This one is legit fun and I highly suggest that you check out the remake that came out not long ago if you like the original! (or you can just get the remake, which includes the original, Decisions decisions). The extras are honestly bare bones, You get an image gallery that looks like it was thrown together in 2 and a half minutes to make it look like the game has more content, Deff one of my least favorite parts of the compilation as it makes it look a little cheap. All in all it’s a nice compilation and worth the $29.99 and if you find it on sale even better! The classics are all here and you can change the aspect to full screen with crisp graphics or it’s original resolution or even throw in a CRT filter to make it look truly old school. It’s a 7/10 for me. I go by the .5 rating system by the way so it’s not a high 7, just an fyi! Try it out if you enjoy classic gaming! Hope this helps

title: Oh so many bugs
text:
You'd think after 20+ years they could work out the kinks in basic gameplay. But, no, they don't seem capable of that. if you are looking for a good soccer game, yes, you should buy a recent FIFA. Probably not the latest version since you might pay a premium for a game that's no better than last year's. But, it's sad that they can't do better. Issues:

- Offsides is called if, when you pass the ball, your player is even 1mm past the 2nd to last defender. No real ref would call it if that teammate is running back toward you since the small distance isn't an "advantage". And, no real ref would call it if that teammate is completely uninvolved in the play. But, FIFA will call it, since the story seems more important to them than getting the rules right.
- You can't call for a low cross. If you have the ball, you press 2x 'X'. If you 2x 'X' when your teammate has the ball on the wing, you'll get a lob, the defense will clear it out of the box, and you'll get dinged for "bad call for pass".
- If you call for a pass while your teammate 'A' has the ball and 'A' passes shortly after you call, 'B' will often try to pass to you, even if they're in a horrible position to do so. And, your rating will be dinged as a result.
- When I play as forward (I play in career where I only control a single player), I frequently get called for being "out of position" even though there's zero indication on the screen that I'm out of position. I use the camera mode that is half way between my player in the ball. When the ball is near my goal, I can't see my player (except on radar). If the computer has some odd view of my position, I get dinged in the rating.
- If I'm center forward and one of my wing teammates is out of position, I get dinged b/c the computer thinks I should swap with the out-of-position player. The out-of-position player doesn't even try to get back in position (even though the ball is far away, near our goal), yet my rating suffers.
- The rating does not understand the value of attempting a high risk/reward pass. When I'm playing center forward, I might make as many "bad" passes as my midfielder, but my midfielder's passes are brain dead whereas I'm trying to score a goal. Yet, I get dinged just as much.
- The computer doesn't even try to make good passes (I play at the "world class" level). Some passes go directly to the defense. No sane player would make a pass like that.
- Many crosses go to the goalkeeper. A lot of crosses are placed in the goalie box (the smaller rectangle). Occasionally this works in real soccer, but, in FIFA, the goalie is extra powerful so these crosses almost never work. Considering how special they make the goalie, the crosses should be going to around the penalty spot.
- Throw-ins in '17 were horrible. If I was receiving, they'd go to where I was when I pressed "A" and often go right to the defense. They're better in '18, but still go too often to a contested spot.
- Passes from the computer aren't aware of the defense. Real players will look for teammates that are open. Not so in FIFA. Often, I will pass to a teammate because a defender is pressuring me. Often, I'll get a pass right back even though there's a defender on top of me. Hello?!?!
- If you started a game with the wrong difficulty, you can't change it and difficulty isn't obvious when you start a game. This is especially a problem w/ my son: I play at world class, but he plays at Amateur or Semi-Pro. Sometimes when he plays alone or when we play together, we start a game at world class w/o realizing it. They should really make this more obvious and/or easier to change.

Even with all the warts, I still play. They have all the teams, the game play is overall good, and career mode is nice (though the expectations after 1.5 years become silly).

title: Good for the money but a step down from the G930
text:
I used to have a G930 for several years and decided to give the G533 when my last G930's frame cracked and I needed a headset the same day from a local store. If you're just looking for something above-average and can deal with little annoyances, then this is a decent choice.

THE GOD:

An audiophile might find fault in the sound quality but for us normal human beings, it sounds fine - rich, booming bass and decent mids and highs. I use these all the time for conference calls and can hear everyone very clearly and my voice seems to come through perfectly fine. Would I use this to record myself if I wanted to become a singer? No, but that's not what these are for.

It's also pretty comfortable. Fairly lightweight, and I can wear these all day every day without my ears hurting at the end of the day. I have average-sized ears and these fit comfortable over them.

They're not really noise-canceling (at least not more than any other device that goes over your ears). This isn't a good or bad thing - it was just one of the star ratings, and I'm not sure why.

The battery life seems decent, and I have yet to have an audio signal glitch (which was a rare but recurring problem with all the G930s I ever owned), which is good. The range is pretty decent, as well. I wore these while I went to the kitchen to make myself lunch, and I was probably a good 30-40 feet away from the receiver with about 4-5 walls in-between and no line-of-sight, and there was no audio dropout or loss in quality.

I have 2 big complaints with this headset:

1. My first main complaint with the microphone is that my old G930 used to have a red LED at the tip of the microphone that would come on whenever my microphone was muted, so it was easy to know at a glance. It may not seem like it would be hard to remember if you're muted or not, but when you're on lots of calls where you're constantly muting and unmuting, it's pretty handy. On the G533, the mute/unmute button will simply play a 2-tone sound - there's no visual indicator. When there's a lot of other audio happening, it can occasionally be hard to tell if the 2-tone sound was the UNmute or the MUTE sound, so I might have to press it again to figure out what mute state I'm in.

2. My second main complaint is that plugging in the micro-USB cable to charge this headset is a serious pain, especially if you're just trying to keep the headset on while doing it. First of all, the volume dial is right next to the charging port, so if you're just trying to feel for the space where the charging port is, you're going to accidentally roll the volume dial, which is annoying. Then, since it's micro-USB, the cable will only plug in in one direction. So if you finally manage to get the cable into the little space, if you had the plug facing the wrong way, you have to do it all again. And even when you do get it in the right way, there's enough space to turn it into one of those situations where the plug never seems to find the port, and after about 15-20 seconds of fumbling, you get irritated and have to take off the headset to see to plug it in.

This was a problem with the G930, too, although at least the G930 didn't have the volume dial so close to the port. I read that the G733 is USB-C, which should help quite a bit, since you don't have to worry about the direction anymore.

title: Good sound, but no noise isolation and bad mic
text:
I picked up a pair of these when I needed to send my trusty G930 headset in to get exchanged. My wife and I work back-to-back in a home office, and she is on the phone a lot, so I was looking for a headset that was comfortable to wear all day and would effectively isolate noise so that her voice wouldn't carry into my mic for my calls (mic noise cancellation), and also would not intrude on my music when I wasn't on a call (headphone noise cancellation).

The box advertised all of this, so I went ahead and got it.

PROS:
- It is indeed comfortable for all-day wear.
- Good audio quality (better bass than the G930, but otherwise equal quality, IMO)
- Being able to retract the mic is nice.
- The 3.5mm plugs mean I can use these with portable music players when I travel.

CONS:
- Microphone quality is terrible.
- Microphone mute switch doesn't work 100%.
- No advertised "30dB noise isolation" in the headphones.

On my very first call, I kept being asked whether I was in a busy office or a train station or something because the microphone was picking up -everything-. I tried to lower the volume, but it was impossible to find a setting where the other party could hear me without hearing everything else in the room (not to mention noise / static galore).

I also tried to use the in-line mic mute switch, but it apparently didn't do a full job - it just muted the volume of the microphone by about 90%, so you could still hear things through the mic at a very low volume (confirmed by listening to the audio stream on loopback).

These two things meant that I had to keep going to the softphone's mute button and un-muting myself to talk, then re-muting afterwards. Very inconvenient.

As far as the "30dB noise isolation" goes, I might as well not be wearing the headphones. I can hear everything outside the headphones extremely clearly, even my wife typing on the keyboard (it's a soft-touch keyboard, too, so the raw sound is not that loud). I have no idea who thought that there was ANY noise isolation whatsoever.

These will be going back to the store as soon as I get my G930 back.

title: PvP;  not so much econ or PvE
text: This game has been out for 2 years; I played in it from beta up to Fall of 2009.  In this time frame, a lot of changes happened.  FSL opened up with high hopes and 8 servers.  In the past 2 years, that shrank to 2.  The ship combat system is very innovative, and that is the game's main strength.  The emphasis these days is on PvP play, with the balance of power constantly shifting between British, French, Spanish, and Pirate realms.  You can still have fun if you prefer PvE, but that is secondary, and it is difficult to make a difference in the Realm vs. Realm plot of the game if you are not a combat monster or part of an organized group.  There are areas where incautious or new players can be forced into involuntary PvP play, which is part of what drove me away from the game.  If you lose a ship in combat, you will be penalized with loss of gear, which was a major irritant for casual play because of the effort to rebuild.  There can be a lot of trash talk, so go into it with a thick skin.  I liked the game while I was playing, but I was mostly a PvE or economic player, and the gradual drift towards PvP eventually made me look for alternatives.

title: A Must For Every WWE Fan Old & New
text: So i was able to get this when Amazon had it on sale for $30. At that price i was sure not to be let down had i not liked the game, like WWE 12, which for some reason came off as too big of a change with very little payoff. The main selling point to me, much like many others was the Attitude Era, which hands down is the greatest feature ever put into a WWE game. Being able to relive all the moments i remember from my childhood, the classic matches, incredible moments, and all the characters in between. (Not to mention they show stock video footage as you progress, heck they show more in this game than the WWE Attitude Era dvd recently put out). There were times when i was jumping up and down with excitement like i did all those years ago, the same excitement i would get from playing old classic THQ games No Mercy and Wrestlemainia 2000 for Nintendo 64. The entrances are great, still some issues with commentary and crowd noise, maybe not as noticeable without surround sound, but a minor flaw to say the least. The game card flap then velcro's down to provide extra protection of the screen and hold the switch in place.

All of the zippers are smooth. There's no weird plastic smell. Overall, very impressed.

Negatives
None. Wish I had purchased one with color zips. I purchase the entire black one. Which is great, but I wish I had some color to make it stand out in the bottom of my bag.

title: Flowers DIE?
text:
Sometimes I'll go a week or more without playing my old Gamecube Animal Crossing game. A New Leaf has flowers that wither and die! So that's kind of an issue. The trees are too small compared to the humanoid figure in A New Leaf, too. Look at a Gamecube version capture and a New Leaf capture. Why are the trees so small? Weird.

In my old Gamecube save, after 12 years, I have *LOTS* of flowers. And they look great. And I don't need to water them constantly. This is kind of a big deal with me. I really like planting flowers in the Gamecube version. I'm not so sure I want to commit to watering so many flowers in New Leaf.

I'm not wild about being the mayor of the town and having to organize things. I just want to play the game. I don't particularly want to be responsible for the whole town.

The area at the back of the shopping district / high street is disturbing -- some kind of showcase for home designs? Why is it so big? It's not a pleasant area. I wish it had been devoted to big garden plots to grow vegetables on, something like that. I don't like the Happy Room Academy in the first place. That big wasted space on the map is creepy, makes me think of nightmares where stuff doesn't make sense. Why is it on the map?

I still prefer the point of view in the original game, the way the camera moves as you run along.

The flowers are too detailed in A New Leaf. They just are.

The Island is fun to visit, but I miss Kapp'n rowing his boat, and his songs in the Gamecube version were a lot more fun. He seems to have gotten married and settled down and become... boring. He traded his rowboat for a motorboat? Why was that considered to be an improvement?

The mini-games on the Island are amusing but something I'd think of more in a Monkey Ball game. You collect medals, which you use to buy items on the Island.

The wet suit and goggles are great, but you can't see anything under water, which is something of a disappointment.

Interaction with Tom Nook is minimal, his nephews run the store on alternate days from one another.

You know, all the pieces are there, but it's not as much fun as the Gamecube version. I never played Wild World and I was seriously unimpressed with City Folk. I was hoping this would be another great version, to the point where I spent $275 or whatever it was buying a 3DS XL. And I haven't been playing the game constantly, or even often, really. Meanwhile, I *STILL* play the Gamecube version nearly every day.

I wish they'd expanded the Gamecube version, not reinvented it. Maybe over time I'll grow to enjoy New Leaf more. Right now it feels like work to play it. Kind of like a cartoony Sim City.

I still love the Gamecube version. I'd like to think that I'll grow to love New Leaf. I remember feeling excited and happy first playing the Gamecube version and I wonder why I don't feel that way about New Leaf.

From what I can recollect the band instantly fell into the standard L.A. black hole of one-album-success-and-a-lifetime-of-heroin-use. But I'm surprised to have to dig to find this album again, this truly is one of the best rock albums ever recorded.

title: They should call this Glit-Cha because it's so glitchy
text:
I'd give this half a star if I could. When it works, it's awesome, but this hardly ever works and there are two reasons why - the charger it comes with (and any others you can buy, really) is junk and it requires "outside knowledge" of how to update the puck so it works the way you want it to. I expected to take this out of the box, turn it on and Go! Nope, that most definitely isn't what happens with this little tool.

There were zero instructions in the box and their website is pretty much just a visual diagram of what the different screens mean with no real instructions either. It wasn't until I ran into someone else with one of these that I learned there is an app you have to download to update the firmware on the puck and change any settings (do you want it catching every monster? only new ones you don't have? do you want it to spin pokestops? do you want it to vibrate?). More often than not, the puck will randomly start doing what it wants to do which isn't always what you've set it to do so naturally, you'll pull out the cable (it has to be plugged in and charging) to update it, again, until you realize the puck isn't connecting to the app no matter what you do. The problem here is also twofold - is it the app or is it the charger? You don't know so you'll waste time deleting/reinstalling the app only to realize it's not the app but most likely the charger which brings me to the next design flaw...

The charging dongle is worthless. Even when you have it pushed all the way in, the puck often doesn't charge because it will slowly ease itself back out just enough to not make contact with the charger. If the puck isn't connected to the port well enough, it can't connect to your phone to do any updates with the app.

Before you say, "well, she just doesn't know what she's doing," you should know that all 4 of these that I ordered have been like this and everyone I've encountered that owns one has confirmed that theirs too are glitchy.

title: Best wireless gaming headset but I still prefer my wired sets
text:
I'm a musician and audio geek, have been collecting high end headphones, amps, etc for 20+ years and have been playing PC games even longer than that. For the past few years I have been using the Sennheiser Game One headset with the GSX 1200 Pro amplifier as my gaming setup. While the Game One doesn't sound quite as good as some of my other high end headphones, it sounds amazing considering the price and is super comfortable with an excellent mic for voice chat. I have used a number of other wireless headsets and never been that impressed with any of them but I was excited to see what Sennheiser came up with. A good friend of mine has the Bowers & Wilkins PX gaming headset which is probably the closest competitor to the GSP670 in terms of sound quality for a wireless headset (and also in a similar price range), so I will include some comparisons to that headset also.

First off, I think it is worth pointing out that all wireless headsets make some concessions compared to wired ones, so you may want to keep that in mind when considering whether a wireless headset is appropriate for you. All wireless headsets have a degree of latency, this GSP 670 seeks to reduce the latency using the 2.4GHz dongle connection instead of bluetooth and it is notably better than others but there is still some latency. It seems that the headsets prioritize incoming data over outbound data, so the latency is much more noticable when using voice chat but I also notice it while playing FPS games (for instance when playing McCree in overwatch or using the Deagle in CSGO, both have a very sharp sound that makes the latency more apparent). For this reason I would not recommend any wireless headset if you intend to use it as your main headset for competitive FPS gaming. If you aren't super competitive though and you are the type of player who doesn't spend time worrying about your refresh rate and other peripherals input latency then it probably won't bother you.

Aside from the latency issue, all wireless headsets are heavier and less comfortable than wired ones due to the included batteries. While this usually isn't an issue for shorter gaming sessions, it can cause fatigue and discomfort if using the headphones for an extended period. Lastly, all wireless headsets tend to have a compressed sound due to the wireless transmission protocol which is most notable in the low frequencies. The best wireless headsets (such as this one from Sennheiser and the aforementioned B&W PX) do a lot to mitigate these issues but they still can't match a good wired headset. For that reason, I feel that wireless gaming headsets are generally best suited for situations where you are going to be sitting a good distance from the screen, ie gaming from the couch or something. If you are just sitting at your desk in closed proximity to the PC then it doesn't really make sense to use a wireless headset in my opinion.

If you've considered the drawbacks and still think a wireless headset is the way to go, then I would definitely consider the GSP 670 as it has arguably the best sound quality of any wireless gaming headset I have tried (after firmware update and some EQ tweaking). It has better bass response and to my ears a more balanced soundstage than the B&W px. While the GSP 670 wins in terms of sound quality and battery life, the PX is in my opinion much better looking and more comfortable than the GSP670.

I normally wouldn't comment on the aesthetics of headphones since I'm usually not planning to wear my expensive headphones outside the house.. but for a gaming headset it is perhaps noteworthy since some people wear them when streaming. The GSP series are without a doubt some of the ugliest headphones I've ever seen, and the 670 are even uglier than the others in GSP series since they are slightly wider due to the internal electronics for wireless. Unless you have a ridiculously wide head these are going to look really silly on you. Its very confusing considering that almost all of sennheisers other products have a very sleek and refined appearance, including the older Game One/Game Zero series. While I do prefer the sound of the GSP 670, I would feel like a fool wearing them on an airplane despite their good noise isolation, whereas the B&W px are much more travel friendly (and have better active noise cancellation).

So if I were in the market for a wireless gaming headset it would be a tough call.. the GSP 670 is slightly ahead in terms of sound quality, battery life, latency and mic quality but the B&W PX has better active noise cancellation, more portable, lighter and more comfortable and has a much more stylish and refined look. Personally I would probably go with the 670 since sound quality is most important to me but again it would be a tough call and I don't think you can really go wrong with either of them.. both are much better than the average wireless headsets on the market.

title: An excellent expansion in an awesome world. Naughtydog never disappoints
text:
Naughtydog literally never disappoints me. I have had game development companies run strong for a decade and all of a sudden change the quality of content they put out--that has not been the case with Naughtydog, and continues to not be the case. This standalone Uncharted 4 expansion is really great and expands on two characters in a meaningful and interesting way. It is sad not having Nathan Drake around but it does not detract from the game whatsoever. Uncharted: The Lost Legacy brings back all of the fun of Uncharted 4 with great puzzles, fun combat/stealth mechanics, and as always, crisp, fine-tuned tech that delivers great cinematic scenes and gameplay.

This expansion will deliver approximately 8 hours of gameplay compared to Uncharted 4's 15 hours--which is a good amount of content considering the lower price of this expansion. I really like the idea of re-using core tech and making optimizations over multiple expansions. This allows more content to be made without swamping the developer with more work. This also allows for tech optimizations that may help development projects farther down the development pipeline(The Last of Us 2 anyone?) while keeping customers entertained and enjoying the characters that naughtydog has taken the time to build.

Character development and storytelling is what Naughtydog does best and that is illustrated again in Uncharted: The Lost Legacy. Playing these games is like taking part in a movie and that is something that Naughtydog has been able to execute in their recent games over and over. Another benefit I found from purchasing this game on Amazon is that it included a digital copy of Jak and Daxter: Precursor Legacy. Crash Bandicoot and Jak and Daxter are the games that got me into Naughtydog in the first place. Being able to go back to my early Playstation days has been a treat and is just icing on the cake. If you are a fan of Naughtydog games you will enjoy this game. It is an expansion but it feels like its own game in a way. As an Uncharted story fan, its enjoyable getting to learn more about the other characters. I cannot recommend this game enough.

Dimensions of the box and the contents can be seen in the photos I have uploaded.

Included:
Standalone Blu-Ray and case for Uncharted: The Lost Legacy
Digital code for Digital download of Jak and Daxter: Precursor Legacy

Pros:
*Crisp tech that delivers awesome gameplay and graphical fidelity
*Great storytelling and character development
*Centered on a new main character and still maintained my interest
*A fair price for the content offered

Cons:
*None

Additional Considerations:
Buy any Naughtydog game. You wont be disappointed as a gamer. I'm definitely more into Uncharted and The Last of Us, but even Jak and Daxter and Crash Bandicoot are fun games to me.

Overall: 5/5 stars (>=.5 rounds up, <.5 rounds down) => 5 stars

title: A very sharp looking console to play a very sharp looking game! Could not ask for more!
text:
This is one sharp looking console. This is the newer model and slightly thinner PS4 and the artwork is very well done and looks great. The game included is a physical copy, case and all. My copy did not have a game manual inside of the box--however I believe that is the norm these days. The quick start manual was actually very useful and setup time was under ten minutes.

The set comes with everything you need to get up and running immediately:
*Uncharted themed console
*Blue/grey controller
*HDMI cable ( ~8ft - Not gold plated)
*Power adapter cable (~5ft)
*USB controller cable (~5ft)
*Mic/headset that plugs into controller (~4ft)
*PS4 manual
*Quickstart guide for setting up the console
*Sealed copy of Uncharted 4

Pros:
*Great looking console.
*Came with everything needed to get going out of the box.
*Physical copy of uncharted 4

Cons:
None

Other Considerations:
If you want the PS4 hardwired to the internet you will need to provide your own cat 5e or cat 6 cable. This set--understandably--does not come with one. If you do not have a cable you can connect to a network via the wireless NIC inside of the PS4. If you have Wireless N or AC it should be pretty comparable to being wired. The great benefit to being hardwired is slightly better latency(especially in wireless congested areas) and easier--really zero--setup time.
Another thing to consider is the fact that this package does NOT contain a vertical stand. If you want one it has to be purchased separately.

title: A design flaw of the keyboard is a huge problem
text:
I am making these comments as a non-gamer. It may be that this keyboard is made specifically for gamers and not meant to be used by anyone else. However, I have owned for some time another brand of gamer keyboard that I use regularly, and it doesn’t have the design flaw that this keyboard does.

Pros

1. It's appearance is attractive, especially the fact that it lights up in blue when plugged in.

2. This keyboard comes with a mouse, and the mouse is also very attractive. It lights up in blue and red when plugged in.

3. This keyboard is both full size and compact in design.

4. The price is reasonable.

Cons

1. A design flaw of the keyboard is a huge problem! I have been typing on a computer keyboard for 40 years. And on every keyboard I have ever used, the Enter key is one key to the right of the Single-Quote/Double-Quotes (“Quote”) key. When you want to press the Enter key, you simply lift up your right pinky finger and move it over one key. Inexplicably, this keyboard includes an extra key between the Quote key and the Enter key! I cannot state strongly enough how enormous a negative this is. There may be some reason for gamers to have a keyboard designed this way, but the keyboard is useless for everyone else. It is simply unusable to me. As a touch typist, the first time I used it, I reached my finger to hit the Enter key and was shocked when nothing happened. I wasn't looking at the keyboard, and for several additional, frustrated taps, I tried again and again to engage what I naturally assumed was the Enter key. Then I looked at the keyboard, and I couldn't believe my eyes. I was hitting an alien key between the Quote key and the Enter key.

Why would anyone design a keyboard this way? If I tried to train myself to use this keyboard, I would quickly develop repetitive stress injury. It is much too far for my pinky to comfortably stretch to reach the Enter key.

Again, this keyboard may be designed specifically by gamers for gamers. But if you are not a gamer and just are looking for a glow-in-the-dark keyboard for a reasonable price, I highly recommend that you look elsewhere.

title: Deep as a puddle with no real soul
text:
This game is VERY thin and repetitive with little to no soul. The entire game boils down to basically this:

1. Go into a new very linear sand-themed cave that's basically identical to the previous very linear sand-themed cave
2. Fight a handful of super easy enemies that go down in a couple swings
3. "Solve puzzles" - I mean, juggle your team configuration back at town so you have the guy with the ability you need to open this or that lock
4. Find the new guy inside the cave that you were told to find and talk to him for some really generic "thanks for finding me, let's go home" kind of dialog
5. Return to your oasis/town, micromanage a few "shops" that you can't buy from - this part especially feels like a huge amount of wasted potential
6. Maybe "craft" something if you've gotten far enough in the story to have the guaranteed drop item that makes it (why not just drop a weapon instead?)
7. Repeat

This game loop isn't inherently bad for a few repetitions, and I'll say it did manage to hook me for a couple hours. title: Goodbye Rift CV1 -  The S is the S#@!
text:
Let me start by saying, I've had every Oculus under the sun. From the various developer versions, to the Rift Consumer. Days before this review, I actually had the Quest! I was so excited, but in the end, I returned it for the Oculus S. Read on:

First off, I found the Quest to be way too uncomfortable.. The all in one tech, means it has more hardware packed into the front than you PC powered headset, making it front heavy. I've read every suggestion and watched every video on how best to make it wearable, but nothing worked. I figured, OK, it's a trade off - I have no cords attached, isn't that alone amazing? Well, turns out, not really. See, I started going on a "Quest" to compare games between my ol' Rift and the new kid on the block; I tried Rec Room first. The frame rate on the Quest seemed good enough, but wait, why are the signs on the walls a bit blurry, and their edges, jagged? Maybe it was always like that but I never noticed? I walked up closely, and now they were super sharp. So now I'm looking at the play panel and notice, not every adventure is available yet (they will be coming though). OK, I switch to my Rift, and load my Rec Room from the lovely Oculus Home (something the Quest doesn't have). First thing I noticed, the colors weren't as vibrant as on Quest, and yeah, there's that screen door effect which is more noticable. But hold on! All those same signs, from the same distance are not blurry or jagged? I realized, that's how they compensated on the Quest as it's not as powerful as a high end PC.

Now I switch to Robo Recall. On the Quest, it looks really good, but now what's this? Something doesn't feel right. The shooting just feels a bit off. The frame rate seems to struggle at certain points. I switch back to the Rift version, and now things are how I remembered - super fast and every action you pull off is instantaneous. Next up VR Chat. The Quest version looks good - the frame rate is not a problem. Someone informs me that not every avatar will show up on the Quest due to the hardware limitation. At this point, I've beginning to have second thoughts. I was planning to sell off my Rift and just stay Quest, but I feel the link cable may not be the answer, at least for me. I don't want any shortcomings, and I want my entire Steam Library to work as well as my Oculus Store games. My battery is beginning to get low... and so is my enthusiasm.

This is what made me decide on switching it out for an Oculus S. My laptop is a powerhouse, and it has a mini displayport, so I was set. Hook up was super simple. The S was instantly recognized, and my Oculus Home loaded up with all my previous purchases. The Screen... killer! Much sharper than the Rift. but the black level is not as black as the Quest (another beautiful screen), as the Quest uses OLED. I went back to the Rift, still plugged into my desktop computer. It seemed so washed out and almost blurry compared to the Rift S.

As for Rift S sound, it exactly like the Quest...firing out of the headband, and like zero bass. Good not terrible. The Rift's built in awesome headset will be missed. Still, I can always plug in my own, even better than old Rift headphones. Problem solved. As for comfortability.... perfect! Oh my goodness, it actually beats out the original Rift which I always considered the most comfortable (I also had the original Vive which was a head's worst enemy). The S uses the "Halo" system, similar to Playstation VR, but even more comfortable.

Yeah, I have one long cord attached to my headset, but I don't mind. If I kept the Quest and went for the link cable, I'll be back to where I started anyway. No sensors taking up space, and awesome full room+ scale. So now, I have all my Oculus Store games, along with my Steam VR purchases, without any sacrifices, limits or coming soons. I finally can put the original Rift up for sale. I'm super satisfied and quite blown away.

A final note: If your PC is now powerful enough, than the Quest is a no-brainer. It's an amazing accomplishment. If it's your first VR, and not coming from a high end PC experience to compare, you'll love it. If you have a high end gaming PC, then I would totally go for the Rift S, as you will get the whole nine yards, without compromise.

title: Ridiculously-Amazing
text:
(Purchased the Plush Edition which is why it's not showing as a Verified Purchase)

Sumo Digital has taken Media Molecule's masterpiece to a whole new level. Right from the start, you can see how much brilliance they've added to this game. The challenging campaign is simply off the charts this time around, with so much going on, in every delicious layer. Trust me when I say, if you're a fan of the series your jaw will be on the floor the entire time. The new, crazy weapons, inventory-style system and quest objective list really transforms this into an grand scale adventure. Forget just platforming, wait until you see how many RPGS the community comes up with this time! Not to mention, a whole new array of shooters, puzzle, pinball, sports, and other games which will exceed anything created with the previous version (and those were superb!).
Check out the campaign maps which will remind you of moving from level to level in a Mario World game. I also love the fact that the game is backward compatible with just about everything, including your already owned costumes and adventure packs.

The music .. seriously the best ever in the series. LBP 1 and 2 had their share of awesome tunes, but LBP 3 is a continuous treat to the ears. One level sports a brilliant Rock & Roll setting, which features licensed 50's-style music. I couldn't believe I was hearing "Mr. Sandman" while bouncing off walls (I'm old lol), and "I only have eyes for you" while drifting in and out of space. Oh, and don't even let me get started with Ziggurat, a Russian-themed level with an incredibly-kicking symphony (just found out it won awards). You will be blown away both visually and audibly.

Between the new characters, top down view, 16 layer depth and a monster load of new tools and other features (you'd need a book the size of War and Peace to list), you're going to be exploring and playing for a long time to come.

One of the main draws to the Little Big Planet series is collecting as many of the tools, stickers, costumes, goodies, etc.. as you can find along your journey. There are gamers who just want to play, and not get involved with the building aspect. They'll race through all main story levels either solo or co-op, however, this will cut down their time spent to complete the campaign. Luckily, they have thousands of community levels plus a number of official expansion packs to explore. If you're the creative type, and plan to build something of your own, you'll want to hit everywhere, including all the side games/missions. This will certainly make for one long, rewarding campaign. I've been playing for 10 hours and I'm just about to find the second new character. The joke of it is, I haven't even touched the community levels yet, which I expect to be mind boggling.

Almost forgot to mention (thank you edit) -- just like the former LBP's, there are numerous tutorial levels which introduce you to the main building tools/features, however, now it's called the "Popit Academy". This hybrid tutorial adventure combines learning how to use the tools while playing through a good number of brilliant levels. You see, there's lots of fun to be had beyond the campaign! You'll want to stick with it as you'll earn lots of valuable items to fill that goodie bag. Early tutorial levels may set off a bit of restlessness with those well trained in the land of LBP , but nevertheless, they'll be hooked. Not to mention, vets can also skip the academy and head to the database of tutorials to watch instructional videos for the newer and advanced features.

There are definitely a few quirks (as there are with most launch titles) that will surely be sewn up with patches (no pun). As I type this review, Sony has been doing a lot of behind the scenes maintenance as well.

LBP2 was the only game I continuously played on my PS3, long after other games developed cobwebs, and LBP3 is the main reason I purchased my PS4! You guys/gals at Sumo Digital are magicians! Oh, by the way, wait until you unleash "Oddsock".....

bouncing off walls (i'm old lol), and "i only have eyes for you" while drifting in and out of space. oh, and do not even let me get started with ziggurat, a russian-themed level with an incredibly-kicking symphony (just found out it won awards). you will be blown away both visually and audibly. between the new characters, top down view, 16 layer depth and a monster load of new tools and other features (you'd need a book the size of war and peace to list), you're going to be exploring and playing for a long time to come. one of the main draws to the little big planet series is collecting as many of the tools, stickers, costumes, goodies, etc.. as you can find along your journey. there are gamers who just want to play, and not get involved with the building aspect. they'll race through all main story levels either solo or co-op, however, this will cut down their time spent to complete the campaign. luckily, they have thousands of community levels plus a number of official expansion packs to explore. if you're the creative type, and plan to build something of your own, you'll want to hit everywhere, including all the side games/missions. this will certainly make for one long, rewarding campaign. i've been playing for 10 hours and i'm just about to find the second new character. the joke of it is, i have not even touched the community levels yet, which i expect to be mind boggling. almost forgot to mention (thank you edit) -- just like the former lbp's, there are numerous tutorial levels which introduce you to the main building tools/features, however, now it's called the "popit academy". this hybrid tutorial adventure combines learning how to use the tools while playing through a good number of brilliant levels. you see, there's lots of fun to be had beyond the campaign! you'll want to stick with it as you'll earn lots of valuable items to fill that goodie bag. early tutorial levels may set off a bit of restlessness with those well trained in the land of lbp , but nevertheless, they'll be hooked. not to mention, vets can also skip the academy and head to the database of tutorials to watch instructional videos for the newer and advanced features. there are definitely a few quirks (as there are with most launch titles) that will surely be sewn up with patches (no pun). as i type this review, sony has been doing a lot of behind the scenes maintenance as well. lbp2 was the only game i continuously played on my ps3, long after other games developed cobwebs, and lbp3 is the main reason i purchased my ps4! you guys/gals at sumo digital are magicians! oh, by the way, wait until you unleash "oddsock".....

title: A Smashing Good Time for All Ages
text:
Just finished off the 2.0 Avengers campaign. I have to say, it was a total blast from start to finish (no pun intended). The character sculpts are wonderful, and in game, Iron Man and Thor are the two you're going to play with the most. The Black Widow is fast with hand to hand combat, but she just doesn't have the same impact as the other two heroes. I must admit, however, building up her skill levels results in some very cool dual handed bullet bursts. This makes her one deadly force in the Power Disc game, Escape from Klyn. In the main adventure, Black Widow's disadvantage is that she can't fly, so getting around New York City at decent pace requires a vehicle. Oh, they're readily available right from the start, but it kills the high energy flow when having to make pit stops to summon fast transportation. With Iron Man and Thor, you press a button, you levitate and another button sends you soaring at heart pumping speeds - - no wheels required. I can't comment on the other characters, as I haven't opened anything additional, but I'm getting ready to dive into Guardians of the Galaxy.

Yes, there are TONS of enemy frost creatures on the Loki side of the fence, so get use to fighting the same type of icy cold enemy over and over (with variations in their sizes and abilities). Also, like the 1.0 edition, missions can feel repetitive at times. This may bother some, but between the number of awesome moves, and the very welcomed Skill Tree, every fight felt like grand scale mayhem The insane abilities and special moves of your Super Hero are a sight to behold. Even the interaction with the surroundings is so well done. I also found the missions to be less frustrating then some of drawn out ones from 1.0 (except for Pirates which was my fav from that set).

There is so much to do with the starter set, that you really feel like you're getting your money's worth. You have the main campaign, plus the two power discs, each containing their own full game. These power disc-based games are of much smaller scale when compared to the main adventure, but believe me, both games are beefy enough to stand on their own. Interestingly enough, it appears there are two more games (as the menu shows) ready for when Brave and Stitch are released. Plus you have the official playsets that are sold separately ( Guardians of the Galaxy and Ultimate Superman).

Then of course, all roads lead to the beloved Toy Box where you can do just about anything. Avalanche studios packed in an insane amount of new toys, gadgets, interiors (now you can build indoors), landscapes, skyboxes and more. If you don't feel like you have the skills or time to build your own game, then download one of many offerings from the community. One of the best changes to the new 2.0 system is the way you obtain new objects from the Toy Box. Gone is that annoying, random "Wheel of Misfortune" style toy dispenser where you had to rely on luck to get the item you needed; now you simply purchase items with blue sparks which are easily earned throughout your adventures. No more spending your life backtracking through a completed game to try to find toys you may have missed. Not all items are readily available, but as you make a purchase, more goodies are unlocked through a branching system.

There are a number of other areas I didn't cover (hall of heroes / Super heroes, survival mode, the game-like tutorial, etc..), but overall, I say if you're a Marvel SH fan, this is the game you want. In fact, this makes the best use of the franchise yet! You may find yourself addicted enough to start collecting all the characters, even the 1.0 cast, who work perfectly in the 2.0 ToyBox (they too have stats now!). And in closing, I'm of many fans who have a feeling that the next in the series will be Star wars (2015). Talk about a new hope!

title: + for Xbox One and Amazon & Microsoft
text:
I purchased this from an eBay member who secured a Day One Edition, which is why my review doesn't show as an Amazon verified purchase. The original buyer purchased it from Amazon back in June and had it delivered to me when I did a "Buy it Now" from Ebay. Well, it turns out, I was one of the unlucky ones with the infamous, faulty grinding drive; no games would load.I spent the first half of the evening mastering the voice commands, checking out game highlight uploads from the community, setting up the TV integration, and firing up a little Killer Instinct. Who knew, later in the evening this excitement would all come crashing down, when I tried to load up RYSE, only to discover my unit's disc player sounded like a paper shredder.

I didn't want to deal with Microsoft and its complications to send back, so I simply looked up the order number that the original buyer provided me with and thankfully I was able to return it to Amazon as a gift (since i wasn't the original purchaser). Amazon is shooting out a replacement immediately. THE BAD NEWS: It's going to be the "Standard" version, after paying a pretty penny (above list) for the Day One Edition. The reason why I'm not giving this a one star review (as angry as I am) is because the console is too amazing not to get the stars it deserves. I also have the PS4 and I have to say, I like them equally for different reasons. I will say,the Xbox One does feel a bit more next gen thanks to the TV integration and the new Kinect, which makes the old one seem like a disposable camera from the 90's.

Once you tweak the settings and spend a few hours learning the way of the console, you will have it at your demand using a pretty extensive library of voice commands. Yes, sometimes, I had to repeat myself, but for the most part, it works surprisingly well. As for gaming, there's not much I can do with a broken disc reader, but I'm already loving Killer Instinct with its insane, larger than life characters and sick amount of detail. It seems like the Xbox One can blast around graphics without breaking a sweat. The demo for Kinect Sports Rivas (the jet ski racing) looks like Wave Race on steroids with its gorgeous, vibrant visuals, and the level of control through the new Kinect is pretty impressive. I think having the new, advanced Kinect being standard will finally push motion control out of gimmickville and into welcomed arms. Oh, and dig into your apps and install this hidden gem called "Xbox Fitness". Gold members will be in for a big surprise with this compilation of free work out programs that go as far reading your heartbeat. There's some pretty extensive workouts here which read your body sort of Dance Central-style, and even includes achievements among other great features. I'm surprised Microsoft didn't emphasize this great set of extras. Overall, I'm very excited about the future of this console (and the PS4).

UPDATE: Got my replacement unit super fast (love love love you Amazon) and Microsoft is giving away a free XBOne game to all those who had a defective unit. Thank you for handling the situation very well, Microsoft.

UPDATE: As for the big name titles, so far, I've only played Ryse: Son of Rome and my jaw has dropped below sea level. I've never seen such amazing character models in my life. This is no FMV nonsesne either! I love the extensive fighting techniques and stats tree that can be increased as you progress. The story is intriguing (not historical, though), and the acting is top notch. Despite the mediocre reviews, I am SO SO glad I generally never listen to game journalists. I am enjoying this game immensely, and I love the way it ties in with SmartGlass support on my iPad. I've yet to play Dead Rising 3 and Forza - those are up next....

title: If you own one, you'll know......
text:
As a gamer for many years (since the Atari 2600), I've experienced just about every form of entertainment technology, including today's high end tablets. A few months back, I was not even thinking about getting a Wii U. I saw the Gamepad and TV combination and thought, so what's the big deal about playing a game on the big screen, and having its map and inventory in your hand? And if you already have a tablet, then why bother playing Wii U games on the supplied Gamepad? Well, when you have one at home, it's a W H O L E different ball game.

When you first get the unit, you do have to be patient as the system updates to the latest OS. This process can take a few hours as the file is large. No one told you to sit there and look at the screen, yet Nintendo came under fire from the media because consumers actually had to wait an extra few hours before they can start playing? Imagine that? How dare they update the system to add new features? Grant it, those should have been included before the release, but this happens with various forms of tech these days, just not a long! If you're a parent setting this up for your kid(s), I would suggest doing it while they're asleep, unless they are one of those rare, patient gems (if so, pat yourself on the back).

The battery life on the GamePad is short - like three or four hours. I keep my charger cable nearby so I can still play while the pad is plugged in and charging , or periodically drop it on the cradle for a quick recharge while I take a break; It's really no hassle at all! It's not like you're taking it outside anyway. I have the screen brightness cranked at max which is visually pretty impressive by the way. It's no "Retina" display like an iPad, but it's still very sharp and a lot better than I expected!

MiiVerse is amazing - like a huge on-line community which is tied into every form of media on the Wiiu. Play a game, press a button, and switch to Miiverse to comment on it, or ask for tips! Then, jump right back to your game! Watch a YouTube video, and swap to Miiverse and you're in the YouTube discussion area. People can leave straight text messages, or use their stylus to hand write or DRAW a note; a lot of the sketch drawings submitted by users are amazing! MiiVerse alone is a very involving atmosphere that will keep you quite busy even without playing games. Sony's been trying to improve their similar social community known as "Home" for years, as for quite some time, it was not well received, yet, Nintendo's MiiVerse hits it out of the park at launch. The Browser for the WiiU is by far the best of the game console browsers - it's lightning fast, and works brilliantly to utilize both TV and GamePad. In addition, the GamePad can double as a TV/Cable Box remote which is ridiculously-easy to set up. Come December, Wii U owners will be able to download TVii which will turn your Wii U GamePad into an excellent TV companion, with visual programming guide displayed on the GamePad, including access to DVR controls.

I've only played three games so far: NintendoLand, ZombiU and an Nano Assault Neo. NintendoLand is packed with mini games for solo and group play. I'm not going to go into details, but there are so many layers of things to discover, that it reminds me of the original Nintendo days! When you begin to play NintendoLand and see how the various games interact with the GamePad, you can't help but getting that technology RUSH! Where you suddenly realize how brilliant this system is and begin to imagine what's in store! At that point, you're already looking for which game to buy next. You'll want to see what other games are like and how they work out with the GamePad. Most games can even be played directly on the GamePad, so if someone wants to use the TV, a quick finger touch switches the game to the small screen; All intact, full speed ahead! You've heard of console quality gaming on a small screen - well, this is LITERAL! I love how both displays can act independently, or show off the same information which you can flip between. The Gamepad even has surround sound and a headphone jack!

ZombiU is no doubt one of the scariest games you will ever experience. The atmosphere is so daunting, you'll be horrified to take the next step. The GamePad becomes your survival kit, with inventory manipulation, mapping via surveillance cameras a 360 degree, Augmented Reality-style scanner, and even voice navigation. There's a ton of functions UbiSoft intelligently incorporated into the GamePad. Trust me, you play one evening of this and you'll know you're in a different league then the 360 and PS3. I own both units, and I still adore them, but already, Wii U takes the top spot for me.

Nano Assault Neo the WiiU's answer to the PS3's lovely Super Stardust HD. Nano's environments are amazingly-detailed, as you blast away the enemies in this twin stick delight. The Wii U's GamePad becomes a live map showing the baddies swarming around, as well as locations of the game's currency to purchase upgrades. The acquired drones can be positioned and rotated for angle of fire right from your GamePad. It's polished, arcade goodness backed by a fantastic techno soundtrack. This was the first game I downloaded in the E-Shop. Next I'm going for Trine 2!

There is SO much more to elaborate on, as the WiiU has many other features to cover. After a few nights or learning the system, I've becomes more and more anxious to get home and play! I've come to realize, all the negativity that is getting spewed are from people who simply don't own the machine. These are haters of anything that they don't own themselves, plain and simple. Then there's the irresponsible journalists, who will induce head scratching as you wonder how they got their job. Many who have this need to fuel their articles with controversial quotes or useless top 10 ten this or 10 worst that ; they seem to get off finding even the most minute issues. Sure there are a few kinks for Nintendo to iron out, but it's only been out just over a week (as of this review). Remember when the 360 and PS3 launched? BOTH systems had haters and whiners, along with visions of doom and gloom. Heck, the 360 even survived one of the highest defective rates (Red Ring of Death anyone?), and still came out on top after a number of years.

Overall, I'm incredibly impressed and can't wait to see what the most creative developers do with the GamePad / TV combo. Plus, based on recent reports, this could be the Indi Game developers platform of choice which is a win-win situation!

title: My Kinect has Blood on its Sensor!
text:
One Step Forward..

I have to agree with the higher critic scores on this one. Let me start by saying, this is a Kinect game like no other. The story is cliche, with over the top acting, but that never stopped the Resident Evil series from being loved to death. Besides, what's a campy horror flick without bad acting? Maybe we should inform some "professional reviewers" that this isn't Hamlet: The game.

Gross Fest Dead Ahead

The graphics are dark and foreboding, like they should be --- with shades of browns, rusts, gold and a ton of blood red; actually, make that a more than a ton. Rise of Nightmares seems like part Saw, part House on Haunted Hill(the awful remake) and a "rail-less" House of the Dead. There's even a creepy sprinkling of Silent Hill here and there, but don't expect any type of complex adventure which sets that series apart. The sounds are disturbing, with moans, groans, screams of torture, footsteps, clangs, electric shocks and much more, backed by a wonderfully eerie music selection.
The gore in RON is generally over the top, though there are a few scenes which I found disturbing, and as for being scary? Well, at moments it actually can be! Go ahead, play it at night on a big screen with the lights out; raise the volume and make sure you don't have on dark clothes so the sensor can find you in the darkness. Now, don't tell me you won't feel tense as you turn each corner. Not to mention, the game does have few jump scenes which were gladly welcomed. Perhaps those complaining about it not being scary should try not playing it with the sun shining into their room or at a dorm party with six drunk dudes.

Self Control

The controls seem to be an issue for some reviewers, yet according to the real audience, they're working out fine. Now and then, I had a bit of trouble backing up or turning - but for the most part, I've been plowing through this horror ride, kicking all sorts of zombie flat butt without a problem. If you're really stuck, you can use the auto icon by raising your right hand, allowing the game to walk for you. It won't help with encounters, but it aids in getting out of weird spots or when you're feeling disoriented. Your arm will tire quickly, which I feel is a good thing, otherwise, you'd be using it throughout the whole game..and come on, that's no fun! The game uses check points, which sometimes can be a hassle when you've just made it past the wall to wall buzz saws, or a unhealthy large party of the undead; luckily, most check points are not painfully spaced. As for saving the game as in, I've had enough for tonight, well, that's done at the end of each chapter, so be sure to complete an entire chapter before hitting the eject.

I'll trade you - my pocket knife for your machete.

There are lots of weapons to find which is part of the fun, especially when the more devastating weapons come in to play. When you find something like an ice tong or chainsaw, you can't help thinking - oh man, they are SO dead now...well, dead for good this time. Think about this... instead of pressing a button the conventional way, you mimic the motions of actually holding one of these babies. Trust me, it's very satisfying, but you didn't read that here. Sadly, weapons wear down with use, so you've got to find a new one soon or you'll be fighting with your hands and feet. Speaking of feet, I love how the Kinect senses your foot as you kick a zombie down while preparing to slice and dice. It also gives you a second to breath while other zombies are lunging at you.

Yeah, So?

Overall, I'm loving Rise of Nightmares, though admittedly, I'm more of a fan of subtle creepiness over gore. Sega's mature rated release is easily the most interactive on the Kinect yet, utilizing a host of clever, immersive gestures that help keep the game from feeling repetitive. Rise of Nightmares is what Kinect is all about, and hopefully, will pave the way to even grander scale games which will utilize this device in more innovative ways. Bravo for taking the risk, Sega!

title: Game of the YEAR(S)!
text:
I'm an adult..lets just say..well over 40, and I've seen and experienced just about everything in the computer and video game world. Of all my years of electronic playing, only two games kept my attention for years (no not days, months..years!): The RollerCoaster Tycoon series on the PC and Little Big Planet on PS3. Perhaps because I love anything which lets you use your creative skills and doesn't end via three day completion or quarter of the way boredom.

Little Big Planet 2 goes so way beyond the original to the point that, I don't think I ever want to play anything else - ever (well at least until part 3 is released lol). There is so much to do that you get your money's worth in a way that no other game can provide. It's a bit overwhelming at first: Do I play the brilliant Tutorials and collect all the goods? Should I explore the millions of Community Levels, or do I begin playing the epic story devised by Media Molecule. Perhaps I should design my moon, or earth, or just queue up a bunch of recommended levels for later play. And after all is said and done, there's still the core part of the game: Create Mode!

There's no end to the types of games you can build with this insanely epic sequel. The original Little Big Planet, paved the way with games which later went beyond the general theme. The original tool set was obviously designed with side scrolling platforming in mind, but creative individuals thought out of the box, and created games that you'd never thought could be accomplished. It was quite obvious creators had to go way beyond the limits of the tool set to come with something, other than what the game was intended for. I'm sure every creator hit a wall at some point and thought.... "If only Media Molecule would have included..."

Well folks, they DID! Little Big Planet 2 has more tools than your hardware store. Plus tons of new objects, materials, stickers, special effects, and more. With the crazy new power ups, you conjure up unbelievable ideas. One major break through is definitely the "Controllernator" which actually lets you map commands to the entire PS3 control pad. This revelation lets you create games in just about ever genre. The rage has just begun, and already we're seeing sports games, RPGS, puzzle action, adventure, retro games, casual, casino, 3D shooters, even cinematic movies! Not to mention, games specifically designed for versus multi-player which are identified by a special icon. Let's put it this way - many of the new creations will have you thinking you're playing a completely different game. With over 3 million levels, there is no end to this spectacle. Every day you venture into Little Big Planet 2 is a new experience. So, go ahead, jump in and choose anything your heart desires, or build your own epic arcade adventure. Rest assured, you will not be leaving this planet any time soon.

title: Exceeded Expectations!
text:
When Sony first announced the Move controller, I'm sure everyone was scratching their head with questions like: Why bother, Nintendo already has this covered? What's with the glowing ball? Why the camera?

Forgot all you've learned with the Nintendo Wii. I have the utmost respect for Nintendo for getting the motion control ball rolling, and I enjoy the Wii system for what it is, however, the motion control on the Wii is not all it's cut out to be. I'm sure like many of you, when you first got the Wii at launch, thought the motion sensor would track your every move. You couldn't wait to bowl, box, or swing a sword, just like you would do in a real environment. The sad truth is, all of the wiimote's movement which "talk" to these games could easily be accomplished on your couch - even laying down. A simple flick of the wrist would translate to an on screen action. No need to stand up and bowl, why bother doing a full arm swing of your sword when it can be done without much effort on your part. In 2009, Nintendo released the Motion Plus add on for the Wii mote which certainly make it a lot more accurate, but not enough games support it just yet, and it still doesn't come close to what Sony has done.

So what makes Sony's PS3 Move such a big deal? Well, for one thing, we're dealing with true 1:1 motion control. That funky glowing ball that was the brunt of many jokes happens to be the key to tracking your every moment; this, in combination with the PlayStation Eye. Once you begin to play any of the Move's games, you immediately sense you are not dealing with anything like the Wii. Not only does it sense anywhere in view your hand is, but it also detects how close or far you are to the TV.

Sports Champions is amazing. The Table Tennis is so realistic, it's almost eerie. All the sports included are a blast to play (well, except for the Frisbee thing which I don't find interesting even in real life). Unlike WiiSports or Resort - you WILL work up a sweat because you will not get anywhere trying to sit in a reclining chair while the PS3 reminds you that your not in range. ;-)

The other two games I've checked out were the EyePet and Start the Party. Both games use live camera feed, so now the player is inside the game! Yes, true augmented reality here folks. Your pretty illuminated PlayStation Move Controller, suddenly becomes another object. Just look at the screen, you're now holding a Paint Brush, a tennis racket, or Ray gun! Folks, you have to see this to believe this. Yes, combining the player with the game's objects and its surroundings is another thing the Wii can't acheive.

Overall, I'm so blown away by the Move's accuracy, The starting line up of games isn't much yet, but there's something for everyone and any choice will put a smile on your face. Plus, Sony and other manufacturers are already releasing patches to incorporate Move control into existing games like Resident Evil 5 Gold Edition, Tiger Woods 11 and much more. Oh, and loving the demo of "The Shoot" - can't wait for October. The system is very easy to set up -- and calibration is easy and super fast.
