title: Emotional game with great storytelling !
text:
Well, it seems most people here covered the reviews on the game so I will keep things short. Visually, it's impressive. One of the best AAA games out there right now. The story in general once you start it will be impossible to let go of and not finish it. They covered all past games and Nate's adventure around the globe. They show a side of him that deals with everyday life for everyone. Showing his normal life now vs his global treks around the globe. It really makes you see how everyday you wake up like a robot and do the same over and over again and not even notice it. However you see things from his perspective. Anyways, I have not completed the game but currently working on it and in chapter 11 and was blown away by the chemistry all the voice actors have, I would say this surpasses Uncharted 2. The music goes with the flow of what is happening inside the game which really sucks you into the storytelling and action sequences. I have nothing negative to say on it.

Multiplayer I was impressed with. Everything in game can be bought or unlocked by using multiplayer points won in game. The only thing is the points unlock items randomly or paying for points to allows you to select them. All stages are free to avoid dividing the community.

The MP plays like a mix of The Last of Us and Uncharted 3. You can revive downed allies like TLOU however they have boosters that can be bought in game (gun upgrades, more bombs, helpers etc) I liked the fact that every time you buy an "upgrade" inside the game (RPGs, GUNS etc) they cost more the next time so it avoids being abused. They have a section that teaches you how to use the new items or moves (hooks, one hit kill charge, bombs , mines etc) standards Deathmatch and capture the flag type modes. They also have a section for ranked matches online instead of friendly. It still 'feels' like an uncharted game when playing online similar to UC2-3.

I loved The Last of Us but Uncharted has always been fast pace and I was afraid that they would slow down the online in UC4. This time Naughty Dog found a good mix between fast pace action with timing and semi planing similar to (TLOU) so that made me happy. This time the online is fun and feels challenging not just run and gun. The online is also stable (I have 100 down and 26 up) results of online stability varies case by case but even a friend who has 50 down and 6 up stated that it was very stable.

title: First thing I have to say, they are incredible.
text:
Don't hesitate on buying these. I wore mine out a week ago playing God of War 3 and I was originally planning on sending them to Sony for a replacement. The rubbers wear out on some Playstation 4 controllers that are first generation.

This was probably made that way so you could angle them in from any direction and then straighten them once on. They look nice and make the controller stand out. title: First time Dead or Alive player
text:
I never review something I haven't bought from Amazon, but was given this game as a gift and felt like writing a review.

Never played any of the DOAs on a Sony system till this one. This was my first entry into the series and a long time Tekken, SF and Soul Calibur fan.

Game plays great, models are bright and vivid, what caught my attention more was the interactive stages and how highly detailed they are as well as the deep combo system and move list. Similar to Tekken, yet has it's very own unique play style. I like the fact you have to do the correct input for everything to work rather than buffing moves. If you need to press forward, forward, kick, punch and back. It has to be done precisely. Tekken gave you slight leniency with the input commands, but not DOA. This is not a negative, its a plus. This means your opponent has to know the move commands rather than button smash. This forces anyone picking up a character to know the moves and generally force them to learn the game.

The stages at first I was under the impression were dull, until I learn how to smash someone into them. (interacting with them) setting them into motion. Collapsing building floor in mid fight that throws you off the side, barrels that light up setting the environment on fire, electrical ropes in a ring that set off lights and cheering all add to the atmosphere. Some when triggered, can hit a character into them setting off chain of events. In the tiger circus stage you can smash someone into a ring, which forces the tiger to jump thru a hoop hitting you.

They have: story mode, arcade mode, vs, tag battle (2 vs 2 swap mid fight) and 7 vs 7 team battle, online mode, training, combo masters, tutorial and spectator mode as well as movie mode and the ability to take and save pictures similar to a photomode on TLOU Remastered.

One of the things I enjoyed was the ability to play arcade mode, tag battle, or training and have the PS4 look for an online battle in the background as I played. Than just press and hold options to accept the invite. This can be turned on or off before you start the game. Nice way to unlock costumes and practice, while randomly getting an online challenger instead of going into online mode itself. In online mode, you can select a hosted game or play rank match. The online was stable, i'm running 60 down and 12 up and only had a few minor lagged matches. This should be eliminated if you set preferences online.

Each character has their own tutorial and combo tutorial. This makes it easy for you to try new characters out and not get stuck to one.

As for the tons of DLC in the PSN store. This is optional clothing. Much better off buying the full game itself, and its cheaper. You have to unlock the clothing by playing, instead of paying to have them unlocked or buying characters. There are some outfits not in the disk, but the majority are unlocks from the disk, characters etc. The core mode on the PSN is only for people that are curious about DOA but would rather not invest in the full game. Each character runs $3.99 and 4 given free out of 32 playable. (as you see much better buying the disk). The disk or full game download also includes trophies, which I read buying core mode and purchasing things seperate doesn't.

Characters models are well done, as for the added "breast physics" they have an optional "natural mode" which is a next gen only add-on using the soft engine, "DOA" and "LR" which is exaggerated motion. DOA and LR mode allow you to shake the controller to have the boobs bounce or sway. (depending the direction you shake or move the control). They also included an off mode. In my opinion, turning them off the female characters look like plastic dolls. As for the visual upgrades, characters and backgrounds have a solid look to them, no flickering or random item disappearing as you walk around.

Negative: The only negative I could find is the lackluster story mode. They basically did a story mode similar to Injustice Gods among us that linked characters into one big match threw out the story. You play as everyone, but for people like myself with no past history of previous games its hard to connect the non obvious things. As you play each character they give a few sentences of what's going on or who they are. The story mode is entertaining, because it gives a glimpse on what's going on, just not mind blowing.

Beyond that it's still a good game and the fighting system is well done. Easy for a beginner, but has an intricate fighting system for pro.

WARNING: For people using Shareplay, Koei blocked unlocked movies, and the movies in story mode as you play. You can shareplay with a friend, even play vs mode using shareplay co-op couch mode, but they only allowed you to select a few stages and not all of them or the 2ndary stages. If you plan on letting a friend watch you play story mode, (as I did over the weekend) it blocks the movie for the person you share played with. Letting them only see the fights in story mode. All other modes he can access even if you hand the controller over: (Tag, vs, tutorial etc)

I was going to list this as a negative, but it's hardly a negative since the story mode in DOA 5 Last round was not phenomenal, just okay. Hopefully they patch this, but I am having a great time playing it. You mostly buy it for the fighting system and online or offline matches.

title: Excellent game
text:
I will warn you that I never played any of the old Thief titles so my opinion is from a "new series" point of view.

Games good. IF your into that style of games (Stealth). Not sure if you played any of the old ones but it was considered one of the games that created that style of game play back in the day tied into stealth.

Its not the same as dishonored, but they are completely different. Dishonored even on hardest setting was easy. Here, they emphasis stealth. Higher levels hard modes the ability to kill and move list drops further and further or not allowed. Example, Knockouts allowed but no kills. Not be seen, but kills allowed etc..

There is no free movement by the way (GTA V style) and exploring is pretty much centered on picking gold, items and loot from people or in closets, safes etc. 1 section may have doors to pick or windows to break in. The game is divided into sections, for example town A, B and C each require a load like old school games. Some may be thrown off by this because loads are pretty long. (not bad, just noticeable) Stages are decently huge. But what makes them feel long is the stealth tied to the game. You cant just free run everything. The guards are murder bots basically. The moment they hear or see you instantly turn murderous and track you.

You can run and hide till they lose interest but the pattern on how they walk changes afterwards. Some stages have regular people walking by, who you can steal from behind. Its a quick time event.. But if they notice you and yell robber. (alerting the guards and you get the idea). In terms of openness: they do allow you to climb over crates, up walls if it has the correct marking for wall run and over ledges as long as it looks like it supports a real human could use. (everything). If you see a few crates that a normal human could crawl up on , you probably can too and not limited to the blue scratches on walls. This also extends to rooftops.

You can also do typical things like pick up glass and throw it to make a noise and alert others to that area to change the pattern or let you creep behind them. For example, I had to steal a mask. First time I did this was waiting for the guards to change patrols, as they walked to the left and right side, I went in and picked the lock (quickly) getting in. They have a lock pick ability, than you hit a button to lock it and move to the next set of springs to open the door. A misses lock pic will make a sound. The 2nd time I just alerted the guys to all go in one side to get in, 3rd time I noticed the back room was open and snuck in the back-way. I have also heard there was a wall opening too. Being inside a house with people, can last about 30 minutes with no load. Mostly because they are walking back and forth OR sitting and you cant just walk around making noise. There is a "light" meter that shows your level of invisibility to someones eye. Pure black 100% hidden. You can walk slowly and not be seen. In a room that I blew out all 6 candles. The guy didn't notice me so he walked back and forth making something with only his candle on two desks lit. (I robbed him from behind twice and stole things around him. Than ran off.) In another save, I alerted him that he knew someone was inside but all candles were off. While he walked back and forth in the room trying to find you. Even than, you are so hidden that you could steal a purse from his back two times in pure darkness as long as he doesn't face you, you are hidden. If the light meter reads "dark" you are practically 100% hidden especially with crouch.You also have to be aware of how much noise you make too.

Story so far is typical but matches with the settings. Since I am in master mode,its slightly harder. Every difficulty has set rules and one that uses a custom hard setting. You basically pick locks, various safe boxes and that type of stuff like gold from the ground or peoples hidden money. You also have to be rapid and careful because you can trigger warnings. The reason I mentioned dishonored, is because some have said its more fun. Dishonored was based off Thief,(I have heard) but had other elements and was easy. But like I said everyone has an opinion. Thief has a higher difficulty curve even on easy. I am familiar with how Thief plays.. Obviously graphics are good in 1080p. (PS4 at least) Everything you have to buy upgrades like you focus ability, sweep, and in general these things called poppy seeds that enhance vision, see items on the ground from far away etc. Its very slowly pace and careful. No run and gun sections type of things.. At the most run and hide. You can upgrade things like dexterity which allows you to steal two purses from one target in one hit making the quick time event faster. Quicker lock picking ability that lets you imagine the ability to see the locks from the inside to help you unlock them vs using the analog pattern to light up. There are also upgrades to let you walk in areas making less noise or hidden longer etc.

You have an ability called sweep, which is the same as a shadow moving across the floor in a sweep formation. Sweep, is similar to Blink in Dishonored. You also have water arrow, fire and rope. (random other stuff) Rope can only be used on specific areas. Water turns off a hanging torch or anything with fire as long as the guards not holding it to allow you to creep by a lit area. You also have side missions aside from the main one. About the sweep ability: if you need to dash from one lit area to another. Sweep makes you a quick shadow blur. You can also sweep in shadows or ducking which gives the look like your materializing forward or backwards. From a first persons perspective, its a duck and dash just quick like a blur. I was able to shadow dash backwards while looking at a cop walking towards me (I was hunched over by a crate). This allowed me to avoid getting up, turn, than run and hide. You also have a watch ability. Basically stare threw his eyes and just watch conversations and walking pattern.

Audios good too. Occasionally, the audio seems louder when people are talking. (Hard to tell which room or direction they are in). I am only on stage 4 or 5 as of yesterday. I switched to harder settings to master mode because I wanted more of a challenge from my first play threw. In my opinion it needs to be played harder to get a good feel on people being careful. If a stealth game is to easy, it wont feel like a challenge or like your a real Thief. Easier settings guys don't detect things like voice or walking on glass etc That makes it to easy. Since the stages are semi short divided by sections.. The harder it is, the better and longer the stages feel since you have to be ultra careful. You can pick pocket anyone as long as they have a purse on their side or back. This includes guards. Some stages that require you to be fully 100% undetected while breaking in, if they see you the game re-loads. So far for the most part of the game its not required. (basically, giving you a chance to get in and out but also make mistakes and allows you to run and hide and try again).

However it will be awhile to get use to the stuff and you will have to start over a lot till you get the hang of it. Since they have to load the stage again, some might get annoyed by it. BUT when your use to the moves and things he can do to play stealthy. You rarely see a load. They also do a good job on the story by reading threw news paper, load screens or items you pick up like special things stolen. Take a chance on it. I don't really like reading game reviews because many of the guys are so critical that any little thing drops the score and it effects sales of the game or bad word of mouth. title: Review from a Tomb raider fan since the very first game.
text:
I will keep this simple, since im at work but felt the need to review this after competing. The game is incredible.. lets just say, Lara is back the moment you beat the game. (without giving anything away) you will get the same feeling after completion. It really is a mesmerizing game and the PS4 edition blows the last generation one of of the water. if you have a sound system, you will love the audio recording from simple water, rain, thunderstorm and simple gun shots echoing in the woods. They did an excellent job. not just visually. The island itself feels alive.

Old Tomb Raider games my thoughts:

Tomb Raider stayed the same way even mechanics for years and needed a reboot. 11 games and you don't really know much about her as a character besides the obvious she raids tomb for artifacts. If you have no back ground on a character, and they barely speak (Lara back than) you have nothing to connect with besides the basic's that she raids tomb. Angel of darkness tried story elements and changed the combat system but way to late in the series that it felt experimental. The game was garbage according to people and is universally the worst Tomb Raider, I felt it was something to new and to late in the series when you trained your fans to play her one way and limited back story. What made Lara good at its time was because there was NOTHING like it back than, especially in 3D models puzzle adventure. However now with HD graphics, realism and top games like Uncharted, Thief etc. You do need to connect with characters.

Reboots tend to be looked at with a careful eye, because many older fans just like how she played and was from the first games..Or connected to a past memory when they played this while a kid.

However, they did do her justice in this games story line, music , action and pretty much every category in this new reboot. You connect with Lara and from a video included in the game itself on extra. You see her become who she is. You see her personality get harder, determined and overall back to the old Lara we all know. In mid game you see her change, from simple things like how she lands, talks or walks across gaps, tree limbs etc.

I sometimes hear old tomb Raider fans say they understand its a re-boot but than fall right back into the nostalgia trip, and start up with: "its not like the old Tomb Raider", she doesn't duel pistol anymore, to scary, tense, not enough puzzles. I see this like this: The original Tomb Raider game never existed and this is a brand new game. This game will have no connection to the previous games as far as we know. You won't see Natla or Zip or Allister. This is way before the original. Something to show us how Lara became Lara. (trust me you will see it the same way as your playing threw). Some old fans say they understand this, but they really don't, because they start back in the Nostalgia trip wagon of how she usta be and nit pick instead of sitting down and enjoying the game.

Sit down as a blank slate if your an old fan and just play it. Puzzles are not presented the same way as older games because of the scenario she is in. (stuck on an island with no real experience). Some are easy, others quick. And foremost, explore. Each area has a list that tells you what optional thing to look for. Relics, documents that explain the story, personal notes and diaries. The diaries explain the game better as in whats going on outside of cut-scenes but people in the island. With relics, Lara makes her own personal comments on them and even have hidden extra info when observing the relics by moving them around.

GAMEPLAY:

At first she feels limited and bare-bones.. but that all changes as you gain skill points. You can make her go the survival direction, Brawler or hunter. Even possible to have all of them leveled up. The touch pad is used for a map or lighting torches or turning them off. Controls are solid.. Especially when she starts gaining skills.. Everything just works fluidly like 2nd nature.

This is definitely a game i'm glad I waited for the PS4 version instead of getting it last gen. Visually the game is superior graphically like night and day. I have owned every single Tomb Raider game minus the collection. This is the Tomb Raider game in a long time I truly enjoy, she needed a good reboot and they did an excellent job. Very happy its in my collection.

WARNING:

It is possible to beat the game by just going to story points instead of searching and exploring. If your not familiar on how Tomb Raider works or new to the series, encourage yourself to search. But its not forced on you. This can make the game feel smaller or quick to beat. The old games you had to get everything in the stage to move forward since it was a big puzzle. They never had stage items and towards the end of its life they started to add minor things here and there. This one, everything is optional on the side. This can give an illusion the game is small if you avoid searching for items. Each section has a percentage and main section map with all hidden items. It took me hours to collect many of the items in each section which is marked at 100% when done. But I choose this direction to fully enjoy the game. Instead of rushing threw it. You can back track using the camps which makes it easy to get past items or open areas with upgraded equipment later on.

MULTIPLAYER:

Its okay.. But remember this game could stand on its own without multiplayer. I have no negative or positive opinion on it. Its wacky and feels tacked on but does have its moment. Just don't buy this game strictly for multiplayer. its mostly a single player experience. Which was the main reason in getting it. It does have multiplayer trophies if your into that. However, this opinion is only based on a hand-full of times I played online. I was hooked on single player but will be online more now that I competed the game at 100%. Currently on my 2nd play-threw but focusing on the online aspect.

This is definitely a game you want in your PS4 collection. In my opinion, it shows off the system better than most launch games and on par with Killzone and Battlefield 4. (as in visually impressive) and excellent sound recording and story-line. You will not regret your purchase.

title: A mixed bag
text:
The PDP 3-in-1 Folio for the Nintendo Switch is a mixed bag. Most importantly, the Play-On Mode is not comfortable to me, so it will not be well suited to any on-the-go gaming. The design of the Folio is set up so the middle folding piece is awkwardly sandwiched between the Switch and the grip pieces. This makes for a clunkier playing experience to me. The Folio tries to circumvent the bulkiness of the middle piece by incorporating magnets into the design to ensure each piece locks together, but the heft and shape of the Folio work against this solution. The grip pieces themselves are less comfortable to me than holding a Switch on its own. As a result, I think the best product for me personally is a Switch carrying case where I can remove and play it with its intended ergonomics that are quite good and comfortable.

Despite the drawbacks of the Play-On Mode, the other two modes work as advertised and provide benefits that may justify purchase of the product on their own. The Stand Mode feels much sturdier than the built-in Switch kickstand, and offers multiple angles from which to set up the Switch. text:

This one is three-piece, so the joycons still detach easily, and it is not quite as tight in the dock as the other case was.

However, like the other one, the bumps on the lower rear of the joycons make it a bit harder to store in my travel case. I mean, it still fits in, but it isn't held into my travel case as well as it is without those bumps. However, I think those bumps are important in case of fall.

It is true that if you dropped just the middle section with the case attached, it probably wouldn't make a whole lot of difference, but this is overall probably the best style of protective product you're going to get without losing some real functionality. title: Ever miss the pre-'90s keyboard "CLACK" sound as you key? The RK ROYAL KLUDGE brings it back!
text:
I am so grateful to have had an opportunity to use this, I love mechanical keyboards. It's a little bit of nostalgia coupled with that special feel you get of working with a quality tool.

This board makes that great "CLACK" noise when you strike a key (you could tap it, of course- though those of a certain era who grew up with manual typewriters know well of striking), it's SO satisfying. I typed a thing and I MEANT it.

This keyboard is quite compact at just over 12" long and about 5" wide, though it doesn't feel crunched together. It's stylish as all anything, the only prettier I've seen have been custom builds. The highlight of the arrow keys and groupings of function keys is good-looking and useful for gamers (I can't tell you how many times I've wasted an item, or fired the wrong spell or skill in a game by not paying enough attention to which hotkey I was triggering).

The backlighting is fun, and while it can help you easily figure out where you want to be poking about it- I'd be just as satisfied with this keyboard without it.

Despite its small size, there's a bit of weightiness to the keyboard, it can be recognized as the same as when you're holding something well-built. This is going to last for years and years (and well before you factor in being able to swap keys should one fail). Again, this is a quality tool- it nearly screams it in appearance, weight, feel and performance.

It's very helpful to have multiple ways to connect the keyboard to your PC, wired or not. It's very clever to have the USB-A ports built into the unit, especially if you'd want to utilize a wireless number pad as well and not use all your PC slots.

Several of the other reviewers have said a lot of good things about this keyboard and I agree with them- this is a great unit. I am very lucky (and grateful) to have received one to try out, and having used the RK ROYAL KLUDGE I'm a believer in the product. I fully understand its value and should I ever need to replace this one, I would.

While the color I received, the Americano Black, is a limited edition color (as is its counterpart, the Macchiato White), the RK Royal Kludge lineup has a pretty wide selection of colors (though some exclusive to other models). If you're looking to treat for yourself, do it- you'll be glad you did.

title: Very good sound quality; a bit bulky for extended wear
text:
Overall, these are a pretty decent set of gaming headphones. They aren't loaded with options, but the basics -- namely sound and build quality – are well done considering the price point.

The build quality in particular is impressive for the price point. These feel very solidly built. Even issues such as the cords are well done. I inadvertently gave the cord a stress test – I’ve been mainly using Bluetooth headsets and forgot this was corded. I got up from the PC and gave the cord a pretty good stress test that it passed with flying colors. No complaints at all about the build quality.

The sound quality is also very good for the price. It’s a bit thin on the upper and mid ranges, but nothing objectionable. Good bass response which is aided by the around the ear cup design. Very good sound isolation when wearing these. It’s not audiophile-level sound, but for the price, it’s very respectable.

The mike is adjustable and can be removed if you just want to use these for sound. There’s a handy in-line control for volume and mute.

My primary complaint is comfort. The ear cups are covered with a mesh-like material that I had hoped would allow for some air circulation. However, it’s not very effective – the heat buildup becomes uncomfortable after about 45 minutes.

The upper arm padding is thick but could be a bit softer. The rather firm padding on both the ear cups and upper arm, coupled with the overall weight of the headset, got tiring after a while.

While these fall a bit short in terms of comfort for me, I feel they still warrant a solid four star rating for the sound and build quality. They are a good value set of gaming headphones that can withstand some measure of punishment without breaking.

title: Great for phone use; nice key feel; very compact
text:
Overall, I'm quite pleased with this bluetooth keyboard even though it was not exactly what I was expecting. I thought it would be larger, but instead it's about 6 inches wide and roughly 2.5 inches tall (measurements are approximate since it has an irregular shape). That size makes it very easy to carry along with my phone. It does not, however, make it a good replacement for the onscreen keyboard on my Kindle Fire 8.9.

The keys have a nice feel - there's a positive click when each is depressed. I really like that - nothing worse than a mushy feeling keyboard. It has a standard QWERTY layout, with the top and bottom rows dedicated to function keys. It also has a touchpad on the right-hand side that is pretty responsive. While that may be a plus for some, I'm not a big fan of that -- I'd rather live without the touchpad and have the keys be larger in size.

The battery is internal and, to the best I can tell, is non-replaceable. I'm not thrilled about that, but it does have the benefit of keeping the keyboard thickness and size down.

The overall fit and finish is fine - it's not so rugged that I expect it would withstand rough treatment, but it appears more than capable to put up with normal bumps in daily use/being carried about.

It paired just fine with the 2 devices I've used with it (Kindle Fire 8.9 and a Samsung phone). No problems keeping it paired while in use, even when I was moving about.

It comes in a nice plastic case that's good for storing it when its not being used.

Great choice for phone use, especially if you're like me and find it very frustrating to try to peck out anything longer than a password on a phone screen. Not a great choice for a tablet, however, since the key size on the keyboard is actually smaller than the on-screen key size on a larger tablet when in landscape mode. I won't detract from the rating for that issue, but it's something to keep in mind.

title: So far, so good!
text:
It's only been about a week, but I'm very happy with this keyboard so far. I'm a writer who spends roughly eight hours a day, sometimes seven days a week at the keyboard. This one is responsive and gives me that satisfying click-clack this typewriter-training typist loves - some might find it annoying, though, and the space bar is particularly loud. That did throw me a bit at first.

I tried four different ergonomic setups with this before I found one that didn't result in hand fatigue: keyboard alone, both with the legs up and down, and then keyboard with wrist rest, legs both up and down. What finally worked for me was legs up and a wrist rest. I don't see this working without a wrist rest for any programmer or writer.

I'm also impressed with the battery life. I haven't recharged since I had it, though, granted I don't use the lights. I honestly didn't mean to let it go this long but I keep forgetting to plug it in at night despite the sticky note on my desk.

As other reviewers have mentioned, it's heavy. For me, that's a good thing because it doesn't slide around. I can't see traveling with it, though.

I also like the build. Unlike the last mechanical keyboard I had, which lasted only a couple of years, these keys are less gappy. That's perfect for someone with the unfortunate habit of eating at the desk no matter how many times I tell the kids to not do that because it trashes your keyboard. ;)

What would it take to make it a five for me? Probably a built-in wrist rest though, at this price point, I'm not complaining. I'm very happy with it.

title: It was good while it lasted
text:
It just didn't last long enough. I don't expect a mechanical keyboard to fail in three years, yet, this one did. Correction: in a way, it failed from the beginning. Number keys kept popping off and had to be put back on at least once a day. Annoying, but not enough of a deal breaker to send it back.

But, recently, the left control key started failing on certain functions - such as cntrl shift end and home. It still worked on others, though. I tried taking apart the entire left side of the keyboard and cleaning it, but nothing worked. As a writer who often produces thousands of words a day, this was unacceptable. Oddly enough, the right control key worked just fine and for a while I limped along using that key for certain commands but I was afraid I was teaching myself habits I'd come to regret once I again had a fully functional keyboard.

When it worked, though, it was a great keyboard. Highly responsive with a great tactile feel. If I were rating on that alone, it would definitely be a five.

title: Awesomely Cool!!!
text:
I LOVE this thing!!! It's beautiful to look at, exceedingly fun to play and easy to set up. It only comes with one controller and nunchuck so I had to buy 3 more of each. I couldn't find genuine Wii controllers and nunchucks in red so I had to settle for 1 black and 2 white each. No big deal though since it helps to keep it clear who's controller is who's. We've had it since Christmas of 2010 and am just now writing this review. So, I've had some time to play with it. Just the games it comes with are great fun, and there is a plethora of other games to buy. I like the Sports Wii golf game the best. The kids could play Mario all day and I bought "Wipe Out" and "A Boy and His Blob" as extras. Those games are o.k. but Mario is our favorite. Best to use rechargeable batteries in the controllers since it will go through your AA's pretty fast.

Just lately connected it to Netflix - OH MY GAWD!!! What a wonderful thing! Movies and shows download via your wireless router and it's just great! It keeps us entertained and informed (news, internet, etc...) and it's everything and I could have hoped for. I was hoping I could connect a wireless keyboard to it but you can't do it that way. You have to connect the keyboard via a cable which I haven't done yet but will eventually. I don't surf the internet much using the Wii but might would if I could just easily type in the web addresses. To use the controller is a S-L-O-W process and highly prone to mistake making since that directional thingy inside the controllers is always bouncing around and buzzing and throwing the arrows off the letters on the screen.

I'm not going to get into the technical aspects of it, the other reviews have covered all of that very well. I'll just say that you DON'T have to have a degree in computer science to install it. It does take a little trial and error since you probably will have questions the owner's manual doesn't cover. It took a while to get Netflix going since I had to run back and forth between the Wii console and my desktop upstairs but it finally loaded and you get one month FREE on Netflix - can't beat that! Then it's only $7.99/month and they keep adding more movies and shows depending on what you've already watched. Not everything you might want to see is available but a boatload of stuff is.

This whole thing is really a lot of fun - it's almost too good to be true. I can't help but expect something to go terribly wrong............but I certainly hope not!

title: The balance and quick adjust makes this a game changer
text:
[[VIDEOID:8b7a3d936ac0ca2f356b89c67ce69bba]] It's a battery, it has over 3000mAh I've measured and I'll be doing a complete drain test on it and updating this later. This is the results of one extended six hour gaming session due to wife being sick and sounding like a chainsaw / nothing else for me to do other than play Iron Man VR and Beat Saber until 4am so take this as a fairly short turnaround review until I update it with battery drain stats.

First off, attached video here of unboxing and assembling the thing. It's easy and you'll see I managed to mess it up twice and nearly drop the Meta Quest 2 twice... learn from my fail, or don't. It's easy, just wasn't easy to film.

I got the battery pack mostly because I keep having time to play with the Quest 2 and finding out I left it running and it's dead as a doornail. My use case was not extended playtime, it was the ability to actually use it when I wanted to and had done this.

What I discovered yesterday was with the quick adjust knob I can get this on a kid's head to watch the Bee VR movie for the umpteenth time in about 10 seconds. That's... lemme tell you... the default strap system ended up we just put stuffed animals in and this is so much better. So much.

I charged the unit up and played quite a while last night. Longest VR session I've ever had, not because I run out of battery but because sick wife and there was no reason to even attempt to sleep. One of the things I noticed was normally my neck hurts. Didn't this time. The counterbalance I believe was helping however it could also have been that I was using just different movements, or perhaps my neck just didn't bug me.

The only things I think really could be improved here is the battery is a magnetic attachment and if you're adjusting behind your head you can accidentally pop it out. Maybe a locking clip? Also use a flat cable for the USB-C charging wire with a 90 degree turn as opposed to what ships with it so you can't snag it accidentally.

Also the documentation - give me some instruction on how to put this thing together... I figured it out, but this was my first strap replacement and I did not know how the things popped out... you'll see if you watch the video me doing it wrong again and again and again. Only about three times....

Yeah, fiveish hours in I am very impressed with it, and I'll do a full on battery drain on it when I can figure out how to force it to charge my measuring tool (which currently sees it as a source to push power to rather than get it from).

title: Cool looking case, gluing issues, locks that can be defeated by hamsters
text:
[[VIDEOID:eb5860fecee5ac4fd869b2cb7f95f448]] Let me tell you this thing looks cool. It is cool. But it's not that cool and suffers from some excessive cheapness. Oh, I love it and it now is where my Quest 2 lives, but let's go through this.

The case - this can be found on Amazon for about half the price. Not the foam cutout mind you, but a higher quality metal carry case. I suspect you're mostly paying for the foam on this one because there's nothing special about the exterior case.

So, paying for the foam let's look at picture #2 above - all the foam was glued into the case (what you have to do, I'm not complaining. All the foam at the edges looks like picture 2. Just not particularly neat. If you're going to charge $40 or so for foam work, make it neat.

Unit comes with two keys to lock it. You can unlock with a fingernail. Handle connection just looks cheap.

Positive: foam cutouts will keep your Quest 2 from moving. Negative: There's so much space they could have used to put things like booster batteries or a remote or just storage that was not cut out right. I mean sure this looks cool but rearranging the cutouts you would have had so much space free.

This is the type of case I'd expect to pay half of what they're asking... It's lightweight aluminum, cheap locks and handles, and non-expertly glued foam.

I do not hate it, I actually like it, but it's just cool looking, not cool functioning.

title: Wondering if I bought the Bizaro version
text:
I'm still playing the game, I'm only about 3 hours into the thing and somewhere around 80% completed according to the game, and I'm not having fun any more, and this really bothers me. I just shelled out $60 something and I can't say I've ever had a feeling during this that I was doing anything meaningful other than saving a block of Metropolis idiots (they run into you while you're punching your opponents and are sent flying).

I'm trying to do one of the side missions where I fly around and collect things, but Metropolis gets attacked every 10 seconds by a band of flying ice dragons and their companions the fire dragons. Or I'll get wrapped up in a fight with the guy who multiplies over and over again yet only manages to have 3 or 4 lines and they're so freaking corny it hurts.

I really wanted to like this game... honestly, I got sucked in because of the demo being so short... I thought "there has to be more to this game, and it's probably frickin' awesome"... I'm really not finding the frickin' awesome.

There's a large beautiful city here every 3rd building seems to have the same texture, in the distance you can see a giant dam which looks like it would be fun to fly over to, but forget about that. Metropolis is a huge series of islands with an unreachable mainland and no possible way the citizens could reach it. No airports, appears to be a sea-based town only. The mainland, if I am guessing right, has a cliff facing Metropolis that is roughly 25 miles high, which is about the same height as the unreachable dam that you also can't visit.

And there're numerous problematic dichotomies - one example is you are charged with taking care of the city, keeping things from getting damaged, and yet you get achievement points for things such as ripping the globe off of the Daily Planet and throwing it down the streets. Another is you go to take a challenge and turn into Bizaro and have to destroy as much of the city as you can to advance.

And for the Man of Steel, I feel more like I'm playing the man of pretty darn strong rubber. I can lift 60,000 pounds in this game, and throw it, and it bounces off any buildings it hits. I can hit a pedestrian while in a fight and they get right back up but if one of the opponents hits them, they go down instantly. I try and pick up the injured person to take them to the ambulance (where I then drop them 20 feet to their rescue) and will manage to pick up the wandering pedestrian who is walking through a burning car to get in my way.

Metropolis takes a little too much damage and Superman drops to his knees and looks like he's crying. It takes the same amount of damage in two back to back fights and, well, for some reason it's fine.

While playing I also learned that when the game spawns 15 flying enemies in certain areas the game will lock up for a while. Friend of mine was watching and said my XBOX had shut down due to overheating and I pointed out that you could still go the menu and to wait for a bit, and then it did whatever it was doing and started speeding up, and that it was always when there were that many flying enemies. Duplicated the problem a few times.

I don't know what I did exactly, but I blew one of the bosses into orbit for a while, and when he came down he landed in the ocean. He did not move, nor could I swim or fly underwater. I tried using my heat vision to hit him but noticed all I was doing was damaging Metropolis. I was fighting Bizaro at one point and I knocked him into the one highway that exists... could not get to him. Both these incidents I had to reload the last save.

I've gotten to the point where I save every single event due to bugs like these.

I wish I had my money back, or the game I expected

It all seemed so perfect until it wasn’t. Less then two weeks after purchase, the RGB lighting suddenly dimmed and only a few keys had light coming through. I tried to turn the lighting off and on again, switching the lighting modes, etc. But the lighting was stuck on Blue, with only a few keys lit up. The keyboard was charged at over 75% when it happened, so lack of charging was not the problem. A few days after the lights suddenly started working again, so I thought they perhaps it was a temporary malfunction. But less than a week later, the RGB lighting got stuck on blue with only a few keys lit up. For context, when the RGB lighting stopped working the first time, I had the lights set up on the violet color. The second time, I had it set to yellow. After this second time of RGB not working, I have decided to return the keyboard before the return window closes. It is really too bad. It was great while it lasted, easy in the eyes, and great to travel with.

title: Initial review - woah.
text:
I guess I'll do a top to bottom on this - This is my initial review after just an hour or so with the board, so I can't yet speak to longevity, but I am going to be using this in the field as a paramedic for typing reports, so rest assured that it will be dropped and beaten on quite a lot, so if there's any issues I will update the review.

Starting with the packaging, it's clean, small, minimalist, no plastic or bubblewrap anywhere. All recyclable apart from a single twist tie for the nice braided cable. Legit. The instructions are small and easy to follow.

The braided cord is very nice and a good length, and I absolutely LOVE the way they designed the 2.4ghz dongle (which I bought it specifically for) to slot into the back very securely but still be easily removable.

I really appreciate the layout of the function controls, they're very easy to read and intuitive, with no bloat.

The chassis is very very stiff and sturdy feeling, no deck flex at all. All the touch surfaces are frankly ridiculously premium feeling.

The all flat and close together keycaps initially felt really weird but within a few minutes I was back up to full speed. The "J key is very very slightly recessed and I can't tell if this is intentional or not. J and F are two of the indicator keys with bumps for placement, and the F key isn't recessed. I really don't notice it when typing anyways and it's almost invisible unless you're looking. I really like that it doesn't use springbars for the larger keys, but I have noticed that if I edge tap the spacebar on the very end., it will quite often not register. I had to look for that issue though, since I do generally strike it in the middle.3/4 but if you're the type who hits space right next to alt, you will get some false misses.

Overall though the keycaps don't wobble hardly at all and feel very nice. I like the barest hint of a tilt with the feet down and nice angle with them up. It's very stable and doesn't slide around at all, with a nice heft.

I'm not normally a fan of blue switches, the two other full size boards (an early mech, Razer Blackwidow Ultimate and some noname $50 beater) that I've used with them, even with O rings, drove me nuts enough to get rid of them. But the switches on this one are barely louder than a brown. Very precise and satisfying for a blue. Weight is perfect and they're very very smooth, too. No friction, no wobble. They do have the same issue all blues, have where if you're repeatedly tapping a key, you don't have a super precise amount of feedback on when the key is going to register, so until you're used to it, you have to really tap every key with intent and purpose. I do think this issue is FAR more pronounced on full sized blues though, and it's quite a lot less present on these low profiles. Still I would prefer tactile browns for a typist board, and I'd love if they released a version of this board with at least reds and browns in addition to clicky blues.

The RGB lighting is absolutely superb. The light reflects off the aluminum backplate too, so you do get nice visual lines between the keys. Tons of neat modes and truly enormous customization in color, brightness and speed. You need to have it be wired in order to do the custom modes initially, but once you're finished, it will save them into the board for wireless use.

Overall, I can't really understand how they're selling this thing at the price it's listed and still making a profit. I'm not going to be replacing my custom built board for home anytime soon, but for the reasons I got it (the dongle is nice for locked-down work computers that don't have bluetooth enabled and I love that it pops right out with a thumbnail and stays in place VERY securely) It's kind of insane. If they made a version with browns instead of blues (or better yet, hot-swappable so you could do custom switch setups I'd be utterly smitten. There are a few little flaws but again, for the price, nothing even remotely problematic. Enormous kudos to RisoPhy for this little thing.

title: 2 for 2, failed buttons. Just get a Deathadder
text:
I wanted to like this mouse. I like the position of the buttons (particularly the toggle DPI that lets you have a "snipe" button - more mice need that) and the general shape of the mouse, but it's just got so many problems, including abysmal build quality (which is shocking for logitech)

For starters, it's weirdly draggy and a bit heavy, even wired and with zero weights in it. I can't see anyone wanting to add more of the included weights - the point of this kind of mouse is to start LIGHT and let you tune it, not start heavy and let you make it worse. Genuinely heavier than my full size WIRELESS teknet mouse that I use for my media PC.

The feet lasted okay, they're starting to feel worn after a year of use on an aluminum banshee pad mousepad (I usually got about 2-3 years out of a set of feet on a Razer Deathadder) And they're very sensitive to picking up schmutz. Replacement feet are not readily found, you're gonna be using teflon tape. The combination of really meh feet and really heavy/draggy weight makes the mouse wildly imprecise after only a couple months. Even with teflon tape over the feet, I still can't make a "clean" drag across my mousepad with a smooth cursor movement. Not even sure it would when it was new. The aforementioned teknet mouse still absolutely glides after years. I think it's just because the 502 has SIX absolutely gigantic pads, and other mice I use tend to have 3 or 4 much smaller feet at most, which keeps the inherent friction lower.

Cord is okay if used with a mouse bungie.

The scroll wheel is abysmal. It has a side/side rock, which is already not good for a proper gaming mouse (they all have a habit of mis-registering mouse 3 clicks) but this is easily the worst I've ever experienced. I am used to the design, but this one is so bad and vague that I had to straight up disable the rocker, so now I only get about 15% of my middle clicks mis-sensed. The ability to unlock a scroll wheel is nice when I have to turbo scroll through a 300 page document, but again, in GAMING practice, is just one more way the scroll wheel feels incredibly vague and inaccurate.

mouse 4 is just set too far back. You have to press it with the knuckle of your thumb, which requires an incredibly awkward "palm pinch". If you use all the mouse buttons in a game, you're going to hate this thing so much.

And the thing is INCREDIBLY fragile. My first one's left click broke just sliding off my chair onto carpet, the whole mouse button itself sheared off. The second one's L2 switch itself is now failing, as it registers right click but doesn't register HOLDING it. After only a year, this is appalling. If you play MMO's, this makes steering an absolute nightmare. If you play FPS games, right click iron sight/scope becomes agony.

And there's something about this mouse that gives me really sweaty palms, which is weird because I have a kind of hybrid palm/fingertip grip that keeps my palm usually hovering just above the mouse

My deathadder was only replaced by this mouse because I suspected the skin flakes embedded in the chassis had evolved a new form of life. This one is getting hucked in the garbage because it fell to pieces in a little over a year and a half. I am staying away from Logitech for a few years after two absolutely atrocious peripherals and going back to the good old iron duke of a Razer Deathadder.

title: Too slow, the learning curve is wrong.
text:
From Software has a long history of games with an intense learning curve (dark souls and DS2 are the most recent examples of this) and once you get comfortable with the controls in AC3 and 4, the games open up to you like a perfect rose of rewarding, deep, and complex gameplay. ACV is nothing like this. The learning curve is still there, but it's not the controls. Before, with good play, you could make even the heaviest AC's dance and the lightest ones nearly unhittable. In this, everything feels ponderous, slow, and unsatisfying. They don't have the heavy, immense, powerful feel of mechs from the mechwarrior series, they don't have that heavy, militaristic and mobile feel of hawken, they just feel like lumpy, slow, unglorious pieces of tripe. Weapon balance is horrible, whereas in previous AC games, you could literally make any weapon work with enough practice, most weapons in ACV are abjectly useless. I also don't like having no back weapons, it tones down the variety too much.

I do understand that lots of people disliked 4 because it was just too fast, and ultralight AC's dominated heavies, but I felt it was fast and dramatic and oh-so-stylish. 3 was great in different ways as well. The general fanbase wanted the game's pace slowed down dramatically, but from software took it way too far in this release, and refocused the game in the wrong way.

People love AC on AC combat, and the AI arenas were great. but team combat with reasonably fast AC's is just not feasible, so they slowed it too far down in an attempt at making big, multi-AC battles. This is not Mechwarrior or hawken, it's unpolished, slow, and unrewarding. Simply adding online matchmaking in 1v1 or 2v2, MAYBE 3v3 arenas to a game like AC3 or 4 would have hit the sweet spot for online play. It also would have been easier to implement and wouldn't have ruined the single player experience, which is traditionally all an AC game is about.

Armored core games have terrible stories, terrible voice acting, and somehow manage to be unbelievably compelling and fun. The plot in V is just nonsense. It's boring, slow, repetitive, with none of the grandiose challenge of 4 or the subtle complexity of 3. AC games are traditionally single player focused and make you feel like an important piece of the world you interact with. In V, you're just a dude in a world that gives you no reason to take interest.

Menu screens are convoluted and horrible. AC construction is uninteresting, complicated, and the variation is just so undramatic that you have no real incentive to build focused AC's based around a specific combat style or weapon, it pidgeonholes your AC into a specific weapon type based on your platform. I understand the reasoning behind this, but I used to build tank AC's for very specific reasons, not just because they're the only things that can use a weapon I like. I want an AC to work how I want it to work, I don't think all snipers should be quad legged. The 3 element type system is badly explained and badly executed.

In short, I was horrendously disappointed with ACV, despite being a hardcore fan of the series. I am a single player gamer who occasionally likes to challenge himself to a bit of multiplayer. Forcing me to interact with this online system is an instant turn-off, and the story did nothing to keep me engaged. with every other AC title I've put months of time into them, with V I stopped almost immediately after finishing the campaign, because it was just. not. fun.

Two stars because it's not BROKEN, it's just not fun.

If you want a more fast paced and tactical team based mech game, Hawken is free.

If you want a mech game that has slow, immense, and powerful team based gameplay, Mechwarrior online is free.

If you want a game that has the traditional excellence of real AC games and true depth of story, gear, and gameplay, dark souls and DS2 are where you want to be.

If you have to play armored core, either buy 4 and for answer, or go back and play them again. Because ACV is just a disappointing, slow, unrewarding experience.

title: Going back to TW2005.
text:
I had given TW2006 a pass... well, more accurately, I didn't even have my own PS2 until my roommate moved out and took his with him. By that time, I had already been playing--and loving--TW2005 for the better part of a year. By the time I was ready to move on to the next level, TW2007 was out and I upgraded.

And promptly downgraded again.

There are a lot of good ideas in TW2007; unfortunately, the gameplay and game physics are what kills this game.

I do not expect to play this game like I do TW2005; I have worked my way up in the earlier game, and I know I have to start all over again. I do not expect to be hitting 350-yard drives. I do not expect to be able to stick a ball on the back of the green and draw it halfway back to the front. I don't expect to be able to spin it out of the sand or rough. I expect to play poorly again as I work my way through the new game.

However, when a putting meter tells me to aim four inches left and level with the hole, I aim five inches left and miss, and it goes fifteen feet past the hole, that is not a simple misread but a serious flaw in game physics.

I've been playing real golf for twenty-some years, and even when I was a beginner, I never had yips like that. If they are trying to simulate a learning curve, they are doing it in a way that discourages trying again. I can understand sliding one, two, three feet by, maybe even four--I've done that enough times on any number of golf courses under all kinds of weather conditions.

When it rolls twenty feet past and there is no indication of the green being anywhere near that steeply graded, this is nothing I as player could have predicted and prepared for. And it sucks all the fun out of what should have been a fantastic game, and it makes it unplayable. I set my copy aside months ago. I doubt much I will pick it up again. And it does not make me optimistic about TW2008.

TW2007 gets 2/5 for having a lot of really good ideas that, were the game playable, would make this a terrific sim. I love the new courses... unfortunately, we're still saddled with the abysmal Emerald Dragon, Paradise Cove and Greek Isles--at least Greek Isles has the decency to have a couple windmills. Add a clown face into whose mouth you have to put the ball, and it wouldn't be inappropriate. For what a tricky but playable target course should look like, I might suggest Pine Valley--either as a course to include if the rights can be had, or as a course to emulate so Emerald Dragon, Paradise Cove and Greek Isles can be retired back to the minigolf course that doubtless inspired them.

And for a good round of golf, get a copy of Tiger Woods PGA Tour 2005 and give this version a total miss, unless you happen to like being lied to by your caddy.

title: Decent-ish keyboard with some flaws.
text:
There aren't many 10-key (full-sized) hotswap keyboards available. This one has the basics down; it's decent, solid, affordable and really is a hotswap RGB keyboard. The cord is not detachable, but is long enough and seems high-quality, fabric-covered and thick. The metal bevelled edge not only looks nice but feels nice.

And it is compatible with MX switches. I replaced the alpha keys with Zilents, which are more tactile and quieter, great for the Zoom era. For those keys, I also tossed on some Aura Pudding caps, which work great with the backlighting.

But not only is it not perfect, it has some real let-downs.

On mine, out of the box, some keys wobble badly. The right shift, for example, is unstabilized. It does have stabilizers installed, but on some keys the stabilizer is not connecting/popping up. I'm not a keyboard hacker, so that's not something I intuitively know how to fix.

I swapped out the alpha and a few key switches (didn't touch the shift or anything near it). Perhaps a quarter of the pre-installed switches were really jammed in there, tighter than just from the tabs. Because of this, it's hard to get them out. It also means the tabs will be broken on those switches if you intend to salvage, but that's not an issue for me.

Lighting effects are configured via software, which isn't bad so much as it's essentially undocumented. I couldn't find any manual or help for it. There are quite a few stupid effects - you'd never use ping-pong or glorious because it just turns your keyboard into waves of light and dark - but how do you use, for example, Fast Run or Pass, both of which highlight the key you've pressed, with a different backlight? It seems it should be feasible, but not at all obvious.

Update: This keyboard is also extremely static-sensitive. The top of the case is metal, and if you have a little static on you, it resets.

title: Dragon Quest Builders 2
text:
I played and loved the origianl DQB, and as well as being an overall fan of Dragon Quest in general, so this was a must-buy for me.

The game is extremely engaging. No spoilers here, but I'm in the third chapter now. Now sure how big overall the game is. There are tons of improvements to the original which makes it a worthwhile investment. Even if you've never played Dragon Quest Builders 1, or the mainline franchise, if you like crafting and building, this is a great game.

I dock one star for a few issues:

* Slow pacing. Like a traditional JRPG, this has TONS of dialog. Most of the dialog is easy to step thru by just mashing the A button, but there are some story-centric scenes which cannot be skipped and just take forever to wait out.
* Very small UI scale. In handheld mode, it can make it a squint-fest and there is no way to increase the font or stuff.
* I haven't unlocked free-play mode. I guess just like the original, you have to finish the game first. That might be a turnoff to some people who just want to be creative. There is a built-in social media network where you can share screenies and some of those are AMAZING, I just wish we could get there sooner.
* Frame rating issues. Generally the game runs smoothly, but I've had one boss battle which was fairly involved, NPCs running all over the place, monsters popping up, and the boss itself hurling attacks, and it really hammered the Switch's performance.

Issues aside, it's a great game and no regrets.

Who else named their slime Rimuru?

title: My never-ending time waiting for Portia to load...
text:
Edit May 19. Shortly after my original review, they released the waited-for patch, but it doesn't garner an upgraded rating. See the end for additional patch comments.

TL;DR - as much fun as this game is, it is equal part frustration. Wait and see if the upcoming patches address the performance but until then, I can't in good heart recommend this game.

Possible spoilers ahead.

I've been playing this since the eshop release date and have finished the main story, which currently ends after the final battle (and one followup mission to reconstruct). Apparently the PC versions are at a higher release than the console versions, and as of this writing, the developers promise a patch "sometime" in May, to add additional content as well as addressing deficiencies in the console ports.

If you like Story of Seasons or Stardew Valley type games, you'll feel at home here. Rather than farming, this game focuses on crafting. You're set in a post-apocalyptic world. You are a Builder whose job is to use remnants of lost technology to craft things to the behest of the mayor or the other townspeople. Like SoS or STV, there is a whole social order where you befriend people and can marry.

There is plenty to do and see. The main story line leads you to improving your technology, creating newer and better machines. You'll unlock new zones with higher level resources to collect. Most of the new zones have type types of ruins for you to explore; the abandoned ruins are where you mine for ore and collect forgotten technology. The hazardous ruins are where you combat monsters and have a better chances of collecting forgotten technologies. You'll need those, as some of the items are un-craftable.

There are also secondary missions, usually unrelated to the main story but sometimes unlocked after certain events. Then there are also commissions which is typically in the form of an NPC asking for something to be crafted.

There is a bit of combat but it's kinda lame with limited options. You basically just mash the attack button. During some of the main missions, you'll be accompanied by NPCs who are stronger than you and can even do most of the combat for you. During the leadup to the final battle, including the final battle itself, I basically sat on the perimeter and let the NPCs beat the bosses.

There are a lot of technical issues with the game which prevent full enjoyment.

The initial loading screen is unbearably long. We're talking upwards of 5 MINUTES. There appears to be serious performance issues with the game where you will experience this enormous lag in various places. Zoning in and out takes a noticeable amount of time. Navigating menus can be exceedingly slow. There is one series of secondary missions which asks you to take a series of photographs, and if you make a mistake, it take take an inappropriately long time to move thru the menus to take photographs. The game does not use the built-in Switch screenshot mechanism for the in-game photos.

At least twice, when zoning out of a building, I fell thru the ground, and just kept plummeting forever. The game automatically puts you to sleep after a specific in-game time, so I just had to wait around for that to happen. Luckily there is no penalty for staying up too late.

Three times the game simply crashed, and the switch reported something to the effect that "the software has encountered an error and will close".

During the final battles, your Switch will slow down to a crawl where controller presses may feel as if they were not registered.

There are other issues (such as terrible proof-reading and grammar usage), but none as bad as the performance issues. After a game crash, if it didn't take 5 minutes to load, I would be a little less annoyed. And while falling thru the sky, the same loading time prevents me from simply re-starting the the Switch home screen. I also like to play different games, but I really have to stop and think "if I stop this to play Diablo for an hour or so, I'll have to wait forever for it to load".

Speaking of Diablo, I cannot accept the smug statement that the switch is "underpowered", when games like Diabo, and other games like first-party Nintendo stuff, can manage better. Even "simpler" games like Farm Together perform better, which said game has noted issues with distance and mild lag during auto-saves, but can still handle counting thousands of individual timers for each crop planted without performance hits.

Path 1.0.4 notes.

With the 1.0.4 patch, they've tried to address some of the game-stopping issues. Load times are still abysmal. Performance hits seem more common now. Graphics lag has increased. When exiting menus, there is a noticeable delay before the game response again. Crashes are more abundant - in the time I've been playing the patch (4 days?), I've crashed five times.

On a positive note :-/ They've added much more content. The main story continues after reconstruction, and there is a new area (as well as new ruins). Without having played the PC versions, it appears the Switch version is now more in-line with that.

title: Old school music indeed
text:
tl;dr: buy this. The music kicks.

If you are old enough to remember things like cracked loading screens on the Commodore 64, demos, or stuff like some of the original NES game music, you'll probably find yourself experiencing a massive wave of nostalgia. Even if you aren't old enough to have lived thru the halcyon 8-bit days, any fan of chiptunes will love this game.

As expected, the centerpiece of the game is the music, and what glorious music it is. The game is your basic rhythm game: follow the markers on the screen by pressing one of the buttons (sometimes including the shoulder buttons), There are several play modes. The main mode is the basic story mode, which unlocks various tunes to play in arcade mode. Arcade mode is just a free-for-all where you can replay a song at different skill settings. Once you finish the main story, you unlock the chicken levels. 50 levels of more of the same, and additional tunes to unlock, but they add insane distractions on the screen while playing. Some of those distractions will effectively block the scrolling markers, so do your best to get your rhythm-foo working at peak efficiency. There's also a multiplayer mode, but I have not tried it.

title: The Now Loading Cafe
text:
Was excited to buy this since I first started to hear about it on various gaming sites. I figured with the person who created (the original) Harvest Moon (now known as Story of Seasons), the $60 price tag was worth a day-one purchase, but now I regret my purchase. Hindsight tells me I should have waited for at least some critical reviews for a game whose price tag is as high as Nintendo's own AAA properties (which are usually worth their price, but that's another topic)

I have probably about 10 hours into the game, and my dragon is at the second stage; not sure how much more it'll grow, but I do not think I will find out. Loading times alone are not worth it, every zone-in is met with a loading screen. Sometimes you'll even get loading screens without zoning. The loading screens last long enough to interrupt any sense of engagement.

There are other issues, such the shampoo-rinse-repeat cycle you're involved with. Wake up, go downstairs and you'll probably be greeted with a cut scene that expands the current chapter. Once that is done, go outside and harvest ingredients until time runs outs, and it'll run out pretty fast because the clock is a tad bit faster than my comfort level.

The artwork is definitely beautiful, and I seem to recall seeing somewhere that the creator likens the game to a storybook unfolding, but like a storybook that is linear, that style doesn't quite fit this game model.

title: Farm Sim 2017
text:
Since it's asked in the questions, and altho answered, I figured it can't hurt to mention: this is not Farmville, Harvest Moon, Stardew Valley, or any of those social farming games. This is straight up a farm management simulation, and you have to take care of every little detail, from sowing seed, to harvesting and selling, and if you find any free time, you might want to try your hand at animal husbandry or forestry.

There's a steep learning curve. I wouldn't even call it a curve. It's kinda like they say, here's a jumbo jet, you can figure the rest out. The tutorials only mention basics like "oh, you need to feed and water your animals". But in between that is figuring out what do to. Every task has a tool, and there's not a whole lot of in-game documentation to figure it out. Wanna fertilize your newly sown wheat? You need to buy a front-loader attachment for your tractor, but before you do that, you need to customize said tractor so it can USE front-loaders. When you do that, you need to buy a pallet loader to load and transport fertilizer. If you've figured all that out, time to bring that fertilizer back to the farm and load it in to your fertilizer attachment, which you forgot to buy when you were in town! You'll use every single button and combinations of buttons on the Switch. Individual shoulder buttons or both at once, sometimes a shoulder button and left stick down. If you have multiple attachments on your tractor, you need to select which tool you want to use.

There are plenty of on-screen status indicators, and sometimes some brief descriptions text to help you along. You can hire workers to help with some of the drudgery, like sowing seed, which is just driving back and forth for an hour or so,. but workers cost money. Haven't been able to figure out, or even tell, if workers can deliver goods to sell.

The graphics are pretty amazing, and you can jump out of your tractor at any time and walk around. You'll even see other people wandering around town, and if you want, there will be cars on the road, always getting in your way.

I've played FS on a 3DS, which is an extremely simplified version of FS, kinda like they just took the Android mobile app and ported it to the 3DS, so I thought I was prepared. But the 3DS version is a Tonka toy in comparison. As far as I can tell, the only thing that is lacking from other versions is multiplayer and mod support.

If you're already a fan of the franchise, you'll know what to expect, but this time, it's portable. I would point out that tablet mode may be a bit stressful on your eyes, as some of the fonts are pretty tiny, so I prefer docked mode.

If you're new to the franchise, give yourself a few hours before making judgement. This is not the kind of game you can pick up and 15 minutes later make a call. You'll want to spend time in the tutorials, and then a few hours in career mode, and you might want to even restart career mode. It's a long term game, so the initial time investment is going to reflect that.

title: The Lost Valley, version 2.0
text:
If you're familiar with Natsume's take on the Harvest Moon games called The Lost Valley (TLV), you'll already be familiar with this one. This is basically TLV 2.0. They improved a few things, tweaked the story a bit, but much is still the same. Like TLV, there's a lot of potential but it ends up being undeveloped or issues ignored.

For me, frustration factor outweighs enjoyment and after 30 hours and just over two in-game years, this is getting put away.

The camera is still the camera. It's an automatic camera that magically swings around without your input, but more often than not, ends up looking in a direction I don't want. You can use the shoulder buttons to swing the camera manually, but there is no way to override the automatic focus.

There are two other camera views: overhead and farming. Both are essentially the same, but farming view keeps your character pointed in the same direction, making it easier to more quickly terraform or farm. But these additional camera views still have an automatic focus and will still swing around. Take an example. I'm trying to dig out a path to the Underworld, which is on the same edge as the town entrance. No matter which camera view I try to use, it still swings wildly and makes it extremely difficult to see exactly where I am digging. Just give us a straight view with no automatic swings.

Objects such as people and animals are impassable barriers. If anything is in your way, you will not get around it. I found this more pronounced in the barn. I have four animals (horse, sheep, cow and donkey) and they can't get out of their way to eat their food. You can watch them try to perform this intricate dance to maneuver around each other to reach their feed troughs. If an NPC or two are in the barn, navigation space is even more limited. I've seen them get stuck in a corner, walking into the wall. The workaround is to either exit and re-enter (rezone) or pull up a menu like the save menu. If a harvest sprite is blocking the bridge to the harvest goddess, well, rezone...

Boulders spawning right in front of my house. Often. Like, several times a week. When I wake up and go to the valley, it's like there was a meteor shower, last night, and every night. Trees will respawn too. Sometimes you'll rezone on the same day, and where there was no boulder or tree five minutes ago, oh wait, there's one now... It's just too aggressive.

Resource acquisition is rage inducing. You'll need a metric ton of a particularly rare material but the resource node only respawns once every few days. I've long since been at 100% with my selected marriage candidate but I will never get material. The workaround is something called save scumming, which is to save just prior to hitting a resource node, and reloading if you do not get what you need. This should really not be a viable gaming strategy. Another workaround is to use the harvest sprites, but they only work once every other day, and weekends off.

I've mentioned "the work around" at least twice. Workarounds are illustrative of design flaws.

title: Return to PopoloCrois
text:
I've played Harvest Moon games, now generally known as Story of Seasons, but I've not heard of PopoloCrois before, but that's not affecting my game play. If I were to compare this with anything, I'd undoubtedly say this is a bit like Rune Factory, which takes a core RPG and adds a bit of Harvest Moon features. This is heavily story-driven and the farming aspects are sorta taking backseat to everything else. It's also very slow starting, so be prepared to invest some time before you get into full swing. Even at 5 hours play time, I've not fully unlocked everything, and I'm trying to keep myself from looking up spoilers so I don't quite know how long the game is. But being one of the rare types of newer games that included a full-color manual, I know that I've still unlock StreetPass.

The game is probably pretty niche and there's nothing wrong with that. For myself, I find myself feeling a bit blasé about recent big-name releases, so this is a refreshing change of pace. There's not a cast of thousands, characters whose names I can't remember or even care about. It's not epic. It has nice colors and music, a handful of quirky characters (so far), and an overall feeling of classic JRPG game play. I keep saying "so far" or "right now", since I don't know how the game progresses, but 'right now" I have a four-member party who are searching for some number of dungeons to clear so I can progress. Movement is visually similar to classic JRPGs, with an isometric view of with your characters travelling the world and having random encounters. That's where I shudder; I guess games like Pokemon or the older, classic Final Fantasy games have given me an aversion over random encounters. You can adjust the rate, but I still have it set at the highest (which I think was the default).

Combat is decidedly JRPG: an off-world zone with a grid pattern and turn-based combat. You can toggle auto-combat or manual combat, and I've been running mostly on auto with no real problems. If I'm annoyed by the high rate of random encounters, I turn it to manual combat and select "run", but you can lose gold if you run from an encounter.

Well, I won't go on, but if you want something that's pretty stress-free, that won't cause you to rage-quit or tempt you to throw your 3DS against a wall, this is a very nice change of pace.
