title: Not as bad as some make it out to be
text:
I suspect that many people who wrote other reviews did not play other Lego games for Vita when they compare it to other releases. PS4/xbox lego games are usually open world, and vita/3ds versions are more mission oriented because the specs of handhelds don't have enough power to run it the same way as big consoles.

With that in mind, it is certainly a decent enough game, similar enough to other lego games. It is easy enough to be fairly mindless, but there are some missions that I had to sweat on to actually be able to finish. I completed it in 2 days, and still trying to unlock all of the achievements a few weeks later. It gets a bit repetitive, because you need to do missions several time with various characters because you need specific abilities to influence certain objects to get the achievements, and you can select only one character for a playthrough of a mission. I don't really like that the achievements page is shown only after you make the character selection, so you don't really know who exactly you would need unless you've been literally playing the same level over and over again. Still, it's enjoyable enough to keep playing.

title: Fantastic Wheel and Pedal Set
text:
I've recently gotten into Dirt Rally 2. The addition of the G923 setup is simply amazing.

I currently use a Thrustmaster T Flight HOTAS X and Flight Rudder Pedals for Star Wars Squadrons in VR. However my last wheel and force feedback equipment was a loooong time ago. My last wheel was a CH Products Virtual Pilot Pro flight yoke, and I had a Logitech Wingman Force 3D stick... So to say that this new wheel is an upgrade is an understatement.

There is no comparison between using a wheel and game controller. None. Anyone who spends significant time playing racing games is truly missing out by not investing in a wheel and pedal set. Even though they can be costly, you need to think about how many hours you spend in the game and divide the cost of the equipment by those long hours. I'm multiplying my enjoyment by a factor of ten for about $0.50 per hour played.

The force feedback and wheel vibration is amazing to me. Simply amazing. Even though I play DIRT on a 32" monitor, I find the force feedback wheel and pedal setup to be just as immersive as playing Squadrons in VR on full HOTAS/Pedals without force feedback. God help me when I get a better GPU and go VR with Dirt...

Packaging is fairly unremarkable for such a pricey item. Which is, in a way, good to me. I'd rather have value go into the product as opposed to trying to impress me with the unboxing experience.

Installation and setup was a bit more on the complex side. If you already have a HOTAS/Pedals setup, this is pretty much comparable. Profiles for games. Learning curve. Etc. If you're coming from a plug and play joypad, it will be a real chore. Just set up defaults for your game of choice (hopefully supported) and start from there. I used defaults for Dirt 2.0 for a day, then went online for superior settings (a la google). I found that less feedback was a better experience for me.

Pedals are comparable in quality/functionality to my all-plastic Thrustmaster Flight Pedals. The metal pads do add a much better tactile feel/immersion. Technically, they should last far longer than all plastic pedals. However, the failure point is likely to be in the all-plastic base or plastic pedal attachment mechanisms. So I don't see the overall device lasting much longer just because the pedals are metal. But I'll take metal when I can get it...

Wheel is amazing to me. I don't have any other point of reference except my lanky old retro flight yoke that I also used for racing games back in the day. Materials and weighting feel very professional, not like plastic junk. The customization options are very impressive. I'm definitely underutilizing and will likely never take advantage of all the options. And that's a good thing...

This is 100% recommended.

title: Good with caveats
text:
I've used the standard Quest 2 strap as well as the Elite strap. This sits somewhere in-between them both...

To me the Standard strap is horrible. Creates a tremendous amount of pressure on the face and leads to a large amount of sweating.

The Elite strap was a great improvement. Sadly mine developed a crack after about 10 hours of use and I sent it back for RMA replacement. I've been waiting for two months for them to send me my replacement... Even after numerous emails.

So I was very excited to see the Dethinton strap.

Size: The Dethinton is an "Elite-like" strap that actually, really, fits into cases made to fit the regular and Elite straps. I have two cases that I purchased specifically because they could fit an Elite and Elite with Battery. This strap fits into those cases easily.

Packaging: The Dethinton strap comes in a nice case with Quest-like graphics on it. The case is generic, without the Dethinton name on it. Likely that we'll see many name-brands using the same design in the same box.

Strap: The build quality is very good and a perfect match for the Quest 2. Strap portion seems a little thicker than the Elite strap, so most likely less prone to breakage. The sides of the straps behind the ear bulge about 1" away from my skull on either side. Significantly more clearance than the Elite strap - but likely reducing stress points that caused the Elite strap to crack so quickly. Its a bit less esthetically pleasing, but much so.

Padding: The rear padding is removable and secures firmly using Velcro. I don't see this coming off regularly. The top strap is high quality and is sweatproof on the side that is touching your scalp. The temple area attachments that affix to the Quest 2 are sturdy. They take significantly more effort to affix to the Quest 2 than the Elite or Standard straps.

Adjustability: The Dethinton is fully adjustable, just like the Elite strap. However, the Dethinton strap makes a very cheap, toy-like noise when you twist the screw on the back to decrease the strap circumference. The sound is very "plastic-toy ratchety" and does not inspire long-term confidence. However, sound aside, the adjustment is very secure (and possibly a sign of a heavier-duty and sturdier mechanism).

Overall this is an excellent strap. The only downsides are the difficulty of attaching the strap to the Quest 2 (non-issue if you won't be taking it off) and the ratchety sound of the wheel on the rear of the strap.

Already I feel like a fool for purchasing an official Quest 2 Elite strap. Paid 2x as much and its been in the hands of Oculus MUCH LONGER that it was in my hands...

Save yourself some pain and just purchase this instead.

title: Feels like a movie, not a video game
text:
This comes with two Metro games, and both are decent games.

The first game, Metro 2033 is an alright game, but has some frustrating aspects to it. One of the most annoying things about it are the long videos it makes you watch. Overall, it feels like you're just watching a movie, not playing a game. There is so much talking it's insane, and boring. And oddly enough, you would think the long conversations would explain everything, but they don't. You have to find journals and read them so the plot makes more sense.

The other most annoying part is the actual killing. The monsters you kill seem to always take a different amount of bullets to kill. Oddly enough, sometimes your little revolver will bring down a beast with one shot to the head, while your AK47 takes a couple bursts of fire. Other times my revolver headshot wouldn't bring down the beast in one shot. There is no consistency in the killing which makes it annoying. Once the beast is dead, it will take forever to fall down, so you will still be shooting it and wasting ammo not knowing it's dead already. Usually the shotgun will take 2 shots to kill something, but sometimes it takes 4 for no apparent reason...

You can customize guns with basic add-ons, but it's pointless because you can just go kill somebody who has the same gun with more attachments on it for free. So every time I found a place to customize my guns, I just walked past it.

Also, whenever somebody is talking, you have to look directly at their head to hear it. If you want to look around while somebody is talking to you, you won't hear a word they say. This gets fun when a group is talking...

The second game is pretty similar to the first, but the overall feel is improved a little bit. However, you will still be watching tons of boring videos and conversations.

What I like about these games is that you can choose to play as more of a survivalist, or make it more of a shooter. There are also plenty of opportunities to explore areas that are otherwise not required by the main quest. You also have several opportunities to sneak around in the dark and kill your enemies silently rather than go in guns blazing.

For the price, this game is worth getting. Just be aware you will be watching tons of videos and listening to way too many conversations, and the combat needs a little work.

title: So Relieved After Beating It
text:
I bought this game after reading these reviews, and I just now beat it. Here is what I like and don't like:

What I Like:
This game is long. My Steam account says it took me 23 hours on medium difficulty. If you explore more, and frequently hide to wait out bad situations, the game will take longer. If you try to run through the game, run past people, and avoid secondary rooms, this game might be shorter for you.

Alien Isolation is definitely scary. Another reviewer put it best when saying you should not play this if you have a heart condition! The developers did an excellent job creating an overall scary environment, and a creepy feel throughout the game. I like that this game is not all about trying to use the typical jump scares, or darkness to scare you. Those tactics get old quick. In this game you will quickly find that you are creeped out when nothing is even happening. There may be nothing around, nothing jumping out at you, and no darkness, but you will be scared. It's the unknown that gets you. Not knowing if the vent in the ceiling has something in it, what lies beyond a mysterious door, or whether you are making too much noise. And not to forget, not knowing if you are being followed.

The developers did a good job making the game unique to each player's style. I would disagree with saying the alien "learns" based on what you do as some reviewers have put it. I think those players probably just did the same thing over and over again and made it easy to be caught. If you use all available options for different situations, you will be successful without being unfairly punished. I played this on medium difficulty and actually found the alien to be quite "dumb" many times, such as walking past me, or when I'm doing the shuffle game with him on one side of a table, and me on the other, keeping him on opposing sides without being discovered.

The environment is fun. There are lots of things to interact with, stories to read, and places to explore. There are lots of things to find or do that are secondary to your main objective. The environment constantly changes on this old space ship too. It creaks, moans, changes, and falls apart as you are on it.

Noise is important and it makes the game interesting. How you choose to deal with situations will dictate how much noise you make, and how much noise you make will decide how much you see the alien. Whatever you do, don't run, and minimize using guns.

You can craft items which is cool. However, I found myself hoarding tons of crafted items without ever using them. I actually beat the game without ever using a flashbang or smoke bomb, and having only used other items to see what they did. But it does provide you with unique options for situations.

What I don't like:
Sometimes it gets annoying when the alien is constantly hunting you, in one specific area. How could the alien be so interested in me that he ignores the rest of the HUGE SPACE SHIP!!?? The alien would often hunt me in some random room and then refuse to leave me alone, even though there are other humans standing around in the open and making noise elsewhere on the ship. This annoyed me a little bit.

Some things get really drawn out and you may forget what your original objective even was. For example, the elevator breaks and you spend the next hour on a detour, forgetting what you were doing in the first place. The ending of the game is also a little drawn out, but maybe it's more "realistic". Decide for yourself.

Overall I'm happy with this game and will play it again on the hardest difficulty because I know there are places I did not explore, and I would like to mess around and use different tactics next time.

Buy this game.

title: Fun but nothing too amazing
text:
As a lifelong Halo fan, this is what I think of the Master Chief Collection...

Multiplayer has been having problems but should be fixed now so I'm not going to talk about that as all the reviews complain about it.

As for single player, the first two Halo games have been remastered and it's definitely cool to see them with new graphics. I also love that you can press a button and instantly switch to original graphics. It's amazing to see the difference.

What I don't like about the updated graphics is that they basically just upped the brightness and added tons of new lights to make the graphics look better. They did a great job but some of the more dark/creepy areas are now bright with random lights, taking away from the unknown and making it boring. What used to be a drop off into the infinite darkness is now a drop off into a well lit up hole.

What I really hate is there is no theater mode for campaign. On Halo 3 and 4 you could record video and take screenshots on campaign. Say bye to that. Apparently there is limited theater mode for select multiplayer game types. This is sad because going into theater and watching a game from a 3rd person perspective or even the enemy's perspective was a lot of fun on Halo 3.

Beware this does not include ODST or Reach which are two of my favorites. Halo 3 and 4 have not been remastered.

I would still recommend buying this for the updated graphics on the first two Halos. And the multiplayer is fun, especially playing old Halo 2 maps. You can play those in the original graphics or remastered.

I guess I just had my expectations too high for this. I still like it as a loyal Halo fan though.

text:

Instead of being able to find all quest items in one area, you must manually switch quests or fulfill the entire quest to go back and dig up another item. The gift receive button is the same as the quest accept button making it hard, if possible at all, to accept a gift when a villager has a quest for you as well. It is very easy for people on XBOX LIVE to steal your gold. (Over 5 million gold of mine was stolen before I knew what was happening.) Repairing homes takes too much time and makes renting out property too much hassle for what it's worth. (Can I get a 'repair all' button?). Many other glitches in-game (the dog doesn't fetch when playing fetch.)

Final Thoughts: The game makes itself hard to play. Your dog, who is supposed to help you find treasure, often runs in circles while barking with a treasure symbol over its head, instead of leading you to it. And the same with dig sites. Lionhead Studios should have had a staff member or tester actually play the game before they released it.

title: Simple and fun game for young kids
text:
We got this for our DD for Christmas last year. She was 5. She had no problem playing the game on her own and it really kept her interest for a fair amount of time compared to other games. It is simple - no reading involved for the really little ones so they can navigate on your own. There is no fear of "dying" in the game or racing against a clock so it's good for young ones there as well.

Basically the kids can care for the hamsters - feed, water, exercise, put to bed, potty, etc. - and then they can also run them through tracks to earn points. You unlock more hamsters as you play the game and make it through the various mazes. With this being a larger head strap, most headphones will not fit on your head while using this. Wired earbuds are still able to be used with this head strap. The instructions also do not show how to take off the included head strap, which can be difficult for new users to do considering that the Quest itself does not come with instructions to change the head strap.

title: Weapons & Armor Pleeeease!
text:
I gave this game a whooping 5 stars, but that doesn't mean I loved everything about it, though it does mean what I didn't like wasn't due to a fault on the part of the programmers, rather that my displeasure arose from the simple fact the progression of weapons and armor was, in my opinion, poorly done. At level 20 I was getting - still - level 6 & 7 armor and level 9 swords and the like. I've been playing video games since the first game I ever played, (Star Trek Space, written by my husband on the Commodore 64, so I am not new to the gaming world or role playing titles by any means. As a former Software Etc. Manager, I was in a unique position to play the latest and greatest games on the highest end machines, (again, due to my husband's design & assembly talents), and these all began with poor graphics, excellent storylines, and the hope of keeping a particular company alive to do better as the machines improved all performance areas. Inquisition is a marvel of gaming titles, in that the storyline is adequate to keep one's interest, the graphics take full advantage of the PS4's capabilities and the characters are, (finally), diversified enough to represent races that have formerly been suspiciously absent in gaming's vast universe.
BUT...come on, 1 point for each level progressed? Would be great if there were but, say 4 areas to improve, but there aren't, and each area has multiple subareas to be "grown" so your character(s) can fight the dragons with a reseasonable hope of victory. Needing 40,000 points to gain a level isn't unusual, but the weapons and armor gathered from the battlefield after defeating one's enemies should garner valuable gear not readily found elsehwere, or perhaps not easily obained through creation at a forge. I like the idea of making and enchanting gear, and I found the blueprint method of doing so fun, but I made armor better than the best I ever found after playing 360 hours and defeating all comers with tenacity, tact, and sheer willingness to restart fights 3 or 4 times before winning them. I enjoyed exploring the map, (yes, the time I spent in the land of the programmers took me to places I was stuck in, nearly went blind from clipping in, and walked off precipices unseen resulting in my death), but in the end it was worth the effort. A game that is great fun and not frustrating other than the poor weapons and armor progression. I may be alone here, but M&M 1-10, Wizardry, Skyrim, and others all had a way of letting the player obtain better weapons and armor with each level gained, and yes some of those were hard fought for, but at least they were available. Kill a dragon get a level 3 sword? Kill a boss and get, what...some gold and a crappy shield? A 5 star effort, with a 4.0 gear progression system.

title: One bullet - one kill
text: I learned that motto is from the Army and might have been used as early as WWII. However, in the movie, "Sniper", it is more than a motto, it is the religion. A sniper taking two shots to complete what one should have, is a dead sniper. Stealth is the ticket to success here, and the game uses reality as its model which makes success something very difficult to obtain. A good thing? Maybe and maybe not. Games are meant to be fun, simulations are meant to teach. This title wants to be both, but leans heavily toward the latter over the former. Points are to be earned , a ranking to be improved, and a lot of targets to get rid of. BUT, weather is a large factor in a sniper's life, and the wind can play havoc with a bullet in flight, exposure can be the difference between success and dying, after being caught and perhaps "questioned", though that is not a part of this program. I like a game that rewards careful, intelligent play with better weapons and higher ranks, the point system doesn't really interest me beyond using those points like money, to buy better sniper rifles, scopes and ammunition. Use of camouflage is incorporated and movement is a factor - be a heavy-footed storm trooper and your target will either disappear or be protected to the point of having to bomb his location to the dissatisfaction of your bosses and yourself. Your own hands may shake in other games, but if they do here-you will miss your target. Nerves of steel, eyes like a hawk, and the best equipment available at the time, plus the overall gameplay and number of missions work to make this a top game in the genre, but this is not just a 1st person shooter. Run and gun will NOT work here. One point was not given, making the difference between a great game and a fantastic game. My reason for this was just this: it was perhaps too reality rooted for my ability to deal with the variables of the occupation. My fault I know, and I know this is not a problem for some, (my own son is an excellent shot in real life and found the game to be very compelling, even as realistic as he thought any game should get), but for the vast users of the title, I doubt the highest level of difficulty will ever be realized. I play at the easy level, (the only shooter I must do this with), and still have trouble, on the normal level of difficulty things get darn-right frustrating. For reality, fun, and replayability this is a solid 4-star title that is well worth the cost of admission. For those looking to be a living-room sniper, this might be a bit too challenging, in that the targets and others react to a missed shot or a guard down instead of the target. Brutal on the most difficult level of play, but a great challenge for those more apt to seek a living by living the "one shot - one kill" religious life.

title: PS4 Christmas
text:
At 60, with 24 hours to 61, I was given a PlayStation 4 by my son. With a PS3 already hooked to the 100" screen & projector, he set this new game console up for me and provided 3 games to keep me up from Christmas morning to bedtime the following day! With unbeatable graphics capability, truly ergonomic controller, and a super fast, multi-core chip, the PS4 is without a doubt the premiere console on the market today. I had Assassin's Creed: Black Flag for the PS3 so I had to purchase the upgraded version for the PS4, but I paid only $10 with the promo code that came with the game. Now I play it exclusively on the PS4, the graphics are far better, the game plays faster and the multitasking capabilities of the PS4 make it all the more fun to use. I have gone from the game to the internet, (for hints only-I hate cheats or so-called "Time Savers", and then right back to the game without missing a beat. Movies stream smoother than on the PS3 or the Roku 2 or 3, (I have both), and when playing a Blu-ray or DVD movie, it far more quiet, the motor is nearly silent, which I can't say for the PS3, which I enjoyed for the past 31/2 yrs. This is a console I look forward to having a very long time and adding games & movie titles to my growing collection. In brief then: Sturdy construction, silent running, excellent streaming, great sound reproduction, ergonomic controller with more controls available through the use of the touchpad, easy install, included cables for controller and earpiece, fun factor, ease of software use, overall confidence in the Sony brand, finally-let's face it, this is another PlayStation and who wouldn't want one? title: I love the concept, but certain things take away from the fun
text:
I love the idea of this game. Basically you play a character who chooses to quit taking his "joy" pill and instead try to remember the past, which is mostly your brother and what happened to him along with the rest of the world. The joy pill basically is a pill that does what it says. It makes you happy and joyful, and forget all your troubles. While on joy everything around you appears bright and colorful and safe. While off it you see the truth, a foggy and dull world full of rotten food, etc.

So the idea is great! I love it. However, my biggest problem with it are the following:

Food and water: You have to eat and drink water every so often. Failing to do so results in low stamina which means you can't run for as long, and it also affects fighting.

Sleep: This too affects your stamina if you fail to get enough of it.

The above (food, water, and sleep) offer no fun to the game at all. It's just annoying as hell to deal with. Why they thought this would add value is beyond me. Never once during any other game that I've played in the past did I say to myself "Boy, I wish my character required food, water, and sleep. That'd be so much fun!" -- NOT! It's annoying. The only game that gets away with that are the Sims.

Another annoyance: There comes a point in the game where you'll be made to take joy pills to blend in with the town you're in. The problem is Joy pills only lasts 1-2 minutes in real time. It's highly frustrating having to constantly search for a booth (where the pills are located) every 2 minutes when all I really want to do is explore. And no, you cannot fill a bottle with pills. You may be able to find a loose pill that can be carried with you here and there, but overall you'll be relying on booths. If you fail to take your pill on time the crowd will attack you. Even if you hurry and run into a booth to take it, they're still after you! So if you plan to explore, good luck. I struggled so I gave up.

Furthermore, there are glitches and bugs with the game still. I feel they released it too early. They should have waited until they were fixed.

Overall, still an enjoyable game. Could be better is all.

You can choose to enter the building any way you wish. Maybe on your first play through you'll want to enter the sewer first in order to get up into the building. Then maybe on your second play through you'll change it up by entering the front door. Then on the third play through you may decide to enter through one of the windows up top.

There are multiple ways to kill people too. You can keep it simple by killing them with a sword or other simple weapons. Or, you can get creative with your powers (these powers get upgraded by you as you make your way through the game) and do something such as create a swarm of rats to kill your target. You can get even more creative by having your target shoot themselves. This involves freezing/slowing time just as they shoot off their gun, giving you just enough time to then possess them so you can walk their body right in front of the bullet and then toss them into it, thus killing them.

So if you think you'll just memorize it from your first play through, guess again. You'll have to figure out the code a second time because they will change it on you.

If you want the bad ending, you're free to kill as many people as you want (the bad ending is much easier to achieve). If you want the good ending, you'll have to be more careful by doing your best to be stealthy and not kill anyone or to kill as few people as you possibly can. This can be done by choking your victims or putting them to sleep with a sleep dart. When you do, you have to put them in a safe place so this way other guards won't see them and rats won't reach them and kill them.

Overall, it's an amazing game. Get it if you enjoy stealth games!

title: Love it, but it needs more games
text:
Let me start off by saying I am a long time Nintendo fan. I started out in the early 90's with an NES, followed by an N64, followed by the Wii, and now the Wii U.

I love Nintendo for allowing backwards compatibility on the Wii U and for allowing us to transfer our content from the original Wii onto the Wii U. I have to say this though, the instructions made it tough to transfer at first between the two consoles. I ended up having to go to a youtube video just to see how it was done and I finally managed to do it. Just make sure you have an SD card, as well as your original wii remotes ready (preferably 2 wii remotes if you have them. 1 will do the job, but that requires constant syncing and unsyncing between the Wii U and the original Wii console. If you have 2, then you just need 1 remote synced to each console, making it much easier and faster to transfer your content). Keep in mind, once you transfer your content, your original Wii is empty. Everything you did is now on the Wii U.

Now, let's move onto the Gamepad. The gamepad is an interesting way to play. I personally did not think I would like the gamepad that much (I am very picky when it comes to controllers), but I actually do find it to be quite fun to play on. Some games, like Nintendo land, have you use it a lot. Then there are others, such as Super Mario U, that give you the option to use the gamepad or the original Wii Remote. With Nintendo Land, you can do fun things such as tilt the remote to move your character around. Then there are others that allow you to use the gamepad to look around, almost giving you that full 3D effect in a sense. It's definitely different from any other console out there!

Furthermore, the gamepad makes navigation a lot easier in comparison to the original Wii. On the original Wii, typing on the keyboard required you to use the wii remote to point at each letter on the TV screen (this was a pain in the behind because it was such a slow process!!!). Now, on the Wii U, the keyboard is on your gamepad, allowing you to select each letter the same way you would on a tablet. This makes navigation so much quicker and a lot less frustrating!

The TVii is a good tool to have as well. I have not played around with it too much yet (I rarely watch TV these days anymore), but I have checked it out. I do enjoy the TV guide they provide for you on the Gamepad, allowing you to scroll through it and select a particular show you want to watch. If you already have a TV guide on your TV to begin with though, then you probably won't be as amazed by this feature because you already have it. Personally, for me, I love it because we are old school in my house. We just have regular cable with no guide, so having it on the Wii U gamepad is really useful for me.

Also, similar to the original Wii, you still have Netflix, Hulu Plus, Youtube, etc. Again, these things are FAR more easier to navigate thanks to the keyboard on the gamepad now.

One thing that disappoints me so far is the lack of games. I currently play two games: Nintendo Land and Super Mario U. No other games really interest me at this moment, but I do hear they are in the process of making them later on in the year, which is good news. You can either be an early bird like me and get this console now, so that way you are all set and prepared for the new releases in the fall. Or you can hold off and just wait until the titles are available before buying the console. I personally like to be prepared ahead of time, so that way I'm not forking up all my money at once, but that is just me.

Lastly, I want to talk about MiiVerse. This was another feature that I did not think I would use much, but I actually find myself posting quite a bit on there. MiiVerse is a way for you to connect with anyone worldwide. You can share comments, start discussions, give each other tips on how to beat a level, etc. You can even draw and post your drawings. I have hand written messages on there, as well as typed messages, and some drawings. The pen that comes with the gamepad makes drawing very easy and fun. You can draw just as good as if you were using a pen on paper. It is that accurate!

Overall, the Wii U is a great console! As I said, it just needs more games, but the games will come as time passes. What we have now are just the launch titles. So again, either hold off and wait for the games to come, or get yourself the Wii U console now and just play your original Wii games on it until more Wii U games come out.

title: I really wanted to love this game, but I just couldn't.
text:
First off, I am a big Assassins Creed fan. I especially loved the Ezio franchise due to the story, the awesome gameplay, and the fact that Ezio himself was such a bada$$. I beat all of the Ezio games within a week because I was so eager to finish the story.

Then, AC3 came out. I was very excited to continue the story. However, I was disappointed and here is why:
-Connor is boring. I'm sorry to put it so bluntly, but it is the truth. He bores me. There is nothing exciting about him at all. When it came to Ezio, he at least made me feel like a true Assassin. With Connor, however, I just don't get that same feeling because his character is so dull.
-There is too much running around! I swear, I can't tell you how many times I had to literally run, and run, and run some more to get from point A to point B. You are slowed down by so many things too, such as a mountain range. I will be running in a straight line, but then bam there is a mountain in my way and I have to figure out a way around it.
-Too many cut scenes. I enjoy cut scenes, but not when they are as excessive as this game is. I feel like I'm watching a movie with the amount of heavy cut scenes they added to this game.
-The story is on the dull side. I get bored to the point where I stop paying attention anymore.
-I feel as though all I do is fight those guards at times. It's fun at first, but it loses it's appeal quickly. You can only fight so many guards before it gets repetative and therefore boring. The older games, such as AC2, were not anywhere near this bad when it came to the guards. The guards chased you down in the older games, but it was not as excessive as AC3 is.
-Most importantly, this is the FIRST AC game that I put down and have yet to finish. I do plan to finish it one of these days for the sake of the story line, but the game is just such a big disappointment that I can't pick up the controller just yet. In time I will, but I need a break from this terrible game.

It saddens me to leave a bad review. I gave it 3 stars only because it is an AC game and it is fun to a very small extent. I do like to know what happens in the story too. Other than that though, it's just not a super fun game like the others before it.

title: This game made a gamer out of me again!
text:
For the past 10 years or so, I was not much of a gamer. There was no game out there that really brought me in and made me want to play it for longer than 1 hour at a a time. My boyfriend has an XBox 360 and tried to get me interested into a variety of different games, but none of them held my interest. We came to the conclusion that I was simply not into gaming.

However, one game finally did grab my attention. That was this game, "Assassin's Creed 2." At first I simply watched, but later I found myself asking "Hey, can I take the controller for a bit?"

The story is downright amazing. You play as Ezio Auditore da Firenze, an assassin who witnessed the hanging of his father and brothers. He then seeks vengeance against the Templar Order, and their Grand Master, Rodrigo Borgia, who had ordered the execution. Ezio is a highly likable, strong character. When you see his family being executed, you feel anger rise within you. You are rooting for him to take revenge. You want him to succeed and you can't wait for him to complete his quest! If a video game can make you feel the same emotions as your character, then it's definitely a great story. The characters are so deep. It really brings you in. You feel like you are Ezio.

Throughout the game you are given various missions to complete. My favorite mission types involved the ones where you had to quietly follow a particular individual and attempt to kill them. It's one of those missions where you have to be careful and know where your boundaries are if you wish to be successful. There are a lot of missions throughout this game, most of which involve killing, but you are an assassin after all so this makes sense. The killings can be interesting. As the game goes on you will learn how to kill two opponents at one time, how to disarm an opponent, how to kill with a single stab, etc.

As for the controls, they take getting used to in the beginning, but you will quickly learn how everything works. Pretty soon you will find yourself climbing buildings, jumping, and leaping from great heights into a haystack without a problem (aka leap of faith).

Overall, this game is the reason I purchased an XBox 360 for myself. I went from someone who plays practically no video games to someone who plays 5-6 hours per day. I'm not sure if I should be proud of that, but at least we know this is a fun game! If you are a fan of adventure games, then purchase this one! You will not be disappointed.

title: Go with 4 GB and then get a 320 GB hard drive
text:
I originally was searching high and low for a 250 GB Xbox 360 console. I had the option to order it online, but I chose to go out to a store instead to be safe (I don't trust online orders if the amount is high). I ended up visiting my local Target. The most they had was the 4 GB console. I was reluctant to purchase it at first, until I learned that I can buy a hard drive to add more space. I ended up purchasing the 4 GB console at Target for $180 (this was the sale price when I went). I also got a $20 gift card on top of that, since it was offered at the time I went, which was a bonus for sure.

I then searched for a hard drive. I was going to get a 250 GB hard drive, until I saw a 320 GB one with Lego Star Wars 3. I ended up getting the 320 GB, since it was a good deal (only $100 at Best Buy at the time I went there).

Overall, the point I am trying to make here is that it is well worth it to get the 4 GB and then get a hard drive for it (preferably the 320 GB if you ask me, but it is up to you of course). I ended up spending a total of only $280 to turn my XBox 360 into a 320 GB console, whereas the retail price for the original 250 GB console is $300.

I would also like to add that this XBox console is NICE! It is very quiet compared to the older models and the games play very smoothly. This console comes with AV cables, but I chose to not use them. I instead use my HDMI cable that I purchased on my own a few years ago. This makes the picture appear more sharp and crisp, similar to a Blu Ray compared to a standard DVD. Also, I love the built in Wi-fi feature.

title: Reminds me of Super Mario 64, but better!!!
text:
When I was a kid my friend and I would play Super Mario 64 constantly! It was such a fun game with amazing graphics (for the time it was released in that is), amazing 3D play, different worlds to choose from with over 100 stars to collect, etc. It was HOURS of fun and I honestly never thought they would ever make a Mario game like this one again. This saddened me, for I truly did want to play a sequel to SM64.

Until about a week ago, I won this game off of ebay for a fraction of Amazon's price (I prefer to write my reviews on Amazon over ebay ... don't ask why lol). I was so happy I got this because it arrived in the mail yesterday and so far I have played all day yesterday and all day today. It truly is an amazing game and reminds me of SM64. Mario still has most of the same movements as he did in 64 (back flip, triple jump, etc) so it feels like a sequel in a sense. It's as if my childhood was brought back to me at the age of 21. It truly does put a smile on my face =)

Now, let's go further into detail with this game: You use the nunchuck and wii remote to play this game. Some people have complained, saying they want the option to use the classic wii controller, but in all honesty I am not at all bothered by this. To me the nunchuck with the wii remote is exactly like any regular old controller, just that it allows you to separate your left hand from your right hand. Plus, Nintendo didn't have much of a choice to begin with because the controls in this game involve aiming your wii remote at the screen in some parts to collect star bits (helpful little items that allow you to pay for things or stun enemies), turn into a bubble and float around in the galaxies, steer yourself on top of a rolling ball or sting ray that's in the water, etc. So to those wishing they had the classic controller, there are just far too many controls in this game for Nintendo to have done this with just a normal controller.

Now, going even further into detail: The object of this game is to go from galaxy to galaxy, collecting as many stars as you can, again similar to SM64. Some stars are extremely easy in my book, but others are definitely more challenging and require several tries before you manage to get the star. Even on the stars that are overly easy, it is still a ton of fun to play. I enjoy in certain galaxies where I can jump anywhere I want and I can never fall off! After all, it is SMG so we know gravity is meant to pull you down in this game to prevent you from falling (so long as no black holes are around to suck you in that is ... those you have to watch out for). I also enjoy the newer power ups in this game such as having Mario turn into a bee where he has the ability to fly and stick to the bee hive, or Boo Mario who can turn invisible and slip through solid bars and float to higher places, or ice mario where he can freeze water and walk on it. I haven't beaten the game yet, so I do not know all of the power ups, but I love the power ups I'm seeing so far!

I do have ONE complaint about this game though that I also had with SM64. That is the camera angles. At times I have died in this game as a result of poor camera angles. I'd have times where I was unable to see where I was going and then suddenly run into an enemy or something. Sure, you have the ability to adjust the camera angles on your own, but even when I do this I'd still have a bit of trouble or I wouldn't be fast enough because something decided to come attack me. Despite this one flaw, I still feel the game deserves a 5 star rating. It is that good!

Overall, if you were a fan of Super Mario 64 then you will love this game. I highly recommend this game to any Mario fans =)

title: A game that deserved more recognition
text:
I first played this game about 10 years ago while I was a kid. It was fun then, and still is to this day at the age of 21. It is a game designed for those who enjoy puzzles. This is basically like a 3D puzzle game. You are a beach ball, controlling your way through this 3D puzzle world in search of keys. These keys open up the exit block, which allow you to continue to the next level. Along the way you are, avoiding traps such as spikes that pop you or ice that causes you to slip off the edge, etc. The first levels are easy, but then you run into even more complications along the way such as invisible blocks or blocks with burners on them or blocks that only allow you to travel in one direction or blocks that break apart shortly after jumping on them. It is hard to fully describe how challenging this game can get through a review alone, but trust me this game gets hard as you get higher and higher into the levels! And it's fun too because it forces you to think! At times I'll find myself replay a single level 10 times, thinking of how I should complete it without failing again. And when I do figure it out I feel accomplished because it was so challenging. Sure it might be frustrating because it's hard at times to have to replay and replay and replay until you figure it out, but at the same time it is fun. It wouldn't be fun without a challenge!

Also, this game is rare. I have a copy right now at home that I plan to keep forever. I see some people trying to sell it for a pretty penny (not everyone, but a lot of people try selling it for $100+ on some websites). I wouldn't sell it for any price. It's far too much fun to give up. I also wish they would create a sequel, but I highly doubt it'll ever happen since this game didn't get enough recognition for a sequel. However, it most certainly deserved the recognition nonetheless.

If you enjoy puzzle games, I recommend this one.

title: So much fun ... Makes me feel like a kid again =)
text:
When I was a kid I was big on video games. I had numerous NES, N64, and Sega Genesis games that I always played. Anyway, I am currently 21 years old and have had a hard time enjoying a lot of the newest video games of today because I personally enjoy the old school feel of video games, vs. today's more modern games. My boyfriend got this game for me as a Christmas gift and I am so happy he did because it is a ton of fun!! It brings back memories from when I sat on my NES all day long or Sega Genesis or N64. It really does give you that "old school video game" feel as you play it, while still keeping excellent graphics and scenes and game controls as you play your way through the levels. This game absolutely amazes me with the scenery in it from oceans to jungles to forests, etc. The game play is excellent. I love shaking the wii remote and nunchuck (or the wii remote alone if you prefer to play with just the wii remote) to do the ground pound to unlock secret items or areas in the game. I also really enjoy this on one player when you have the ability to use Diddy kong on your back as a jet pack. 2 player is also fun because you play as Donkey Kong, while your partner plays as Diddy Kong. Your partner can either run through the level with you or jump on your back from time to time, which allows you to use the jet pack for more precise jumps.

I will admit, I have never played any of the older Donkey Kong games, so I unfortunately can not compare. However, as an old school video game lover who has never played a single Donkey Kong game in the past before this one, I absolutely LOVE this game and regret the fact that I didn't play any others like it in the past. This game does make me want to go backwards though by playing some of the older Donkey Kong games.

All in all, I highly recommend this game. It is so much fun and I am extremely happy that my boyfriend purchased this for me =)

I bought this controller over the Razer Kishi because I also wanted the option to use it with my iPad. It worked great for the PS1 ports I was playing and the few Apple Arcade games I played. That would happen no matter what I played. I think it has to do with the battery getting low. Speaking of the battery, the controller uses mini USB to charge instead of Type-C in 2022, which means having yet another cable to carry. There are also no “select” and “start” buttons which typically are used as a button to call up a game’s world map.

What this controller does right is it’s easy to connect, charges fast, is energy efficient AF, and has an overall good feel if you don’t mind light plasticky feeling gamepads. The buttons and joysticks feel solid, and the triggers feel alright with tension that’s good enough. It does feel robust though.

The colors are fun, and the general function is there, but for the price, there is better on the market.

I do not believe this controller is worth $50. I thought I was happy with it and could handle its “quirks” until I realized it's missing L3/R3, which have been on controllers since the PS2. title: Best Combination of Stealth and Assault yet, for XBOX
text:
The best combination of stealth and assault yet!

Splinter Cell Blacklist is a great combination of using both stealth and assault attacks for various missions. The side missions each have their own style, some requiring absolute stealth while others almost require a visible attack. I did, however, run into a glitch at the end of the last coop mission for Briggs COOP Mission 4 and that is why I gave this game 4 instead of 5 stars. I and a random player from Xbox Live fought through the whole mission and got trapped in a non-completing sequence where we were left restarting the check point over and over to a hoard of enemies that eventually stopped and left us nothing to do. Other than that heartbreaker I would give the game 5 stars. (UPDATE: Ubisoft has stated a update is coming out to correct this glitch)

I really liked the purchasing of the weapons and gadgets as well as the ability to customize the components of most. This added a little extra fun for someone like me who is OCD with their games. The storyline was cool (as are all of the Xbox 360 games in this series). I was all in all happy with this purchase and would recommend this to anyone who likes games beyond "hack and slash" and FPS (first person shooter) genres

title: Mortal Kombat
text:
It was "Portal Kombat" week, and if you're one of the cool and geeky gamer kids you know exactly what I mean. I had my toss up between buying Mortal Kombat, or Portal 2 (or even both). I made my choice and I went ahead and pre ordered Mortal Kombat off of amazon. I got my pre order 10$ credit, and my pre order bonus code for a character, outfit and fatality.

I am so glad I had gotten Mortal Kombat (9). The story mode is amazing. It kept me so interested. It's like a remastered remake of Mortal Kombat 1-3. Also there's added background story, and some new characters like "noob", "kratos", and "cyber subzero". Even background story on "cyrax". Mind you I know nothing about mortal Kombat history except what I was told and what I've seen on Mortal Kombat versus DC Universe. Anyway, I was so excited to find out why cyrax became cyber cyrax, and I even got to play with his human form and such in story mode. I felt so bad for Scorpian, even worse for Subzero. Raiden is amazing in the story as well. Oh I even learned some history about kitana, and gosh... that Mileena girl is a freak. I'm trying so hard to not give any story mode spoilers.

Oh, okay. So there's this challenge tower, full of 300 challenges. It's so fun, once you hit 25 you ding a achievement then another for completing 100... But some challenges are tough as well..

Online play right now is laggy and takes forever.. Not sure if a update will correct this. The game itself comes with a online play code which will activate the online play, (meaning don't buy the game used or else you buy the code from xbox. one time use only).

The ladder/arcade has some hidden fights (so fun, I love secrets and they ding achievevements). The ladder is fairly easy to complete. Complete it with every char and ding a achievement.

The graphics are superb and absolutely stunning. I am very happy with this game, I am still playing it, I've only had it about a week now, but I'm loving it. I'm sure any fighting game fan or Mortal Kombat fan will feel the same. It's so worth getting.

title: Finally Weather!!!
text:
For years now I have begged and written in numerous Sim fan forums about how badly I wanted EA to focus on giving our Sims a more community like feel, with carnivals, events, and holiday gatherings that would take place in town square. Similar to Nintendo's Animal Crossing.

Granted the Sims are nothing like Animal Crossing, it irritated me that such a simple basic game like that could offer a more community atmosphere than my Sims games could in an open world on a PC!

When EA released Sims 3 Seasons, it felt as if the developers had read every word, every plea I had ever had for my beloved game. Finally I got everything I was looking for. Right down to being able to finally swim in the freaking ocean!

What The New Expansion Pack Offers:

The Sims 3 Seasons packed in all 4 major seasons which rotate according to your own preferences. You can adjust how long each season will last in the options tabs.

During the summer months, your Sims can go to the beach, get a tan or sun burn, and host pool parties. At the very last day of every season, a community event will take place in the new town park. This park is a magical place and it rotates and it decorated with each passing season, according to the season. At this community event you will find an onslaught of new things for your Sims to do, from carnival games, to rides, and new postcard picture booths.

During the fall season, your Sims can visit the park to pick pumpkins, and later bring them home to care them. It added a real sense of family tradition to the game, which I appreciated.

During the spring season, your Sims can visit the park to hunt for east eggs that will be hidden around the area.

The charm is there all right, but after cycling through all 4 seasons a few times, visiting the community park got somewhat repetitive.

However things added that really lit up my world was the fact that the fun did not just end at the community park, the Seasons expansion pack added a day for your children to go trick or treating in the fall. Teens can play pranks like lighting bags of poo on fire on the front porch of their victims, or throwing eggs.

Besides just that, the fall season also allows you to host festive dinners, similar to Thanksgiving. During this event, those Sims invited to the party will bring plates of food to share at the table. I found this little extra to be endearing.

The summer season is probably the most recognized one in the game, as the summer season has not been changed in years since the release of the game. I truly wanted to just quickly hurry through the summer season, but I was glad I didn't.

The summer season adds a quirky new twist where your Sims who are outdoors for too long can either get a sunburn or a tan. They also can now swim in the ocean, and host pool parties. The community park also hosts a summer event according to the season.

Winter months of course bring in the snow, giving your Sims a holiday gift giving party, and other really fun new additions that deal with the winter season.

What I liked in particular were the new winter seasonal outfits that your Sims will change into when they go outside on cold days. We saw this in the Sims 2 already, but it was a feature we missed!

The addition of being able to click on any house in the neighborhood and add Christmas lights to their homes was probably my favorite addition to the game, and it really allows neighborhoods to sparkle and twinkle at night.

In the spring season, the Easter egg hunt takes place in the community park, as well as an array of other fun things for your Sims to do. Like kiss a girl at a kissing booth! A dunk tank would have been cool to see.

All in all the Sims 3 Seasons by far added the most and newest element to the game since it's release years ago, This is an expansion that should have taken place many years ago, but even with its very late arrival, I am happy with it. It is what we have been waiting for. And now that EA has given us what we wanted, I am sure the news of Sims 4 will soon follow.

title: Expensive
text:
I unfortunately wish I would have purchased a screen protector for my Nintendo Wii U Game Pad the exact same day I bought the console. This is primarily because my Nintendo Wii U Game Pad stylus pen came with a jagged little flaw, that I did not even recognize before it was too late.

My stylus pen had a rough edge on one side of its tip, which resulted in me really scratching up my game pads touch screen.

Once I discovered the flaw, I realized that I needed a screen protector immediately, but I also needed a new stylus.

When I came across the Wii U, Write & Protect Pack, I felt anger toward Nintendo; was this something Nintendo already knew about? How convenient! New stylus pens and screen protectors!

The package came to $9.99, which is not too bad in price, but it stinks that Amazon sells similar bundles for far, far less in price. However with me needing both a screen protector and a new stylus immediately, I went the more expensive route, so I didn't have to wait for anything to come in the mail.

What You Get:

Inside of the Wii U Write & Protect bundle, you get 2 screen protectors designed to protect your screen, and 2 different colored stylus pens. I hoped to find one with a black stylus pen to match my Game Pad, but they did not have that option available. Inside of the slim envelope sized package you will also find a Wii U screen cleaner cloth.

How To Apply:

It's pretty self explanatory, however with the added cleansing cloth, you will need to wipe down your game pads touch screen with precision. Make sure there are no hairs, fibers, or any other debris stuck to the screen, otherwise you will mess the whole application process up.

My Use:

Unfortunately I totally destroyed the first screen protection filter. When I removed the sticky side protection seal, a small piece of plastic stuck to it, which I could not get off without smudging the protector. I ended up having to toss that one, and prayed with my second attempt that some little rouge piece of plastic did not float up and land on the sticky side of the screen protector as I tried to apply it.

I luckily was able to get the second one on, but not without flaw. There were still air bubbles underneath, which were a real pain in the butt to try and work out from underneath the seal.

Once the protector was on, I noticed that my touchscreen was not quite as responsive to touch than when I did not have one on it. It's really a catch 22, without the protection you risk scratching your screen, and with it responsiveness is not as on par. You have to press harder for the screen to respond, which I found to be a little annoying, but something I can easily get used to.

When it comes to the added stylus pens, there is nothing to write home about. Just 2 new colors, and they do have a selection of colors to pick from.

The added cloth is a bonus, which I liked, as it cleans the screen and the overall game pad with ease. The microfiber texture is likely what allows it to work so perfectly. Please though, make sure that when you use it on your screen that there is no dirt on it, as you could end up scratching your screen while cleaning it off with the cloth.

Overall:

I feel like I over paid for just a small cloth, and piece of plastic. Although I have a sense of protection now when it comes to my screen, the price is just way too high for what you get, and if you mess up applying the protector, you only have 1 more attempt. For the price of this set, they could have included more screen protectors.

If you've played any other game in the series prior to this, you've already made up your mind about whether or not you like this game, it's just a question of whether you want to get this one for the new music, or if you're OK with the streaming service that comes with a monthly membership that all of your previous games had.

This cart comes with 40 songs, but only about fifteen are songs or are by artists that I'm familiar with. Yeah, I'm not the most "pop" and "dance" guy around, but that seems pretty low. There are many multicultural hits on this cart, though, and that's good for some added flavor. I wish there was a way to get more without there being a monthly fee for it. In the past, games like DDR could pack a pretty big number of choices into each game, and they got a bunch more "big" hit songs, and a wider variety of styles, genres and decades into the mix.

The children's section is particularly sparse. There are 9 different tunes for little ones, as compared to the 12 or 13 on previous releases. Be forewarned: one of the songs is the dreaded "Baby Shark".

Really, the game is just fine. I tend to prefer the long-lost dance games of old, and it seems like Just Dance is the last of a dying breed, so I'm happy to live with it. I just wish the song choice was a little better.

title: 1/2 of a Great Package
text:
This is a cartridge version of two downloadable games available on the Nintendo eshop, together in one package. Each will pop up as a separate icon on your home screen, and each functions as it's own complete game, so I'll review them as separate products.

Wheel of Fortune is not my favorite TV game show, and this game really exacerbates it's flaws. The game is slow, with many (fortunately skippable) scenes of spinning and pulling up letters. While the graphics and the flow of the game is very similar to what you'd find on the actual show, it makes the game feel plodding and slow. When you solve, you need to spell the words out, letter by letter. There are touchscreen options for handheld to allow you to almost type your answer, but letters are not arranged as a keyboard, which does make things a little harder. There are also a few odd pairings, like winning a trip to Italy in a prize puzzle about France, but that's forgivable. Ironically, I did enjoy the montage of the different countries that pop up in the prize descriptions, but overall, this game felt like one long cutscene. I'd give it a 2/5.

Jeopardy is much better. There are no cutscenes whatsoever, no spelling of answers, and not much to get in the way of the joy of simply answering trivia. The game is not perfect by any stretch. Trivia buffs will find most clues very easy, and even the hard ones are made simpler by virtue of all the clues being multiple choice. There are three separate answer choices, presented to each contestant, and the options do not change. Therefore, if the two opponents choose wrong answers, you will be presented with their wrong answer choices, as well as the correct one. title: Too Many Unlocks
text:
The original Carnival Games on Wii was a favorite at our house, and one that we played for hours on end, despite the fact that it wasn't really a "quality" game - it was just fun. The new Carnival Games is very similar - it's a shallow mini game collection in which you need to unlock just about everything, making it one of the most annoying games that I own.

The first unlockable is clothing customization, which is just fine. Earn tickets to trade in for silly hats? No problem. Options are quite limited, but this is the kind of unlockable I can get behind.

After that, though, almost everything in this game is hidden behind a wall of requiring "tickets" earned through game play. You start with only a few games, and need to unlock more as you go. It's fairly easy to play the few games one or two times apiece to earn the 75 tickets needed to unlock bowling, but it takes 2,000 to open other games, and that's going to take ages.

Motion controls, one of the calling cards of the genre, are not enabled by default, but need to be unlocked with high scores in each individual game. Despite the Switch's improved Joycon controls, motion controls are still an imperfect slog, and need to be calibrated before every game. It's also impossible for one player to use them while others use joystick controls - it's all or nothing.

The games themselves range from OK to terrible. Admittedly, I have not unlocked them all, but Skeeball and Cup toss are pretty good, as is Ring Toss, albeit long. The bowling game looks fun until you realize how easy it is - my seven year old was regularly scoring 250+ in only five replays with joystick controls. The baseball game is equally shallow, with few options and repetitive, slow swinging that allows you to hit home runs with ease, motion controls or not. The drone racing game has terrible graphics and worse controls.

Overall, this is not a recommeded purchase, except maybe for very small children.

title: Another Just Dance
text:
Just Dance 2019 is the first of the series I've played in quite some time. Just Dance was never my favorite of the music/dancing games on the original Wii, but now it's the only one left, so I guess that does speak to it's staying power.

To Just Dance fans, this is probably an automatic buy. To those like me who haven't tried out the series in some time, the game is still just OK in terms of measuring your responses, and it's got a very complicated series of menus to navigate in order to eventually get to the songs. There are a ton of options in terms of ways to play this game, and you can different controller inputs, playing with as few as one joycon if you have a group. Like you'd expect in a modern game, there's a paid subsctiption service that allows you access to a number of newer songs, and it's easy to get to from multiple menus, which feels a little pushy in terms of it's advertisement. That said, there are plenty of song choices to keep you dancing for some time, but as you learn to navigate the system, it can feel like a significant chunk of the game is hidden behind a paywall, which is disappointing to say the least.

Once you're dancing though, it's easy to forgive the game's faults, because like all dancing games, this is a great party favorite, and one that gives you a good workout as well. You won't worry quite so much about failure because it's not as hard to pick up with a song if you fall out of rhythm. In most situations, the game will be measuring your entire body through one joycon, so it's forgiving of those (like me) with questionable footwork and unorthodox movements. This is far from the old standards of DDR which require precision timing, and are more on the spectrum of fun than skill. That fits with the reason I bought my Switch, so this makes a good addition to my collection.

title: A no-fee MMO
text:
Admittedly, I'm not much of a MMO guy. I never really liked the idea of paying subscription fees, persistent internet connections, having to rely on a bunch of strangers to fight alongside with, and lets face it - the story is absolutely going to suck. There is no other way to do it.

Guild Wars offers something different than the majority of MMORPGs today - it's a one-time fee with no recurring subscription fee. I picked this up because I love the change in business model, although it likely means that the support lifetime of the game is shorter. Despite that, I think it's a good choice, and having heard so much about the original Guild Wars, I was pretty excited to give this game a try.

I think it's a pretty good game. You don't need to level grind as you do with a lot of other MMOs - just about anything you do will give you some form of XP without having to do the repetitive quests like many other games require you to do. I haven't tried out very many of the character classes, but there is a good variety available, although they do tend to work pretty much the same (I play my warrior-type character the same way I play my wizard-type character and find similar success).

Some other notes:
- The graphics are pretty good.
- The world is scaled to fit your current level. You won't find many areas that you cannot access right away - some people love this, I don't.
- Some more unique classes - I can't wait to try the Necromancer.
- I love the dye system - it allows you to change your armor colors so you have a more customized look.

title: A fantastic return to MK Glory
text:
I've never been really good at MK games, and so I avoided them like the plague in favor of Street Fighter and other games like that back in the day. Now, I'm sick of the cartoon characters and looking for a little more realistic violence, so I grabbed this based on good reviews from Amazon.

First things first, there's a lot of stuff to do in this game. There's the cheezy little racing game, the RPG/Adventure mode, the ability to create a character, a whole room full of unlockables, and two different one-player fighting modes, plus two different kinds of training modes. That's great. I would have loved to see a fighting mode where you simply fight one computer player without having to do the Arcade mode, where you eventually run into those big stupid boss characters. For now, I just play the Arcade mode and quit as soon as I lose to Goro (or whoever), and then start over, but it is a little silly to have all of this stuff, and to miss something basic like a one-on-one versus mode.

There's over 60 characters here, and the balance is incredible. I think there's only about one or two completely unplayable characters, and nobody seems completely unstoppable, which is astonishing for a game of this depth. I initially thought that Sub Zero, Frost and Sektor were all really bad, but surprisingly, one of my friends came over and simply destroyed me with SZ, and another one thinks that Frost is playable, though I think that's questionable. In the end, it's about playing style, and that means endless hours of fun for those who are willing to put in the time to learn.

And learn you must. The controls seem a little strange at first, but there are two practice modes and a video to help you get the controls down. Most of the motions seem pretty straightforward too. You want to do Johnny Cage's kick move? It's back-forward, just like it should be. You want to do the uppercut special? It's just like the motion you'd be doing if you were actually executing the move, looping down and then up, towards your opponent. Does it take some getting used to? Certainly. MK experts on other systems will probably not be able to just pick this up and run with it, although you can plug in the classic controller and go at it more traditionally. Personally I love the new fatality system, especially with motion controls, since it actually lets me do some of the moves, which I could never do back in the day, and since the controls are pretty much the same for anyone, it's not hard to remember exactly what to do. Are the controls a little finicky from time to time? Of course, but that's pretty par for the course as far as I'm concerned.

Overall a fantastic game, and something you should definitely have in your collection (or is that kollection?)

title: Arcade action
text:
The best part about this game is that it's not Smackdown vs. RAW. That line of titles is more realistic, yes, but it's very hard to play with any real strategy, as the first person to hit any kind of move often can dominate the entire matchup. WWE All Stars is a completely different beast, but you probably already knew that from looking at the box. The character models are totally whacked out - I kind of hate them - but at the same time, I think they work a little bit for this style of game.

You hit a simple punch, and your opponent goes flying. You try a finisher, and you both leap into the air, spin around and land in slow motion. You literally bounce your opponent around, juggling them with punches and kicks while they bounce around the ring.

It's got some of your typical aspects of SVD: the career mode, the unlockables, and different types of matches, though there are far less choices here simply due to the size of the ring; a ladder wouldn't fit nicely in there with the two giant characters, so you get no TLC, ladder matches, or things like that. What is glaringly absent from this game is a regular tag team match, as the only kind of tag team action you get allows all four people to be in the ring together. It works, but it is limiting.

The choice of characters is well done. One thing that I particularly liked was the fact that you have different styles of characters now. One thing I never liked about SVD was that Rey Mysterio and Big Show were basically very similar in terms of the speed at which they moved and the strategy you could use to win with them. In All Stars, the Big Men are slow and powerful, while the other smaller wrestlers can literally fly across the ring, though they do significantly less damage.

It does suffer from some convoluted controls, where shaking the wiimote does any one of five different things depending on where you are, but for most gamers, it's nothing compared to trying to hit specific moves in SVD. The sound and the announcing is also very simplistic and repetitive.

Overall, this is a great game, and one that you should seriously consider if you're a wrestling fan.

title: The best?
text:
In my opinion, this is the pinnacle of the XCOM series. Yes, the pinnacle. As a long-time fan of the series, I recently went back and played them all again, and I have to say, this one takes the cake.

While Terror from the Deep and UFO defense are, in and of themselves, unbelievably outstanding games (the first is often considered the best computer game of all time), I think they are simply too outdated for today's player, whereas this game ports PERFECTLY since it doesn't require you to micromanage as much repetitive stuff. The real-time play mode is a necessary component to this, in my mind, because you're not tracking your troops around a map for 40 minutes waiting for an alien to come out. Many fans of the first two will scoff at this, citing that it doesn't take as much skill to run the missions in real time, but I think it really adds to the gameplay in ways that the first two cannot compete with.

Another element of the gameplay that works really well is that the aliens are more diverse and unusual in this game than they were in the previous two. They consistently outdo you in terms of technology and bring more tactics to the game than they seemed to have in years previous. Some will complain about the graphics and the fact that the aliens come at you in a rainbow of colors, but I think it works pretty well. You need different tactics to approach each kind of grouping. A popper alien is best handled by approaching it using long, narrow corridors that will let you shoot him down before he gets to you, while a group of Android and Skeletoids is best handled in a large open area later in the game when they bring out there devastator cannons.

While it can be a little repetitive over time, as the UFO missions will always repeat and the aliens have a tendency to break into the same buildings over and over, this is a great game that was extremely overlooked when it came out, and still is today. Buy it through Steam, where it will cost you $5, and it will work well on nearly any computer rather than getting the discs here. This is one of the very last DOS games to come out, and it doesn't work all that reliably in Windows.

title: Great Game, Annoying Features
text:
I got brawl after having finally bought and played the original SSB on the Wii virtual console during a blizzard. It was great, and so I went out and spent the money on the new, updated, awesome version. And for the most part, this is a new, updated awesome version of that game. It has a large number of problems associated with it, though, which I think you should know about before you get it.

Character Imbalance: having the 30+ characters that are available to you is really good, but some characters are so good that you can't really beat them if your opponent knows what they're doing (meta-knight and snake come to mind). Some characters are so bad that you're absolutely screwed if you use them (Ness and Olimar - and don't give me that nonsense about "if you know how to play them they're good"; they're weak, have random attacks, and fly like crazy). There are some balanced characters among the rest, but most of them play almost exactly the same.

Silly levels: There are a lot of really good levels, and even some large levels, which is nice from time to time. However, if you get stuck in a place called "New Pork City" the game is basically a button mashing festival because your character will be so small you can't even see him/her, you'll just see the little arrow that points out where you're standing. Other levels move left and right, or up and down, which is a nice change of pace, but they almost prevent fighting and strategy because your whole goal has to simply be survival. Then there are the levels where you can literally stay alive almost indefinitely because you won't get away from bouncing off the walls. In two of the Star Fox levels, there's a huge Star Wars-like battle going on in the background that will completely throw you off. There's good variety, but a lot of levels that will make you groan when you have to play on them.

Too much randomness: when you get a Pokemon ball to throw at your opponent, any one of about fifty different Pokemon will pop out and do something. Each one is totally different, and to be honest, I don't even know what two or three of them do at all. You can get a glass case thing, from which an older video game character like Little Mac or the Excitebikers will pop out and chase opponents around, but sometimes these guys all just jump off the side of the stage. Sometimes, I'm pretty sure they attack you. When I play as Peach and I go for the Turnip Toss, sometimes I pick up a bomb that blows up in my face and kills me. Then there's the problem of the Super Smash Balls, which sounds like a good idea, but is actually a totally cheap kill move, since there's no telling at what time they're going to explode, and they one-shot kill almost any character, no matter their life. There is also a three-part gun item that works the same way. When those appear, the entire group of characters stop what they're doing and go after the ball because it's imperative that you get the Smash away from your opponents. All of this leads to a very random, skill-less battlefield that often benefits those who are lucky rather than good.

At the end of the day, Brawl is a pretty good game, but it's not going to be for everyone. It's got a mountain of features, literally hundreds of things that you can unlock, but it has a lot of difficult features that will drive some gamers, usually the super-competitive "I MUST WIN AT EVERYTHING" gamers, absolutely crazy. If you're looking for a fun game that many people can simply pick up and play, then this might be for you.

What puts this game over the top for me is simply the sheer number of things you can do. There's a "classic" mode where you progress through fighting different battles to get to face the hand, and there's a new adventure mode that is pretty cheezy and simplistic (and incredibly long), but offers you some cheap platforming options. As you play, you'll unlock challenges in the "event" mode that test your skills in different ways (capture two characters in an egg as Yoshi, destroy all the breakable terrain as Pit, etc.). There's a stage builder, which is really quite fun, and allows you to use songs you've unlocked and stage objects you get after beating certain other parts of the game. There's even a classic games arcade where you can play demos of old Nintendo games, some of which are available on the virtual console.

Overall, there's a lot to this game, and there's a lot more to the gameplay than meets the eye. Sure, you can button-mash and win, but if you learn how to control many of the characters with a higher degree of skill, it can make for a really fun time.
