title: A solid tenkeyless backlit wired mechanical switch keyboard
text:
I really like this keyboard. It has the very nice and precise tactile response you get from a mechanical keyboard with their take on "blue"-style switches. (And the sound, unfortunately, but it's not at all fair to order a "blue" style keyboard and then complain about the keyclicks -- it's what they do.)

The actuation force is a bit lower than "real" Cherry Blue MX; I think I saw that it's around 45 cN whereas the originals tend to be in the range of 55cN. This is not in any way a problem; I actually like the resulting feel quite a lot. It's a good fit for the low-profile keys, but between the reduced actuation force and the low-profile keys, if you're the sort who hammers the keys, you'll bottom out the keys pretty hard.

I also really like the low profile keycaps, which are one of the key features that set this keyboard apart from a competitive field. It's very compact, and the low-profile keycaps help keep it from turning into an ergonomic nightmare. I much prefer this approach to full-size keycaps and the inevitable fat plastic bib that sits in front of the keyboard to elevate the wrists.

I did deduct one star because this TKL (tenkeyless) model, despite being the perfect size, lacks the RGB backlighting of its full-size brother. If the TKL version was available with per-key RGB backlighting, I would not only give it 5 stars, but I would immediately buy another one.

There are a couple of other minor issues; the deck isn't metal, but that's entirely attributable to the very reasonable price point of this product. The included USB cable also seems a bit dodgy, prone to disconnecting if wiggled just so. I replaced the cable with one of my own to rule out the possibility of a bad/loose socket on the keyboard, and had no further problems. If you're going to pack this around on a regular basis, it might be worth the investment to pair it with a nice, high-quality cable like the excellent and durable Anker PowerLine+ Micro USB, available here on Amazon.

EDIT: After following my own advice, I found that I had to sand down the plastic cowl on the Anker PowerLine+ cable a tiny bit to get it to fit into the recessed jack of this keyboard. So, another high-quality cable might be a better choice.

Ultimately, the best thing I can say about this keyboard is that I bought it for gaming, but when it arrived I plugged it into my work computer so I could make sure it worked, and I ended up typing on it for the rest of the day because I was enjoying it so much. Then, tonight I stole it from the gaming computer to write this review. ;-)

title: Mushy, imprecise keyboard
text:
I really wanted this to be the high-end backlit chiclet-style scissor-action keyboard for Windows that would be as good as a high-end laptop keyboard, or the old-model Apple aluminum wired keyboard I use with all my Macs.

It isn't. The membrane/scissor keys are soft and mushy and imprecise. The spacing seems weird. The keycap font is just bizarre. Within two minutes of plugging it in, I knew that it was going back. I've got an extra $15 USB keyboard I keep around for when you need an extra keyboard, and this one feels about the same.

I do a great deal of programming and a great deal of gaming. I'm not sure this is good for either one. It's got gaming style cues (like the crazy font), but the tactile feedback isn't precise enough. (The Apple wired keyboard is much better at this. When Apple is out-gaming your gaming product, you gotta stop and take stock.)

The ergonomic palm rest on the front isn't removable, which is unfortunate in tight spaces.

This keyboard is discontinued now, and I think that's for the best.

title: Best SpongeBob Game EVER!
text:
I've played a bunch of SpongeBob games before, some of them were ok, but this one beats them all!
I'm an art student, so yeah, I CAN'T STOP DRAWING!! So when I came across this one, I just had to get it. For all you parents out there concerned about any religious background and/or supposedly traumatic endings from the previous two drawn to life games, don't worry, because this one left those things out (I mean come on! It's SpongeBob!).

This game's a lot of fun, although it constantly feels like a Mario clone (a custom Mario at least). It's not too complicated, but kids under 8 might find it extremely hard to draw and clear the levels. The story's genius and feels a lot like a direct sequel to "Frankendoodle", which has to be my favorite SpongeBob episode so far. The boss battles are hilarious, and they make you want to beat them over and over again. I just wish the game had an extra save file, so I could start over without erasing all the crazy stuff i've drawn. I also would've wanted the game to be a bit longer... 20 levels is OK for some people, but that still feels kinda short to me. Oh well, at least it took me 2 weeks to beat it, instead of two DAYS like another game I got, plus I can doodle the day away without wasting paper!

So overall, AWESOME! There REALLLY should be more games like this one out there!

title: Only for die-hard VJ fans
text:
Man this game's hard to find!

As much as I love Viewtiful Joe, I have to say I'm really disappointed with this one game. Yeah, it's got REALLY good graphics, and Joe's got these cool new powers, but the game is EXTREMELY SHORT. I beat the story in two days, so you might beat it in much less time if you're a hardcore gamer. It's bare bones: just a game, one character, three difficulties, and once you beat it the game's over. You can't go back and replay the previous levels unless you start over in a new file (so you go through the trouble of buying all those power-ups for nothing).

If you still want to play this game though, rent it, borrow it from a friend, or get it at a much lower price. It's just not worth the 17 dollars I had to pay for (plus shipping).

title: Definitely one of the best made computer games I've played
text:
If I could go back to June and tell myself not to buy this game I would. But generally hindsight is that much clearer, especially 250 in game hours later. I was a huge fan of tf2 for many years, but this game makes it feel irrelevant immediately. Combining the strategy of MOBAs such as Dota 2 (or League of Legends if you must) with the off-beat first person shooter style of TF2, Overwatch has taken me by storm and captivated me ever since the first time starting it up. Definitely one of the best made computer games I've played, and Blizzard's continued development and support in balancing, updating, and in general caring about the game have been a nice alternative to Valve's cashing out with TF2.

I accidentally purchased the origins edition, I only wanted the normal edition, and the only reason I purchased on Amazon was that I had a gift card I wanted to burn. Origins comes with exclusive in-game skins (which I really couldn't care less about) along with other purely cosmetic additions. I really don't benefit from any of this, but if you're that sort of collector I'm sure you'll love what else Blizzard has included.

title: Excellent, when it works
text: This headset has a good sound and, because they are lighter than other similar headsets and they have very soft cushioned ear pads, they are extremely comfortable to wear. I have also been extremely pleased with the quality of the sound recorded from the microphone. I've used this headset for voice-over recordings, online gaming, and talking on Skype, and I've been thrilled with the quality. I've recommended this set to numerous friends and family members because of the high quality combined with the low price. However, although this set has a good sound and records very well, this set won't last very long. I bought my headset about a year ago, and it has worked splendidly for the last year. But, today I was using it to record some audio for a project and it crapped out on me. The earphones still sound fantastic, but the microphone no longer works. However, because of the cheap price and great quality, I've decided to purchase another set. Some people have reported sound problems, which also happened to my sister. I suspect that problem might be related to the long cord. The cord on this headset is about six feet long, which is great for an extended reach, but bad because it means there's a bigger chance that you're going to roll over the cord with your chair or snag it on something and yank it off your head (I believe my sister did that, which damaged the headset). So, if you're careful you may be able to avoid that problem. In my case, the mic stopped working, so I assume that the wires in the positionable microphone have become frayed or loose. Although I'd expect that to happen over time, I do not expect that to happen in just a year. However, this headset is so cheap and the quality of the sound is so good, I'm still going to purchase another set. The bottom line with this set: Fantastic sound reproduction and recording capabilities from a cheap-as-dirt headset, but you pay for that in shortened lifespan.

The keys are hot-swappable Eighteen of the lighting modes offer different types of light movement, two of the modes are all lights on or all lights off (on my keyboard, the all lights off setting is mode 2 of FN+INS, even though the User Guide states that the light mode for that setting is "Sparkle,") and eight are targeted gaming light configurations depending on what PC game you are playing; including COD, NBA, and Auto Racing games. This is a wired USB and backlit keyboard, is not, however, RGB, as the lighting is in fixed rows of multicolor rainbow LEDs; the lights are bright enough in a low light or darkened room, but the orange number row suffers from washout/ glare in direct lighting.
The Amazon listing says the keyboard works for both Windows and Mac, but I have had no problem connecting it to my Chromebook, so I have high hopes it will work for Linux users.

Even though I could enter the mode, it is, unfortunately, unclear, from the included instructions, how to program the settings (e.g. FN+END is supposed to be for record/ storage, but it also states FN+END is to enter the custom pointillist state.) It would have been helpful to have step-by-step directions, with examples, on creating a custom lighting mode. When I attempted to make my own light mode, all I was able to do was get either a few keys to light up, get a fully lit, or completely dark keyboard, so I'm not really sure how to generate a pattern.

The Bottom Line: At $29.99, the targeal keyboard is a reasonably priced mechanical keyboard. While not an actual RGB keyboard, due to the fixed colors, it has a good number of preprogrammed lighting modes; including eight gaming settings. The targeal Mechanical Gaming Keyboard - 104 Keys, would make a great low-cost, starter mechanical keyboard for a young PC gamer and leave more cash for games this Christmas.

The wireless dongle works well, and the keyboard holds a charge for me for about five days, though I don't know about a lengthy gaming session.

One major positive is KOLMAX 's K10 keyboard is sealed against liquid damage. I spilled 32 ozs of chai on the keyboard, and it still functions; too bad the glitch with the lights didn't show up until after the spill; I could then contribute the issue to liquid damage.

The Bottom Line: KOLMAX K10 Wireless RGB Keyboard is inexpensive for the features at $26.99. It holds a charge, the dongle has never lost connection, and the liquid seal holds up to a big spill. Even though I have had issues with my keyboard, and I could simply have a glitchy keyboard, across-the-board the KOLMAX K10 is a good value for what you get.

title: Not as good as I hoped
text:
I really wanted to like this, but I just don't. My kids got me playing Just Dance 2 for exercise, and when I saw this billed as a workout, I figured it would be even better. But it isn't.
First of all, I tried the mini-games. Yuck. The motion sensors don't seem to work very well, which is super annoying. And when you punch out the kangaroo her eyes roll back and her tongue sticks out, which is kind of disturbing. Decided I really hated the mini-games and would try the dancing, which is the main thing, of course.
So, the dancing itself is fine. The tutorials are pretty good and there's a great feature where you can slow it down a lot and loop just one step so you can practice it over and over again. The workouts are fun, with great music. So what could be wrong? Well, the biggest gripe is the many screens you have to go through between songs. Now, I borrowed it at the library and if I owned it I could set up my own workout and maybe not have that problem, I'm not sure.
The other gripes I have is, first, that sometimes the movements of the characters is slightly out of sync with the music. Secondly, I did one workout several times one day and suddenly two of the three dancers were wearing skanky Las Vegas-style showgirl outfits, complete with high heels and feathered headgear. What the heck is that??? I thought it was particularly weird because it's obvious to me that most people using this product will be women, and why they thought we would want to see scantily clad female animations is completely beyond me.
Overall, I decided that I enjoyed Just Dance 2 more. It's just more fun, and my kids and I like doing it together. I'm still researching and will be trying the Ubisoft Broadway dance game and the Zumba for Wii soon.

title: Plasticky Easter Egg quality plastic case.  Laughably sad quality.
text:
The foamy packaging material they put inside the plastic shell feels more protective than the actual product itself. I think it is a bad sign when your "protective case" requires soft, foamy material to keep the case from getting broke in the mail.

The case even sounds like the same material as those 2 piece plastic easter eggs when you grip your Switch tight in your hand with the case on. I suspect this case will crack and break very easily if dropped or handled with much pressure. It is sturdy when the top is down but if you accidentally put much pressure on it in your bag, expect no protection and a broken case. It comes across very junky material. And to add insult to injury: it looks like my fingers are dipped in ink - that's how bad it holds on fingerprints.

Another point of discontent, is that the top flipper is removable but the way it is removed is a joke. You bend the extremely hard, brittle, slippery plastic cover and this dislocates two tiny little plastic pegs that comes out of the round holes they are stuck in. It feels like it is going to break in my hands.

In conclusion, I am hugely disappointed with the feature item of this set: the bonus items are the best part, as they are the parts I am not disappointed with. This is one of those cases that shouldn't have even been made IMHO. It feels like a dollar store item. The control caps are hard to get on but I like them. The gray matches the gray switch. I am not going to try the screen protector because I am returning. It feels like a decent screen protector. The set is worth keeping if you need a screen protector and joycon thumbcaps (I notice those items are expensive here on Amazon but I don't think they should cost what they do). I think you get a dispostable easter egg plastic case for free, basically, but I don't care to have the additional accessories enough to pay $12 for them. Overall, if the set was $5 I would keep it for the screen protector and thumbcaps and use the case until I am sick of it.

Often when my husband is playing COD, the Xbox will just shut off on him after 15 - 20 minutes of play. In order for it to turn back on, he has to unplug the power supply from the Xbox and wall, and then plug it back in after 5-10 minutes of rest time. Then it will usually work again for the rest of the evening/night. This usually happens at least once a day, often twice. It has become very annoying, so we'll be buying a new power supply soon. You may want to purchase an additional one if you haven't already!

title: Great Mouse if You Don't Mind Holes or Creaks
text:
I own a lot of mice- probably every mouse you could buy at Best Buy and a lot of up and coming mice companies' mice.
With that said, I appreciate the Xtrfy M42 for at least trying something new. The swappable shell is nice and sturdy. Doesn't feel cheap at all. You basically get a sensei type shape, or a flatter viper mini shape. I preferred the Sensei shape. Over time, the shell began to creak a little bit. It doesn't really bother me, but I know some people really hate that kind of thing.
The feet are fantastic. Very smooth and clean.
The clicks are awesome- well, the main mouse 1 and mouse 2 clicks. The clicks are sturdy and satisfying. The side mouse buttons are alright. Nothing special, but not noticeably worse than other other mouse I use. The scroll wheel... this ones tough. Basically, the actual scroll is one of the best I've experienced. It's smooth but tactile enough to be pleasant and discernable, but the click of the scroll wheel takes a noticeable amount of force. Like, I really have to think about it when I push the thing down. It's a big reason that the mouse isn't my main mouse.
Lastly, the cable is ok. It looks cool on the retro version of the mouse, but it's heavy and it is felt whenever I move the mouse, even in a bungee.

TLDR;
Great M1 and M2 clicks
Passable side button clicks
Tough scroll wheel click but satisfying scroll
Great feet
Good shell shapes with a bit of creak over time
Cable is... ok. Bungee helps but it's still weighty compared to the mouse

title: Satisfying To Type On
text:
I've been through basically all of the gaming keyboards now. I've felt the top echelon each brand has to offer i.e. Razer, Corsair, Logitech, Steelseries.
The only other keyboard that I think comes close to this one is the Apex Pro TKL, but this one is still better.

Pros:
1. Switches offer just the right amount of feedback, so you aren't always making mistakes when typing on these very, very smooth linear switches.
2. The stabilizers are very good on these switches.
3. The feeling of the actual keycaps are pleasant. It just feels good to type on these switches. They have a nice bounce back to them that make them feel more responsive than other keyboards.
4. The RGB on this keyboard is far and away the best of any keyboard out there. There are other keyboards with brighter lighting, like the Apex Pro TKL, but the AIMO intelligent mode on this thing is unreal. It kind of just slowly and smoothly mixes the colors in and out on your keyboard. It's hard to explain, but it's easily the most pleasant rgb experience of all the keyboards I have had.

Cons:
1. ABS keycaps. Okay- so this doesn't matter to me this much, but these are ABS keycaps and they most definitely DO collect a lot of oil so, if you spend a lot of time looking at your keycaps for some reason, be prepared to clean them often.
2. Height- this keyboard is not low profile by any means. You will want a wrist rest with this keyboard. I bought a glorious wooden one and it wasn't too bad that way. I prefer using the one that came with my apex pro tkl though and it works perfectly.
3. The ping. This bothers some people apparently. It's there and you'll notice it but if you wear headphones, even open back ones- it's basically a non-issue. I like the sound otherwise.

Differentiating with the Apex Pro TKL, the keys on this keyboard are a little heavier but just as smooth. It's easier to make typos on the Apex Pro TKL because the keys are so light. Now, that can be taken care of by changing the sensitivity of the keys on the Apex, but I don't like messing with that all the time and prefer to keep the sensitivity high. That means it might not even be an issue for you.
Also, because the keycap design on the Vulcan TKL Pro is so different, it might be hard to find replacement keycaps for it. I put some Razer PBT keycaps on my Apex Pro TKL and it feels great. Took care of the ABS shine and everything.

title: Works Flawlessly- Far superior to the Mixamp pro tr
text:
This DAC is far superior to the mixamp Pro tr from Astro- not to say that the Astro one is bad by any means, but this one is just so much better and more functional.
I have had this DAC for two days now, and I felt like I needed to do this thing a justice. Two or three other reviews on this thing at this time rated it horribly and I don't understand why.
I'll review this bad boy in categories for simplicity.

1. Aesthetics:
This DAC is beautiful in my opinion. Minimalistic, but clean. Straight black with a pleasant white screen across the left side of it. It will look good on any desk.

2. Functionality:
The DAC allows for a lot more customization than the Mixamp pro tr. It gives you the option to turn virtual surround sound on or off (obviously). You can choose from a small list of preset EQs (the one out of the box is flat, which some people like, but I found it to be very underwhelming.) Currently, I run the "smiley" eq. I think it really brings any headset to life. You can choose a high or low gain (use high, it'll make your headset louder.) It has it's own mic monitoring (WORKS GREAT), and it allows you to adjust the volume of your mic (I just leave mine on 6 and it seems to work fine. No complaints from friends in my PS4 Party or players online in Apex Legends.)
You can switch your inputs from PC (haven't used my DAC on PC, but I'd imagine it works just as good) to Hi-Res audio (disables the ability to customize any of your previously mentioned stuff as far as I can tell), and PS4.
You can change the brightness of the display and the timeout of the screen, and lastly, if you own a pair of the arctis pros, you can customize your earcup colors and the color of the muted mic light on the edge of the microphone.

3. Setup:
The first thing I did when I got these out of the box was plug them into a PC, type "steelseries software" into google, download the software, and upgrade the firmware on the GameDAC. The software seemed to recognize the DAC immediately, so I have no complaints towards the software for the DAC. The software gives you a lot of options for customizing the gamedac. To be honest, I didn't look into it because I didn't really care all that much, but from what I glanced over, they were pretty much all the same things you can adjust on the DAC itself.

4. Sound:
Arguably the most important thing here, the sound from this DAC is INCREDIBLE. I'm not an audiophile, and I don't have audiophile headphones. I use the Astro a40 tr headset I got from the bundle with the mixamp, and the sound really is just so good. As I stated above, the sound straight out of the box might be a little underwhelming for people that aren't audiophiles. Again, go through the EQ menu and choose "smiley" or even create your own! I play a lot of Apex Legends right now, and everything is so clear with this DAC. Footsteps? Too easy. Gunshots? Can hear them from across the map. This DAC blows the Astro one out of the water.

5. Might help people with correctly setting up GameDac on ps4:
I figured I'll put this here so people don't incorrectly hook this up to their ps4.
If you have a ps4 slim, you are going to need an HDMI to HDMI + Optical splitter so you can connect the optical cable from the back of the DAC into the ps4 slim. If you have the original ps4 or ps4 pro, you'll be fine.
First, download the software and firmware update as I stated in section 3.
Second, Plug the usb cable and optical cables into the back of the gamedac and ps4.
Third, go to the ps4 settings, scroll to "sound and screen" and go to audio output. Change it from linear to optical output. For my ps4 slim, just change what I believe was "linear?" to dolby or dts. Not sure if either makes a difference. I have mine set to DTS and it works fine.
Fourth, go back and scroll to devices. Click audio devices. Make sure the input and output say "USB Headset (SteelSeries GameDac) or something like that, and that you turn the output to headphones volume all the way up. I also have just the chat audio going to the headphones, not all audio. I just turn down my monitor all the way so the game sound doesn't come through both my headset and monitor. From there, you should be good to go!

TLDR;
Easy to set up. (make sure you download steelseries software and firmware update)
Works flawlessly with PS4.
Allows for use with any headset (provides a 3.5mm adapter).
Looks amazing.
SOUNDS GREAT.
Very loud and clear.
Provides mic monitoring.
Blows Astro mixamp tr out of the water.

Side note for those of you who were avid fans of KOTOR and KOTOR 2: this game does not follow along with those games in the least. No mention of them or any characters in those game's... It's as if they never existed, in fact, I don't even think this is in the same century as those games. I think they got the time period's wrong with this game but... I'm no expert.

title: Disappointing.
text:
I haven't come in here to brag or to bash, but I wanted to post my review on here for those who want to read. Warning, this review is opinionated.
I AM a Battlefield veteran and have been playing the Battlefield series ever since the demo of BF1942 came out. My roots with this franchise go way back and I have seen all of the progress and design choices being made from start to finish. While my PC gaming days have somewhat come to an end, I have this game on the Xbox 360.
Let's start off on the Beta for the 360. Yikes. I think all of you who played the beta were sweating a little bit before the game came out, with good reason. It was a mess. RIDDLED with glitches, poor hit detection and connective issues that prevented you from getting/staying in a game. Well let's all take a deep sigh of relief because all of this was glossed over.... For the most part.
At first when I sat down with BF3, I immediately went to the singleplayer. The singleplayer caught a lot of flak from reviewers for why, I am not sure. It was actually quite surprising and immersive compared to other Battlefield campaigns. Hell, BF1942's singleplayer was nothing more than a bot match on the Multiplayer maps. Am I saying it's covered with gold? No, it has it's linear issues and occasional hiccups, but for the most part, it's right on track with awesome sauce as the Bad Company games were.
Not long after I had a good go with single, did I go to multiplayer. Ah yes, the multiplayer. What the Battlefield series has ALWAYS and FOREVER will be known for. It comes to a very large surprise that it simply does not hold up to it's predecessor. Bad Company 2 multiplayer was tasty, I mean it was very very good. This game is still plagued with glitches that were present in the Beta. Did a lot of it get fixed from the Beta? Sure.... But they're still there. I still notice them. So a patch that may or may never come to fix them will not earn any of these points back. Glitches I am talking about aside from lag: Vaulting over objects only the instantly appear back in front of them, going prone then instantly popping back up or into crouch, going prone and then clicking the sprint button whilst running from fire, only the instantly go BACK prone and receive many shots to the @@@.
Am I bashing the game just in the presence of glitches? No. We must also take in to account that the graphics are just simply disappointing.... Even with the "HD graphics" installed, they are NOT good!!!! Bad Company 2 graphics were finger-lickin... You could see the individual threads of enemy fatigues, you could see the dirt smudged on your teammates faces... You could interact with the map and feel as if you were truly there... Do you remember those epic tank battles across the mountain sides of Heavy Metal? The shells that impacted the ground would actually indent the ground creating craters that affect those who walk/drive through them. None of that exists in Battlefield 3. It just doesn't.
The "My Soldier" customization... A distater area. I mean, who okayed, morever CREATED, the layout that they put on the progression/stats/customization screen? It's God awful. The only way to see what guns you have unlocked or are you are about to unlock is the keep flipping to the right and left and seeing if it has a tiny little "lock" icon on it. Where the hell is the big gun graph that Bad Company 2 had? I'm not saying that that was the most perfect and elegant thing ever, but it sure as hell blows this out of the water. Why can't I check the progress I made with a particular gun? I can't check how many kills I've made with a specific gun? The only way I see any type of progress with a gun is to see how many attachable's I have available for it. Cool.
Frostbite 2.0? More like Frostbite 1.1; better yet: Frostbite .05. Where is the destruction for crying out loud? 9/10 rockets I shoot at walls do "NoThInG". Has anyone played Red Faction: Guerilla? THAT was destruction... THAT was a league above all else... This is a step backwards. It's almost embarrassing. Remember in Bad Company 2 when if you shot enough walls out of a building, it would collapse? Sigh, I miss those days.
Battlefield 3 is a mess. Singleplayer is fine, but it really lacks it's heart. The claims DICE and EA has made about Frostbite 2.0 were nothing more than a scam. The graphics are not what they were from Bad Company 2. The playability is a step down. The whole game is a step down. It really hurts me.
Have fun PC users, because the Xbox360 version of this is a damn shame.
Bring on November 8th please.

title: Peggle Nights
text:
The sound effects, along with the brilliantly vibrant colors, play a crucial role in the game. Every time you hit a peg, an effect resonates, with each a pitch higher than the last.
This kind of design keeps you riveted to the screen, even though you're pretty much helpless to control much of anything after you've launched your shot. Yet you sit there in a gleeful stupor listening to the sounds build, watching the explosions of bonus points and hoping for the best.
Then there's the big payoff at the end, when the last orange peg is hit, the game screen zooms in, moves into slow motion to emphasize the importance of the moment, and from your speakers explodes a rendition of Beethoven's Ode to Joy alongside bright sparkles, polychromatic explosions, and eye-searing rainbows.
Even if you miss that last peg by a small margin, the screen still zooms in and drum roll sound effect is still played, and you'll find yourself moaning aww in disappointment along with the crowd in the game.
PopCap knew exactly what they were doing when designing this title, and everything's pulled off remarkably well.

You don't have all that much control over how games of Peggle play out, PopCap still managed to create an engaging experience by infusing the addictive qualities of slot and pachinko machines into its title through a masterful implementation of sound effects and color. So while you can never predict exactly where the ball will bounce, you'll want to keep playing just to see if you can get it right the next time.

With Peggle Nights, PopCap offers a bunch of new boards and a few new features, though the gameplay is more or less unchanged. Still, Peggle fans should absolutely dive in, and if you've never tried Peggle, you really should. Just make sure you've got some time to spare before you load it up.

Quirky characters that spout nonsensical phrases, an excellent board layout and even a colorblind mode. A shiny, polished game.

These graphics are really impressive. The use of color is expertly implemented to reinforce the game's addictive qualities.

Crisp, clear effects that greatly enhance the game's appeal and staying power.

This isn't a title you play for 20 minutes, it's something you'll want to continue coming back to.

Just a really fun game! Quite time consuming - a rainy day game for sure.

text:
At first I balked at paying the extra price for the CE even though I had purchased the LK CE. Well I was playing my vanilla version today and happened to be running a troll (I run Alliance and Horde toons) and I thought I would do a little rep grinding in Mulgore. I was out at Red Cloud Mesa doing the low level quests and the background music was phenominal (I found out it is Cataclysm song "Call of the Elements"). While overlooking the cataclysmic changes to the region from Fargaze Mesa if you don't think the composer and artists didn't do a wonderful job on the music, you don't deserve to play WoW. I had already heard some good music in other revamped Cataclysm areas, but something about this and the game ambience sounds in the background haunted me like an image of Native American spirits dancing near a burial ground. I looked everywhere for the Cataclysm soundtrack and couldn't find it. I decided that did it, I knew the art book (these are excellent by themselve and worth the price alone to some), the pet (if you collect the pets like me this is a must have), and cards (the rare loot card could make the price worth it alone especially if you get a mount) have value as well, but the soundtrack definitely sold me on the CE version. Merry Christmas to me and anyone else that decides they have to have it. The shipping was fast but I am disappointed in the cards with the game. I got 100 Cenarius flowers and my wife got 50 pet biscuits. Honestly this is lame (all the reward cards for 50 or 100 uses of something aren't worth the paper they are printed on and certainly not the decoding and making a trip to Booty Bay to see Landro) and people that buy the CE deserve a better reward. If these limited usage items were a reusable item or trinket like they give for seasonal quest achievements it wouldn't be so bad. But finite limited use items for us loyal fans that buy the CE, I think we deserve better. That's why I give it four stars instead of five.

title: A true opinion from a guy who spends time at a real track!!....
text:
I myself have an 02 Z28 that has a custom 414 c.i. engine with a 200 shot of spray...and tons of mods. Im in the 9.9x sec range. I love the track and have lots of friends with some very nasty 8.xx and lower range cars. My car doubles as an autocross... with all that in mind... GT5 dissapointed me for these reasons:

*AI cars ride on rails
*Their purpose is not to win but to keep YOU from getting to 1st place in said race
*The spectators look like they were put in game a day before it shipped and are from the super nintendo/Genesis days
*AI cars dont react to bumps and collisions the way you do
*Can't alter driver's name in the "coaching mode" to something custom nor even the color of the uniform or style
*AI cars follow same patterns
*Testing rules and guidelines don't apply to AI cars
*There's like 127 Nissan Skylines but NOT ONE pontiac trans-am of any year but there's a pontiac Vibe???
*Lots of cars that are nothing to do with sporty but exist here while other key cars that should have been here weren't (Like a crappy SEAT 1.6L car sold in Europe or middle east with 70HP... but there is no AUDI Auto Union which is one of the key cars in racing history and if a real one existed today would be worth $10 Million + but its not important enough to be in this game)
*The opening and it's music are so bubble gummy video gamer..
*The driver walking animations are silly and goofy
*WAAAAAAAAY to much emphesis on car looks, handling, mods but rest of game is not polished
*Rehashed tracks from old games look better but not "5yrs in development" better.
*The track creator.... really isn't!

There are great things about this game, but if you want a true racing simulator... this is NOT it. Cars handle great and react to mods correctly and of course they look good... but you can clearly see that 80% or more of this games ridiculous production time was spent on those factors and nothing else. This is Polyphony's own fault. With so much time everyone expected perfection... far far from it.

I took this game right back. I still am sticking to my Burnout Paradise, sure it's older and its nothing about racing simulation but its racing and FUN and the mechanics are far better. And it's graphics can hold it's own again most of GT5's.

title: 90% Same Game as P2
text:
Patrician III is not much different than PII, so if you have PII don't buy this game. I enjoy playing Patrician, but the only useful feature this "new" version offers is the ability to save and edit your trade routes. Now for those of you who are new to Patrician games, you should buy this version.
I enjoy the historically based games that merge city building, battles and a touch of RPG all in one. In the beginning you have one ship and no reputation...As the game develops you can easily become overwhelmed in the micro managing of 15-20 different cities,Numerous ships, politics, housing, industry, and just plain old buying and selling of goods.
Many of the other reviews go into the specific historic issues as related to the Hanseatic league, but all you really need to know is you need to make money. Buy low-sell high! That is all you need to know to start. You trade goods from town to town with your ship(s).
As you begin to gain money and status, you will start to learn which towns need certain goods(Which I won't go into here), and then to build industries, housing, more ships, etc. Eventually you become targeted by Pirates. The battle graphics are very basic and controls very low tech. I has hoping for an improvement from P2, but it is the same. Some battles take 15-20 minutes, esp. when you have to chase a badly damaged ship against the wind. Don't buy this game if you are into battles... I think they were an after thought.
My first P3 game is now 40 hours long, and I control 30 ships and have offices in 5 towns. I don't even turn the game on unless I have two hours to spend. I enjoy the game very much and try to automate as much as possible to allow me to keep an eye on the markets and fine tune trade routes for the most profit. My defenses are quite good to cover trading, and when a pirate attacks they are usually sunk or captured... but there goes another 20 minutes. You control the speed of the game, but as slow speed your trade routes will take so long you might look up and the sun is rising!!!
If you enjoy reading historical fiction and sim-city type games, then buy this game, but don't tell your wife... or husband.

title: Way better than the one that comes with the Oculus Quest 2
text:
This item is much better than the OEM. A lot like the old Oculus Rift straps where you can twist a knob to tighten/loosen up the fit.

Facebook spared *every* expense when they designed the headstrap for the Quest 2. The original OEM strap is basically made from elastic waist-bands cut from worn-out pairs of Zuckerberg's Fruit-of-the-Looms that they fashioned into head-straps.

The padding is well done and the tightening mechanism work fairly well. It's made of thinner plastic than I'd prefer, because it feels like it may eventually break.

The back-of-the-head piece spreads out the pressure well and it's padded enough to feel comfortable. It's fairly easy to assemble and fits on the Quest 2 very well. It stays on tight and doesn't feel like it's constantly about to slide off like the OEM waistbands (straps). If there were a little bit more weight in the back, it would be balanced perfectly.

The only nitpick I would have is that the plastic is thin and it doesn't scream quality. It's between mediocre and good. Pretty decent, but not outstanding. But the value is great. If it breaks then it's still a great value to replace if needed. It's survived almost a year without breaking -- but I don't put it through a lot of abuse and I'm careful when wearing it.

Overall, this is a great value for a mid-range head-strap. Not the best in the world, but comfortable and wearable. Five stars.

title: Nice idea, but not much more than a cradle for charging.
text:
This doesn't really add much except for a place to put your Deck in an upright position. The charging plug just a simple extension, although it does have a 90° plug that keeps it a little bit more tidy looking.

Don't get me wrong, the product is what is described and the price isn't bad if that's what you want. It's just a charger with two extra USB-A jacks. It would allow you to add two USB devices.

The main problem is that the USB-A jacks won't let you hook up any accessories that would connect to your Deck. It is only useful for charging. No data connections, though to be fair, it does say in the description that there is no data transfer.

So at the time of this writing, it's a $15 cradle with two USB ports that can be used with the charger. It doesn't come with an adapter, but you can use the one that comes with the Steam Deck. Also, the Steam Deck charger is only 45W total, so if you're charging the Steam Deck, there won't be much power left over for charging a phone or whatever you might plug into a USB-A.

If all you want is a cradle to put your Steam Deck in so that it stands upright, this will work. But there are better docks that actually function as a proper dock -- with HDMI ports, sound, and USB-C connectors which will basically let you hook your deck up like a desktop.

Even the cable extension isn't that great. It can't be plugged in after you put the Deck into the cradle because it's too short. So you have to plug it into the Deck first, *then* you can get the Deck into the cradle -- but it takes some bit of stress on the plug/cable because it's a tight fit. Eventually, the cable may stretch making it easier, but it's worth pointing out that having such a tight fit could put too much stress on the Deck's input jack.

Personally, I wouldn't call this a "dock". It's a "holder" with a cable extension.

I give this two stars because the price isn't bad, it charges the Deck, and the cradle looks a bit better than just laying your deck flat on the desk. And the cradle piece is padded with some spongy rubber so it won't scratch the screen. Other than that, nothing going for this "cradle".

I would have given it another star if it worked with converters like USB-A to HDMI or USB-A to Ethernet, or even if you could plug in a keyboard and mouse. But that doesn't work.

For now, until they upgrade the ports to allow data transfer, then I'd give this a hard-pass unless you just want a cradle.

title: Sturdy and durable, works with Oculus Link for Quest 2 to PC
text:
First, this is a very durable cable and sturdy. The braided cover is tough and should take a lot of wear compared to the bare cable. Especially if you use this for VR, you'll probably be stepping on it occasionally, so this should be perfect for most people unless you're a maniac when you play VR games.

I can confirm that this works with Oculus Link and connects my gaming laptop to my Quest 2 headset without issues. I use the included Velcro™ cable-tie to attach it to the headband of my Quest 2 headset near the back so that the cable drops behind my back.

If I had any complaint it would be that it is almost *too* durable. It's really stiff and it comes coiled up (because it's a 20-foot cable). It has a tendency to maintain the coil after taking it out of the bag. It still works, but the coiling can be annoying when moving around. Hopefully the cable will "relax" a little and won't try to coil back up as much with longer use.

This also charges and powers the Quest 2 while it's in use. I've used this for several hours at a time and the battery level was still almost 100% afterwards.

This particular cable has the larger USB-A connector (usual rectangular USB plug) on one end and the smaller right-angle USB-C connector on the other end.

I've tried several other USB-C connector cables with Oculus Link and this one is comparable in quality, but is the longest of any I've tried so far.

I think that most of the problems that people experience with cables using Oculus Link can be attributed to their PC hardware rather than the cables themselves. Unless it's a really cheaply made cable, it should work. If you try more than one cable and still can't get it to work, chances are that the problem is with your PC and not the cables.

Overall, at $27, this is a bargain over the brand-name Oculus cable and seems to work just as well. As usual, YMMV.

title: Terrible game not even redeemable by talented character actor, Nathan Fillion.
text:
This is pretty much a watered down version of Destiny 1, with marginally better graphics. Some of the player-versus-player levels are identical to those in Destiny 1 except with slightly different textures. Seriously, I like the idea of "code reuse" but not in a game where you're expecting new content rather than a cut-n-paste of an old level. It's amazing that they thought that would be acceptable. Some people may like it, but I expect a new game to have NEW content.

Compared to Destiny 1, it's plain boring. I found myself logging into the game yesterday and I had already done the maximum leveling for the week, so I played another game.

And that's not even the worst. The most greedy, arrogant thing that they're planning (and they are actually bragging about it) is to add another DLC release in December. So, I can pay another $30 for another cut-and-paste copy of Destiny 1 with different textures.

Activision really blew it with this one. Destiny 1 was a pretty good game for all it's flaws. No game is perfect.

Unless (by some miracle) the next DLC gets tons of outstanding reviews, then I won't be playing (and paying) for anything by Bungie again.

Seriously, the game content and development seems to be controlled by a sadistic autocrat who demands that the game be played the way they want it to be played. Then if you find a sneaky (i.e. Fun) way to glitch some incredibly tough spot in the game, they'll patch that quicker than they will fix actual bugs.

The reason I gave this game two-stars rather than the zero it deserves, is basically Nathan Fillion. Only because of Nathan Fillion. He deserves a 5-star review, but the game is not called "Somewhat witty lines read by Brilliant Character actor Nathan Fillion." I'd rather watch reruns of Firefly or Castle than play this game just to hear Nathan Fillion fire off cheesy wise-cracks written by mediocre story editors.

title: Very comfortable, quiet, designed for speed
text:
I bought this for gaming, but I also needed a keyboard that works well for programming. Overall I enjoy the keyboard, but for programming I have a few annoyances.

1. I'm EDSF, Not WADS. So having the nub on the "W" key gets kind of distracting. Gamers have all gotten used to having it on the F, and it should always stay on the F.

2. I don't know many gamers that use Up and to the Left, and Up and to the Right, especially on the directional keys. The orientation of the direction keys is critical for quick access to each button. The 1 over 3 design allows you to quickly feel for the right key. Having the 2 additional arrow keys makes it more difficult to move over to the arrows while typing, and there just isn't enough benefit to justify having them there.

3. I would have loved to see USB ports on the keyboard. The other version has them, and I was a little bummed out when I got this one and it didn't.

4. I love EVERYTHING else about this keyboard and the software that comes with it. Everything was thought through well and designed with a lot of considerations. I haven't gotten a lot of the keys customized yet, but the fact that I can setup multiple profiles that can switch based on the application that's running is fantastic.

I have customized some items:
1. NUM LOCK now opens Calculator (I use it a lot)
2. SCROLL LOCK does nothing now
3. INS (Insert) is disabled
4. UP/LEFT is now just Left
5. UP/RIGHT is now just Right

I'm curious what customizations other people are doing. In summary, really nice keyboard.

title: UPDATE 11/5/17 - STILL My new favorite game as of 3/8/17 - 5 stars - WITH SPOILERS
text:
This is a great game--my new favorite. I have to give it 5 stars overall. The scenery is probably the best I've personally seen on the PS4. The weapons and equipment are pretty realistic, in my opinion. I just recently stopped playing Metal Gear Solid 5 after playing that and nothing else over the last 9 months. I believe this game is like Far Cry 4, GTA 5, MGS 5, and Fallout 4 all wrapped into one (with a little imagination). I own all those games for PS4, and I believe this game takes most of the best elements from the others mentioned above. The sheer number of vehicles and weapons and equipment is amazing. There are some significant pros and cons to this game, however. In no particular order, I don't agree with being able to switch to any weapons that have been unlocked whenever I feel like it. I'm not carrying all my unlocked weapons with me at all times--that would be extremely cumbersome. For the fun factor, tho, it is great. My favorite sniper so far is the MSR. I don't have the 50 cal unlocked yet, but I'm told it can even shoot down the Apache helicopter with 1 shot. My favorite machine gun is the M249. Nothing stands up to the 249 except the "Apache" Unidad helicopter, which incidentally looks almost exactly like a Cobra helicopter. I was carrying a bullpup assault rifle with a grenade launcher, but that pales in comparison now to the damage the trusty M249 deals out. I'm still using the standard 45 caliber pistol. I use everything suppressed except the 249. I absolutely HATE that (at least on Arcade level) I cannot drag off the bodies of enemies I've killed. I believe that should have been implemented into this game. I loved that on Far Cry 4. As for the Unidad, I think it's total BS that I can shoot down a gazillion Unidad helicopters, obliterate hordes of Unidad soldiers, and destroy lots and lots of Unidad vehicles, and they just keep coming and coming and coming--and then they kill me. I have pushed the Unidad alert level to LEVEL 4 on several occasions, just to see if I could kill them all. Even on Arcade level, I can't kill them all. Another thing that is hokey is a minivan should not be able to go up an almost vertical mountain. It is fun, tho. The vehicles take an extreme amount of damage before they blow up, generally. In real life (which I realize this is a game), I would not be able to take a Lambo-looking sports car cross-country and run over cactus after cactus and smash into stone walls, etc, etc, etc, without totaling the thing out in the first crash. I LOVE the sync-shots. It really helps with the stealthy sniper approach. When all else goes to hell, tho, I bring out the M249 and get to work. I really like being able to upgrade weapons, as with Fallout 4. I like stopping vehicles and pulling people out and taking their cars as with GTA5. The scenery really reminds me a lot of MGS5 and FC4. Not surpising, considering who produced this game. What I really, really, really like about this game is it IS fun. I have probably spent 30 hours playing so far, and it has gone by like a snap of my fingers (almost). And, I'm just on the very easiest level. I am going to have to get a lot better at this game to even think about upping the difficulty level. The AI on this game is really pretty good. My AI soldiers, as in my 3 teammates and the rebel soldiers, are really pretty good. They have senior moments on occasion and can't figure out where to go, but for the most part, they are right there beside me or at least very close in a gunfight. The enemy soldiers AI reminds me a lot of MGS5. One shot unsuppressed (and sometimes even suppressed), and they have my location, and they are coming for me and my team. I hate the SAM missle sites. I have gone in and wiped them out in order to steal an aircraft only to discover that there was another SAM missile launcher in range that enjoyed shooting me down. Flares would have been a nice touch to be able to drop out of an airplane or heli, I am going to try switching seats with another player and try decoying an incoming missile with a flare gun, but I bet it won't work. But I am going to try it if I can line everything up. I have gotten stuck in the map 3x so far. Each time, I have fallen down into a crevice somewhere, and the only way I could get out was to fast travel out. That used to happen to me in Skyrim back in the day. But for the miles and miles or km and km of map this game has, I suppose I can excuse a couple glitches here and there. I'm pretty sure this is operator error, but I am not good at base jumping yet. I've got it figured out how to jump out of a heli or an airplane, tho. The parachute is really cool. There are a ton of different vehicles available. I hardly have to walk anywhere, but I do it just to try to discover everything on the map. Usually everywhere I go there is lots of ammunition available, which is nice. Not sure how realistic that is, but it makes the game more fun. I don't like how I have to stand directly in front of the ammunition crates in order to re-load ammo. Same thing goes for the supply tagging. It seems like I have to be right in front and touching each crate in order to load or tag. When doing air-to-air combat, it is difficult for me to fly a heli and shoot the guns all at the same time while still trying not to get shot down. Luckily, my guys out on the sides of a small heli do a lot of shooting, and they take out a lot of enemies while I perform my "circle of death" going around and around a target. I'm sure some company will come up with a game better than this in the future, but for now, this game is the bomb. 5 stars.

*** UPDATE 4/3/17 ***

I still love this game. I'm level 28 now. I've unlocked a lot of cool weapons and gear. My favorite loadout is still the MSR in the sniper slot, M249 in the light machine gun slot, the P45T in the pistol slot, and the standard drone. For destroying vehicles and especially that pesky Unidad "Apache", I do switch to the HTI for a 1-shot kill. I have been using the explosive drone a lot for taking out SAM sites and generators. Some of the bases are almost impossible to get into, and the explosive drone really helps on occasion. For example, there is a Serpentidad (or something spelled close to that) in the bottom center of the map. It is crawling with Unidad. It also has a SAM site and a generator. Blowing up the generator opens all the gates, and destroying the SAM site helps with a mission underneath it on the map in order to steal a +3000 medical supplies helicopter. I had to attempt that mission 3 times to get it done. I got shot down 2x, and then I figured out that the SAM launcher was in that Unidad base. So, I had to take out the SAM site first in order to not get blasted out of the sky by missiles on the 3rd (and successful) attempt. So far, the SAM launchers and Unidad are my worst enemies. I can't say for sure how many, but I think I shot down about 15 Apache helicopters one time when I was discovered sneaking around the Unidad base after I had released all the prisoners out of the prison. It is ridiculous how many soldiers and land-based vehicles and helicopters spawn almost immediately after the previous units have been destroyed. They just keep coming and coming, in waves LOL, and the only way I have found so far to get the Unidad alert down from 4 stars is to run and hide somewhere that Unidad cannot find me. Eventually, they give up, but it takes a really long time to outrun Unidad. I have still been playing on the easiest level so far since beginning the game. I have discovered almost everything on the massive map, but I still have a long, long way to go before I can finish the game. I also think it is a bit unfair for me to spot and mark targets with my drone and my AI crew somehow targets them and can wipe them out with a single shot, sometimes even thru what appears to be solid walls. My recommendation is to get the MSR, HTI, M249, and the explosive drone as soon as possible. I also think that the fastest revive skills and best binocular skills are a must. The binoculars are very handy maxed out for when drones are jammed. I have now seen videos where the streamer uses the EMP drone almost exclusively to take down road convoys. I haven't done that yet. I usually just assault the escort vehicles from the air and then land next to the truck and loot it. From the ground, I usually shoot up the rear escort vehicle and then run the other 2 vehicles off the road and loot the truck. I love the helicopters for close air-to-ground combat. I fly, and the AI teammates shoot the crap out of everything once I give the order. I'm thinking I may start playing online, but I haven't done it yet. I'm thinking that human teammates will probably do better than the AI. BUT, the AI teammates are very good, in my opinion. The AI enemies are almost always very good. A couple times the AI teammates and the AI enemies have gotten stuck around vehicles or other obstacles, but usually they are very, very "smart", sometimes too smart, especially when I get surprised by an enemy AI it seems that way. I've gotten stuck in the map a couple more time and have had to fast travel out. Not a huge deal, but a minor irritation. Even when I happen to get KIA and re-spawn fairly close to the mission objective, I hardly ever do it the same way the second (or third) time around. It just seems like the AI soldiers surprise me sometimes by taking different routes, especially in the cities. At a fixed location, like a "steal an airplane" mission, they are pretty much in a concentrated area, but they do walk around a lot sometimes, and if they are alerted, they will come looking for me. I absolutely hate the "X" being the machine guns on my helicopters setup. The way I fly, I don't think I can (or will) change the button to control the fixed guns on helicopters. It is a huge pain in the butt to shoot missiles or fixed guns. In order to shoot from anything other than head-on, I have to tip the nose of the heli way down in order to shoot down from any significant height to engage targets on the ground. I believe I have crashed my helis several times because I was pushing too many buttons and manipulating the joysticks on my PS4 controller all at once. I love (and hate) the bullet drop on the weapons. I don't think there is too much side wind pushing on the bullets, but there is definitely bullet drop for many calibers once I'm shooting over 200m. I like this so much better than Far Cry 4 in that respect. The game is still really fun for me, and I'm going to keep playing it until I'm tired of it. 5 stars remains!

*** UPDATE 11/5/17 *** with SPOILERS

Still my new favorite game. I've discovered some glitches with the game since the last patch, but overall the game is still very good. I finished the game for the 2nd time on EXTREME/TIER ONE Level 19 when Karen Bowman shot El Seuno a few times and finished him off.

The good:

TREMENDOUS improvement in the helicopter controls over the "classic" controls. In my experience, I can't play the game on the hardest level (EXTREME) and Tier One without using armed helicopters. If you haven't learned how to fly helicopters, you'd better learn. I need them and so do you, especially to take out the armed convoy escorts. I've almost perfected the takedown of all convoys.

I like the realism that comes along with the helicopters. It seems like the wind and rain have an effect on flying. I also like that my helo doesn't slide down the fing mountain now every time I land at a slight angle.

Along with Tier One came the HTI BDC Desert Camo, etc, etc, etc, on STEROIDS, lol. I maxed it out to Level 15. Nothing else even comes close. This 12.7 / 50 cal sniper is an absolute MUST. I also leveled up my ACR to Level 30. It is the best assault rifle for me.

I also like the ballistics of each rifle in the respect that I have to compensate for elevation on all rifles, and windage and elevation on moving targets. No more putting the crosshairs on a target 500m away and headshooting him every time. I think this last patch improved on the distances targets are visible thru the high-power scope. My longest shot has been 795m. I've seen on the internet where somebody made a 1200m shot? On my PS4, I can't even see an enemy that far out, so that shot must have been on a PC, I think anyway.

The bad:

One shot (even suppressed?) and everybody in the world knows exactly where I am? I'm calling BS on that one. I haven't gotten stuck in the map lately, but today when I was transferring El Cardinel from a 4-door sedan to a helicopter, the game wouldn't let me cross some terrain. Really pissed me off. I had to put EC back into the car, drive the car right up to the helo, and then take him out of the car and stuff him into the helo. Good thing no Unidad or SBC were around or I would have gotten smoked. Still pissy about wave after wave after wave of SBC and Unidad that miraculously appear from thin air to fight me with soldiers and vehicles and never seem to run out. Still hate the SAM launchers. I have found that I can land close but still out of range and blow the SAM launchers up with Explosive Drones or C4 or grenades. Once you blow up a SAM launcher YOU CANNOT GET SHOT DOWN AND REVIVED, or the SAM launchers will miraculously re-appear--fully intact and ready to shoot you down. It is amazing how quickly a bunch of soldiers and drug dealers can rebuild a complicated piece of machinery like that... The only way I have found to defeat the SAM launchers is to blow them all up (there are 3) that surrounded the area where the mission was to "Open the Bank Vault". I used an armed helicopter to fly in and out of that area after I took out the 3 SAM launchers in the vicinity (and never got shot down or revived). It is almost impossible to defeat the hordes of soldiers unless you have an armed helicopter, did I mention that? The little SBC white helicopter with machine guns is the best one. The one with rockets is OK if the targets are (and they are rarely) stationary.

Still a great game, and I have been playing it and nothing else for almost 8 months. I am going to keep playing it until I find something better. Far Cry 5 is supposed to be coming out 2/27/18, so I'm sure I will need to be playing that when it arrives.

I paid about $60 when this game came out. Now it is about 1/2 that. If you like an intense action shooter where you can drive and fly and deal out massive amounts of destruction, you owe it to yourself to play this game. The harder levels require some careful planning to get thru the missions. No more smash and grab with brute force. The hardest missions for me were the ones where I had to remain undetected. If you like strategy/careful planning (sometimes) to go along with your mayhem, this is the game. Buy it and plan on spending a lot of hours playing it. 5 stars remains.

for me and my team. i hate the sam missle sites. i have gone in and wiped them out in order to steal an aircraft only to discover that there was another sam missile launcher in range that enjoyed shooting me down. flares would have been a nice touch to be able to drop out of an airplane or heli, i am going to try switching seats with another player and try decoying an incoming missile with a flare gun, but i bet it wo not work. but i am going to try it if i can line everything up. i have gotten stuck in the map 3x so far. each time, i have fallen down into a crevice somewhere, and the only way i could get out was to fast travel out. that used to happen to me in skyrim back in the day. but for the miles and miles or km and km of map this game has, i suppose i can excuse a couple glitches here and there. i'm pretty sure this is operator error, but i am not good at base jumping yet. i've got it figured out how to jump out of a heli or an airplane, tho. the parachute is really cool. there are a ton of different vehicles available. i hardly have to walk anywhere, but i do it just to try to discover everything on the map. usually everywhere i go there is lots of ammunition available, which is nice. not sure how realistic that is, but it makes the game more fun. i do not like how i have to stand directly in front of the ammunition crates in order to re-load ammo. same thing goes for the supply tagging. it seems like i have to be right in front and touching each crate in order to load or tag. when doing air-to-air combat, it is difficult for me to fly a heli and shoot the guns all at the same time while still trying not to get shot down. luckily, my guys out on the sides of a small heli do a lot of shooting, and they take out a lot of enemies while i perform my "circle of death" going around and around a target. i'm sure some company will come up with a game better than this in the future, but for now, this game is the bomb. 5 stars. *** update 4/3/17 *** i still love this game. i'm level 28 now. i've unlocked a lot of cool weapons and gear. my favorite loadout is still the msr in the sniper slot, m249 in the light machine gun slot, the p45t in the pistol slot, and the standard drone. for destroying vehicles and especially that pesky unidad "apache", i do switch to the hti for a 1-shot kill. i have been using the explosive drone a lot for taking out sam sites and generators. some of the bases are almost impossible to get into, and the explosive drone really helps on occasion. for example, there is a serpentidad (or something spelled close to that) in the bottom center of the map. it is crawling with unidad. it also has a sam site and a generator. blowing up the generator opens all the gates, and destroying the sam site helps with a mission underneath it on the map in order to steal a +3000 medical supplies helicopter. i had to attempt that mission 3 times to get it done. i got shot down 2x, and then i figured out that the sam launcher was in that unidad base. so, i had to take out the sam site first in order to not get blasted out of the sky by missiles on the 3rd (and successful) attempt. so far, the sam launchers and unidad are my worst enemies. i ca not say for sure how many, but i think i shot down about 15 apache helicopters one time when i was discovered sneaking around the unidad base after i had released all the prisoners out of the prison. it is ridiculous how many soldiers and land-based vehicles and helicopters spawn almost immediately after the previous units have been destroyed. they just keep coming and coming, in waves lol, and the only way i have found so far to get the unidad alert down from 4 stars is to run and hide somewhere that unidad cannot find me. eventually, they give up, but it takes long way to go before i can finish the game. i also think it is a bit unfair for me to spot and mark targets with my drone and my ai crew somehow targets them and can wipe them out with a single shot, binocular skills are a must. the binoculars are very handy maxed out for when drones are jammed. i have now seen videos where the streamer uses the emp drone almost exclusively to take down road convoys. i have not done that yet. i usually just assault the escort vehicles from the air and then land next to the truck and loot it. from the ground, i usually shoot up the rear escort vehicle and order. i'm thinking i may start playing online, but i have not done it yet. i'm thinking that human teammates will probably do better than the ai. but, the ai teammates are very good, in my opinion. too smart, especially when i get surprised by an enemy ai it seems that way. i've gotten stuck in the map a couple more time and have had to fast travel out. not a huge deal, but a minor irritation. way down in order to shoot down from any significant height to engage targets on the ground. i believe i have crashed my helis several times because i was pushing too many buttons and manipulating the joysticks on my ps4 controller all at once. i love (and hate) the bullet drop on the weapons. i do not think there is too much side wind pushing on the bullets, but there is definitely bullet drop for many calibers once i'm shooting over 200m. i like this so much better than far cry 4 in that respect. the game is still really fun for me, and i'm going to keep playing it until i'm tired of it. 5 in the world knows exactly where i am? i'm calling bs on that one. i have not gotten stuck in the map lately, but today when i was transferring el cardinel from a 4-door sedan to a helicopter, the game would not let me cross some terrain. really pissed me off. i had to put ec back into the car, drive the car right up to the helo, and then take him out of the car and stuff him into the helo. good thing no unidad or sbc were around or i would have gotten smoked. still pissy about wave after wave after wave of sbc and unidad that miraculously appear from thin air to fight me with soldiers and vehicles and never seem to run out. still hate the sam launchers. i have found that i can land close but still out of range and blow the sam launchers up with explosive drones or c4 or grenades. once you blow up a sam launcher you cannot get shot down and revived, or the sam launchers will miraculously re-appear--fully intact and ready to shoot you down. it is amazing how quickly a bunch of soldiers and drug dealers can rebuild a complicated piece of machinery like that... the only way i have found to defeat the sam launchers is to blow them all up (there are 3) that surrounded the area where the mission was to "open the bank vault". i used an armed helicopter to fly in and out of that area after i took out the 3 sam launchers in the vicinity (and never got shot down or revived). it is almost impossible to defeat the hordes of soldiers unless you have an armed helicopter, did i mention that? the little sbc white helicopter with machine guns is the best one. the one with rockets is ok if the targets are (and they are rarely) stationary. still a great game, and i have been playing it and nothing else for almost 8 months. i am going to keep playing it until i find something better. far cry 5 is supposed to be coming out 2/27/18, so i'm sure i will need to be playing that when it arrives. i paid about $60 when this game came out. now it is about 1/2 that. if you like an intense action shooter where you can drive and fly and deal out massive amounts of destruction, you owe it to yourself to play this game. the harder levels require some careful planning to get thru the missions. no more smash and grab with brute force. the hardest missions for me were the ones where i had to remain undetected. if you like strategy/careful planning (sometimes) to go along with your mayhem, this is the game. buy it and plan on spending a lot of hours playing it. 5 stars remains.

title: Uncharted 4 gets 4 stars for now
text: Uncharted 4 - gets 4 stars for now.  I may upgrade it to 5 stars later.  I not read any other reviews, yet.  For graphics and scenery, I would give this game a "10" if they allowed it.  That's probably the best thing about the game so far.  Breathtaking.  I really like how the game started me off with a tutorial, learn by doing sort of thing.  It took me a little getting used to, but not bad.  I have been playing Fallout 4 for the last 6 months (I'm on my 3rd time thru), and it did take me a little getting used to these controls, but not bad.  The two big things I don't like about this game, are:  I haven't figured out how to crouch except with the L stick and circle.  If anybody knows a better way, please let me know.  I'm used to doing it with the R stick only in the past.  Also, my biggest pet peeve so far is it feels like i'm playing a game watching a movie.  There are so many cut scenes that I have actually set the controller down on several occasions and only picked it back up when I realize my character is standing there waiting for me to move him.  There has been a ton of jumping and climbing and swinging so far as well.  I did not play any of the previous 3 versions, but I assume this is the norm for this series.  Joystick control is very good.  Load times are fairly long on occasion.  Save times are fast.  The story line is great.  They came up with a few things I never saw coming in the first couple hours of play.  Lots of action.  I absolutely LOVE how you can blow up stuff the bad guys were using for cover to get at them to shoot them.  The flipside to that is the bad guys can destroy YOUR cover as well.  This is probably one of the most, if not the most, realistic game I've played so far in that respect.  I realize this is a video game, but I would say the jumps and swings and all the climbing that Nate does are pretty unrealistic.  For a human to leap about as he does, it is almost superhuman.  That being said, this is NATE, lol.  I'm at the part now where the cross is going to be auctioned off at the black market sale at the fancy house.  So again, 4 stars for now, with possible upgrade to 5 coming.  Buy it, if only for the scenery...
