title: Far Cry 4 - PS3 - updated 1/11/15
text:
Far Cry 4 - PS3 - 5 stars with disclaimer and ***spoilers***. First, let me say that I have not read anyone else's reviews, so what I say here may be similar to other reviews, but I didn't want any other bias than my own to influence the review. Also, I will be doing a little spoiling down towards the end, so if you don't want to know, please don't scroll down past the ***spoiler***. The opinions expressed herein are my own, and my review is rather lengthy, so if you want to read it all, please pack a lunch. :) I was/am a huge Far Cry 3 fan, and Far Cry 4 is growing on me rapidly.

The Good: (in no particular order)

Thank goodness for the improved driving controls. You can now use 1 stick to go forwards, backwards, and turn. If you have a pistol equipped, you can use your other stick and look and shoot with the hand not used for driving. I love the auto-syringe construction and use for healing. It was truly a pain on FC3 constructing all those syringes--I want to play, lol. The Buzzer 1-man helicopter is a great addition to the game with 1 drawback--you can't go too high or the alarm will sound, the oxygen gets depleted, and the Buzzer will stall and possibly crash. You get to ride an elephant (with proper training, of course)! It is a very, very, tough animal, and it can take out almost anyone and anything--including flipping over cars and trucks! The "bait" is a welcome addition for attracting predators so that they may be harvested for their skins to craft slings and satchels and the like. I really like the addition of the "karma" meter. Now, a player cannot go around nilly-willy shooting civilians without some penalty, and the player is actually rewarded pretty heavily for doing good deads that award the karma points. Having the route highlighted to the waypoint markers on the map/radar is also really good. The game will show you what it thinks is the best route to get to your marker/waypoint. There are some really cool new animals for the game, and some of them are really kind of funny (but still dangerous) like the honey badgers. The Kyrat are very gracious when you save them from getting slaughtered in a skirmish, both with rupees and XP. The radio towers from FC3 are replaced with bell towers in FC4, and they are a little easier to get thru, but only slightly unless you use my spoiler (below), but they are better. I absolutely love the fact that now in FC4, you can kick and slash and break boxes and boards and shoot locks off doors in order to get them out of your way to access certain areas. The artificial intelligence for this game is very, very good, in my opinion. It is amazing how the animals respond when I am trying to hunt them, and how the bad guys attack and react when in combat. You can buy your wingsuit early on in the game, altho I haven't quite got the hang of it yet. I think it is a little more finicky in FC4 that FC3, tho, so that is almost a "bad". The map is new and improved and better than FC3. The graphics are better on the map and on the game than FC3, but FC4 is amazing for the scenery. I absolutely love the mortar. I haven't gotten to the part where I can pick it up and take it with me, but even stationary, it is an incredible weapon. Use it once, and you will squeal with delight, and you will be hooked, lol. Ok, maybe no squealing, but you will like it, I'm almost positive.

The Bad: (in no particular order)

We need to talk about the animals, lol: Some of these new animals are just down right annoying: The most annoying animal in the game is the eagle. Those *&^%$ come out of the woodwork and attack at seemingly the worst possible times. Last time, I was lining up for a headshot on a bad guy when I got dive-bombed by an eagle, and it screwed up my whole plan, ha. Probably the second most annoying animals are the honey badgers. They are cute, but annoying, and they will bite--ferociously. The rhinos are almost impossible to kill unless you use a heavy machine gun. The purple leaf plants appear blue on land, and the blue leaf plants appear blue in the water. I believe a color-blind person must have done that part of the game. As far as the people are concerned, the Kyrat are terrible drivers, lol. It seems like they are pretty bad shots, too, and they are constantly getting into skirmishes and need you to bail them out. Another thing I don't like is I just get ready to go on a mission and the fort I just liberated gets attacked. I feel like it is my obligation to fight the bad guys, even if I want to do something else. That brings me to another point: There are too many "wild goose chases" in FC4, in my opinion. It seems like I set my sights on going to liberate a fort, and the game tells me I need to go rescue some hostages, kill a courier, blow up Pagan's Wrath convoy, or hijack a supply truck. That's all well and good, and I do get XP and $ for it, but I wanna do it at my pace, not when they tell me to. I think there may be some settings in the console that I can modify those notifications, but I haven't checked it out thoroughly yet. Next irritation: the mountains and rock climbing. Jeez, enough of the Himalayas already, lol. When I want to go somewhere, I don't want to have to get there by always following the road, etiher. And due to the oxygen restriction on the Buzzer, I can't fly over some mountains. Ok, I'm whining, but I still don't like it... The grapple hook is an interesting yet annoying addition to the game. There are some places you just can't go without climbing rocks. Well, I don't want to climb up or down rocks sometimes. It is pretty realistic, tho, having the ability to swing on the rope and drop onto a ledge. Listen to the background music: If Def Leppard hasn't sued for copyright infringement, they probably should, unless FC4 got permission. The music at one point sounds just like the intro to "Gods of War", which is fitting for this game. The bad guys are smarter, much smarter, than in FC3--especially the mortar operators. How they can see me through that scope is beyond me, even when I'm under cover of trees and foliage. I think the game designers juiced up the artificial intelligence on FC4, and I'm playing it on "easy" right now to get the hang of it. And it hurts really, really badly when I get hit with a mortar round--as badly as getting trampled by a rhino.

*** SPOILERS *** Read at your own risk:

Learn how to shoot well with the bow and arrow. Get the best bow and sight and arrows as quickly as possible. This is the absolute best way to go early on, as far as I'm concerned. It is very rewarding to get clean kills and harvest 2x as many skins compared to blowing the @#$% out of animals with a machine gun as well as taking down enemy soldiers quietly. Once you find a Buzzer copter, keep track of that location where you found it on your map. I have one spot that continuously re-spawns a Buzzer at that location. The Buzzer is very handy for bell towers. I have landed a Buzzer on the 3rd or 4th level of a bell tower and just went right in and hijacked the broadcast without navigating the obstacle courses on the lower levels. If you do it right, you can land a Buzzer on a tower, hijack the broadcast, and then get back on the Buzzer, and fly to the next bell tower. The only downside is if you haven't liberated forts along the way, you have to fly clear across the map sometimes to get back to where you got killed last--and with no Buzzer. I have had tigers climb up into a bell tower with me and attack as well as those damn eagles roosting up there and attacking me when I walked in. Oh, watch out for the bees, too. They are ferocious. Don't even be in the same zip code and smash a bees nest, lol. As for Pagan's Wrath convoy, there are always 3 vehicles, heavily armed. Get yourself your grenade launcher or RPG (preferred) and mark them on your map when it is announced they are on the move. Then set up about 200m down the road and let them come to you. Blow the hell out of them with the RPG, lol, and you should be able to kill them all with 3 or fewer shots, depending on how you set up. If you try to take them out with a light machine gun, you are gonna get yourself killed. Grenades and cocktails will work OK with proper placement. Speaking of machine guns, you need a heavy machine gun off a truck or machine gun nest in order to take out the Rhinos. Jeez, those things are like taking on the incredible hulk. And they are fast. And they do a tremendous amount of damage when they trample you. I shot one 4 or 5 times with my bow and arrow, and it still didn't go down... So I just got myself a truck with a mounted heavy machine gun and went to town on them. Also, I did have some trouble finding Yaks. Yaks are marked in 3 places on the main map, and I had to work pretty hard to get at them. Identify all animals (if necessary) with the camera, and then shoot 1 and skin it and get bait and then move quickly after them. Keep chasing after them so they don't get away, or you will have to start all over again finding them in order to harvest more. Use silenced weapons whenever possible to shoot bad guys. If you can, make headshots every time. It's 10 or 15 XP for a regular kill, and almost double that for a headshot. Get the heavy gunner takedown perk as soon as possible. I was getting 375 or 400XP last nite for heavy gunner takedowns, and those really add up nicely for skill points. Forts are brutal. After the 5th restart, I finally took one down by myself. I used the signature weapon "warrior" as my machine gun, and I carried my silenced sniper rifle, my small grenade launcher, and RPG (must have). Make sure you have max healing syringes and 100% body armor before starting in--you're going to need it. You need the RPGs at the end to blow up the helicopters, yes, plural--I had to kill (2) helicopters before liberating the fortress. It was indeed "very hard" as described.

I will write more later, but for the 10 or so hours I've played so far, I love it, and I've barely scratched the surface of the game except for hijacking bell towers and unlocked a few weapons. I have much, much more to go.

*** UPDATE 1/11/15 ***

I STILL LOVE THIS GAME. I "finished" it in about (60) hours. I didn't do EVERYTHING or collect everything, but I got enough to finish the game. If a player wants to just do enough to get all the way thru it as fast as possible, I bet it could be done in 20-25 hours, but that's just a guess. I actually like it better than FC3 now. I like how the missions are less video-intensive cutting to the scenes/missions the game makes you do in order to finish the game. I still hate the grapple hook, lol. I still love the Buzzer--it's one of the best things for far travel and taking down bell towers. I LOVE the "Buzzsaw" special weapon. Have Buzzsaw, will demolish darn near anything I want... The Auto-cross(bow) is also very, very good, altho I believe unrealistic. That being said, there are several things in the game that are a bit far-fetched, so I won't dwell on it/those things... I really like the A50 semi-auto sniper rifle, too, altho I feel it is not quite as deadly as the Z93 fitted with high power scope, suppressor, and extended mag. The rocket launcher I got after completing (4) Longinus missions was really cool, but not as practical as the old standby RPG. Longinus is a trip, lol. He's crazy, but cracks me up. I hate Shangri-La--I don't know why anyone would go there unless they had to. I understand putting it into the game, but it was just irritating to me. I hate the demons, too, lol, at all their appearances in the game. Reggie and Yogi were stupid, too, for the most part, which follows since I had to interact with them to get to Shangri-La. I like how the forts can be reset and re-played. I like the Arena for constant action and mayhem, lol. I sided with Sabal, killed Amita, and let Pagan Min go (how could I, lol?), on the easy setting. I'm going back thru the game now, and I'm going to side with Amita, kill Sabal, and proly kill Pagan Min this time. Pagan has such a sense of humor, I must say, that's it's going to be difficult to bring myself to killing him, but I think I can do it this time. I still love riding elephants. They are almost unstoppable and they can travel great distances quickly. The best weapon overall in the game early on is the bow with the circle sight, in my opinion. It has great range and is very quiet. I did figure out I CAN kill rhinos and elephants and yaks and such with the bow and arrow, but it takes a lot of hits, usually around (6) or so. More later. BUY IT!!!

title: The Last Of Us
text:
This is a very good game overall. There are several things I like and several things I don't like about the game. Let's start with the dislikes: You have to do what the game tells you to do, or you can't move on in the storyline. It is very rigid in that sense. I also don't like how when you shoot bad guys, even when you shoot them with a bow and arrow, and they've never fired a shot at you, AND they are carrying guns, most of the time, nobody has any ammo on them when you search the bodies! Or if they do, sometimes they have very little ammo on them. Then, to add insult to injury, kill a couple of infected, and these critters are carrying ammo! It's crazy! I'm sure the game developers did that so you couldn't stockpile too much ammo, but with the "parts" upgrades, you have to earn the ability to carry more ammo, anyway, so it didn't make sense to me. I also don't like how dark the screen is sometimes. I realize if this were an infected apocalypse, most likely there would be times when we would be in the shadows. There's so many dang buttons to push, I sometimes forget which buttons do what, but I'm getting used to it. Now for the likes: I like/love how realistic it is, compared to how it would or could be in the event of an apocalypse. You might have a million guns, and very little ammo. You might have a shortage of supplies in general. Food might be scarce, and we might have to really scrounge to find anything edible. I "like" how some characters are just out for themselves, it seems. I think people will really be like that if an apocalypse ever occurs. None of this cut and dried, good vs. evil. Those people aren't completely bad, but that doesn't mean they wouldn't use a situation to their own advantage to survive, including leaving your character behind or screwing you over, lol. The scenery is amazing. I have seen other landscapes that are very good (Far Cry 3 recently), and this is just as good. I really like how this game makes me think about how to solve a problem to get to the next "level". Because the game "makes" you follow the chapters how it wants you to, you/I know there has to be a solution to get to that next chapter/level. I love the fact that I can find parts and upgrade weapons. The upgrades really do seem to make a tremendous difference (for me) in the game play. Also, the weapons are realistic. We should be able to come up with a rifle, a shotgun, a couple pistols, a bow & arrow, and the striking weapons like the baseball bat, machete, 2x4, and the lead pipe. Oh, that's another gripe, lol, you should not be able to break a lead pipe after killing a couple infected. I can see breaking a ball bat, a 2x4, and maybe the machete, but the lead pipe is a stretch, altho I realize the game must go on, lol. I would have liked to see this game sell for about $40, but even at $60, I believe I got my money's worth. I am 61% thru the game on the easiest level right now, and if I change my mind about the game, good or bad, I will report back here. Definitely buy this game. You won't be sorry.

**UPDATE** 7/21/13 **partial SPOILER at the bottom** I just finished the game on the easiest level yesterday. It's still a great game. It was still pretty hard for me. I can imagine if I decide to play it again that it will be much more difficult to complete on the higher levels. These infected are merciless, lol. They swarmed me and bit my neck with no remorse at all. My best advice, now that I've finished the game once, is to concentrate on maximizing a few key skills, as in maximum health and steady aim, and also to maximize a few key weapons. I prefer the shotgun for close range (with max "clip" capacity), the rifle for long range, and the scoped pistol for all ranges. One thing about that scoped pistol--it's essentially a 1-hit, 1-kill weapon most of the time. The downside to that pistol is the reload time and "clip" capacity. (To be more technical, a "clip" is a stripper clip used to load "magazines", and magazines are what hold the bullets that feed the pistol, rifle, or shotgun, generally. A "gun" is a field gun or large piece of artillery, not something you can hold in your hand.) You military personnel will appreciate that lesson, lol. Anyway...that scoped pistol is the bomb. Unfortunately, by time I got it in the game, I was using my "parts" to develop my rifle and shotgun, and I had already used a LOT of parts on the semi-automatic pistol. You really do have to choose which skills and weapons you want to develop, because there's not enough skill points and weapons upgrades parts to completely upgrade every weapon. As for bombs, they are the equivalent to a proximity grenade. Carry 3 with you at all times whenever possible. They are the single best hand-thrown weapon available, in my opinion. I love the explosive power they have, and they also stay un-exploded until an enemy comes within range. Throughout almost the entire game, there are entirely too many bottles and bricks, lol. I personally found it difficult to want to pick up bottles and bricks when there were multiple enemies in the vicinity. It really was too dangerous with several clickers and runners mucking about. Once 1 of them "sees" you, they are all on you in an instant, so the bricks and bottle have to be very precise if you use them. Bricks and bottles come in very handy, tho, in a burning restaurant, js. One thing that was neat and horrifying all at the same time was switching between the 2 main characters in the last approx. 30% of the game. I will say the scenarios were excellent, and again, probably realistic as to what COULD happen in the event of an apocalypse. **SPOILER** I hated the very end. Maybe that's what the designers were trying to make me feel. I didn't like that Ellie got taken, I got knocked in the head, and that they were going to cut her open. I didn't like having to kill people who were essentially "good" people looking for a cure to save mankind. I didn't like that I earned an assault rifle so close to the end of the game, when I definitely could have used that rifle against the hordes earlier on in the game. I imagine a good player could do just fine without it. I felt like the game ended pretty abruptly after that. I also couldn't tell whether Joel was lying about finding other "immune" subjects, or if Ellie was the only one. Regardless, still a very good game. You should still buy it. :)

title: 4.5 stars - great game
text: This game is awesome.  It would get 5 stars except for a couple negative things:  First of all, I would think someone from Remington would review the weapons being used in the game since a lot of the weapons are manufactured by Remington.  For example, most shotguns can only hold 3 rounds unless there's a magazine extension attached.  I've earned a shotgun that holds 12 rounds!  Great fun, but not realistic.  Yes, I know this is a shoot 'em up hunting game, and sometimes they do have to bend the rules a little to make it more playable.  I personally own an 870 SuperMag Turkey gun, and even with the mag extension, in real life, it only holds 6 + 1 in the barrel.  Ok, I know I'm nit-picking, but get it right, would ya?  The game creators did such a great job on this game that I would think they shoulda got the guns right.  Another gripe I have is the high-powered rifles that shoot the powerful 30 caliber rounds don't take down the game as well as the shotgun or bows do.  The bow is actually one of the best overall weapons you can use for big game, and the shotgun is great for small game and birds.  The bow usually takes down big game with one shot.  The shotguns are probably the best all-around weapons.  It's kinda cheesy, in my opinion, to use the shotgun to kill everything.  You can really rack up some combos with the shotgun, tho, because you are actually hitting the targets but not killing them with one shot.  Another thing I don't like is switching from weapon to weapon.  It would be nice if you could just pick a couple weapons like the bow, the shotgun, and one rifle, and have just 3.  Just like Cabela's Dangerous Hunts 2011, you switch weapons with the joystick on the nunchuck.  It's not too bad, but you actually have 5 weapons to choose from when you earn them, and in a pressure situtation, you can over-manipulate the joystick and pick the wrong weapon.  You have a bolt-action rifle, a semi-automatic rifle, a shotgun, a handgun, and a bow.  So far, I've determined the semi-automatic rifles and handguns are almost worthless in the game.  Starting out, your bolt-action rifle and bow are your best friends.  I'm using a 40" flatscreen TV, and it's still difficult to determine which rifle is which sometimes.  I actually look at the magazine capacity to tell which one is which most of the time.  That's another thing--I personally own a Remington 760 Gamemaster, and it does not hold 20+ rounds!  It holds 4+1 in the chamber in real life!  Anyway, I'm using my TopShot Elite rifle for this game.  I personally think it's the best option.  The Z button is the trigger, and the C button is the reload button.  A player shoots so much, it's nice to have the softer buttons.  It's also nice to have them located together.  I tried this game with my Wii Zapper, my CTA Sureshot rifle, and the TopShot, and like I said, the TopShot was and is definitely the best option for me.  High scores demand accuracy for this game (a lot like Grand Slam North America), so it's nice to use a rifle-type controller with a stock for stability's sake.  You don't ever want to miss to make it thru some of the levels.  I have made it through the first 18 levels in about 6 hours, and several of them are extremely challenging.  I think I have 3 more levels to go, and Level 19 is almost impossible!  I think the idea of the game is to get at least a bronze medal on each level, and then go back and get a gold medal on each level after you've unlocked the best weapons.  Ok, all that having been said, the game is extremely challenging, but also extremely fun.  There are so many critters to shoot that it's darn near impossible to get them all.  The sound effects and graphics are tremendous.  The music is also very good.  I know I concentrated a lot on nit-picking the negatives, but play this game for yourself, and you will see how good it is.  I put it in the same class as Cabela's Dangerous Hunts 2011 and Top Shot Arcade.  Overall, a very excellent game--well worth the money.

title: Big Buck Hunter Pro - 4 stars
text: Big Buck Hunter Pro (BBHP) gets 4 stars overall.  It is a great game with only a couple drawbacks.  Starting with the negative:  No gun calibration mode (not that I found anyway--please let me know if you find one).  I had to literally move 15 feet away from the screen in order to get the crosshairs to line up with my 32" color TV!  I was just on the fringe area of my sensor setting for the Wii, but it still worked/works.  Number 2 complaint:  No individual replaying of problem screens.  By that I mean if you do terribly on a screen, you have to play that entire area (again, unless someone knows differently) over again to get to that particular screen and play it over.  I just finished Top Shot Arcade with all gold medals (see my review), and I really like the fact that you can play screens over and over until you are satisfied with the results on that game.  Now for the good:  The graphics, sound, and screenplay are excellent.  The announcer cracks me up, too.  I think he's a little over-complimentary at times, but he makes up for it when you shoot a doe, believe me.  I really like how you can adjust the brightness of the game with 3 settings.  Some games are so dark.  By the way, this actual stand up arcade game sells for between $4-$5000 if you want the original.  I just got this game with the gun on sale for about $40 delivered.  Absolutely worth the money.  The gun that is included with the game is a pretty good gun.  Had I not already had a Top Shot Elite (TSE) gun, I would say the BBHP gun was the best, but the trigger on the BBHP is a little sticky sometimes, and will not always engage the button on the nunchuck smoothly.  I do prefer the pump on the BBHP gun over the TSE gun, but trigger on the TSE gun is much, much better because you are engaging the trigger directly on the TSE gun.  So, if you have a TSE gun, definitely use it for this game, and don't pay the extra for the BBHP gun unless you can get a really good package deal like I did.  I would like to see the screens last a little longer and have more targets to shoot, however, this being like the original game, you only have what seems about 20 seconds to do what needs to be done, and then that screen is over--just like the original.  I think this game is pretty difficult, and I've played a bunch of hunting games.  On a scale of 1 to 5, and 5 being impossible, I'd give this an 4--just like my review.  Overall, this game is awesome.  Well worth the money!

title: Top Shot Arcade - Should Be: Top Shot Big Game Hunt
text: When I bought this game, I thot I was going to be in a shooting gallery, basically. Turns out this game is more of a big game shooter.  It is a very cool game. I've been using my Top Shot Elite gun that came with Cabela's Dangerous Hunts 2011 (another excellent game--see my review). There are only 2 things so far that I don't like about this game: on screens where you have to pull the trigger and pump the gun a lot, it can get very tiring, especially the bonus screens, and the other think is minor, but there's a load time between every screen. Sure, it's a time to rest if you want, but I'd rather get to the action than to wait every time a screen changes. Compared to Remington's Grand Slam North America (another shameless plug for another great game)there are a LOT fewer animals to shoot, and it seems like the screens only last about 60 seconds, so you need to make every shot count for sure. Another thing I like about this game is the animals seem to react to your shots. For example, you shoot squirrels and coons and possums and birds for bonus points. If there are no bucks to shoot (you only shoot bucks thru the entire game--no does) and you shoot a small bonus target, the does that are on the screen will spook and run right after the shot. I thot that was a pretty cool feature. I haven't finished the game yet, so I don't know if you can earn a semiautomatic shotgun (which would be very cool) by completing more levels. I did see a thing flash on the screen a couple times about unlimited ammo, so it could be an option later on. Overall, the game is very good and very fun. 4 stars.

title: Sureshot Rifle for Wii - pretty good with some tweaking
text: This rifle got 4 stars because I had to tweak it a bit.  Do what I did at your own risk.  If you are an impatient person and / or not mechanically inclined, you may not want to do any modifications.  The first 2 of the 4 things are pretty easy.  First, my experience is you have to be about 10+ feet (yes, I used a tape measure)from the TV in order to get the reticle to line up very closely with the sight on the rifle.  If you are too close, the reticle will not line up properly.  The downside to this is it's harder to see your targets the further back you go.  I recommend as big of a TV as you can afford. I played using my friend's 60" flatscreen LG, and it looks and works great.  I only have a 32" tube TV at home, but it's OK.  As a side note, I actually took the "barrel tube" off of the front of rifle to give it more of the shotgun look.  I'm using it for several of Remington's hunting games as a shotgun.  Second, even with the instructions, the nunchuck can be difficult to put in and take out. My experience was routing the cord thru the left slot on the inside compartment could be a little tricky.  You want to make sure the cord is routed out of the way so the C and Z buttons on the nunchuck engage properly, and also so the nunchuck itself seats properly in the compartment.  You will only need the B, A, and cross buttons for some games, so you might not even install the nunchuck sometimes.  It does give a better feel with it in there, tho.  The next steps get a little more difficult.  I had trouble with the B or trigger button sticking in in the depressed position, so I had to put a stronger spring inside to force the trigger to return further forward after a shot is fired.  So third, you need to take out all the phillips-head screws in the body (don't lose them!), cut thru the 3 stickers on the bottom of the compartments (these stickers show you where to put the controllers), and pull the 2 halves of the rifle apart.  There is a piece of plastic just ahead of the trigger guard.  It is about the size of a medium-sized piece of chewing gum and about the same thickness.  This piece has a bit of glue on it inside, so it's not going to come out easily most likely.  This is a spacer for the 2 halves, most likely so the halves don't cave in when screwed together.  Once the 2 halves are apart, you can see the linkage from the trigger up to the B button on the controller.  Luckily, I think the designers did a pretty good job on this rifle, from a ruggedness/sturdiness point of view.  I just slipped the original spring off the linkage, got a slightly longer and stronger spring, and slipped it on the linkage post, and put it back together.  If you don't have a box of springs (I bought mine from Harbor Freight Tools), your local hardware store can most likely match one up for you.  The spring needs to be strong enough to return the trigger to the forward position (without sticking) after every trigger pull, yet light enough so you don't wear your finger out trying to pull the trigger, so you may have to experiment a bit.  Fourth, I took the ring sight off the front of the barrel while I had the 2 halves apart.  It comes out easily.  If you prefer the ring sight, then leave it on.  I put the 2 halves back together, inserted my controller, and started playing.  It works great now, and I don't forsee and problems into the future.  Alot of work you say?  Of course it was.  What's it worth to you, tho?  I love my hunting games, so it was worth it for me.  I also noticed my scores have increased on every game I've played since my "fix".  Yes, I know I shouldn't have to do this with a gun right out of the box, but I wanted it to work better, and I thot I could fix it.  I'll probably buy another one and tweak it right out of the box.  That way myself and a buddy can play 2-player on these big game shooters.  I chose this rifle over the sniper rifle because the C and Z buttons are on the sides of the frame, not on magazine.  I read several comments about how the magazine-mounted buttons were awkward and made people get sore hands, cramps, etc.  I was playing my shooting games with a Perfect Shot Pistol prior to buying this rifle.  I am more stable using the rifle.  You can use this rifle for any game that uses the B button for the trigger.  With the nunchuck in place, all buttons are accessible on it and the main controller.  So, to recap, this would have gotten 5 stars had I not had to modify it to make it work how I thot it should work.  Hope this helps anyone who is looking to buy a rifle/shotgun.

title: Awesome Game - 5 Stars
text: At $35 on sale, this is one of the best shooter games I've played on Wii.  The gun is worth $30 by itself--I've priced similar guns.  I started out on the first gallery, and within a very short time had 3 more galleries unlocked.  OK, so my hand did get a little sore from pulling the trigger and pumping the pump, but it's well worth the inconvenience.  As an avid hunter, I might have an advantage over someone who has never hunted, but I think anyone with decent motor skills could pick it up and be successful pretty quickly.  Once you get used to the controls, this game is SO addictive and so fun.  I would pay $35 just for the first 4 levels.  I priced the arcade version of Big Buck Hunter, and it's $5000 for the standup game!  It does get pretty hard at Gallery 4, and that's as far as I've gotten.  I didn't even play the campaign at all last nite--just the galleries.  If you've got an itchy trigger finger, this game is for you.  There are tons of critters to shoot, and you only have to switch back and forth between a rifle and a shotgun, pull the trigger and reload your 3-shot rifle or double-barrelled shotgun.  The power-ups are great--slow motion, unlimited ammo, 2x points, marksman (thermal imaging kinda), and health are all really cool. title: Very deceptive, and lasted just over a year before keys failed
text:
This is deceptively marketed for a few reasons, and has given me a very negative image of the Cougar brand and their products. (My Cougar Ultimus RGB was not refurbished)

First, my Cougar Ultimus RGB was advertised as an RGB keyboard. Yes, there is a row that is red, a row that is green and a row that is blue, but there is a single color for each key, and it cannot be changed. That's not a huge issue by itself, but it's part of a trend.

Second, the keyboard is marketed as having red switches. When I read that I am buying a mechanical keyboard with red switches, I assume the keyboard is using replaceable switches. That is not the case. Each "switch" is soldered into the board, including a separate capacitor (I believe it's a capacitor) for each key that is soldered, separately, to the back of the PCB board. The fact that each "switch" is soldered to the board means you cannot meaningfully expect to use this board after the first key fails. In a true mechanical keyboard with Cherry switches or knock-off/competitors switches, these switches, in addition to the keys, are replaceable.

Third, the keyboard, which is already being marketed has having switches, has an industrial look with four screw heads on the front and back of the board. This suggests that you're buying a mechanical keyboard that was meant to give the users access to the board. This is *not* the case. You cannot easily access the internals of the keyboard.

Fourth, Cougar markets the Ultimus as having an "impressively sturdy metallic design" that is "sturdy, durable and stable". My son's "w" key started failing just over a year after buying the board. Once it was no longer reliable at all, I discovered the "switches" were soldered to the board, and saw that the individual keys are inconsistently, and in some cases poorly, soldered to the PCB. Getting the "w" key working was as simple as reheating the original solder on the "w" switch connectors, and removing some of the excess solder in the process. Unfortunately, while the "w" works consistently after this, the "," key transistor was damaged while trying to pry the keyboard apart, as it not meant to be opened by the end user.

A 1-year warranty is not impressive, but it's not unreasonable for a mechanical keyboard with an impressively sturdy metallic design that is sturdy, durable and stable since you can replace switches if you need to. That's what Cougar marketed their keyboard as. But the switches are not replaceable, and it is not sturdy, durable or stable since the poor soldering lead to failure under light to moderate usage just over a year after buying this product.

text:
This is deceptively marketed for a few reasons, and has given me a very negative image of the Cougar brand and their products. (My Cougar Ultimus RGB was not refurbished)

First, my Cougar Ultimus RGB was advertised as an RGB keyboard. Yes, there is a row that is red, a row that is green and a row that is blue, but there is a single color for each key, and it cannot be changed. That's not a huge issue by itself, but it's part of a trend.

Second, the keyboard is marketed as having red switches. When I read that I am buying a mechanical keyboard with red switches, I assume the keyboard is using replaceable switches. That is not the case. Each "switch" is soldered into the board, including a separate capacitor (I believe it's a capacitor) for each key that is soldered, separately, to the back of the PCB board. The fact that each "switch" is soldered to the board means you cannot meaningfully expect to use this board after the first key fails. In a true mechanical keyboard with Cherry switches or knock-off/competitors switches, these switches, in addition to the keys, are replaceable. (Yes, you can replace Cherry switches with soldering, but you can also replace a Cherry MX switch without soldering.)

Third, the keyboard, which is already being marketed as having switches, has an industrial look with four screw heads on the front and back of the board. This suggests that you're buying a mechanical keyboard that was meant to give the users access to the board. This is *not* the case. You cannot easily access the internals of the keyboard.

Fourth, Cougar markets the Ultimus as having an "impressively sturdy metallic design" that is "sturdy, durable and stable". My son's "w" key started failing just over a year after buying the board. Once it was no longer reliable at all, I discovered the "switches" were soldered to the board, and saw that the individual keys are inconsistently, and in some cases poorly, soldered to the PCB. Getting the "w" key working was as simple as reheating the original solder on the "w" switch connectors, and removing some of the excess solder in the process. Unfortunately, while the "w" works consistently after this, the "," key transistor was damaged while trying to pry the keyboard apart, as it not meant to be opened by the end user.

A 1-year warranty is not impressive, but it's not unreasonable for a mechanical keyboard with an impressively sturdy metallic design that is sturdy, durable and stable since you can replace switches if you need to. That's what Cougar marketed their keyboard as. But the switches are not replaceable, and it is not sturdy, durable or stable since the poor soldering lead to failure under light to moderate usage just over a year after buying this product.

title: A great idea, good execution, but not one size fits all
text:
I was looking forward to the Onza for about a year before I finally got my hands on one. And it really is a very impressive controller, and assuming Razer's worked out their quality control issues I would highly recommend it to many people. That said, even though I have not had any QC issues with my own Onza TE, I am back to using my standard wired 360 controller with a [[ASIN:B0010YEFSS Xbox 360 Controller Silicon Sleeve - Clear]] and a KontrolFreek [[ASIN:B002R2JCNK FPS Freek (Classic White)]] on my left analog stick. At the end of the day, the deal breaker with the Razer Onza was this: It's just too small.

I'm a tall guy and I have relatively large hands. Outside of video game controllers, I rarely run into a situation where I feel like something isn't comfortable because it's too small for my hands. Keyboards, mice, gloves, sporting equipment grips...they're all cases where a proper fit helps maximize comfort and performance, and they're all available in different sizes. Third party controllers have been available at the same size as the Xbox 360 controller and smaller, and I've bought a [[ASIN:B0000AI1KT Microcon Wireless Controller]] for my son, as I know a properly sized controller makes a big difference. Sadly, there hasn't been a large controller available this console generation, so my sleeve + FPS freek solution is the best fit I've been able to find.

Performance wise, there are a lot of things in the Razer Onza controller that I am quite happy with, enough that I really wanted to find a way to use it as my main controller. After using it for a while, my main pros would be as follow:

- Excellent backlighting on face buttons (although and option to turn this off would be nice for people who play in dark projector rooms)
- Excellent tactile and audio feedback on the face buttons, which have very little travel distance. This was probably the single most impressive part of the controller for me. Clicking these buttons feels, and sounds, very much like clicking a high quality mouse button, and were the buttons both a little bigger and a little farther apart, they'd be perfect.
- Fantastic cable. It may sound minor, but I game on high quality wired arcade sticks and wired controllers, and the quality and length of the cable of the Onza is better than any of my other peripherals. A very nice touch.
- Rubberized coating: Similar to the silicon sleeve I use on my Xbox 360 controller, this is a nice touch that is definitely an improvement over a standard plastic controller.

The things I don't feel strongly positive or negatively about are as follows:
- Programmable shoulder buttons: These are a great idea, but they are too small, too close to the normal RB and LB buttons, and cannot be mapped to the D-pad directions, despite the D-pad basically being split into four distinct buttons. I am sure, with time, I could have gotten used to these, but their size and proximity to the RB/LB buttons was a constant reminder of how small the controller feels in my hands.
- Adjustable tension knobs did not have nearly the impact or usefulness that I thought they might. While they can be adjusted, I didn't find a "sweet spot" in tension that I missed when I went back to my standard 360 controller. I definitely appreciate this feature, but it's not as important as I originally thought it would be.
- The location of the start and back buttons are out of the way. For games where you want to use the start and back buttons regularly, mapping one or both buttons to the programmable buttons is probably far more efficient and ergonomic than trying to use the buttons in their current location. For games where you want to use the start and/or back buttons regularly and also use the programmable buttons for other functions, their location may be frustrating, but I don't consider a con the way some other people do.
- It seems like there's a slightly reduced travel distance for the triggers, and they feel different, but I didn't feel like they were much better or worse than the standard 360 controller.

Other than size, the one area where the controller disappointed me was the D-pad buttons. The d-pad was supposed to be an improvement over the 360, but it isn't. While the d-pad on the normal 360 isn't great, it can be used in a lot of different genres. The Onza's design suggests it was specifically designed for use as for discrete buttons to be used for inventory selection, but the clunky plastic buttons don't even excel in that area. I can't imagine anyone trying to use it to play retro games, fighting games or anything else where you'd want precise 8-directional controls. Worse yet, the programmable buttons cannot be mapped to the D-pad, so you have no choice but to use the d-pad.

If I wore an M-sized men's golf glove, I'd probably love the Onza. I'm confident I'd at least like it enough to at least give it four-stars and use it instead of the 360 standard wired controller. But as it is, it's too small. I understand that it looks about the same size as the 360, but it's ergonomics (which might make it feel better for people with the right sized hands) make the size disparity feel worse, and it feels even smaller once you compare it to a 360 controller with a silicon sleeve.

I wrote Razer, and even got a reply back, about the controller size. It sounds like Razer is at least considering the option of making the Onza available in a larger size. Someone should. With all the time and money people spend gaming, there's surely a built-up market of adults with larger hands who'd gladly spend money on a high quality controller made with their hand size in mind.

I'm hopeful that Razer will take criticism of the first Razer Onza TE, and use it to create an updated and improved version. Should a larger version of the Onza be made available, I will buy it. Ideally, they'll update the Onza with a better D-pad, the option to map the d-pad buttons to the programmable buttons, and make it available in different sizes (maybe S, M and L?). An L or XL Onza with a better d-pad that can be mapped to the programmable buttons and an option to turn the back-lighting for the buttons off would basically be my dream controller, hopefully one that I'll see one day.

title: The best Call of Duty game I've played yet
text:
I am a huge fan of World at War, finding the zombies, multiplayer and single player to all be excellent game modes. I was also very impressed by Call of Duty 4's single player and multiplayer, but found myself very let down by a short, offensive and unentertaining single player campaign in MW2, coupled with a buggy multiplayer experience that I gave up on within a few months of purchasing the game. (For a long list of my complaints, see the Amazon review I wrote for MW2: http://www.amazon.com/review/R2ATUPNS1NWWKR/ref=cm_cr_rdp_perm )

I was tentatively hopeful that Black Ops would provide a more enjoyable experience. I was blown away by how good this game is. First, if you view my MW2 review, every single one of the key issues/suggestions I had has been fixed/implemented in Black Ops. Beyond that, the single player is longer, more entertaining and more interesting than MW2. The multiplayer feels more like COD4 and COD:WaW than MW2, which is a very good thing in my book. However, the game does borrow many of the ideas, perks and tweaks that MW2 implemented, which results in the best COD multiplayer experience I have seen yet.

Zombies also makes a return in COD:BO, with two full fledged maps, as well as a hidden game (Dead Ops Arcade) and the classic game Zork both being accessible through a PC terminal hidden in the main menu of the game.

All said and done, a fan of the single player will find that the intel, variable difficulties and enjoyable campaign will provide over a dozen hours of entertainment. I know first hand that zombies alone can provide dozens and dozens hours of entertainment, and the multiplayer is the best online FPS experience I have had on the 360 to date. (I consider it superior to the past COD games, as well as Halo, Gears of War and Battlefield games.)

I've spent well over 250 hours on both COD4 and COD:WaW, and I highly expect to find even more enjoyment and reasons to keep playing with Call of Duty: Black Ops. While not all game types will align with everyone's tastes, I fully expect there to enough here for every fan of first person shooters to be able to find enough entertainment to justify a purchase.

When we did lose people, they had no way of telling us, we had to figure out who was and who wasn't there. If Modern Warfare 2 would allow Party Chat, they'd be able to say, "Hey guys, I got booted." But virtually every game mode requires you to leave party chat to play. Even game modes where you can speak the entire time. Yes, you do have the option to mute people rather quickly, and my friends who played for several hours today muted hundreds of people today...but even then, if you want to talk with your friends about work, life and the game while playing, you have no idea who could be listening in to your conversation. If this is supposed to make us talk to people, it's just going to result in groups of people talking over each other, as I expect quite a lot of people will keep chattering away, but will have either muted everyone who's not their friend or set their Xbox settings so they can only hear people on their friends list. (The Xbox 360 party chat function had meant that that wasn't necessary...but if I do keep playing this game, I may have to set my account chat setting to friend list only...which I'd rather not do.)

When we did finally get into a game, over half the games we entered were yellow connections or worse, and the majority of those were quit out of because the connection was so bad it was unplayable. The same problem plagued Call of Duty 4 but wasn't nearly this bad. Treyarch was able to add a "Local" and "Locale Only" search option to Call of Duty: World at War, which allowed my friends and I to wait for a good game. If it took 15 minutes to get a game going, it was better than spending 30 minutes jumping out of unplayable games that we were repeatedly thrown into, losing friends on the way, and constantly having to reinvite people to the party but being unable to talk with them half the time due to the lack of Party Chat. (Party chat allows you to talk during loading screens and when people are booted or trying to join.) Infinity Ward failed to recognize how beneficial the "Locale Only" search option was, which was a key reason World at War was my group of friends' game of choice over the last year. After a full year of caring about each win (2,747), and loss (645), in World at War, I'm already of the mentality that I don't care about taking a loss in Modern Warfare 2, because the number of unplayable connections and friends lost when joining games is going to mean that dropping out of games is going to become a regular occurrence again. Win/loss stats mean nothing again.

Treyarch's World at War was also smart enough to include a "Leave with party" option that meant the party leader could pull everyone out of a game together. If someone was getting a drink or using the restroom, the party leader didn't need to wait for them to return to change game types. In MW2, everyone needs to quit out individually, and again, without Party Chat, people sometimes get lost.

Yes, Spec Ops is enjoyable, and I'm sure the Single Player campaign is enjoyable...but I bought this game for the single player, and the sheer volume of frustrating moments far outweighs the few really enjoyable games that were had. Even if the matchmaking is fixed, I don't see myself jumping in night after night to play Ground War over and over, and the lack of Party Chat is a huge strike against the enjoyability of this game.

I'm sure all my friends will pick this up, and I'm sure we'll play it for weeks...but unlike the +10 days of game time that we put into COD4 or the +15 days that we put into COD:WaW, I don't expect to be coming back to the multiplayer unless some major changes are made to fix the matchmaking and allow Party Chat. (I understand the lack of party chat in S&D...I fail to understand the reason for excluding it from other game types.)

As for the harsh grade, I would have gladly paid $60 for an updated version of COD4 or COD:WaW with new maps, weapons and other extras. I don't need a single player campaign or Spec Ops or anything else. I just needed an enjoyable multiplayer that my friends and I could play while we talked and had fun. The game does a very poor job of providing that. The underlying game looks like it could be great, but the hoops needed to jump through to get into one of those games with friends you can talk to is shocking.

I posted this review to the IW forums a few days ago, and I received the reply: "...these problems with matchmaking will sort themselves out eventually with our constructive feedback to IW."

I hope so. That reply made me think that my review could have been more constructive, and on the off chance that anyone from IW would read it, I made a list of constructive criticism that could help them. I thought that list might be worth adding here, as it clearly points out some of the things this game is lacking, possibly better than my original review did.

Please note that the list below is strictly focused on matchmaking, UI and the ability to play this game with your friends. None of the suggestions would impact the gameplay itself.

Here are the things I think urgently need to be addressed, as they're easy to fix but complete game breakers for many:

1. Party Chat: Put party chat back in for everything but S&D. Put in an MLG game room or whatever alternative rooms you want for angry young racists with a mic that don't want anyone using Party Chat, and let them yell at each other in there. Those of us who view online games as a social outlet to play with friends want this...BADLY. Even Penny-Arcade is wondering why this decision was made. If it was to keep us from talking after we die...why can we still talk after we're dead in game chat in every game type I've played so far? (I have not played S&D yet) Is it technologically impossible to prevent people in Party Chat from playing on the other team? I would love it if Party Chat guaranteed that people in your party would be on your team.

2. Match Making - Lost Team Members: I'm still repeatedly losing party members when trying to get games going. Is this really that difficult to fix? I can understand there are bugs that need to be worked out, but thanks to the lack of Party Chat, there's no way for dropped people to let their team know they've been dropped. A message like, "Party Members were unable to join the game, would you like to back out and get them or continue the game without them?" would be helpful. Baring that, making your squad members easy to visually differentiate (possibly a blue background or text for everyone in the party) which would make it possible to quickly confirm all X number of party members made it. Also, just enabling Party Chat would make it easier to communicate in cases where some people don't make it.

3. Match Making - Bad Connections: I'm still regularly being thrown into games where we have unplayable connections (people in our squad will be all red and yellow connections, even when there's six of us geographically within 20 km of each other jumping into a 6-on-6 game). A "Locale Only" option would be very welcome. I'm happy to sit around for minutes waiting for a playable game. I doubt a patch will come soon enough to make me care about my W/L stats...so I will continue jumping out of games with bad connections...but again, I'm more than willing to wait for a game where everyone on both teams has a reasonable playable connection. Net code improvements? Server upgrades? You guys can do whatever you want there...but until I see a "Locale Only" or "Maximum acceptable ping" or similar option, I'll be of the assumption that you really don't care about my interest in a playable connection, and my team will keep jumping out of matches with bad connections, which is a less than ideal solution when it isn't an issue in other games...

The following are improvements that seem obvious to me, most of which are probably seen in the majority of online games:

1. Leave with Party: This one is obvious. If a group of friends playing together wants to change games types, the party leader should have the option to leave with group. The group can enter games together...why can't they leave games together? COD:WaW did this, so it can't be hard to implement. Everyone dropping in and out separately is annoying enough when you are able to use Party Chat. It's horrible without Party Chat.

2. Add to Squad: There were squads in COD that meant we didn't all have to jump out every time a friend jumped on. They could join the game and if they were on our team, they could join our squad and stay on our team without everyone having to drop out and try to jump back into a game again. Again, this was in COD:WaW, so it can't be that hard to implement and it keeps people playing instead of having them search for games...(with the currently inevitable booting of people randomly and joining games with unplayable connections.)

3. "Invite" option: Why would I want to invite people from the game menu and then play against them? The only benefit I can see for this is people who spam invite people they've played against and beaten... If I use the invite option to invite a friend, I want to play with them. Why not have invites sent this way automatically add them to your squad when they accept? I don't want random spam invites to play against people I don't know, and I was excited at the possibility that we could just invite friends to our team without quitting out of the game.

4. X to skip: I'm not big on skipping levels, and I haven't played enough to dislike any levels enough to skip, so I didn't notice this at first, but why make skipping more difficult than it needs to be? Neither this or the items the follow below are nearly as important as the first six points in my mind.

5. Volume control: Another option I used in World at War that disappeared is the ability to adjust individual volume sliders for the game sound effects, music, and other noises. I have A40 headphones now, so it's no longer an issue for me personally, but if someone's trying to keep the volume at a reasonable level, let them lower the BGM slider and other non game sounds while keeping the SFX (the important game sounds) at the highest setting. When I did adjust these settings, I never felt it gave me any sort of advantage in hearing people in the game, it just lowered the pre and post game music enough to placate my wife.

Lastly, improvements that I'd like to see when getting into games with friends and having fun is taken care of:

1. Barracks Leaderboards: Where did the breakdown by game type go? I could care less about K/D in any game type other than Deathmatch, as that's the only time it's the main point. Even in Free-For-All, killing 25 people and dying 20 times is better than killing 15 people and not dying if you're playing in the spirit of the game...so why create leaderboards that encourage people to focus on kills in game types that focus on objectives? (In the last COD game, I'm 2.27 k/d in TDM and 1.5 in Headquarters, but I believe I have a better win rate in HQ because I play the game...) The new stat system leaves a lot to be desired. It would be great to see a lot of information available, and I understand this may be coming in the future.

2. Lobby Leaderboard: Something to look at between matches when you aren't adjusting classes, and wondering who exactly you're playing with and against.

3. Online Leaderboards: Again these are all things that can be added in the future, and would add to the fun, but aren't as important as the points above: Online stats, iPhone app, Web based challenges you can complete in game, being able to compare accolades with friends, being able to compare individual gun stats with friends, stats by game type, trending stats (k/d average for each hour of a given game type, etc.), etc, etc, etc. There's plenty of data people would love to gobble up, and stats added to my enjoyment of Halo 3 and Call of Duty: World at War. But really, it's secondary to all the multiplayer issues I listed above, and I'd be very happy if IW took those points into consideration and made changes to improve the multiplayer experience for everyone.

Honestly speaking, if all the improvements above were made, my rating for multiplayer would probably be either 4 or 5 stars, depending on how multiplayer holds up over time...but even if there's a great game under all the BS, the BS is currently getting in the way.

As for single player, it's too short, the airport level killed the game for me, and the levels felt uninspired compared to COD4. (Rent, don't buy, if you're only interested in single player) Spec Ops is very enjoyable if you a friend to play it with, but it certainly wouldn't have a big impact on whether or not I recommend the game to someone.

As far as how "fun" this game is...I still feel two stars is the best rating with the current problems it has, and I will update this if IW ever addresses them.

title: Don't.  Just don't.  These things break Xbox 360s.  (read the link in my review)
text:
This is probably the single worst accessory you can consider buying for your Xbox 360. It will adversely affect the power levels reaching your Xbox 360 and can affect the quality of the Xbox 360's cooling as well.

Cooler air coming out the back of the Xbox 360 does not mean that the 360 system components are being kept cooler. When talking about the Xbox 360's heat dissipation the average user doesn't consider the concept of airflow. Using extra fans to add suction to the exit point for air on the 360 disrupts the natural airflow by drawing the stream of air in a more direct route out of the system. This interrupts the engineers' anticipated air route, and the airflow's new behavior likely prevents air from sufficiently passing over components that require active cooling to stay within their operating temperature range.

The more important point, however, is that products like the Intercooler require power, and they are drawing power from the PSU before it reaches the 360, and the power reaching the 360 can (and likely is) outside expected variances as a result.

Those are two reasons why adding a fan, such as the Intercooler can actually create new problems with the Xbox 360's cooling system, and hardware issues can develop as a result of using these products.

Anyone with an Intercooler or thinking about buying a cooling fan for their 360 should read this article first to see just what kinds of problems it has caused:

[...]

For anyone with a warranty, don't even both with these things. If your Xbox 360 is working as is, don't even both with these things. If you're already not under warranty, and you're experiencing issues, and you think the Intercooler or a similar fan might be worth a try, it's up to you. But please keep in mind that you're doing so at your own risk!

title: Give it a chance
text:
I had to rework my expectations quite a bit, but I am in love with this game. I didn't expect that it was essentially a one-player game (2-player if you have a Pro controller), or that it basically presumes online play. With kids in the house I am generally uncomfortable with online gaming but Nintendo really did it well. I've still had a couple run-ins with vulgarity, but the kids didn't notice. It was inoffensive compared to plenty of standard voice chat language with more adult games.

The eccentric aesthetic put me off at first, and so did the initial impression I had with the gamepad motion controls. But give it a chance, it's so worth it.

There are some seriously deep gameplay mechanics at work here. Levels are brilliantly designed, every one has secrets to discover. The range of weapons is astounding. The sound effects and visuals of the ink are so satisfying.

I have spent way more time on this game than any other Wii U title. More than Super Mario Maker, Smash, Kart 8, or any of the other ~20 Wii U games I've bought (replaying Wind Waker might come close though). I'm a 35 year old mom and didn't expect I'd ever get this excited about a new franchise seemingly aimed at kids.

The game initially released with little content, so a lot of early reviewers were unimpressed. It's a shame that clouded Splatoon's reputation, but after playing it for a month Nintendo has been surprisingly awesome about updates and it's pretty exciting.

title: My fave PS4 headphones so far.
text:
This wireless headset is a little pricey, but it does deliver good sound and I've found it's signal to be very stable. (I don't even know what it sounds like when it drops out, something I cannot say for Sony's own controllers with a headset plugged in.) That's what got it up to 4 stars for me right away. Also it came with a really long USB cable that I now use to charge my PS4 controller, now I can actually play with that attached... which solves the "oops, the battery is dead!" problem. I did get about 10 or so hours of time with it on a single charge.

So I told you why I gave it 4 stars, why'd I bump it all the way to 5? The package this came in makes it pretty clear that this is intended only for PS4, no mistaking that. When I plugged in to the USB port I noticed that it did NOT require any drivers from Sony! This came as a surprise because I have a USB headset for PS4 that DID require a trip to the Playstation Store. That implies that it isn't using a proprietary setup! So just for grins I plugged it into my Mac and.. to my surprise, it worked! I did have to fiddle with the Mac to talk to it but it did NOT require any sort of driver installation.

Basically that means that I got a headset that I thought I'd only be using for my PS4 and instead got one that I can use for my computer as well. It's exceeding expectations! Boom, 5 stars right there.

I do have two minor criticisms, neither of which are significant enough to ding the review. First is that it defaults to turning the Mic on when the headset is turned on. Basically what I'm saying is that a couple of conversations between me and my wife unwittingly made it out to GTA V. Now I have a habit of hitting the 'off' button on the mic when I turn it on. I wish it'd default to off. (Note: I have not explored whether or not this is a setting somewhere.) The other is that the first night I had it I killed the battery. I didn't realize that doesn't detect when the PS4 powers down, so it just stayed on. Meaning I have to power it off and on every time I play. Not a big deal, just a little surprised.

Overall, though, I'm happy with it!

title: While not for me, they're still a decent headset
text:
First off, they probably have the best sound / sound control of any headphones I have. Most have one pre-set setting and you cannot change it. These offer you the ability to choose between several pre-set settings (good if you listen to lots of types of music as one setting does not always flatter everything you might listen to). The only downside is if you leave your music on while shifting through to find the best setting, you'll hear the voice telling you what setting you're switching too over the music, so you'll likely want to pause the music, change the setting, listen, if not the setting you need, repeat.

The ability to have them paired with both your computer and your phone and use both at the same times is awesome. Many do let you pair to multiple devices but you can then only use one at a time. This is ideal for accepting calls while on the computer.

It comes with all of the cables you could need.

While not noise-cancelling, they do offer a bit of what I'd call a sound buffer. They're not totally blocking out sound before you turn them on, but they are greatly reducing it. Once on, almost no noise gets in or out.

You'll probably need to read the manual. There's a lot more buttons that the usual 2 or 3 - the right cup housing bluetooth on/off/pairing, volume, and the mic mute button, the left cup houses the buttons for powering on / off, adjusting the sound settings, and the mic settings (there are also multiple mic settings).

The only real downside for me is comfort -- The ear cups having the ability to move is nice as are the ear cups themselves. That said, my ideal headphone has some give to it. I'm prone to severe migraines and ear infections so any headphones that feel like they're sort of gripping my head end up leaving me miserable. These definitely have that clamped down feeling. A little more give to them and I'd have loved them, as they are I just like them but cannot use them very long. Someone not as sensitive will likely love them.

The transmitter is easy to figure out as well, though honestly I really only used it to mute something much quicker than trying to remember what button was where on which ear cup.

Although the fit wasn't for me, I'd still recommend them for most people.

title: So good, I bought 2
text:
Backstory:

My work mouse died so I was in the market for a new one. I searched for mice on Amazon and sorted by highest rated and found the "Logitech Trackman Marble Mouse" with glowing reviews. I bought it and tried it for a few weeks and it just does not have the precise control like a regular mouse. I didn't like it. Since I'm a gamer I thought I would try the Redragon Mammoth even if I was looking for a work mouse. Well, after a week of using the Mammoth I bought another one so I'd have one for home and work.

Redragon Mammoth:

This mouse feels great in your hand. It has a black coating that is rough and gives you the perfect amount of grip. I tried using my old Logitech gaming mouse after using this one for a few days and hated it where I once loved it. Ironically, the Logitech was twice as much as this mouse yet this mouse feels SO much better.

The Mammoth also blows my old gaming mouse out of the water with the programmable profiles. The Redragon Mammoth comes with software that lets you program the buttons. However, what I didn't realize is that it also has 5 profiles. What this means is, I can program one profile for web surfing, and assign functions to the buttons; back, forward, ... then change the profile for a game, and have the same buttons shoot, jump, whatever. As you change the profiles (either in the software or with a button on the bottom of the mouse) the mouse light color changes; red, green, blue, purple, ... This is a VERY cool feature. The software also lets you create macros, which is huge. So for work, I can actually just click a mouse button and it enters my username and password and clicks the Enter key if I want (Yeah, whatever, I'm sick of entering passwords with one capital, one number, an ASCII character, your favorite color when you had your first pet and went to high school). I can automate all sorts of daily monotonous tasks with this.

Gaming:

I am currently using this for Blacklight Retribution and Elder Scrolls Online. The sensitivity buttons on the top of the mouse allow you to change sensitivity on the fly, so I can be in-game and reduce or increase the speed of my cursor. Also, as you change the sensitivity the button light color changes so you can remember that "green is where I liked the DPI setting the most".

Someone mentioned that you would want something different for World of Warcraft ( WoW ). I disagree. I've played WoW since 2006 and this would work great for it.

Bottom line, this is a fantastic gaming mouse. I would have been thrilled with it had I paid twice as much but for this price, it is a bargain.

title: Well worth the money for a very fun ride
text:
My kids and I have played through this game several times. This is what I came away from the experience with; I greatly respect the makers of this game because they got it right. What people want, is some cool over-powered weapons and lots of stuff to shoot. However, you wouldn't want it to be easy and without a challenge right ? So how do you solve that problem ? You throw hundreds of aliens at them. This game is a blast for that reason. Most games give you the cool weapons at the end, or 1/2 way through. Why would you do that to us ?!?!? We enjoy killing things !!! Or, the monsters are few and far between in order to add that scare factor, or element of surprise. Alien Shooter is very well done. Eerie feel and yet major action the whole way through. By the last level there is an insane amount of aliens you have to kill. Just an absolute blast !

They also have lots of hidden items, it is very challenging and there are places you have to try several times in order to make it through. I actually don't know why anyone would rate this game down unless you're expecting graphics like Crysis. It is a low priced game, and the amount of fun you get for that price is well worth it ! You should buy this game because you can't beat the amount of enjoyment you get for the price.

title: Supreme Waste of Money
text:
After playing Supreme Commander 2 all I can say is "Wow". I don't want to repeat what all the other negative reviewers said, but they are all correct. Apparently, what Gas Powered Games was going for on this one was the nostalgic feel of games from 20 years ago. This game takes you back to those happy memories of playing on your Atari or your 286 computer. I didn't believe the other negative reviews that mentioned this, I couldn't believe that my high expectations could be wrong. Seriously, save yourself $39 and just go down the basement and find that old gaming console to get your fix.

I'm getting a kick out of the reviewers who are saying you shouldn't compare this with Supreme Commander and Forged Alliance. Apparently, when you bought "Supreme Commander 2" you should have expected PacMan to load. I know when I bought it I was like "Man, I sure don't expect the prior excellence I've come to expect from this company..." However, had I thought that I wouldn't be so unbelievably disappointed. Yes, it's true, the only way to make this game look good is to not compare it to anything modern that is actually enjoyable to play. Next to World of Warcraft, Dragon Age, and all the other current top games, the only conclusion I can come up with is that their target audience is someone around the age of 5. Otherwise this will totally insult your intelligence.

I could write a book on why you shouldn't buy this game but hey, don't take my word for it, look at all those 1 star votes from once loyal fans of this company.

Oh, and the reviewer that said "Hey, 1 star would be non playable". Lets see... the CD you bought from Amazon isn't playable. You can't play it after you get it for days... You know, I just can't think of another game that you can't play even when you own the CD.

I'm loving the glowing 5 star reviews on release day when NO ONE could get into the game. Yeah, THOSE are legit.

title: So Vividly Clear You Can Hear Footsteps Coming Up Behind You
text:
This Turtle Beach Ear Force XO Four Stealth High Performance Stereo Gaming Headset for Xbox One and Mobile Gaming gives you a more realistic sound experience than the more expensive headsets. The sound is so crystal clear, you can hear a whisper and even hear footsteps behind you. I've never heard footsteps coming up from behind with other headsets- only from the left or right. This headset is truly amazing with it's high performance stereo sound.

The XO Four Stealth Set comes with the XO Four Stealth Headset, which is both adjustable in length up to 1 inch on each side of the head band, and comfortable with it's breathable mesh cushioned ear phones- which also multi adjust to cover your ears completely. Included also is the Ear Force Headset Audio Controller, which plugs into your Xbox One Controller. You have to make sure you plug this straight in as to not bend the prongs and damage the unit. This Headset Audio Controller comes with a bass boost, a game/chat balance, a master volume control and a mic button. You will find you may have to play around with the game/chat balance to get the sounds the way you want them, and then to adjust the master volume control. The bass boost is a huge plus as you can really get some really deep realistic loud sounds for your gaming.

Also included is a micro USB update cable, making it super easy to plug it into your controller and computer to update your controller before you use your XO Four Stealth Headset. There is a removable mic boom with a sponge head cover. This boom is bendable (you can curve it) so you can adjust it to where you like it. It's really great to have a mic, especially if you are online and it works great with Skype. Lastly is included a Turtle Beach sticker and your Quick Start Guide. You'll never find an easier set up to your Xbox One. The headset plugs into the enclosed Audio controller and that plugs into the Xbox controller. That's it- after you upgrade your controller, you plug the 2 plugs in and it's all set. For mobile set up- you simply plug the headset into your iphone, iPod or tablet.

The new features for this XO Four Stealth Headset bring it up to the higher end headsets- only without the high price. The new variable mic monitor lets you hear yourself in the headset and the multi step Bass Boost gives you a really realistic thunderous low end sound. When you get the game and chat volume mix just perfect with the master volume- you can actually hear noises from behind- not just from left and right. This realistic sound makes all the difference for your gaming. The headset is also great when using it for music, tv and movies as well. You can't beat the use of only one cord and no batteries when using this headset. One thing to note, is the audio controller features can only be used with Xbox One, as it only plugs into the Xbox One controller. The sound, bass and clarity you get with this XO Four Stealth, you could never find in a headset in this under $100 price range and for that reason alone it's a great 5 Star Buy.

title: TOY STORY 3- A HIT MOVIE AND A HIT VIDEO GAME!
text:
Toy Story 3 The Video Game is getting no shelf life in our household! This game is rated 10 years and up, but I can tell you even the 4 year olds can't put it down! The game is actually for every age and every family member loves playing it!

There are 2 main playing modes- Story Mode and Toy Box Mode. The Story Mode is fun and challenging where your characters can run, ride and fly through scenes from Toy Story 3. The graphics are amazing and there are only occasional hints of jerkiness in the mainly smooth movements. The Story Mode is very challenging, but also very short. But this doesn't matter if it's all too short, because the Toy Box Mode goes on forever!

The Toy Box Mode is where this game excels! Your imagination makes this game whatever you want it to be! You choose any activity in any order in this vastly large world. You can play as Woody, Buzz or Jessie. You go on missions to earn gold coins which purchase items, buildings or more people. Some people open up other areas and more missions! You can change the town's buildings with paint, flowers and bricks! You can send a towns person into a building and they can come out with a new hairstyle and outfit. You can customize and build constantly! Your imagination makes endless fun in this fantastic Toy Box Mode and the entire family loves it!

I can only remember this much excitement and fun over a video game in the late 80's, when the family went crazy over 2 Nintendo games called The Legend Of Zelda and Super Mario Brothers!! Thanks Disney and Pixar for bringing back the excitement of imagination to a new and old generation!

title: Awesome Game :D
text:
I've never been one to enjoy dancing games, especially the old school DDR (Dance Dance Revolution).
The songs were often too fast, and even though I am a dancer, I had trouble keeping up with the speed of the songs.

However, when I finally got the opportunity to play the Just Dance games, I instantly became hooked and couldn't stop playing.
Just Dance 3 is even more fantastic than the first two, and is now offered on other platforms than just the Nintendo Wii.
I still wanted a game that scored me based on how my entire body moved, and Just Dance 3 did exactly that.
Since it is for the Kinect, there are no controllers or mats, and you are able to move freely. It is slightly more challenging than the
Wii version because the Kinect is picking up your entire body's movement, not just the controller like with the Wii, so you definitely
don't have an option to slack off and just wave your arm around while sitting on the couch.

Just Dance 3 has the original modes to choose from like in the earlier games, and also has added new modes to the mix.
