title: What a Blast!!
text:
For perspective, I am an "accoustic" guitar player (mid-range "Taylor," without electronics). Slow to adopt new technology, I finally purchased a Wii console for my family this Christmas. So we would be ready to go as soon as the wrapping paper was ripped away, I also had "Wii Fit with Balance Board" on hand, as well as a copy of "Guitar Hero III" to use with the "Logitech Wii Wireless Guitar Controller." Basically, the entire family has been playing Wii for most of the last 48 hours, and "Guitar Hero" for most of the last day. I will incorporate comments from my daughter who has never played guitar, as well as from my son who plays electric guitar and has used other guitar controllers and is more accomplished with the games. (He plays most often at the "Hard" level, with occasional strolls into "Expert.")

My controller started right up right away the first time without any problems. Its easy to set up using the Wii controller that comes with the basic console. If you are reading this review, its because you want a high quality experience, so you want your guitar to look and feel like the real thing. Hard wood maple neck. Dark rosewood fretboard. Mother of pearl-like "Logitech" logo on the lower neck. Chrome throughout. It is a very realistic, high quality. If you want the plastic "toy," for your six year old, I suggest getting something cheaper and smaller. It was a very sweet moment, taking this beast out of the box.

I commented to my son that the neck might be slighly shorter than an actual electric guitar, but he said that this controller (entire unit is almost 34" top to bottom) actually has a longer neck than most typical Guitar Hero controllers! For folks who have never played guitar, or are familiar with the "el-cheapo" plastic devices, and people with smaller hands, you will notice that one of the costs of realism is that it may be more difficult for you to get your fingers around the neck. But the five buttons and slide are easy to get used to. Even my daughter (5' 4" - never played before, but with good hand eye coordination) was able to work the neck with her left hand with no problem. (We are all right handed. I don't know what the options are for you lefties out there....If you don't mind the location of the "whammy" bar, I guess you just flip it upside down.) You will need the strap that comes with it, because it weighs alot just like the real thing.

The traditional black picking area over the glossy white is very classy. It is shiny, hefty, and totally cool. This is the kind of gift you want to get your child to guarantee a "wow" moment when it comes out of the box.

My son thought the strum bar was a little longer than he'd seen in other controllers (almost 3 1/2 inches long), which allows plenty of freedom to move the right hand all over the place, and still have some bar to work with. I suggested he learn to strum with up and down motion to prepare for the lightning fast songs, but he is still getting great speed with the Logitech strum bar just strumming as fast as he can with a downward motion, and its relatively quiet.

The buttons work nicely. My son assured me any issues I was having were due to me, not the mechanics of the buttons. And I think he calibrated the timing of the "notes" for a little earlier strumming (using the Guitar Hero software) than I would have preferred. Nevertheless, I'd say the buttons work just fine. Logitech's write-up on the Amazon website is spot on, except perhaps for the sounds the buttons make. Again, it was probably me - my son was playing more difficult songs, and making fewer clicks. But I personally have no problem with sounds coming from the buttons. Just like I have no problem with the sounds my fingers make travelling up and down the base strings on my accoustic Taylor. This may be the software more than the controller, but I like the fact that when you mess up big time, the controller emits a gentle twang; nothing too harsh.

This product is consistent with other Logitech products I've reveiwed in the past. If you take care of them, fidelity is never an issue.

I've got to tell you, for this accoustic player, hitting a few hundred "notes" in a row, tilting the neck up to the sky to activate the bonus and feeling the vibration, fooling around with the "whammy" bar, etc., is hella fun. The star power button is disguised as the pickups, and the "+" button is the bridge. Basically, with the styling and color of this guitar, a little more practice, and a little less shaving, (I already wear glasses), I'll be an Eric Clapton look alike!

And thats what its all about people.

I had high hopes for this headset. I probably should have returned them.

To that effect I still don't know if the app required on XBox One/SX/SS has the ability to update the headset (it would make sense that it should but...). And it's not a USB passthrough issue. One of the VM's I tried I use exclusively for rooting game consoles.

Sound quality isn't much better. Just about any amount of bass will cause the speakers to distort. It just doesn't sound good. I have an old wired set of Turtle beach's that I bought in 2010 that still sound better then these. There is also some kind of connection issue that happens about every 30min of play time. It sound as if it struggles to get a clear connection and the distortion will fade in and out constantly until I reset the head set. It's Very noticeable and very annoying.

You also can not do either XBox or Bluetooth. Xbox sound is on all the time and only Bluetooth can be turned off. That means that if you are trying to use the headset as just a Bluetooth headset it will constantly be trying to connect to an xbox. And every time it tries to locate one, it beeps. And if you do get close enough to your xbox while using the headset it will turn your xbox on. Really annoying stuff.

The only positive thing I have to say about this headset is that it is comfortable to wear for long periods of time.

title: Great Idea
text:
I've had this game for only a week and I am so impressed with it that I felt like I had to write a review. First a little about my background. I bought a crappy little electric guitar and amp around two years ago because I just thought I'd like to learn how to play guitar. I learned a few songs from guitar tabs and a few introductory chords and gained a little familiarity with the instrument. But like with all things, my interest eventually faded and I started playing less and less. The fact of the matter is that learning guitar is hard work, and unless you are incredibly disciplined, you have to be constantly motivated to pick it up and play, or your skills won't improve.

Rocksmith's purpose is for exactly this reason. The game looks and feels exactly like Guitar Hero or Rockband. On the screen you see the virtual fret board and perpendicular to it is a rolling reel of notes that you have to hit in succession as soon as it hits the fret board. All the strings are color-coded, as well as the notes that appear on screen. The great thing about playing this game is that the computer assesses your skill level almost instantly and modifies the difficulty on the fly. Unlike the other music games I mentioned, there isn't a way you can fail a song. To progress through the career mode, you just have to reach a minimum point score on the song selection provided. It's not hard to do either as even if you do badly at a particular song, after a few attempts the computer will ask you if you want to lower the point requirements of the song.

This game allows you to start making real music immediately, and you are made to feel accomplished with such features as a built in tuner, that lets you tune your guitar so everything sounds as it should before you attempt and song. Also Rocksmith turns your speakers into an amplifier. For every song the amplifier is tuned to perfectly match the intended setting of the song so every note you play sounds professionally calibrated. This is such a thrill for me personally because when learning guitar on my crappy amp, I never was able to get the sound calibrated correctly for songs where the musicians used specific pedals and professional amplifiers. These professional tools are super expensive, but Rocksmith's virtual tools are available for no cost to you. You can actually unlock different pedals in this game, and just practice playing your guitar for fun. These features are really something else. They really turn your living room into a professional studio especially if you have a good surround sound system as I do.

Rocksmith isn't just a game, it is a professional musical tool. You WILL learn how to play a real guitar! There are lessons provided that teach you all techniques that you will ever need to learn like bending, and palm muting. This game also teaches you the chords that you need to play. There are musical mini games like Duck Hunt that teach you how to get comfortable with the guitar in terms of switching frets quickly or transitioning between chords effectively. You will be mastering the complex and normally difficult skills needed to be a great guitarist, while having a lot of fun. Learning this games 50+ songs is very easy as well, as you can break them down by section and level of difficulty.

In short, I am very impressed with what Rocksmith has brought to the table. I believe it has started a trend that will continue with other developers and other instruments to make learning to play music very easy and rewarding. Buy this game, it is a steal when considering the value that is packaged together!

title: Good wheel for the money
text:
Context- I spent the last 2-3 years with a Fanatec CSR on FM4 and was waiting for an affordable wheel to jump up to FM6. FM6 is the only game I play. So this review in many ways is a comparison between the two wheels. Overall, for the price, I am happy, though I am wondering if I may be more satisfied by jumping up to a Fanatec CSL.

Pros:

- Physical setup was super easy. Plug and play. I have a bootleg cockpit setup and all I had to do was drill new holes for the pedals.
- Configuration was relatively easy. Took a little trial and error, but I got it to where I'm almost not thinking about the wheel while I use it (which is my indicator of a good wheel)
- Overall precision and control is pretty good.
- Build quality is surprisingly good. The buttons all look and feel good, the metal paddles feel expensive, and the main wheel grip is great.
- Force feedback at 100% is strong enough to probably break wrists/fingers. For me that is useless; I dialed it down to 10% and it gives me enough feedback at that level. I've driven everything from Hondas with "power steering delete" to Ferraris on racetracks in real life, and I've never driven anything with the level of kickback this thing has at 100%.
- Former Fanatec users can save some money by getting an adapter that will enable the use of Fanatec pedals.
- Lap times dropped by about 2-3 seconds with A class cars around most tracks compared to controlled. Looking at telemetrics this seemed to be due to more precise braking and steering inputs. Naturally your mileage may vary.

Cons:
- Wheel is a little smaller than I'd like. Haven't checked the diameter but I'm pretty sure my CSR is bigger. Personal preference.
- No thumbwheel for advanced camera view change in car customization/paint mode/Forzavista in FM6.
- No bolt holes for mounting, and existing bracket hangs low, interfering with my knees when I work the pedals. May have to adjust my rig.
- Pedals feel really cheap (they had to save money somewhere)

Compared to my Fanatec CSR:
- CSR has better mounting system
- CSR has smoother, more nuanced feedback
- CSR turns smoother
- CSR has nicer pedals
- TMX has much nicer feeling wheel
- TMX costs half the price

So in summary, I definitely recommend this to anyone looking to make the jump from a controller to a wheel for the first time. However for my fellow FM4/Fanatec players you might not be satisfied. I only got this yesterday so I will give it a couple of weeks before making a final verdict, but initial impressions are good. This is a great wheel for the money.

title: Amazing SE Console to be SURE!!
text:
I just received my Xbox One S Gears Of War 4 Limited Edition console yesterday. My son has an Xbox One (original) so I have played and am familiar with the platform. I have long since been a PlayStation consumer, this console has changed that.

First of all MS, good on you for including TRUE 4K and HDR resolutions. Secondly, in a market where a 4K Blue-Ray player will cost you $300 easily, may as well pony up the little extra and get the player that includes a next gen gaming system. Sony missed the mark on those items with the "Pro" edition of the PS.

I would also have to admit that the Xbox One S controllers feel more at home in the hand (in this humble man's opinion anyways). I love the controllers so much more than my Dual Shock 4's.

Now for the special edition part:

The first great benifit is the 2tb HDD. I was growing soooo tired of erasing 2 or 3 games every time I brought a new one home because my 500gb PS4 HDD was lackluster. 2tb should clear that problem right up

Next order of business:

That design is freaking sexy!! The red....the insignias.....the real scratches like this thing has been in battle.... Honestly I have been gaming since Atari, Comodore 64, etc. This is the first "Special Edition" ANYTHING I have ever purchased. I never saw the point in spending the extra dollars to get a console that is a different color or just comes WITH a game like ALL consoles USED to do. Well if you got the deal I did this gorgeous edition did not cost much if any more than what the standard editions did but, it was worth every penny. This is the sharpest special edition, nay CONSOLE of any kind period I have ever seen!

The extra sound effects when ejecting a disk or shutting down the console was a nice touch I was surprised by as well.

The controller has all the same design aspects that impress with the console, amazing. Also comfortable enough to game with for hours.

The free included stand to set up you Xbox on it's side was great also. I have never seen the point in spending extra money to make it possible to stand my consoles on their side but now that someone thought to just give me one this is the first console in my household I have actually decided to change the orientation of and I like it.

MS also did right by me by making this a "set top box" and including the ability to run your cable box through in series. Now when I am watching TV I can see my notifications on my console. It is also easier than ever to switch from games to TV. Also, I know there is a ton of stuff I still have yet to discover just as soon as I get that connect, which I never would have gotten if not for being able to voice control TV's and Cable equipment.

Bottom line, worth the money even from the perspective is a "Former PlayStation Fan". Sony I am sorry, and I will be looking for PS5. For now however MS has a monopoly in this household on a ton of products now and I am pleased by this indeed!

If it has any weakness at all, it's that it has a fairly steep learning curve. You can't just pick it up and be competitive in an afternoon. I tell my wife that this game is my version of golf.

The team play, giant maps, jump jets (for flying, truly 3D action), and awesome online performance are all great. But, even the little things are all just right. For example, it seems small, but all of the weapons are intuitive and very well balanced. Pick the right weapon for the right situation. There are no crazy-purple-electro-laser-mega-weapons like in other games. All of the armors have pro's and con's. This is why people can spend hours even just playing one-on-one duels in Tribes 2.

The talk about this game going abandonware is not entirely true. For whatever reason, they cut off the downloads (out of CD keys they said). The best seller series is the way to go if you can find it: no patches needed. (But, free, anti-cheat "defense turret" add-on highly recommended and required by some servers.) If you have to buy used, make sure you get and verify the username and password for on-line play! (And good news, you're able to change the username, too.)

See you out there.

title: Not bad, but not great. But if you're going to buy, get it new.
text: The most disappointing game I have ever played and spent money on. That is not to say the game is awful or even bad, but it's nowhere near as good as I was expecting it to be. I'm a big Twisted Metal fan, with Twisted Metal: Black being my favorite entry in the series. It continues to be. Twisted Metal (PS3) lacks the creative maps and unique vehicles of a great entry like that of TM: Head-On, as well as the dark and interesting characters, style and stories of Black. Gone are the individual stories for every character in the game with their unique vehicles. They have been replaced by an uninspired (and disturbingly realistic, yet ridiculous) larger storyline featuring only 3 characters, all of whom can use ANY vehicle in the game. That is a sin in the Twisted Metal universe. Gone are the unique and variety of maps with hidden areas worth discovering. They have been replaced with a few super large maps that can be split into smaller areas to battle. Some may argue that, in actuality, you're getting dozens of maps. Realistically, however, all of these maps alterations don't change the fact that they feel too similar (they're also not the most eye-catching maps in the world). Speaking of similarities, some of the vehicles feel too similar in this entry. They even have the same specials with very minor modifications! Multiplayer is fine, but with so very few people who play online, the expectation of purchasing on online pass to play online if you purchased the game used is a waste. Buy new if you're going to buy at all (online pass comes with each new copy). But don't expect to be blown away by its multiplayer. There's also the fact that you have to unlock almost everything in multiplayer with "XP" before it can be used online. Ridiculous. I will say it's miles better than its single player, which is also plagued by horribly frustrating events that are far from being the Twisted Metal you know and love. The controls are fine, but locking onto the helicopter is far more difficult than it should be. The game is enjoyable for what it delivers, but it could have been so much better if the creators didn't everything what makes Twisted Metal so fun.

title: First time spending money on a gaming keyboard.
text:
I always just used my K120 Logitech Keyboard, its 10 bucks, I can use up to like 5 keys at once and never had trouble with how many keys Im allowed, its quiet when typing, the keys are easy to press and find, and it did the job well.

However, after 5 years of use, it broke. (Finally, I know right?) and I decided to spend a whole 7 dollars more on a keyboard.

Then I bought this, its terrible, the buttons are clickey, the cord is flimsey, the lights are so shiny it hurts my eyes.

Just kidding.

The buttons are amazing, what become easy to click, became easier, everything feels so smooth, the keys are fairly quiet but its probably just because I am a light typer. The lights allow me to turn my lights off and not have to guess where my keys are when I type. I found my WPM went up by 10 words per minute, originally it was 60, now its 70. Much easier to type because of the smooth and easy transition for my fingers and how open, easy, and strong the buttons are. Each button feels distinct and easy to find for my muscle memory.

The buttons are tough as nails, I can easily tell this keyboard will last a while, its easy to clean under them due to how the keyboard was made, literally can just blow the gunk off with a can of ultra duster.

As for the gaming part, every single key I press reacts, I can press as many damned keys as I want and they all work perfectly. The best part is how the F1 - F4 is set up, each F keys are lined in 4, this means in games that require me to use F1 - F4 are much easier to play because of how the intelligent designers set this up. For instance, in SC2 I need to press the F keys to set up my camera hotkey so its easier to move from location to location, I am CONSTANTLY pressing these keys as Zerg and before I always tended to hit ESC or F5 but because of how these keys are set up, I never make those mistakes again. And due to the distinction of the F keys, I never accidently hit the wrong F key anymore either. Dramatically improving my capability to play.

Whats more, sometimes even with my K120, I have to press more than 5 keys and that 6th key wont go through. This means if I have to run and turn, which is A, D, Shift, and then jump, space, and then press Capslock to talk, and then ult which is `, my ult wont go off because thats 6 keys. In Overwatch this is incredibly common. You need to constantly run, jump, talk, and sometimes ult at the same time. Many times I make this mistake, I will wind up dying or causing someone else to die. However, no longer does this happen with this keyboard!

The LED keys are great, not too bright. I wish I could have a only blue option but I dont mind.

I only have one negative thing to say: The space sucks balls, its loud, and... well its just loud. I am a very quiet typer because of how my fingers have to move quickly accross the keyboard and every time I have to press space I cringe a little. I found out why its like this, the springs arent tightened, whoever made this keyboard made the springs on it very loose however thats also another great thing about this keyboard: You can fix it because you can see the springs, which means with a knife or tweezers, you can easily push the springs apart a bit to tighten up the spacebar. I just havent gotten around to it.

This keyboard is a work of art, for the price, I'd say its 100 percent worth it. I'd say this is worth 60 bucks in my opinion but I'll go with 19, I aint complainin.

title: Better than Bo2, SpawnKills, Camping made EASY.
text:
This game is somewhat of an upgrade from Bo2. It has a modern warfare feel to it, which I like.

What I don't like is the "Spawning". It notorious for spawning you right around the corner from a moving enemy who then might kill you most likely considering they didn't just spawn and are expecting to be able to run in a safe zone, cause you would expect to be spawned in a safer area and not next to an enemy, right.. ? WRONG.

Call of Duty Multiplayer has yet to fix the spawn issue just like the last 3 CoDs. The multiplayer maps as well are way to big than the average CoD maps you are use to. This is a whole different kind of Call of Duty where the maps are Battlefield size and the Camping is made very easy. There are way to many houses, rooms, and windows etc. that are all to easy to camp and only 1 entry point which is the way the camper is facing you. Pretty hard to even stand a chance against a solid camping, grenade proof room in CoD.

I can't really explain the camping, you need to see it for yourself by playing it. So please, REDBOX this game before you do. I love 1st person shooters, but this game is unacceptable and the campaign is so dull.

The Campaign, oh gosh. Lets see, theres a map where you are underwater, and shooting underwater fighting, yes yes yes. Sharks are included in the game, I don't know why. Then theres a mission where you are in space. This part really has no character related to anything you are doing on "Earth" instead of space. You're just activating some laser, then you get transferred to another mission of something else going on. It's really a dull, not well-written campaign. It really isn't fun. The campaign though ,I didn't play Bo2 cause I hated that multiplayer.

Thankfully, multiplayer on CoD Ghosts is fun, somewhat, but its really frustrating to play when you are spawn killed not just once, but twice or more consecutive times in one game. How does one play yet one have a good score if they are being spawned in enemy territory ? It makes no sense, but you know what thats cool. Activision, Treyarch, whoever it may be, Infinity Ward. Doesn't matter.

Call of Duty has been run out dry with modern war Ideas, just as the world has grown tired of World War II video games. I know there isn't much to go off of because we want to make war games with countries, not war games with the USA fighting Al-Qaeda and their corrupt religious ideals.

Seriously though, this game is dull online and offline.

title: More like Multi-Slayer than Multi-Player
text:
When I first played Black Ops 2, I first compared it to MW3, not the first Black Ops. So here's my breakdown.

Multiplayer -

Not such a big selection of guns, very limited in Light Machine Guns and Submachine Guns. There always is a good amount of Assault rifles, but they didn't even include the P90 in this Black Ops. Game takes place in 2025, yet their using RPG's still and its the last launcher to in the game, By the way, there are only 3 Launchers in the game. 1. Smaw. 2. Stinger. 3. RPG. The End of that.

The other thing, they changed multiplayer by a lot. You no longer can get a grenade launcher straight up early in the game, you actually have to level the gun up and it takes time, whether you do good or bad. The perks in the game are changed up too, you no longer can have a perk that makes you immune to UAV's until your level 55. So while you are playing from Levels 1-54, you are pretty much naked to all UAV's. If you can't have a perk to hide you from UAV's, then at least make a UAV a 4-5 kill streak. They have it as a 3 kill streak and everyone in the game pretty much does not have Ghost.

The have also weakened the power of RC-XD's in the game, weakened Grenade launchers, and weakened the Smaw. The Smaw no longer shoots straight and accurate like it did in MW3, it now has a delay and it has a drag when you shoot from a distance, they made the smaw act like the RPG from MW3.

I don't know it is frustrating playing Multiplayer, because the Spawning system in Regular Team Deathmatch is seriously outrageous. I cannot express to you the amount of spawn killings that happen, and it isn't even from kill streaks. There just always is someone near your spawn, the game automatically spawns you near an enemy most times.

If I have to compare it, ALL THE MAPS ON BLACK OPS II, SPAWN YOU LIKE YOU ARE PLAYING DOME IN MW3. IT SUCKS!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

Campaign isn't bad, I like it as always, just watching the clips and the breakdown of the story.

Zombies was kind of crappy, you have exploding fire zombies now. So they blow up next to you, you die. So no point in knifing zombies.

The End.

Game is not worth your money. Save it and buy it when its cheap.

---------------------------------

I was spawned right into an enemy semtex grenade. It exploded and it actually did damage to me, and I literally had spawned, it wasn't a - *get to run for 3 seconds spawn kill* - No, it was die, come alive, blow up. The end.

The spawn engine in this game or whatever the heck you call it, it is bugged or rigged, I can't express to you how frustrating it is to play a 1st person shooter game that is competitive and have multiple spawn kills ???? Wait till they update Black Ops 2, because they really did a Great *Fail* job at their profession in designing a game that is screwing the customers and the players in total.

text:
Playing this game as an upgrade from NCAA 2011, it is pretty good. People expressed a lot of freezing or lagging, I haven't had any as I have played 2 seasons so far. I play 6 minute quarters because honestly.. 15 minutes in game time each in my real life? That would be almost 2 hours or more of playing this game each scenario. If you play your quarters with lots of minutes, that might be why you have so much freezing up on your Dynasty mode, but not mine.

Gameplay, I can't say much for it. Honestly I play on All-American and it's really crap. This is why I give the game a 3 out of 5 overall. When I play this game I realize, when I do screen passes the linemen really run past a block, without any effort of the computerized programmed linemen, are suppose to block.. No not really they run to the right or left then up the field without blocking.

When passing, I cannot express how much B.S. you will experience in the pass game. INT after INT. It is outrageous honestly. You can be a A+ team and play a C- team. If you air raid or pass the ball a lot, then INT's just come as nothing. They are much more common in this football game than I have ever experienced.

The other thing is, when ever I call an audible to make a run-play, the computer instantly picks this up, automatically sends the SS, FS, and all Linebackers to the front of the line showing blitz. --- Really ??? Yes. Really, the computer can read your mind and your plays. It doesn't matter what you do unless you want to burn a timeout on 4th and 1 with a minute to go in the 4th qtr. down by 3. Sure thing.

The Computer also can gut you in the air pass game whenever it feels like it too. This is another thing about the game. You can play a 3 man d-line and have everyone else playing pass with zone coverage and Man-2-Man. This will not work, when the computer wants to score or make a play, it makes a play unless you somehow switch your player and make the play happen yourself, thus making it a "User Pick" or "User Sack" etc.

The Graphics are good, they are an upgrade from '11 but they could have been better honestly. When playing, I noticed the entire marching band in the background of the stands were all the same people and all colored Black. I'm not saying anything bad, just saying the game creators need to put time into the detail and environment and not just copy paste every thing.

What gamers are looking for now, is feeling the atmosphere when playing, thus making it feel real.

I really feel no connection with the game other than I am a college football fan who happens to play games as well.

title: Lightning in a Bottle
text:
Diablo 2 is the most addicting game I have ever played. There is so much in this game that it is not possible to explain it. It is a work of art.

I started playing this game 15 years ago. It is still popular, and it will be played long after people throw out their copies of Diablo 3. Even though the forums don't focus on D2 anymore, it has a replayability and charm that is unique in PC gaming. After all of the patches and new content, it is a polished and really fun game.

Play alone or quest with friends. Try your luck on the closed realms if you want the few items that are not available in Open. Or you can play the other 99% of the game on a LAN! Yes, this is some of the best LAN gaming you can have.

There is a wealth of well-organized information and enjoyable advice on how to play this game available on the internet. Fans love this game, and to Blizzard's credit, they continued to patch and add to the game for over a decade after it game out. It consistently sells well (again, which it will continue to do long after Diablo 3 has been forgotten).

The truth is, this is more than a game. It is a defining experience of gaming. It stole from D&D and many other games before it, and it has heavily influenced many products that came after it. Beyond the gameplay, which is designed by masters and rewarding, the artwork, characters, music, sound, story, names, and atmosphere of the game are detailed and beautiful.

I have been playing videogames for 25 years, and this is one is special. Diablo 2 is lightning in a bottle. Blizzard North is gone, and there will never be another game like this. If you are lucky enough to have the chance to experience this game for the first time, I highly recommend it. Currently D2 and the expansion are only $20; this it the best deal on a game I have ever seen.

In case I sound like a Blizzard salesman, go check my Diablo 3 review :)

title: Great game, needs a little polish
text:
As someone who played a significant amount of Capcom fighting games throughout the 90s, Street Fighter IV does NOT disappoint. Let's break it down...

Graphics: A huge polish over all the previous games. It's a 3D game in look, but it plays like all the rest of the 2D fighters. If you ever played Street Fighter EX, you'll feel mostly at home. What's been upgraded is the overall style (looks like cell shaded, not sure) and a huge boost to dramatic elements associated with pulling off the Ultra moves.

Audio: Finally some love for my sub woofer! The soundtrack addition isn't bad, but I've changed most of the default language options from English to Japanese (much of the dialog is very cheesy).

Gameplay: Huge additions to the mechanics, but it still feels mostly like SF2 from the 90s. It really feels closer to Street Fighter EX with it's mechanics -- and that's not a bad thing.

Online play: PSN stinks (there, I said it). My brother and I play very often to find that it is very lacking. We live in the same city (less than two miles from each other), have the same ISP and we're still fighting the game's netcode because it produces serious lag. We tried last night for one round only for him to hop in the car and bring his joystick.

There are some issues that could get ironed out:
- No double blind selection for net play.
- The challenge modes should show how to complete some of the combos. Youtube is a great resource for this, but the game should have a form of playback.
- Some characters super/ultra are still too difficult for practical use (Guile/Vega). SF2THDR fixes this, I don't understand why Capcom didn't address it in SFIV (while they adjusted other moves, added shortcuts, etc).

What can I say? It's a modern day street fighter that works online and has 720p graphics!

title: Nothing wrong with the game, but BotW just set the new standard.
text:
I'm not pretentious enough to fully review a popular video game on Amazon of all places, so here we go:

The game is a quality game. It's first-party Nintendo on one of their biggest IP's, and the worst they ever make is better-than-average. Let's be real.

Controls and graphics feel modernized in comparison to the original.

The problem is that Breath of the Wild improved on the Zelda formula in just about every single way, so playing this after investing hundreds of hours in BotW feels like I'm trying to play with brain damage. No wall climbing, no flexible weapon/shield choices, no free roaming, no vast landscapes ripe for exploration, and no random events. It makes me feel so caged and restricted that I simply can't enjoy it. I respect the game.for what it is in a vacuum, but remasters don't really exist in vacuums, do they?

Game ain't bad, but you won't like it if you skipped it and then played BotW first. At the end of the day, the real question is "Is this game better today than it was at original launch?" The answer is pretty flatly "No."

title: My first impression is a good one.
text:
This 75% 84 key (tenkeyless) keyboard with Gateron Blue switches was bought to replace a several year old Das Keyboard (with Cherry Blue switches) configured for Mac. There is nothing wrong with the Das Keyboard except that it has that annoying array of number keys on the right side which throws off its ergonomic fitness for typing, making me have to constantly look at it and sometimes miss keystrokes from being off center. (The previous 104 key Das Keyboard was initially installed to replace the OEM Apple keyboard with its Chiclet style membrane switches which severely limits my typing speed and makes me feel like I'm typing in boxing gloves. I also replaced the Apple mouse which has all the ergonomic fitness of a wet half used bar of Ivory soap.)

It is advertised as a gaming keyboard. Fine. Gamers need a reliable fast device, capable of prolonged constant pounding with good tactile and auditory feedback. This is fast and I'll get back with you in a few years as to reliability.

However people who write also need a good keyboard, but without the bells and whistles. Which is my reasoning for immediately pressing the Fn+Light keys to turn off backlighting. I'm still getting used to the feel of it but my first impression is entirely favorable. After just a few hundred words I find that I've entirely stopped looking at my fingers while typing, which is a very good prognostic sign for the future.

The keys have sufficient resistance for fast typing, and the Gateron Blue switches have just a bit more 'jiggle' than Cherry Blue switches. I hadn't anticipated this but it makes for a little more clicky sound and reminds me of the early electric typewriters and Apple II-e keyboards. This is not a bad thing but will take a few minutes to get used to.

Mainly I'm just really enjoying the keyboard for ordinary boring work use; I'm not a gamer. Great value for the money.

title: I love this game.

First of all, why do people review games after only playing for a few hours? Ridiculous.

Second, people are complaining that it takes "forever" to travel because you have to ride horses everywhere. This is just untrue. There are not one, not two, but THREE fast travel options. A map that you can unlock pretty early on, stagecoaches, and trains. But having said that I personally recommend that you ride whenever possible or you will miss a lot of chance-encounter missions, gorgeous environment, and tons of easter eggs.

For me the action and fighting was fine, nothing mind-blowing, it was the beauty and storytelling that make this game special. There are no crazy weapons or insane combos, it's not God of War, but I've never felt so invested in the characters and story of a video game before. The plot itself was fairly straightforward but the voice acting was great and unlike most video game stories you actually see the characters evolve and change from beginning to end. I don't know what else I can compare it to except maybe Last of Us - but honestly I found Last of Us kind of boring, for me this was meatier and there are a bunch of side missions that all have their own multi-part arcs.

I've finished RDR2 now and have moved on to another game, but I think when I'm finished with it I'm going to go back and play RDR2 again. Maybe try being "bad" this time. I don't know, either way I miss the richness of that world and I'm looking forward to giving it another play through.

title: A most excellent pinball game, even on XP, if you know how.
text:
Big Race USA is a well crafted 3D delight. The ray-traced graphics are true-to-life, colorful and stunning. The physics are superb, endowing the steel balls with realistic movement and mass. The tunes are catchy, sound-effects authentic and the voices and spoken lines are hilarious. At high power settings, a flipper will make the ball smack the glass hard, which is very satisfying. It's like having a real, spanking new, well-tuned pinball machine in your room.

The operator's menu lets you create a custom difficulty level where you can choose the number of balls, set how long the ball-saver remains active and tune every other conceivable parameter of game play and scoring. The table-setup option lets you adjust table slope, machine condition and flipper power. You can make it respond like a factory-fresh dream or like a beat-up bar machine if you want. Extras let you examine the 3D game surface in detail with the ability to zoom in to high-resolution close-ups.

I've had this CD for years but I recently tried it on Windows XP with my new Athlon 64 4000+ screamer and was disappointed to find the flipper response was slow and even intermittent. It turns out that XP is not entirely compatible with the versions of Windows that Big Race USA was made for, rendering it unplayable. Fortunately I found a solution on the Web. Run it in Windows 2000 compatibility mode! When I did, all the flipper sluggishness disappeared and the game was fun again.

I play this on my new system in full screen mode, at the highest video resolution with all the bells and whistles turned on. It runs flawlessly with minimal latency. This game is a beauty to behold, still plays well on modern hardware and I strongly recommend you get yourself a copy.

text:
As a flight sim enthusiast i buy most leading flight simulators, if only to satisfy my curiosity. I'm aware of the fundamental difference between the Microsoft and X-plane simulators and enjoy both when i can. i had some experience with x-plane 8 through it's different stages and even though some of the releases were good, some were very,very bad, so is the current release of x-plane (9.31). the flight dynamics really doesn't matter when you have "loose" polygons hovering all around you in mid air. true to this release, the x-plane sim is unflyable and that's after 14 beta versions and 3 release candidates. it seems that nobody bothered to actually check this version on a PC. I gave it 3 fun stars since when you find a release that doesn't have these terrible bugs, it's O.K to use even if it doesn't look as real as FSX. This review refers to a Windows version tested on Win XP machine that runs FSX beautifully and had good releases of x-plane previously installed on it.

V9.41

I took it to a ride a few times and although it flies well, it's still the same difficult, awkward to manage and frustrating software. i set the graphics to some of the highest options but the landscape looks very simple and boring.as well, track IR doesn't work even when checked in the preference screen. maybe if it was easier to configure i could work with it, but i really prefer to concentrate on flying and enjoy the views, as i do, so I'm sticking to FSX. I'll make sure to read about X-Plane 10 when it'll come out but i will not buy it unless it will go through some serious user interface overhauls.

What I dislike most about this mouse is having to use the Logitech G Hub software. You can get things working okay if you get creative with your macros, but it's pretty buggy and just annoying to use. The Logitech Options software that powers the MX-series mice is soooo much better. I'd much prefer if I could use that software to control this mouse. I can only assume that the MX-series and G-series mice are made by wholly separate teams; why else would they have separate driver software?

Going from MX Master to this, I find myself missing the thumb-wheel for sideways scrolling, and missing the MX Master's "SmartShift" functionality, which automatically switches the main scroll wheel between freespin and ratchet modes.

That said, even with the above pain points, I find myself sticking to the G502 full-time, because the sensor is just sooo much better. It's like when Rick showed Morty "true level"... I just can't go back.

title: Great follow on, just wait a bit between games
text:
I played Middle Earth: Shadow of Mordor a while back and enjoyed it so bought this one once the price came down some. I did not remember the specifics of Mordor which was great as it seems like a lot of the same basics are utilized with some new attacks, features, and of course new content. It also seems larger in scope and layout than the original. The attacks can get repetitive but probably a lot of that is falling into a rhythm of a set of attacks that you find mostly works for you.

All in all the variety of attributes for each Captain keeps it from getting too monotonous and even though you find a basic set of attacks that usually works for you, you find yourself trying to remember, or looking up in the guide, some of those mostly unused attacks for getting around some of each captains random defenses. There are still a limited number of characteristic combinations for the captains but there are enough to keep it interesting for the most part. I am currently about 1/3 of the way through the massive story line and not yet bored with the fighting system. Also, I am doing virtually every side mission and skirmish so I likely could be done by now if I were only focused on the storyline and capturing areas.

It borders on being a GREAT game and it is easy to slip into a rhythm of absolutely fun slash and run and attack again and then the fun is shattered when Talibor gets stuck doing somersaults against a wall he should be climbing, as he is getting wailed on by a horde of orcs. The same goes for trying to jump off of a cliff, ledge, or the edge of something. Instead of jumping off your character is doing somersaults at the edge getting hammered by the enemy. If I am "jumping" against a climbable wall or an edge of something the system should be smart enough to get the character to jump up or off. For me this is the most frustrating aspect of the gameplay. However, this is at least offset slightly by some smart aspects of the game. The system *mostly* recognizes that when I "dominate" into a crowd of enemy orcs that has an enemy with intel, it will pick that enemy with intel out of the crowd and let me get the intel from them. Of course the flip side of that is that when you have a crowd of already dominated orcs and enemy orcs all together and you initiate "dominate" it will dominate whatever it thinks is in front of your character, even if it is an already dominated orc. I would hope that it would pick out the nearest non-dominated enemy in front of the character, but alas.

Along those lines there is also the issue of attacks. When in a group of Gondorian soldiers all of Talibor's attacks will fall on orcs. You might bump the Gondorians out of the way but it seems like you do not inflict damage on any of them in the heat of battle. If you are in a group of dominated orcs and enemy orcs the system will allow your character to indiscriminately attack your army of dominated orcs which will include pushing them off of a nearby ledge even though they were helping you fight. At least there is some justification of dominating a previously dominated orc in a group in that it allows you to restore your health but there is little justification in allowing your character to attack your own army of orcs. Maybe attacking your own army builds might or wrath, but usually that benefit is so minimal I do not see the point and would hope that would not happen or there was a way to prevent or disable that.

There are other small complaints such as when I am hanging from a ledge and try to jump up, if there is anything even slightly in the way I cannot pull myself up allowing those below me to possibly shoot spears or arrows into me. However, this doesn't end with my death remotely as often as doing somersaults against a wall or ledge so it is not quite as frustrating. There is a lot to the game and SO many combinations it is easy to accidentally hit the wrong button, or accidentally brush an unintended button along with your intended button and use an attack that drains your might or even wrath when you wouldn't want to. There are also a number of times when battling a captain that it shows the button to hit to block or avoid an attack and then suddenly swaps to "last chance" and hitting the previously displayed button then prematurely activates last chance and the battle is over and you are dead. That is more of just a crappy timing thing, but still frustrating that one would hope the game would be smart enough to catch these things. On the plus side, I do not have the Playstation online subscription but I can still access some of the online material which adds additional content. The online revenge missions are usually a lot of fun and can result in some good loot and added skill points

I have put in a lot of criticism and listed a number of annoyances, but all in all it is a good follow up game and I do recommend it. They did not drop what was best about the first one (I am looking at you Deus Ex 2!) and added enough content and new features to justify a sequel. I would definitely wait between games, as I did, as the general gameplay is similar enough that it could feel redundant or repetitive if you jump right from Shadow of Mordor into Shadow of War, however, for the current price of 10 bucks, it is a steal, and highly recommended for hours of orc bashing/smashing fun!

title: What's to love?
text:
Let me start with a couple of things. First, I loved, I mean LOVED, the original Metro games, to the point of purchasing the "Redux" versions on top of the originals, so buying Metro Exodus seemed like a no brainer. Second I do not easily quit FPS games. Since the original Doom on PC I can easily count on one hand how many FPS games I walked away from and did not finish the campaign. Metro Exodus is now added to that list. I write this at 5AM trying to identify any redeeming qualities in this game while admitting that I have given up and will no longer waste my limited game time on this bag of disappointment. There are some pluses for those intrepid gamers who have the time and fortitude to persevere through a morass of monotonous creature interactions, I however am not one of them. There are a LOT of gaming options out there so trying to complete a game that is not fun is just not, well, fun... That said I still hate leaving games unfinished but this one I can now (finally) easily walk away from. I tried, I feel as though I really did, but in the first main area the endless creature drain just makes this game joyless and unplayable. You gather resources to make nearly everything you may need in the game and early on when they first let you make stuff and you have so few resources you think, "I'll just hold on to these". Then not too long later you feel as though you have a ton of resources and start making stuff and suddenly you are out of resources, and out of resources means you are out of ammo. And this is on top of the fact that none of the weapons seem to do a damn bit of damage to the creatures you're trying to work your way through, even on normal level. I have played a large number of FPS games in the last 20 years, but I still find that for the majority of the games, "Normal" level is the perfect balance of 'story vs challenge' game play. Not in this heap of dung. And that lack of balance wouldn't be so horrible if not for the ridiculous load times when you die (often) from the creatures you cannot kill with your lame weapons. Many games feature a pretty powerful melee for when you are out of ammo or are trying to conserve ammo. Melee here seems to be reserved for only smacking boards to create pathways. And that is only if you have the patience to find the pathways. The highlight system for identifying "interactive stuff" is absolutely pathetic. You have to look at things in a very specific way to get the "use" option to pop up, whether is is a crawl space or resources on a dead body. As you are running through a battle trying to move from cover to cover and grab ammo/resources at the same time, just accept that you cannot do that in this game. Add to that, as you are only trying to grab resources from bodies, you will inevitably swap your existing weapon for whatever crap weapon your latest victim has on them.
How this game has the rating it does I do not know. In the short time I played it I could identify a large number of issues that would kill any joy you may find in it so let me try the pros/cons bit here.
Pros:
Looks good
Sneak feature with humans is cool (I loved Thief for this) so opening sequence in the swamp is good
Mostly open landscape is a plus
Idea of modified/upgraded weapons is always a nice touch
Cons:
Insanely long "Quick Load" load times after dying (I would fall asleep during the load)
Creature interactions are stupid to the point you cannot kill them with your useless weapons or the swamp creatures spit at you from all sides and the big ones routinely wipe out your boat without you even being able to defend yourself
"Normal" mode still leaves you defenseless against creature attacks and depleting resources (ammo and medkits) at a ridiculous rate

title: Decent distraction if gotten on the cheap.
text:
It's an OK game at best. I only play single player campaigns so can't speak for any multiplayer features. The story is decent, but the game play is repetitive with the player essentially battling the same 3 enemy units of varying attributes and skins throughout the entire game with some vehicle scenes interspersed. The graphics are sub par, the controls are difficult, but since the AI is pretty bad the clunky controls are not the end of the world. Reloading was a pain where it sometimes would not take the first time. Maybe they were going for more realism but when comparing it to the slew of other good games out there it just felt off. The game seemed as though it had potential, the player can go around to distract the enemy units, but unless the NPCs specifically tell you to flank (which they rarely do), they do not take advantage of your distractions and may or may not ever get around to destroying the enemy while you are pinned down. One of the best aspects of the game was the "cover" interface and the ability to jump between cover pretty much without injury but it was easy to get stuck behind cover as well. While this didn't cost a battle it was still frustrating.

There are games for sale now for under $5 so with shipping, if you can get it for under $10 total it isn't a bad distraction for a very short story, but any more than that and there are other better options out there.

I can definitely feel the hot air being blown out when the unit is on and my Xbox has not crashed since. It is temperature activated so it usually takes a little bit before it kicks on and will run after the Xbox has been turned off (although it has never run for more than about 3 more minutes).
I don't find the fan to be loud at all. It is basically equivalent to a higher quality computer fan. Yes there is a hum, but it is quieter than a table fan and if you're playing games you probably won't even notice. However, I have not owned this unit very long. As with everything with a fan, I expect it will get noisier over time and eventually fail. But at this price, If I get 2-3 good years out of it I figure I will have gotten my money's worth.
My one criticism is I actually would have put up with more noise for a little heavier duty fan. This one works but I feel like it could move the air a little better.

title: Excellent experience and GOTY contender.
text:
As a long time video gamer who never owned a PlayStation, the Metal Gear Franchise was brand new to me. I immediately jumped into the game and enjoyed the unfamiliar narrative and game perspective. The cinematic scenes are wonderful and lead the story along well.
If you have never played a Metal Gear game, throw the following games in a blender, add ice, and enjoy:
1) Just Cause 2
2) Tom Clancy's Splinter Cell
3) Farmville

The reasoning?
1 - The game has quite a bit of open world, wander around and have fun, but with objectives still tied.
2 - While you can be deadly and run-and-gun in this game (the path I'm taking more of), this game rewards you for being stealthy. You will spend half of your time planning and the half executing your plan.
3 - The game provides you a base to help in research new items and maintain a constant flow of materials and money to further your progress. While there isn't much of a grind to the game, I do find that I have to watch my funds and make decisions on what I want to progress on next.

Two cons for the PC version - no multiplayer as of yet. If multiplayer does matter to you, then I would recommend holding off until Konami announces that their multiplayer servers are stable. Second issue controlling your horse when using a keyboard and mouse. The riding experience is subpar as the controls for riding are not adjusted for WASD so your horse will not make good angular adjustments until you move your mouse in that specific direction. This is fine when running away, but makes life difficult when attempting to fire a weapon while riding.

Based on just the single player experience, MGS V:TPP is a worthy contender for Game of the Year (GOTY).

title: Apart From the L2/R2 Snag, Totally Fine
text:
This controller arrived during the last week of July, 2017.

Have been using it to play Final Fantasy XIV on my PC (Windows 10) for several hours per day since then. (Ok, 12-18 hours per day; I keep it on while writing, typing, transcribing, programming, etc.) It's not STRAIGHT usage, but I'd consider it heavy usage, nonetheless.

Anyway, it's now a few minutes into 29 October, 2017, and the poor controller began to show its age a few days ago, hence my frantic trip over here; you know the symptoms: your character can't move in a straight line, or else keeps running in circles, etc.
In my case, it's also that the system doesn't recognise a hard right turn on the right analogue stick (though I can still press it and get into first-person mode).

Am beyond tempted to open this thing up and see if some dog hairs or whatnot got in there (like the old skool mouses (mice?) that you'd have to clean out every few days, or if the issue is related to springs or gaskets or what.
Truth is, though, that I'm not confident in my ability to pry it open without completely destroying the plastic housing, so let's wait till the replacement arrives, eh?

NOTE: The button-pressing on this thing was never the most... reliable? Like sometimes it would take a shallow half-press to register, other times, it took a major SMASH until the press "counted." It was like this from the beginning, but only got worse as time went on. Again, not sure if it's an issue or materials or dog hair.

I'm grateful for the few months this controller worked "well" (or "well-enough"), and would buy again.

One thing, however--and I don't know if it's related to the game itself, or all USB-for-PC controllers, or THIS controller or what--but the BOTTOM trigger buttons/"bumpers" (L2 and R2 or LT and RT) have NEVER been recognised by my system (again, Windows 10, and NOT Steam version of FF14).
Like, since Day One. I've calibrated and mapped and tweaked like it's going out of style but alas, it was for naught. For the record, I also have a wireless controller for my Mac (SteelSeries, purchased from Big A--well, the other Big A that isn't this one), and IT refused to recognise the D-PAD, of all things. (Yes, lots of frustrations around here, lol.)

Anyway, my experience with this product is limited to the one I got, but I WOULD buy again, and would also recommend to someone looking for a solution to a tech situation similar to mine--as long as s/he knew that this thing would likely have to be replaced "at some point in the near future," which applies to everything under the sun these days (even pricier items).

Happy gaming to all,
SB

title: A fine joystick (and throttle, rudder).
text:
I am longtime flight simmer and own dedicated pedals for DOS PC gamecard 15 pin, and Windows USB version too.
The rudder on this stick is the first that I think is ever bit as good. However you cannot easily program toebrakes onto them (I think that would require FSUIPC (a payware utility for flight simulator).

Both the pedals on the throttle (a large 4 inch wide or so rocker with strong spring), or the throttle (a conventional twist throttle which also has a strong spring- so you don't accidentally engage the pedals when you don't want to). Other inexpensive controllers have twist pedals just as good but I especially like the rocker pedals on the throttle handle. It's on the handle backside where you don't see it from the front view.

The throttle is full size not just a tiny wheel or lever which is much better idea.

The cord between the 2 allow separating them 20" from inside to inside or 26" center to center (see my uploaded images with a ruler). Two setscrews (allen hex wrench) allows coupling the two controllers (stick and throttle) together if you wish).
8 way hat.
Plus 12 more buttons (6 on stick) (6 on throttle).
5 Axis
the elevator and alierons on the joystick.
the rudder (twist axis on stick and rocker slider on throttle-both are springloaded to return to center of course).
The throttle.

If you for instance use the rocker slider for rudder , then the twist axis on the twist can be assigned to another function inside the Flightsimulator key assignments. Or the key assignments page in any other sim.

The size and quality on this controller pair is excellent in my opinion.
Keep in mid it is available in either PC/PS3 or PC/PS4 version.
If you have a PS3 then you buy the first version, PS4 the second version.
Both versions work on a Windows PC computer.

For traveling the whole system packs into a cardboard box 10-1/2 x 10-1/2 x 9-1/2 inches (in other words a tad smaller than a one foot cube).
There is a foam box inside the cardboard box that surrounds the entire thing on all sides, great for traveling!
The stick and throttle are separated and packed in a clever way to fit. I suggest taking a picture of how it fits and folding up the picture and leave it in the box so you remember how. It is very simple if you have the stick and throttle placed in the right way, takes time to figure out if you forgot. :)

The hex key that joins stick and throttle is size 1/8 inch.

Thrustmaster does NOT put a manual in the box with the controller (why I don't know).
Here it is:
http://ts.thrustmaster.com/faqs/eng/thr_eng_00124.pdf

Sometimes things work better than the documentation and product description would suggest.
That is true of this/these controller(s) (in my opinion)!

title: Play it your first time around the block
text:
A lot of people say this is the greatest game in the series. It seems a lot of "impartial" game review magazines and Web sites say the same thing. I can't judge if this is hype or if it's just me, though.

First off, I do not fault the graphics like so many people do. Those who do fault it for this reason are not true gamers. A good game transcends its own graphics. I've said before, even if a game was 8-bit, as long as the story was enthralling, I'd be fine. A real gamer recognizes that aspect.

However, there's a lot of this game that is bad. On to the gist of the review.

A friend of mine has faulted this game as "Final Anime." Truly, it did take on a lot of anime-esque themes and character personalities. I use Cloud as an example. He never grows as a character from the start of the game to the end. No, he doesn't. Get over it. He is the same brooding, emo kid at the end of the game that he was when it started. Not to mention, there's a "huge" reveal about his backstory on disc 2 that's reminiscent of anime, where it diverts from the main story for episodes and episodes and does. not. die. Not to mention, the excessive flashbacks, which, I know are not new to the series, which just play up how underdeveloped the characters are.

Onto the gameplay. Each character is completely indistinguishable from the others. The only differences are pixel sets and limit breaks. Magic should be based on class. In this game, every character can equip any kind of magic. Stats are so similar between characters who are supposed to be fighters and those who are supposed to be mages. There's no distinction between them. The materia system cripples the game because anyone can be a healer or a status magic user.

Sephiroth. Most definitely not the coolest villain in the series. People think he's cool because he walked through fire with a huge effing sword. That does not equate to cool. You want a good villain? Go with FF6's Kefka. He actually DID destroy the world and created a religion unto himself.

I fault the character development the most in this game. No one grows. No, they don't. Deal with it. Real character development can be found with characters from FF6 like Locke Cole. He swears to himself he will never let the fate of his fiancee Rachel fall upon any of his friends.

Also, Aeris isn't the first main character in the series to die. That goes to FF5's Galuf.

Give the game a shot if you're an RPG newbie. It might hold you for a repeat, but it also might not. Take this game with a grain of salt. I own it for completion's sake.

title: Amazing game.  The hype is true!
text:
Wow. Wow. Wow. Wow.
Wow.
Really, it doesn't need anymore words.

This game is insanely beautiful. Motion is fluid and believable, and you'll be sucked in for hours at a time without even noticing. When my husband and I sat down and first started it, it was a story scene that continued to a girl in a room, and then for some reason, the girl stopped moving or doing much of anything. We both sat there dumbfounded that maybe the story had paused, or the game was loading or something. "Try to move", I said. And she responded. Holy crapola! Absolutely NO time between cut scenes and game play. Not an exaggeration at all. The cut scenes and gameplay are completely seamless, both visibly and in the action of play. There are some scenes where your characters talk to each other, even turning their heads to look back or forward to the other character, all while you are currently playing.

Put on some headphones, and you can hear when things are around you. Adds to the creepy factor at times, and really helps in your game play (trying really hard not to leave spoilers). The baddies use sounds sometimes, so by using a good pair of headphones, or using a surround sound system, you'll have a good idea where they are around you. Sounds were not redundant, and were perfect for their environments.

And the level of detail? I have never seen anything like it, ever. I'm not one to reread books I've already read, or replay video games I've already played, but this game is so beautiful, once we upgrade our older lcd, I look forward to playing this game again! It is completely stunning. Blades of grass in the breeze. Smoke, weather, leaves, water and the way you make puddles and how it changes your reflection in the water... Just.. wow.

As far as gameplay, the world *seems* open ended, but really, there is a path set out before you. It's so well camouflaged, however, that it seems like maybe you just got lucky and took the right path at the right time. Eventually, you figure out that it's just cleverly designed. I actually like this in this setting, because it is a particular story line. You don't get different endings as far as I can tell. You learn new skills by paying with "parts" and finding workbenches and vitamins and such. It's a standard thing in most video games, I guess. Parts in this one, "points" in others. Guess not every aspect can be unique. But they tried.

As for story: Wow. It's emotionally deep, it's long, and it will keep you wanting more. Depending on how observant you are on your surroundings, there are stories inside of the story. Notes left behind. Other "signs" of what happened to people. At the end I was like "MORE! Must. have. more." And this is a pretty long game! If there is ever a sequel, there's no question. Must buy.

The ONLY downside is that this game (on PS4) takes up a TON of your harddrive. Something like 45 GB or so. And that's WITH having an actual disc. Yeah. But I guess that's what is required to have that level of of detail and seamlessness, Fair trade.

Overall, probably the best game I have ever bought. This team is amazing, and I look forward to their future releases if they're anything like this is.

title: Concerned about repetitive motion injuries!!
text:
I bought this game for my nine-year-old son and he loves it. The graphics are outstanding. The game play is creative and varied, and generally a lot of fun; and the music is better than any I've yet heard coming out of a GBA game.
BUT...
My concern with this game, (and the only reason I've given it 3 rather than 5 stars), is that some of the levels require repeated, very fast pressing of the same button continuously in order to pass the level... The faster you repeatedly press the A button the faster you go, and if you don't go fast enough, you lose... and when you aren't needing to go fast enough to keep up, speedwise, you need to be manning the B button repeatedly to knock out the bad guys that are flying around, coming after you!... Then the next level requires repeated pressing of the A button again, just to make the guy move (again the faster you press, the faster he goes) I am concerned that our gaming kids may be setting themselves up for problems like repetitive motion injuries, down the road. The game is very compelling and the kids don't like to put it down... but you may want to enforce limited session times (especially when they are on levels requiring this repeated button hitting) just to give their poor cramped hands and wrists a break! (I'm really bummed they designed the control functionality this way, it seems so unneccessary and the game is otherwise quite good!)
That being said, many of the levels have control functioning that is not so stressful and more in keeping with what you may be used to from other GBA games. Anyway, this is just something I wish I'd known before I purchased Dinotopia.

I love the new theme for Akedo Series 3 and my boys ( 3 & 5) were super excited to start collecting the new set. The main trigger helps spin your Akedo figure to do it's normal attacks while simultaneously powering up the special megastruke elemental punch piece (pressing the main trigger X amount of times spins a special dial so that you can press the top button to activate and trigger the special arm and attack.)

The special attack, while looking cool, has a low accuracy and effectiveness rate when in play. Even when it hits in the correct spot, it did not split strike the opposing Akedo Warrior. if not angled just right, it will also go over the head of the opposing Akedo and miss it completely. Sometimes you can use the special attack once...other times you can use it two or more times? After about ten minutes of play, our controller got stuck and the powerup piece does not reset...but it is stuck in the "on" position so now my son can use the special attack unlimitedly...so it's a win in his book. Another con about this controller is that, if you have a figure with a bulky arm or foot for kicking action, it can get caught on the Megastruke punch piece, thus making the attack null. text:

I eventually ditched the InterVideo program and used Dscaler to display the video stream from the gamebridge. This worked rather well, though it requires a lot of processor power to de-interlace the video stream. Unless you have a very fast computer, you'll have to settle for a reduction in image quality or suffer many dropped frames. After picking a de-interlacing algorithm appropriate for my processor's power, there was only the occasional stutter or rendering artifact.

In summary, using the gamebridge with a laptop won't be as good as a TV, but is entirely adequate if a TV isn't available. However, if you use a monitor that is detached from your PC, try a vga converter instead.

text:
I am really glad that I didn't pay for this. It is very, VERY difficult to set up and it came with NO INSTRUCTIONS! There was a little card (about the size of a business card) with lame drawings that meant nothing to me. The ability to get it up and running simply wasn't there.

So I went online and found a REAL owner's manual and I proceeded to hook up using the online instructions. No Go. Nothing worked like it was supposed to and it took a full 45 minutes to get the device to even power up. Then, the onscreen instructions appeared and I tried to follow them, but it couldn't even recognize my internet service and wouldn't connect. Dead Stop.

To make matters worse, the Nvidia Shield needs a remote control to comfortably do the initial set up and the remote isn't included in the original box. It is available as an "extra purchase", making what you get with this initial purchase is not the whole set. So I had to make do with the gaming controller which is too awkward for words. I suppose I could have made it work with more patience, but when the device couldn't connect to my wireless internet, there was nothing else I could do without help.

So I searched their website for technical support, and my choices were FAQs, PAID SUPPORT, and live chat. I chose live chat, which was difficult to access. When I finally accessed Live Chat, I got a message that Live Chat wasn't available. At that point, I had struggled with this thing for 1.5 hours and had enough frustration. I decided not to go any further.

To make myself clear, I am not a novice with these kinds of devices. I own a ROKU 3 and an Apple TV, both of which came with all necessary accessories, connected to my TV and my WiFi, and set up so easily that no instructions were needed. This device bombed right out of the box! I was so frustrated!

If I had ever been able to get it set up without wanting to tear out my hair, I might have liked it. There are A LOT of great reviews here, and so in another person's experience, this might be a decent product. However the initial set up was such a nightmare that I finally was unwilling to invest any more of my time into it. It might me great but if a normal person cannot easily get it up and running without a whole lot of stress, it fails the first and most important test. There are too many user friendly devices on the market, with adequate instructions and reliable tech support that you don't have to pay for. I am really sorry about the time I wasted with this persnickety product. I don't need this.

Perhaps in a few days I might (MIGHT) decide to try again. Not likely, but with all these great reviews, It would be interesting to see if it can be made to work for me. If I can get it up and running and decide that it passes muster, I'll come back and edit my review to reflect. But even if it turns out to be wonderful, the SHIELD will NEVER get 5 stars from me because nothing should be this difficult to start. In this day and age of technological wonders, it seems to me that it would be possible to make thing that are easily useable. And if a company wants to produce a device that is a snarl to operate, as LEAST they should offer technical support that you don't have to pay for.

UPDATE - 1.5 hours later: After waiting awhile, I tried tech support live chat again and was connected to a very nice and patient tech support agent. Unfortunately the agent was as clueless as I was. We spent quite a long time chatting online and they were unable to resolve the issue. The tech support rep suggested that the problem might be my router, however I am not sure this is correct since my router works well with every other device in the house. I have 3 computers, an iPhone, an iPad, a ROKU 3, and an Apple TV and none of these other devices have presented an issue at all. At this time, the case has been kicked up a level and I am waiting for them to contact me. For now, my 1 star review still stands, but I am open to changing it when and if I ever get the problems resolved. But no device that is this much trouble will ever get 5 stars from me - if it turns out to be awesome, I might kick up my evaluation to 4 stars.
